G1.text: ἄλφα a[lfa a {al'-fah} of Hebrew origin; the first letter of the alphabet; figuratively, only (from its use as a numeral) the first: --Alpha. Often used (usually an, before a vowel) also in composition (as a contraction from 427) in the sense of privation; so, in many words, beginning with this letter; occasionally in the sense of union (as a contraction of 260). see GREEK for 427 see GREEK for 260

G2.text: Ἀαρών Ajarwvn Aaron {ah-ar-ohn'} of Hebrew origin (175); Aaron, the brother of Moses:--Aaron. see HEBREW for 0175

G3.text: Ἀβαδδών Ajbaddwvn Abaddon {ab-ad-dohn'} of Hebrew origin (11); a destroying angel:--Abaddon. see HEBREW for 011

G4.text: ἀβαρής ajbarhvs abares {ab-ar-ace'} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 922; weightless, i.e. (figuratively) not burdensome:--from being burdensome. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 922

G5.text: αββα abba Abba {ab-bah'} of Chaldee origin (2); father as a vocative:--Abba. see HEBREW for 02

G6.text: Ἅβελ A&bel Abel {ab'-el} of Hebrew origin (1893); Abel, the son of Adam:--Abel. see HEBREW for 01893

G7.text: Ἀβιά Ajbiav Abia {ab-ee-ah'} of Hebrew origin (29); Abijah, the name of two Israelites:--Abia. see HEBREW for 029

G8.text: Ἀβιαθάρ Ajbiaqavr Abiathar {ab-ee-ath'-ar} of Hebrew origin (54); Abiathar, an Israelite:--Abiathar. see HEBREW for 054

G9.text: Ἀβιληνή Ajbilhnhv Abilene {ab-ee-lay-nay'} of foreign origin (compare 58); Abilene, a region of Syria:--Abilene. see HEBREW for 058

G10.text: Ἀβιούδ Ajbiouvd Abioud {ab-ee-ood'} of Hebrew origin (31); Abihud, an Israelite:--Abiud. see HEBREW for 031

G11.text: Ἀβραάμ Ajbraavm Abraam {ab-rah-am'} of Hebrew origin (85); Abraham, the Hebrew patriarch:--Abraham. (In Acts 7:16 the text should probably read Jacob.) see HEBREW for 085

G12.text: ἄβυσσος a[bussos abussos {ab'-us-sos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a variation of 1037; depthless, i.e. (specially) (infernal) "abyss":--deep, (bottomless) pit. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1037

G13.text: Ἅγαβος A&gabos Agabos {ag'-ab-os} of Hebrew origin (compare 2285); Agabus, an Israelite:--Agabus. see HEBREW for 02285

G14.text: ἀγαθοεργέω ajgaqoergevw agathoergeo {ag-ath-er-gheh'-o} from 18 and 2041; to work good:--do good. see GREEK for 18 see GREEK for 2041

G15.text: ἀγαθοποιέω ajgaqopoievw agathopoieo {ag-ath-op-oy-eh'-o} from 17; to be a well-doer (as a favor or a duty):--(when) do good (well). see GREEK for 17

G16.text: ἀγαθοποιΐα ajgaqopoii?a agathopoiia {ag-ath-op-oy-ee'-ah} from 17; well-doing, i.e. virtue:--well-doing. see GREEK for 17

G17.text: ἀγαθοποιός ajgaqopoiovs agathopoios {ag-ath-op-oy-os'} from 18 and 4160; a well-doer, i.e. virtuous:--them that do well. see GREEK for 18 see GREEK for 4160

G18.text: ἀγαθός ajgaqovs agathos {ag-ath-os'} a primary word; "good" (in any sense, often as noun):--benefit, good(-s, things), well. Compare 2570. see GREEK for 2570

G19.text: ἀγαθωσύνη ajgaqwsuvnh agathosune {ag-ath-o-soo'-nay} from 18; goodness, i.e. virtue or beneficence:--goodness. see GREEK for 18

G20.text: ἀγαλλίασις ajgallivasis agalliasis {ag-al-lee'-as-is} from 21; exultation; specially, welcome:--gladness, (exceeding) joy. see GREEK for 21

G21.text: ἀγαλλιάω ajgalliavw agalliao {ag-al-lee-ah'-o} from agan (much) and 242; properly, to jump for joy, i.e. exult:--be (exceeding) glad, with exceeding joy, rejoice (greatly). see GREEK for 242

G22.text: ἄγαμος a[gamos agamos {ag'-am-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 1062; unmarried:--unmarried. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1062

G23.text: ἀγανακτέω ajganaktevw aganakteo {ag-an-ak-teh'-o} from agan (much) and achthos (grief; akin to the base of 43); to be greatly afflicted, i.e. (figuratively) indignant:--be much (sore) displeased, have (be moved with, with) indignation. see GREEK for 43

G24.text: ἀγανάκτησις ajganavkthsis aganaktesis {ag-an-ak'-tay-sis} from 23; indignation:--indignation. see GREEK for 23

G25.text: ἀγαπάω ajgapavw agapao {ag-ap-ah'-o} perhaps from agan (much) (or compare 5689); to love (in a social or moral sense):--(be-)love(-ed). Compare 5368. see GREEK for 5689 see GREEK for 5368

G26.text: ἀγάπη ajgavph agape {ag-ah'-pay} from 25; love, i.e. affection or benevolence; specially (plural) a love-feast:--(feast of) charity(-ably), dear, love. see GREEK for 25

G27.text: ἀγαπητός ajgaphtovs agapetos {ag-ap-ay-tos'} from 25; beloved:--(dearly, well) beloved, dear. see GREEK for 25

G28.text: Ἁγάρ AJgavr Hagar {ag'-ar} of Hebrew origin (1904); Hagar, the concubine of Abraham:--Hagar. see HEBREW for 01904

G29.text: ἀγγαρεύω ajggareuvw aggareuo {ang-ar-yew'-o} of foreign origin (compare 104); properly, to be a courier, i.e. (by implication) to press into public service:--compel (to go). see HEBREW for 0104

G30.text: ἀγγεῖον ἄγγος ajggei'on a[ggos aggeion {ang-eye'-on} from aggos (a pail, perhaps as bent; compare the base of 43); a receptacle:--vessel. see GREEK for 43

G31.text: ἀγγελία ajggeliva aggelia {ang-el-ee'-ah} from 32; an announcement, i.e. (by implication) precept:--message. see GREEK for 32

G32.text: ἄγγελος a[ggelos aggelos {ang'-el-os} from aggello (probably derived from 71; compare 34) (to bring tidings); a messenger; especially an "angel"; by implication, a pastor:--angel, messenger. see GREEK for 71 see GREEK for 34

G33.text: ἄγω a[gw age {ag'-eh} imperative of 71; properly, lead, i.e. come on:--go to. see GREEK for 71

G34.text: ἀγέλη ajgevlh agele {ag-el'-ay} from 71 (compare 32); a drove:--herd. see GREEK for 71 see GREEK for 32

G35.text: ἀγενεαλόγητος ajgenealovghtos agenealogetos {ag-en-eh-al-og'-ay-tos} from 1 (as negative particle) and 1075; unregistered as to birth:--without descent. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1075

G36.text: ἀγενής ajgenhvs agenes {ag-en-ace'} from 1 (as negative particle) and 1085; properly, without kin, i.e. (of unknown descent, and by implication) ignoble:--base things. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1085

G37.text: ἁγιάζω aJgiavzw hagiazo {hag-ee-ad'-zo} from 40; to make holy, i.e. (ceremonially) purify or consecrate; (mentally) to venerate:--hallow, be holy, sanctify. see GREEK for 40

G38.text: ἁγιασμός aJgiasmovs hagiasmos {hag-ee-as-mos'} from 37; properly, purification, i.e. (the state) purity; concretely (by Hebraism) a purifier:--holiness, sanctification. see GREEK for 37

G39.text: ἅγιος a&gios hagion {hag'-ee-on} neuter of 40; a sacred thing (i.e. spot):--holiest (of all), holy place, sanctuary. see GREEK for 40

G40.text: ἅγιος a&gios hagios {hag'-ee-os} from hagos (an awful thing) (compare 53, 2282); sacred (physically, pure, morally blameless or religious, ceremonially, consecrated):--(most) holy (one, thing), saint. see GREEK for 53 see GREEK for 2282

G41.text: ἁγιότης aJgiovths hagiotes {hag-ee-ot'-ace} from 40; sanctity (i.e. properly, the state):--holiness. see GREEK for 40

G42.text: ἁγιωσύνη aJgiwsuvnh hagiosune {hag-ee-o-soo'-nay} from 40; sacredness (i.e. properly, the quality):--holiness. see GREEK for 40

G43.text: ἀγκάλη ajgkavlh agkale {ang-kal'-ay} from agkos (a bend, "ache"); an arm (as curved):--arm.

G44.text: ἄγκιστρον a[gkistron agkistron {ang'-kis-tron} from the same as 43; a hook (as bent):--hook. see GREEK for 43

G45.text: ἄγκυρα a[gkura agkura {ang'-koo-rah} from the same as 43; an "anchor" (as crooked):--anchor. see GREEK for 43

G46.text: ἄγναφος a[gnafos agnaphos {ag'-naf-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and the same as 1102; properly, unfulled, i.e. (by implication) new (cloth):--new. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1102

G47.text: ἁγνεία aJgneiva hagneia {hag-ni'-ah} from 53; cleanliness (the quality), i.e. (specially) chastity:--purity. see GREEK for 53

G48.text: ἁγνίζω aJgnivzw hagnizo {hag-nid'-zo} from 53; to make clean, i.e. (figuratively) sanctify (ceremonially or morally):--purify (self). see GREEK for 53

G49.text: ἁγνισμός aJgnismovs hagnismos {hag-nis-mos'} from 48; a cleansing (the act), i.e. (ceremonially) lustration:--purification. see GREEK for 48

G50.text: ἀγνοέω ajgnoevw agnoeo {ag-no-eh'-o} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 3539; not to know (through lack of information or intelligence); by implication, to ignore (through disinclination):--(be) ignorant(-ly), not know, not understand, unknown. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 3539

G51.text: ἀγνόημα ajgnovhma agnoema {ag-no'-ay-mah} from 50; a thing ignored, i.e. shortcoming:--error. see GREEK for 50

G52.text: ἄγνοια a[gnoia agnoia {ag'-noy-ah} from 50; ignorance (properly, the quality):--ignorance. see GREEK for 50

G53.text: ἁγνός aJgnovs hagnos {hag-nos'} from the same as 40; properly, clean, i.e. (figuratively) innocent, modest, perfect:--chaste, clean, pure. see GREEK for 40

G54.text: ἁγνότης aJgnovths hagnotes {hag-not'-ace} from 53; cleanness (the state), i.e. (figuratively) blamelessness:--pureness. see GREEK for 53

G55.text: ἁγνός aJgnovs hagnos {hag-noce'} adverb from 53; purely, i.e. honestly:--sincerely. see GREEK for 53

G56.text: ἀγνωσία ajgnwsiva agnosia {ag-no-see'-ah} from 1 (as negative particle) and 1108; ignorance (properly, the state):--ignorance, not the knowledge. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1108

G57.text: ἄγνωστος a[gnwstos agnostos {ag'-noce-tos'} from 1 (as negative particle) and 1110; unknown:--unknown. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1110

G58.text: ἀγορά ajgorav agora {ag-or-ah'} from ageiro (to gather; probably akin to 1453); properly, the town-square (as a place of public resort); by implication, a market or thoroughfare:--market(-place), street. see GREEK for 1453

G59.text: ἀγοράζω ajgoravzw agorazo {ag-or-ad'-zo} from 58; properly, to go to market, i.e. (by implication) to purchase; specially, to redeem:--buy, redeem. see GREEK for 58

G60.text: ἀγοραῖος ajgorai'os agoraios {ag-or-ah'-yos} from 58; relating to the market-place, i.e. forensic (times); by implication, vulgar:--baser sort, low. see GREEK for 58

G61.text: ἄγρα a[gra agra {ag'-rah} from 71; (abstractly) a catching (of fish); also (concretely) a haul (of fish):--draught. see GREEK for 71

G62.text: ἀγράμματος ajgravmmatos agrammatos {ag-ram-mat-os} from 1 (as negative particle) and 1121; unlettered, i.e. illiterate:--unlearned. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1121

G63.text: ἀγραυλέω ajgraulevw agrauleo {ag-row-leh'-o} from 68 and 832 (in the sense of 833); to camp out:--abide in the field. see GREEK for 68 see GREEK for 832 see GREEK for 833

G64.text: ἀγρεύω ajgreuvw agreuo {ag-rew'-o} from 61; to hunt, i.e. (figuratively) to entrap:--catch. see GREEK for 61

G65.text: ἀγριέλαιος ajgrievlaios agrielaios {ag-ree-el'-ah-yos} from 66 and 1636; an oleaster:--olive tree (which is) wild. see GREEK for 66 see GREEK for 1636

G66.text: ἄγριος a[grios agrios {ag'-ree-os} from 68; wild (as pertaining to the country), literally (natural) or figuratively (fierce):--wild, raging. see GREEK for 68

G67.text: Ἀγρίππας Ajgrivppas Agrippas {ag-rip'-pas} apparently from 66 and 2462; wild-horse tamer; Agrippas, one of the Herods:--Agrippa. see GREEK for 66 see GREEK for 2462

G68.text: ἀγρός ajgrovs agros {ag-ros'} from 71; a field (as a drive for cattle); genitive case, the country; specially, a farm, i.e. hamlet:--country, farm, piece of ground, land. see GREEK for 71

G69.text: ἀγρυπνέω ajgrupnevw agrupneo {ag-roop-neh'-o} ultimately from 1 (as negative particle) and 5258; to be sleepless, i.e. keep awake:--watch. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5258

G70.text: ἀγρυπνία ajgrupniva agrupnia {ag-roop-nee'-ah} from 69; sleeplessness, i.e. a keeping awake:--watch. see GREEK for 69

G71.text: ἄγω a[gw ago {ag'-o} a primary verb; properly, to lead; by implication, to bring, drive, (reflexively) go, (specially) pass (time), or (figuratively) induce:--be, bring (forth), carry, (let) go, keep, lead away, be open.

G72.text: ἀγωγή ajgwghv agoge {ag-o-gay'} reduplicated from 71; a bringing up, i.e. mode of living:--manner of life. see GREEK for 71

G73.text: ἀγών ajgwvn agon {ag-one'} from 71; properly, a place of assembly (as if led), i.e. (by implication) a contest (held there); figuratively, an effort or anxiety:--conflict, contention, fight, race. see GREEK for 71

G74.text: ἀγωνία ajgwniva agonia {ag-o-nee'-ah} from 73; a struggle (properly, the state), i.e. (figuratively) anguish:--agony. see GREEK for 73

G75.text: ἀγωνίζομαι ajgwnivzomai agonizomai {ag-o-nid'-zom-ahee} from 73; to struggle, literally (to compete for a prize), figuratively (to contend with an adversary), or genitive case (to endeavor to accomplish something):--fight, labor fervently, strive. see GREEK for 73

G76.text: Ἀδάμ Ajdavm Adam {ad-am'} of Hebrew origin (121); Adam, the first man; typically (of Jesus) man (as his representative):--Adam. see HEBREW for 0121

G77.text: ἀδάπανος ajdavpanos adapanos {ad-ap'-an-os} from 1 (as negative particle); and 1160; costless, i.e. gratuitous:--without expense. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1160

G78.text: Ἀδδί Ajddiv Addi {ad-dee'} probably of Hebrew origin (compare 5716); Addi, an Israelite:--Addi. see HEBREW for 05716

G79.text: ἀδελφή ajdelfhv adelphe {ad-el-fay'} fem of 80; a sister (naturally or ecclesiastically):--sister. see GREEK for 80

G80.text: ἀδελφός ajdelfovs adelphos {ad-el-fos'} from 1 (as a connective particle) and delphus (the womb); a brother (literally or figuratively) near or remote (much like 1):--brother. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1

G81.text: ἀδελφότης ajdelfovths adelphotes {ad-el-fot'-ace} from 80; brotherhood (properly, the feeling of brotherliness), i.e. the (Christian) fraternity:--brethren, brotherhood. see GREEK for 80

G82.text: ἄδηλος a[dhlos adelos {ad'-ay-los} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 1212; hidden, figuratively, indistinct:--appear not, uncertain. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1212

G83.text: ἄδηλος a[dhlos adelotes {ad-ay-lot'-ace} from 82; uncertainty:--X uncertain. see GREEK for 82

G84.text: ἀδήλως ajdhvlws adelos {ad-ay'-loce} adverb from 82; uncertainly:--uncertainly. see GREEK for 82

G85.text: ἀδημονέω ajdhmonevw ademoneo {ad-ay-mon-eh'-o} from a derivative of adeo (to be sated to loathing); to be in distress (of mind):--be full of heaviness, be very heavy.

G86.text: ᾅδης a&/dhs hades {hah'-dace} from 1 (as negative particle) and 1492; properly, unseen, i.e. "Hades" or the place (state) of departed souls:--grave, hell. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1492

G87.text: ἀδιάκριτος ajdiavkritos adiakritos {ad-ee-ak'-ree-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 1252; properly, undistinguished, i.e. (actively) impartial:--without partiality. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1252

G88.text: ἀδιάλειπτος ajdiavleiptos adialeiptos {ad-ee-al'-ipe-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of 1223 and 3007; unintermitted, i.e. permanent:--without ceasing, continual. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 3007

G89.text: ἀδιαλείπτως ajdialeivptws adialeiptos {ad-ee-al-ipe'-toce} adverb from 88; uninterruptedly, i.e. without omission (on an appropriate occasion):--without ceasing. see GREEK for 88

G90.text: ἀφθορία ajfqoriva adiaphthoria {ad-ee-af-thor-ee'-ah} from a derivative of a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 1311; incorruptibleness, i.e. (figuratively) purity (of doctrine):--uncorruptness. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1311

G91.text: ἀδικέω ajdikevw adikeo {ad-ee-keh'-o} from 94; to be unjust, i.e. (actively) do wrong (morally, socially or physically):--hurt, injure, be an offender, be unjust, (do, suffer, take) wrong. see GREEK for 94

G92.text: ἀδίκημα ajdivkhma adikema {ad-eek'-ay-mah} from 91; a wrong done:--evil doing, iniquity, matter of wrong. see GREEK for 91

G93.text: ἀδικία ajdikiva adikia {ad-ee-kee'-ah} from 94; (legal) injustice (properly, the quality, by implication, the act); morally, wrongfulness (of character, life or act):--iniquity, unjust, unrighteousness, wrong. see GREEK for 94

G94.text: ἄδικος a[dikos adikos {ad'-ee-kos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 1349; unjust; by extension wicked; by implication, treacherous; specially, heathen:--unjust, unrighteous. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1349

G95.text: ἀδίκως ajdivkws adikos {ad-ee'-koce} adverb from 94; unjustly:--wrongfully. see GREEK for 94

G96.text: ἀδόκιμος ajdovkimos adokimos {ad-ok'-ee-mos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 1384; unapproved, i.e. rejected; by implication, worthless (literally or morally):--castaway, rejected, reprobate. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1384

G97.text: ἄδολος a[dolos adolos {ad'-ol-os} from 1 (as a negative particle}; and 1388; undeceitful, i.e. (figuratively) unadulterated:--sincere. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1388

G98.text: Ἁδραμυττηνός Ἀδραμυττηνός AJdramutthnovs Ajdramutthnovs Adramuttenos {ad-ram-oot-tay-nos'} from Adramutteion (a place in Asia Minor); Adramyttene or belonging to Adramyttium:--of Adramyttium.

G99.text: Ἀδρίας Ajdrivas Adrias {ad-ree'-as} from Adria (a place near its shore); the Adriatic sea (including the Ionian):--Adria.

G100.text: ἁδρότης aJdrovths hadrotes {had-rot'-ace} from hadros (stout); plumpness, i.e. (figuratively) liberality:--abundance.

G101.text: ἀδυνατέω ajdunatevw adunateo {ad-oo-nat-eh'-o} from 102; to be unable, i.e. (passively) impossible:--be impossible. see GREEK for 102

G102.text: ἀδύνατος ajduvnatos adunatos {ad-oo'-nat-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 1415; unable, i.e. weak (literally or figuratively); passively, impossible:--could not do, impossible, impotent, not possible, weak. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1415

G104.text: ἀεί ajeiv aei {ah-eye'} from an obsolete primary noun (apparently meaning continued duration); "ever,"by qualification regularly; by implication, earnestly; --always, ever.

G105.text: ἀετός ajetovs aetos {ah-et-os'} from the same as 109; an eagle (from its wind-like flight):--eagle. see GREEK for 109

G106.text: ἄζυμος a[zumos azumos {ad'-zoo-mos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 2219; unleavened, i.e. (figuratively) uncorrupted; (in the neutral plural) specially (by implication) the Passover week:--unleavened (bread). see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2219

G107.text: Ἀζώρ Ajzwvr Azor {ad-zore'} of Hebrew origin (compare 5809); Azor, an Israelite:--Azorigin see HEBREW for 05809

G108.text: Ἄζωτος A[zwtos Azotos {ad'-zo-tos} of Hebrew origin (795); Azotus (i.e. Ashdod), a place in Palestine:--Azotus. see HEBREW for 0795

G109.text: ἀήρ ajhvr aer {ah-ayr'} from aemi (to breathe unconsciously, i.e. respire; by analogy, to blow); "air" (as naturally circumambient):--air. Compare 5594. see GREEK for 5594

G110.text: ἀθανασία ajqanasiva athanasia {ath-an-as-ee'-ah} from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and 2288; deathlessness:--immortality. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2288

G111.text: ἀθέμιτος ajqevmitos athemitos {ath-em'-ee-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of themis (statute; from the base of 5087); illegal; by implication, flagitious:--abominable, unlawful thing. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5087

G112.text: ἄθεος a[qeos atheos {ath'-eh-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 2316; godless:--without God. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2316

G113.text: ἄθεσμος a[qesmos athesmos {ath'-es-mos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 5087 (in the sense of enacting); lawless, i.e. (by implication) criminal:--wicked. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5087

G114.text: ἀθετέω ajqetevw atheteo {ath-et-eh'-o} from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 5087; to set aside, i.e. (by implication) to disesteem, neutralize or violate:--cast off, despise, disannul, frustrate, bring to nought, reject. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5087

G115.text: ἀθέτησις ajqevthsis athetesis {ath-et'-ay-sis} from 114; cancellation (literally or figuratively):--disannulling, put away. see GREEK for 114

G116.text: Ἀθῆναι Ajqh'nai Athenai {ath-ay-nahee} plural of Athene (the goddess of wisdom, who was reputed to have founded the city); Athenoe, the capitol of Greece:-- Athens.

G117.text: Ἀθηναῖος Ajqhnai'os Athenaios {ath-ay-nah'-yos} from 116; an Athenoean or inhabitant of Athenae:--Athenian. see GREEK for 116

G118.text: ἀθλέω ajqlevw athleo {ath-leh'-o} from athlos (a contest in the public lists); to contend in the competitive games:--strive.

G119.text: ἄθλησις a[qlhsis athlesis {ath'-lay-sis} from 118; a struggle (figuratively):--fight. see GREEK for 118

G120.text: ἀθυμέω ajqumevw athumeo {ath-oo-meh'-o} from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and 2372; to be spiritless, i.e. disheartened:--be dismayed. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2372

G121.text: ἀθῷος ajqw'/os athoos {ath'-o-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and probably a derivative of 5087 (meaning a penalty); not guilty:--innocent. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5087

G122.text: αἴγειος ai[geios aigeos {ah'-ee-ghi-os} from aix (a goat); belonging to a goat:--goat.

G123.text: αἰγιαλός aijgialovs aigialos {ahee-ghee-al-os'} from aisso (to rush) and 251 (in the sense of the sea; a beach (on which the waves dash):--shore. see GREEK for 251

G124.text: Αἰγύπτιος Aijguvptios Aiguptios {ahee-goop'-tee-os} from 125; an Ægyptian or inhabitant of Ægyptus:--Egyptian. see GREEK for 125

G125.text: Αἴγυπτος Ai[guptos Aiguptos {ah'-ee-goop-tos} of uncertain derivation:--Ægyptus, the land of the Nile:--Egypt.

G126.text: ἀΐδιος aji?dios aidios {ah-id'-ee-os} from 104; everduring (forward and backward, or forward only):--eternal, everlasting. see GREEK for 104

G127.text: αἰδώς aijdwvs aidos {ahee-doce'} perhaps from 1 (as a negative particle) and 1492 (through the idea of downcast eyes); bashfulness, i.e. (towards men), modesty or (towards God) awe:--reverence, shamefacedness. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1492

G128.text: Αἰθίοψ Aijqivoy Aithiops {ahee-thee'-ops} from aitho (to scorch) and ops (the face, from 3700); an Æthiopian (as a blackamoor):--Ethiopian. see GREEK for 3700

G129.text: αἷμα ai|ma haima {hah'-ee-mah} of uncertain derivation; blood, literally (of men or animals), figuratively (the juice of grapes) or specially (the atoning blood of Christ); by implication, bloodshed, also kindred:--blood.

G130.text: αἱματεκχυσία aiJmatekcusiva haimatekchusia {hahee-mat-ek-khoo-see'-ah} from 129 and a derivative of 1632; an effusion of blood:--shedding of blood. see GREEK for 129 see GREEK for 1632

G131.text: αἱμορροέω aiJmorroevw haimorrheo {hahee-mor-hreh'-o} from 129 and 4482; to flow blood, i.e. have a hoemorrhage:--diseased with an issue of blood. see GREEK for 129 see GREEK for 4482

G132.text: Αἰνέας Aijnevas Aineas {ahee-neh'-as} of uncertain derivation; Aeneas, an Israelite:--Aeneas.

G133.text: αἴνεσις ai[nesis ainesis {ah'-ee-nes-is} from 134; a praising (the act), i.e. (specially) a thank(-offering):--praise. see GREEK for 134

G134.text: αἰνέω aijnevw aineo {ahee-neh'-o} from 136; to praise (God):--praise. see GREEK for 136

G135.text: αἴνιγμα ai[nigma ainigma {ah'-ee-nig-ma} from a derivative of 136 (in its primary sense); an obscure saying ("enigma"), i.e. (abstractly) obscureness:--X darkly. see GREEK for 136

G136.text: αἶνος ai\\nos ainos {ah'-ee-nos} apparently a prime word; properly, a story, but used in the sense of 1868; praise (of God):--praise. see GREEK for 1868

G137.text: Αἰνών Aijnwvn Ainon {ahee-nohn'} of Hebrew origin (a derivative of 5869, place of springs); Ænon, a place in Palestine:--Ænon. see GREEK for 5869

G138.text: αἱρέομαι aiJrevomai haireomai {hahee-reh'-om-ahee} probably akin to 142; to take for oneself, i.e. to prefer:--choose. Some of the forms are borrowed from a cognate hellomai hel'-lom-ahee; which is otherwise obsolete. see GREEK for 142

G139.text: αἵρεσις ai&resis hairesis {hah'-ee-res-is} from 138; properly, a choice, i.e. (specially) a party or (abstractly) disunion:--heresy (which is the Greek word itself), sect. see GREEK for 138

G140.text: αἱρετίζω aiJretivzw hairetizo {hahee-ret-id'-zo} from a derivative of 138; to make a choice:--choose. see GREEK for 138

G141.text: αἱρετικός aiJretikovs hairetikos {hahee-ret-ee-kos'} from the same as 140; a schismatic:--heretic (the Greek word itself). see GREEK for 140

G142.text: αἴρω ai[rw airo {ah'-ee-ro} a primary root; to lift up; by implication, to take up or away; figuratively, to raise (the voice), keep in suspense (the mind), specially, to sail away (i.e. weigh anchor); by Hebraism (compare 5375) to expiate sin:--away with, bear (up), carry, lift up, loose, make to doubt, put away, remove, take (away, up). see HEBREW for 05375

G143.text: αἰσθάνομαι aijsqavnomai aisthanomai {ahee-sthan'-om-ahee} of uncertain derivation; to apprehend (properly, by the senses):--perceive.

G144.text: αἴσθησις ai[sqhsis aisthesis {ah'-ee-sthay-sis} from 143; perception, i.e. (figuratively) discernment:--judgment. see GREEK for 143

G145.text: αἰσθητήριον aijsqhthvrion aistheterion {ahee-sthay-tay'-ree-on} from a derivative of 143; properly, an organ of perception, i.e. (figuratively) judgment:--senses. see GREEK for 143

G146.text: αἰσχροκερδής aijscrokerdhvs aischrokerdes {ahee-skhrok-er-dace'} from 150 and kerdos (gain); sordid:--given to (greedy of) filthy lucre. see GREEK for 150

G147.text: αἰσχροκερδῶς aijscrokerdw's aischrokerdos {ahee-skhrok-er-doce'} adverb from 146; sordidly:--for filthy lucre's sake. see GREEK for 146

G148.text: αἰσχρολογία aijscrologiva aischrologia {ahee-skhrol-og-ee'-ah} from 150 and 3056; vile conversation:--filthy communication. see GREEK for 150 see GREEK for 3056

G149.text: aischron {ahee-skhron'} neuter of 150; a shameful thing, i.e. indecorum:--shame. see GREEK for 150

G150.text: αἰσχρός aijscrovs aischros {ahee-skhros'} from the same as 153; shameful, i.e. base (specially, venal):--filthy. see GREEK for 153

G151.text: αἰσχρότης aijscrovths aischrotes {ahee-skhrot'-ace} from 150; shamefulness, i.e. obscenity:--filthiness. see GREEK for 150

G152.text: αἰσχύνη aijscuvnh aischune {ahee-skhoo'-nay} from 153; shame or disgrace (abstractly or concretely):--dishonesty, shame. see GREEK for 153

G153.text: αἰσχύνω aijscuvnw aischuno {ahee-skhoo'-no} from aischos (disfigurement, i.e. disgrace); to feel shame (for oneself):--be ashamed.

G154.text: αἰτέω aijtevw aiteo {ahee-teh'-o} of uncertain derivation; to ask (in genitive case):--ask, beg, call for, crave, desire, require. Compare 4441. see GREEK for 4441

G155.text: αἴτημα ai[thma aitema {ah'-ee-tay-mah} from 154; a thing asked or (abstractly) an asking:--petition, request, required. see GREEK for 154

G156.text: αἰτία aijtiva aitia {ahee-tee'-a} from the same as 154; a cause (as if asked for), i.e. (logical) reason (motive, matter), (legal) crime (alleged or proved):--accusation, case, cause, crime, fault, (wh-)ere(-fore). see GREEK for 154

G157.text: αἰτίωμα aijtivwma aitiooma {ahee-tee'-am-ah} from a derivative of 156; a thing charged:--complaint. see GREEK for 156

G158.text: αἴτιον αἴτιος ai[tion ai[tios aition {ah'-ee-tee-on} neuter of 159; a reason or crime (like 156):--cause, fault. see GREEK for 159 see GREEK for 156

G159.text: αἴτιος ai[tios aitios {ah'-ee-tee-os} from the same as 154; causative, i.e. (concretely) a causer:--author. see GREEK for 154

G160.text: αἰφνίδιος aijfnivdios aiphnidios {aheef-nid'-ee-os} from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and 5316 (compare 1810) (meaning non-apparent); unexpected, i.e. (adverbially) suddenly:--sudden, unawares. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5316 see GREEK for 1810

G161.text: αἰχμαλωσία aijcmalwsiva aichmalosia {aheekh-mal-o-see'-ah} from 164; captivity:--captivity. see GREEK for 164

G162.text: αἰχμαλωτεύω aijcmalwteuvw aichmaloteuo {aheekh-mal-o-tew'-o} from 164; to capture (like 163):--lead captive. see GREEK for 164 see GREEK for 163

G163.text: αἰχμαλωτίζω aijcmalwtivzw aichmalotizo {aheekh-mal-o-tid'-zo} from 164; to make captive:--lead away captive, bring into captivity. see GREEK for 164

G164.text: αἰχμάλωτος aijcmavlwtos aichmalotos {aheekh-mal-o-tos'} from aichme (a spear) and a derivative of the same as 259; properly, a prisoner of war, i.e. (genitive case) a captive:--captive. see GREEK for 259

G165.text: αἰών aijwvn aion {ahee-ohn'} from the same as 104; properly, an age; by extension, perpetuity (also past); by implication, the world; specially (Jewish) a Messianic period (present or future):--age, course, eternal, (for) ever(-more), (n-)ever, (beginning of the , while the) world (began, without end). Compare 5550. see GREEK for 104 see GREEK for 5550

G166.text: αἰώνιος aijwvnios aionios {ahee-o'-nee-os} from 165; perpetual (also used of past time, or past and future as well):--eternal, for ever, everlasting, world (began). see GREEK for 165

G167.text: ἀκαθαρσία ajkaqarsiva akatharsia {ak-ath-ar-see'-ah} from 169; impurity (the quality), physically or morally:--uncleanness. see GREEK for 169

G168.text: akathartes {ak-ath-ar'-tace} from 169; impurity (the state), morally:--filthiness. see GREEK for 169

G169.text: ἀκάθαρτος ajkavqartos akathartos {ak-ath'-ar-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 2508 (meaning cleansed); impure (ceremonially, morally (lewd) or specially, (demonic)):--foul, unclean. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2508

G170.text: ἀκαιρέομαι ajkairevomai akaireomai {ak-ahee-reh'-om-ahee} from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and 2540 (meaning unseasonable); to be inopportune (for oneself), i.e. to fail of a proper occasion:--lack opportunity. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2540

G171.text: ἀκαίρως ajkaivrws akairos {ak-ah'-ee-roce} adverb from the same as 170; inopportunely:--out of season. see GREEK for 170

G172.text: ἄκακος a[kakos akakos {ak'-ak-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 2556; not bad, i.e. (objectively) innocent or (subjectively) unsuspecting:--harmless, simple. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2556

G173.text: ἄκανθα a[kanqa akantha {ak'-an-thah} probably from the same as 188; a thorn:--thorn. see GREEK for 188

G174.text: ἀκάνθινος ajkavnqinos akanthinos {ak-an'-thee-nos} from 173; thorny:--of thorns. see GREEK for 173

G175.text: ἄκαρπος a[karpos akarpos {ak'-ar-pos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 2590; barren (literally or figuratively):--without fruit, unfruitful. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2590

G176.text: ἀκατάγνωστος ajkatavgnwstos akatagnostos {ak-at-ag'-noce-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 2607; unblamable:--that cannot be condemned. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2607

G177.text: ἀκατακάλυπτος ajkatakavluptos akatakaluptos {ak-at-ak-al'-oop-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of 2596 and 2572; unveiled:--uncovered. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2572

G178.text: ἀκατάκριτος ajkatavkritos akatakritos {ak-at-ak'-ree-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 2632; without (legal) trial:--uncondemned. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2632

G179.text: ἀκατάλυτος ajkatavlutos akatalutos {ak-at-al'-oo-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 2647; indissoluble, i.e. (figuratively) permanent:--endless. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2647

G180.text: ἀκατάπαυστος ajkatavpaustos akatapaustos {ak-at-ap'-ow-stos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 2664; unrefraining:--that cannot cease. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2664

G181.text: ἀκαταστασία ajkatastasiva akatastasia {ak-at-as-tah-see'-ah} from 182; instability, i.e. disorder:--commotion, confusion, tumult. see GREEK for 182

G182.text: ἀκατάστατος ajkatavstatos akatastatos {ak-at-as'-tat-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 2525; inconstant:--unstable. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2525

G183.text: akataschetos {ak-at-as'-khet-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 2722; unrestrainable:--unruly. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2722

G184.text: Ἀκελδαμάχ Ajkeldamavc Akeldama {ak-el-dam-ah'} of Chaldee origin (meaning field of blood; corresponding to 2506 and 1818); Akeldama, a place near Jerusalem:--Aceldama. see HEBREW for 02506 see HEBREW for 01818

G185.text: ἀκέραιος ajkevraios akeraios {ak-er'-ah-yos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 2767; unmixed, i.e. (figuratively) innocent:--harmless, simple. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2767

G186.text: ἀκλινής ajklinhvs aklines {ak-lee-nace'} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 2827; not leaning, i.e. (figuratively) firm:--without wavering. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2827

G187.text: ἀκμάζω ajkmavzw akmazo {ak-mad'-zo} from the same as 188; to make a point, i.e. (figuratively) mature:--be fully ripe. see GREEK for 188

G188.text: ἀκμήν ajkmhvn akmen {ak-mane'} accusative case of a noun ("acme") akin to ake (a point) and meaning the same; adverbially, just now, i.e. still:--yet.

G189.text: ἀκοή ajkohv akoe {ak-o-ay'} from 191; hearing (the act, the sense or the thing heard):--audience, ear, fame, which ye heard, hearing, preached, report, rumor. see GREEK for 191

G190.text: ἀκολουθέω ajkolouqevw akoloutheo {ak-ol-oo-theh'-o} from 1 (as a particle of union) and keleuthos (a road); properly, to be in the same way with, i.e. to accompany (specially, as a disciple):--follow, reach. see GREEK for 1

G191.text: ἀκούω ajkouvw akouo {ak-oo'-o} a primary verb; to hear (in various senses):--give (in the) audience (of), come (to the ears), (shall) hear(-er, -ken), be noised, be reported, understand.

G192.text: ἀκρασία ajkrasiva akrasia {ak-ras-ee'-a} from 193; want of self-restraint:--excess, incontinency. see GREEK for 193

G193.text: ἀκρατής ajkrathvs akrates {ak-rat'-ace} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 2904; powerless, i.e. without self-control:--incontinent. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2904

G194.text: ἄκρατος a[kratos akratos {ak'-rat-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 2767; undiluted:--without mixture. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2767

G195.text: ἀκρίβεια ajkrivbeia akribeia {ak-ree'-bi-ah} from the same as 196; exactness:--perfect manner. see GREEK for 196

G196.text: ἀκριβής ajkribhvs akribestatos {ak-ree-bes'-ta-tos} superlative of akribes (a derivative of the same as 206); most exact:--most straitest. see GREEK for 206

G197.text: ἀκριβής ajkribhvs akribesteron {ak-ree-bes'-ter-on} neuter of the comparative of the same as 196; (adverbially) more exactly:--more perfect(-ly). see GREEK for 196

G198.text: ἀκριβόω ajkribovw akriboo {ak-ree-bo'-o} from the same as 196; to be exact, i.e. ascertain:--enquire diligently. see GREEK for 196

G199.text: ἀκριβῶς ajkribw's akribos {ak-ree-boce'} adverb from the same as 196; exactly:--circumspectly, diligently, perfect(-ly). see GREEK for 196

G200.text: ἀκρίς ajkrivs akris {ak-rece'} apparently from the same as 206; a locust (as pointed, or as lighting on the top of vegetation):--locust. see GREEK for 206

G201.text: ἀκροατήριον ajkroathvrion akroaterion {ak-ro-at-ay'-ree-on} from 202; an audience-room:--place of hearing. see GREEK for 202

G202.text: ἀκροατής ajkroathvs akroates {ak-ro-at-ace'} from akroaomai (to listen; apparently an intensive of 191); a hearer (merely):--hearer. see GREEK for 191

G203.text: ἀκροβυστία ajkrobustiva akrobustia {ak-rob-oos-tee'-ah} from 206 and probably a modified form of posthe (the penis or male sexual organ); the prepuce; by implication, an uncircumcised (i.e. gentile, figuratively, unregenerate) state or person:--not circumcised, uncircumcised (with 2192), uncircumcision. see GREEK for 206 see GREEK for 2192

G204.text: ἀκρογωνιαῖος ajkrogwniai'os akrogoniaios {ak-rog-o-nee-ah'-yos} from 206 and 1137; belonging to the extreme corner:--chief corner. see GREEK for 206 see GREEK for 1137

G205.text: ἀκροθίνιον ajkroqivnion akrothinion {ak-roth-in'-ee-on} from 206 and this (a heap); properly (in the plural) the top of the heap, i.e. (by implication) best of the booty:--spoils. see GREEK for 206

G206.text: ἄκρον a[kron akron {ak'-ron} neuter of an adjective probably akin to the base of 188; the extremity:--one end... other, tip, top, uttermost participle see GREEK for 188

G207.text: Ἀκύλας Ajkuvlas Akulas {ak-oo'-las} probably for Latin aquila (an eagle); Akulas, an Israelite:--Aquila.

G208.text: ἀκυρόω ajkurovw akuroo {ak-oo-ro'-o} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 2964; to invalidate:--disannul, make of none effect. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2964

G209.text: ἀκωλύτως ajkwluvtws akolutos {ak-o-loo'-toce} adverb from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 2967; in an unhindered manner, i.e. freely:--no man forbidding him. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2967

G210.text: ἄκων a[kwn akon {ak'-ohn} 或 hekon {hek-ohn'} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 1635; unwilling:--against the will. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 1635

G211.text: ἀλάβαστρος ἀλάβαστρον ajlavbastros ajlavbastron alabastron {al-ab'-as-tron} neuter of alabastros (of uncertain derivation), the name of a stone; properly, an "alabaster" box, i.e. (by extension) a perfume vase (of any material):--(alabaster) box.

G212.text: ἀλαζονεία ajlazoneiva alazoneia {al-ad-zon-i'-a} from 213; braggadocio, i.e. (by implication) self-confidence:--boasting, pride. see GREEK for 213

G213.text: ἀλαζών ajlazwvn alazon {al-ad-zone'} from ale (vagrancy); braggart:--boaster.

G214.text: ἀλαλάζω ajlalavzw alalazo {al-al-ad'-zo} from alale ( a shout, "halloo"); to vociferate, i.e. (by implication) to wail; figuratively, to clang:--tinkle, wail.

G215.text: ἀλάλητος ajlavlhtos alaletos {al-al'-ay-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 2980; unspeakable:--unutterable, which cannot be uttered. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2980

G216.text: ἄλαλος a[lalos alalos {al'-al-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 2980; mute:--dumb. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2980

G217.text: ἅλας ἅλα a&las a&la halas {hal'-as} from 251; salt; figuratively, prudence:--salt. see GREEK for 251

G218.text: ἀλείφω ajleivfw aleipho {al-i'-fo} from 1 (as particle of union) and the base of 3045; to oil (with perfume):--anoint. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 3045

G219.text: ἀλεκτοροφωνία ajlektorofwniva alektorophonia {al-ek-tor-of-o-nee'-ah} from 220 and 5456; cock-crow, i.e. the third night-watch:--cockcrowing. see GREEK for 220 see GREEK for 5456

G220.text: ἀλέκτωρ ajlevktwr alektor {al-ek'-tore} from aleko (to ward off); a cock or male fowl:--cock.

G221.text: Ἀλεξανδρεύς Ajlexandreuvs Alexandreus {al-ex-and-reuce'} from Alexandreia (the city so called); an Alexandreian or inhabitant of Alexandria:--of Alexandria, Alexandrian.

G222.text: Ἀλεξανδρῖνος Ajlexandri'nos Alexandrinos {al-ex-an-dree'-nos} from the same as 221; Alexandrine, or belonging to Alexandria:--of Alexandria. see GREEK for 221

G223.text: Ἀλέξανδρος Ajlevxandros Alexandros {al-ex'-an-dros} from the same as (the first part of) 220 and 435; man-defender; Alexander, the name of three Israelites and one other man:--Alexander. see GREEK for 220 see GREEK for 435

G224.text: ἄλευρον a[leuron aleuron {al'-yoo-ron} from aleo (to grind); flour:--meal.

G225.text: ἀλήθεια ajlhvqeia aletheia {al-ay'-thi-a} from 227; truth:--true, X truly, truth, verity. see GREEK for 227

G226.text: ἀληθεύω ajlhqeuvw aletheuo {al-ayth-yoo'-o} from 227; to be true (in doctrine and profession):--speak (tell) the truth. see GREEK for 227

G227.text: ἀληθής ajlhqhvs alethes {al-ay-thace'} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 2990; true (as not concealing):--true, truly, truth. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2990

G228.text: ἀληθινός ajlhqinovs alethinos {al-ay-thee-nos'} from 227; truthful:--true. see GREEK for 227

G229.text: ἀλήθω ajlhvqw aletho {al-ay'-tho} from the same as 224; to grind:--grind. see GREEK for 224

G230.text: ἀληθῶς ajlhqw's alethos {al-ay-thoce'} adverb from 227; truly:--indeed, surely, of a surety, truly, of a (in) truth, verily, very. see GREEK for 227

G231.text: ἁλιεύς aJlieuvs halieus {hal-ee-yoos'} from 251; a sailor (as engaged on the salt water), i.e. (by implication) a fisher:--fisher(-man). see GREEK for 251

G232.text: ἁλιεύω aJlieuvw halieuo {hal-ee-yoo'-o} from 231; to be a fisher, i.e. (by implication) to fish:--go a-fishing. see GREEK for 231

G233.text: ἁλίζω aJlivzw halizo {hal-id'-zo} from 251; to salt:--salt. see GREEK for 251

G234.text: ἀλίσγημα ajlivsghma alisgema {al-is'-ghem-ah} from alisgeo (to soil); (ceremonially) defilement:--pollution.

G235.text: ἀλλά ajllav alla {al-lah'} neuter plural of 243; properly, other things, i.e. (adverbially) contrariwise (in many relations):--and, but (even), howbeit, indeed, nay, nevertheless, no, notwithstanding, save, therefore, yea, yet. see GREEK for 243

G236.text: ἀλλάσσω ajllavssw allasso {al-las'-so} from 243; to make different:--change. see GREEK for 243

G237.text: ἀλλαχόθεν ajllacovqen allachothen {al-lakh-oth'-en} from 243; from elsewhere:--some other way. see GREEK for 243

G238.text: ἀλληγορέω ajllhgorevw allegoreo {al-lay-gor-eh'-o} from 243 and agoreo (to harangue (compare 58)); to allegorize:--be an allegory (the Greek word itself). see GREEK for 243 see GREEK for 58

G239.text: ἁλληλουϊά aJllhloui>av allelouia {al-lay-loo'-ee-ah} of Hebrew origin (imperative of 1984 and 3050); praise ye Jah!, an adoring exclamation:--alleluiah. see HEBREW for 01984 see HEBREW for 03050

G240.text: ἀλλήλων ajllhvlwn allelon {al-lay'-lone} Genitive plural from 243 reduplicated; one another:--each other, mutual, one another, (the other), (them-, your-)selves, (selves) together (sometimes with 3326 or 4314). see GREEK for 243 see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 4314

G241.text: ἀλλογενής ajllogenhvs allogenes {al-log-en-ace'} from 243 and 1085; foreign, i.e. not a Jew:--stranger. see GREEK for 243 see GREEK for 1085

G242.text: ἅλλομαι a&llomai hallomai {hal'-lom-ahee} middle voice of apparently a primary verb; to jump; figuratively, to gush:--leap, spring up.

G244.text: ἀλλοτριεπίσκοπος ajllotriepivskopos allotriepiskopos {al-lot-ree-ep-is'-kop-os} from 245 and 1985; overseeing others' affairs, i.e. a meddler (specially, in Gentile customs):--busybody in other men's matters. see GREEK for 245 see GREEK for 1985

G245.text: ἀλλότριος ajllovtrios allotrios {al-lot'-ree-os} from 243; another's, i.e. not one's own; by extension foreign, not akin, hostile:--alien, (an-)other (man's, men's), strange(-r). see GREEK for 243

G246.text: ἀλλόφυλος ajllovfulos allophulos {al-lof'-oo-los} from 243 and 5443; foreign, i.e. (specially) Gentile:--one of another nation. see GREEK for 243 see GREEK for 5443

G247.text: ἄλλως a[llws allos {al'-loce} adverb from 243; differently:--otherwise. see GREEK for 243

G248.text: ἀλοάω ajloavw aloao {al-o-ah'-o} from the same as 257; to tread out grain:--thresh, tread out the corn. see GREEK for 257

G249.text: ἄλογος a[logos alogos {al'-og-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 3056; irrational:--brute, unreasonable. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 3056

G616.text: ἀποκυέω ajpokuevw apokueo {ap-ok-oo-eh'-o} from 575 and the base of 2949; to breed forth, i.e. (by transference) to generate (figuratively):--beget, produce. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 2949

G617.text: ἀποκυλίω ajpokulivw apokulio {ap-ok-oo-lee'-o} from 575 and 2947; to roll away:--roll away (back). see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 2947

G618.text: ἀπολαμβάνω ajpolambavnw apolambano {ap-ol-am-ban'-o} from 575 and 2983; to receive (specially, in full, or as a host); also to take aside:--receive, take. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 2983

G619.text: ἀπόλαυσις ajpovlausis apolausis {ap-ol'-ow-sis} from a comparative of 575 and lauo (to enjoy); full enjoyment:--enjoy(-ment). see GREEK for 575

G620.text: ἀπολείπω ajpoleivpw apoleipo {ap-ol-ipe'-o} from 575 and 3007; to leave behind (passively, remain); by implication, to forsake:--leave, remain. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 3007

G621.text: ἐπιλείχω ejpileivcw apoleicho {ap-ol-i'-kho} from 575 and leicho (to "lick"); to lick clean:--lick. see GREEK for 575

G622.text: ἀπόλλυμι ajpovllumi apollumi {ap-ol'-loo-mee} from 575 and the base of 3639; to destroy fully (reflexively, to perish, or lose), literally or figuratively:--destroy, die, lose, mar, perish. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 3639

G623.text: Ἀπολλύων Ajpolluvwn Apolluon {ap-ol-loo'-ohn} active participle of 622; a destroyer (i.e. Satan):--Apollyon. see GREEK for 622

G624.text: Ἀπολλωνία Ajpollwniva Apollonia {ap-ol-lo-nee'-ah} from the pagan deity Apollon (i.e. the sun; from 622); Apollonia, a place in Macedonia:--Apollonia. see GREEK for 622

G625.text: Ἀπολλῶς Ajpollw's Apollos {ap-ol-loce'} probably from the same as 624; Apollos, an Israelite:--Apollos. see GREEK for 624

G626.text: ἀπολογέομαι ajpologevomai apologeomai {ap-ol-og-eh'-om-ahee} middle voice from a compound of 575 and 3056; to give an account (legal plea) of oneself, i.e. exculpate (self):--answer (for self), make defence, excuse (self), speak for self. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 3056

G627.text: ἀπολογία ajpologiva apologia {ap-ol-og-ee'-ah} from the same as 626; a plea ("apology"):--answer (for self), clearing of self, defence. see GREEK for 626

G628.text: ἀπολούω ajpolouvw apolouo {ap-ol-oo'-o} from 575 and 3068; to wash fully, i.e. (figuratively) have remitted (reflexively):--wash (away). see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 3068

G629.text: ἀπολύτρωσις ajpoluvtrwsis apolutrosis {ap-ol-oo'-tro-sis} from a compound of 575 and 3083; (the act) ransom in full, i.e. (figuratively) riddance, or (specially) Christian salvation:--deliverance, redemption. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 3083

G630.text: ἀπολύω ajpoluvw apoluo {ap-ol-oo'-o} from 575 and 3089; to free fully, i.e. (literally) relieve, release, dismiss (reflexively, depart), or (figuratively) let die, pardon or (specially) divorce:--(let) depart, dismiss, divorce, forgive, let go, loose, put (send) away, release, set at liberty. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 3089

G631.text: ἀπομάσσω ajpomavssw apomassomai {ap-om-as'-som-ahee} middle voice from 575 and masso (to squeeze, knead, smear); to scrape away:--wipe off. see GREEK for 575

G632.text: ἀπονέμω ajponevmw aponemo {ap-on-em'-o} from 575 and the base of 3551; to apportion, i.e. bestow:--give. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 3551

G633.text: ἀπονίπτω ajponivptw aponipto {ap-on-ip'-to} from 575 and 3538; to wash off (reflexively, one's own hands symbolically):--wash. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 3538

G634.text: ἀποπίπτω ajpopivptw apopipto {ap-op-ip'-to} from 575 and 4098; to fall off:--fall. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4098

G635.text: ἀποπλανάω ajpoplanavw apoplanao {ap-op-lan-ah'-o} from 575 and 4105; to lead astray (figuratively); passively, to stray (from truth):--err, seduce. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4105

G636.text: ἀποπλέω ajpoplevw apopleo {ap-op-leh'-o} from 575 and 4126; to set sail:--sail away. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4126

G637.text: apopluno {ap-op-loo'-no} from 575 and 4150; to rinse off:--wash. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4150

G638.text: ἀποπνίγω ajpopnivgw apopnigo {ap-op-nee'-go} from 575 and 4155; to stifle (by drowning or overgrowth):--choke. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4155

G639.text: ἀπορέω ajporevw aporeo {ap-or-eh'-o} from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and the base of 4198; to have no way out, i.e. be at a loss (mentally):-- (stand in) doubt, be perplexed. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 4198

G640.text: ἀπορία ajporiva aporia {ap-or-ee'-a} from the same as 639; a (state of) quandary:--perplexity. see GREEK for 639

G641.text: ἀπορίπτω ajporivptw aporrhipto {ap-or-hrip'-to} from 575 and 4496; to hurl off, i.e. precipitate (oneself):--cast. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4496

G642.text: ἀπορφανίζω ajporfanivzw aporphanizo {ap-or-fan-id'-zo} from 575 and a derivative of 3737; to bereave wholly, i.e. (figuratively) separate (from intercourse):--take. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 3737

G643.text: ἐπισκευάζομαι ejpiskeuavzomai aposkeuazo {ap-osk-yoo-ad'-zo} from 575 and a derivative of 4632; to pack up (one's) baggage:--take up... carriages. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4632

G644.text: ἀποσκίασμα ajposkivasma aposkiasma {ap-os-kee'-as-mah} from a compound of 575 and a derivative of 4639; a shading off, i.e. obscuration:--shadow. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4639

G645.text: ἀποσπάω ajpospavw apospao {ap-os-pah'-o} from 575 and 4685; to drag forth, i.e. (literally) unsheathe (a sword), or relatively (with a degree of force implied) retire (personally or factiously):--(with-)draw (away), after we were gotten from. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4685

G646.text: ἀποστασία ajpostasiva apostasia {ap-os-tas-ee'-ah} feminine of the same as 647; defection from truth (properly, the state) ("apostasy"):--falling away, forsake. see GREEK for 647

G647.text: ἀποστάσιον ajpostavsion apostasion {ap-os-tas'-ee-on} neuter of a (presumed) adjective from a derivative of 868; properly, something separative, i.e. (specially) divorce:--(writing of) divorcement. see GREEK for 868

G648.text: ἀποστεγάζω ajpostegavzw apostegazo {ap-os-teg-ad'-zo} from 575 and a derivative of 4721; to unroof:--uncover. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4721

G649.text: ἀποστέλλω ajpostevllw apostello {ap-os-tel'-lo} from 575 and 4724; set apart, i.e. (by implication) to send out (properly, on a mission) literally or figuratively:--put in, send (away, forth, out), set (at liberty). see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4724

G650.text: ἀποστερέω ajposterevw apostereo {ap-os-ter-eh'-o} from 575 and stereo (to deprive); to despoil:--defraud, destitute, kept back by fraud. see GREEK for 575

G651.text: ἀποστολή ajpostolhv apostole {ap-os-tol-ay'} from 649; commission, i.e. (specially) apostolate:--apostleship. see GREEK for 649

G652.text: ἀπόστολος ajpovstolos apostolos {ap-os'-tol-os} from 649; a delegate; specially, an ambassador of the Gospel; officially a commissioner of Christ ("apostle") (with miraculous powers):--apostle, messenger, he that is sent. see GREEK for 649

G653.text: ἀποστοματίζω ajpostomativzw apostomatizo {ap-os-tom-at-id'-zo} from 575 and a (presumed) derivative of 4750; to speak off-hand (properly, dictate), i.e. to catechize (in an invidious manner):--provoke to speak. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4750

G654.text: ἀποστρέφω ajpostrevfw apostrepho {ap-os-tref'-o} from 575 and 4762; to turn away or back (literally or figuratively):--bring again, pervert, turn away (from). see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4762

G655.text: ἀποστυγέω ajpostugevw apostugeo {ap-os-toog-eh'-o} from 575 and the base of 4767; to detest utterly:--abhor. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4767

G656.text: ἀποσυνάγωγος ajposunavgwgos aposunagogos {ap-os-oon-ag'-o-gos} from 575 and 4864; excommunicated:--(put) out of the synagogue(-s). see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 4864

G657.text: ἀποτάσσω ajpotavssw apotassomai {ap-ot-as'-som-ahee} middle voice from 575 and 5021; literally, to say adieu (by departing or dismissing); figuratively, to renounce:--bid farewell, forsake, take leave, send away. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5021

G658.text: ἀποτελέω ajpotelevw apoteleo {ap-ot-el-eh'-o} from 575 and 5055; to complete entirely, i.e. consummate:--finish. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5055

G659.text: ἀποτίθημι ajpotivqhmi apotithemi {ap-ot-eeth'-ay-mee} from 575 and 5087; to put away (literally or figuratively):--cast off, lay apart (aside, down), put away (off). see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5087

G660.text: ἀποτινάσσω ajpotinavssw apotinasso {ap-ot-in-as'-so} from 575 and tinasso (to jostle); to brush off:--shake off. see GREEK for 575

G661.text: ἀποτίνω ajpotivnw apotino {ap-ot-ee'-no} from 575 and 5099; to pay in full:--repay. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5099

G662.text: ἀποτολμάω ajpotolmavw apotolmao {ap-ot-ol-mah'-o} from 575 and 5111; to venture plainly:--be very bold. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5111

G663.text: ἀποτομία ajpotomiva apotomia {ap-ot-om-ee'-ah} from the base of 664; (figuratively) decisiveness, i.e. rigor:--severity. see GREEK for 664

G664.text: ἀποτόμως ajpotovmws apotomos {ap-ot-om'-oce} adverb from a derivative of a comparative of 575 and temno (to cut); abruptly, i.e. peremptorily:--sharply(-ness). see GREEK for 575

G665.text: ἀποτρέπομαι ajpotrevpomai apotrepo {ap-ot-rep'-o} from 575 and the base of 5157; to deflect, i.e. (reflexively) avoid:--turn away. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5157

G666.text: ἀπουσία ajpousiva apousia {ap-oo-see'-ah} from the participle of 548; a being away:--absence. see GREEK for 548

G667.text: ἀποφέρω ajpofevrw apophero {ap-of-er'-o} from 575 and 5342; to bear off (literally or relatively):--bring, carry (away). see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5342

G668.text: ἀποφεύγω ajpofeuvgw apopheugo {ap-of-yoo'-go} from 575 and 5343; (figuratively) to escape:--escape. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5343

G669.text: ἀποφθέγγομαι ajpofqevggomai apophtheggomai {ap-of-theng'-om-ahee} from 575 and 5350; to enunciate plainly, i.e. declare:--say, speak forth, utterance. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5350

G670.text: ἀποφορτίζομαι ajpofortivzomai apophortizomai {ap-of-or-tid'-zom-ahee} from 575 and the middle voice of 5412; to unload:--unlade. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5412

G671.text: ἀπόχρησις ajpovcrhsis apochresis {ap-okh'-ray-sis} from a compound of 575 and 5530; the act of using up, i.e. consumption:--using. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5530

G672.text: ἀποχωρέω ajpocwrevw apochoreo {ap-okh-o-reh'-o} from 575 and 5562; to go away:--depart. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5562

G673.text: ἀποχωρίζω ajpocwrivzw apochorizo {ap-okh-o-rid'-zo} from 575 and 5563; to rend apart; reflexively, to separate:--depart (asunder). see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5563

G674.text: ἀποψύχω ajpoyuvcw apopsucho {ap-ops-oo'-kho} from 575 and 5594; to breathe out, i.e. faint:--hearts failing. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5594

G675.text: Ἀππίου Ajppivou Appios {ap'-pee-os} of Latin origin; (in the genitive, i.e. possessive case) of Appius, the name of a Roman:--Appii.

G676.text: ἀπρόσιτος ajprovsitos aprositos {ap-ros'-ee-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a comparative of 4314 and eimi (to go); inaccessible:--which no man can approach. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 4314

G677.text: ἀπρόσκοπος ajprovskopos aproskopos {ap-ros'-kop-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 4350; actively, inoffensive, i.e. not leading into sin; passively, faultless, i.e. not led into sin:--none (void of, without) offence. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 4350

G678.text: ἀπροσωπολήμπτως ajproswpolhvmptws aprosopoleptos {ap-ros-o-pol-ape'-tos} adverb from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a presumed compound of 4383 and 2983 (compare 4381); in a way not accepting the person, i.e. impartially:--without respect of persons. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 4383 see GREEK for 2983 see GREEK for 4381

G679.text: ἄπταιστος a[ptaistos aptaistos {ap-tah'-ee-stos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 4417; not stumbling, i.e. (figuratively) without sin:--from falling. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 4417

G680.text: ἅπτω a&ptw hapto {hap'-to} reflexive of 681; properly, to attach oneself to, i.e. to touch (in many implied relations):--touch. see GREEK for 681

G681.text: ἅπτω a&ptw hapto {hap'-to} a primary verb; properly, to fasten to, i.e. (specially) to set on fire:--kindle, light.

G682.text: Ἀπφία Ajpfiva Apphia {ap-fee'-a} probably of foreign origin; Apphia, a woman of Collosae:--Apphia.

G683.text: ἀπωθέω ajpwqevw apotheomai {ap-o-theh'-om-ahee} 或 apothomai {ap-o'-thom-ahee} or apothomai ap-o'-thom-ahee from 575 and the middle voice of otheo or otho (to shove); to push off, figuratively, to reject:--cast away, put away (from), thrust away (from). see GREEK for 575

G684.text: ἀπώλεια ajpwvleia apoleia {ap-o'-li-a} from a presumed derivative of 622; ruin or loss (physical, spiritual or eternal):--damnable(-nation), destruction, die, perdition, X perish, pernicious ways, waste. see GREEK for 622

G685.text: ἀρά ajrav ara {ar-ah'} probably from 142; properly, prayer (as lifted to Heaven), i.e. (by implication) imprecation:--curse. see GREEK for 142

G686.text: ἄρα a[ra ara {ar'-ah} probably from 142 (through the idea of drawing a conclusion); a particle denoting an inference more or less decisive (as follows):--haply, (what) manner (of man), no doubt, perhaps, so be, then, therefore, truly, wherefore. Often used in connection with other particles, especially 1065 or 3767 (after) or 1487 (before). Compare also 687. see GREEK for 142 see GREEK for 1065 see GREEK for 3767 see GREEK for 1487 see GREEK for 687

G687.text: ἆρα a\\ra ara {ar'-ah} a form of 686, denoting an interrogation to which a negative answer is presumed:--therefore. see GREEK for 686

G688.text: Ἀραβία Ajrabiva Arabia {ar-ab-ee'-ah} of Hebrew origin (6152); Arabia, a region of Asia:--Arabia. see HEBREW for 06152

G689.text: Ἀράμ Ajravm Aram {ar-am'} of Hebrew origin (7410); Aram (i.e. Ram), an Israelite:--Aram. see HEBREW for 07410

G690.text: Ἄραψ A[ray Araps {ar'-aps} from 688; an Arab or native of Arabia:--Arabian. see GREEK for 688

G691.text: ἀργέω ajrgevw argeo {arg-eh'-o} from 692; to be idle, i.e. (figuratively) to delay:--linger. see GREEK for 692

G692.text: ἀργός ajrgovs argos {ar-gos'} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 2041; inactive, i.e. unemployed; (by implication) lazy, useless:--barren, idle, slow. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 2041

G693.text: ἀργυροῦς ajrgurou's argureos {ar-goo'-reh-os} from 696; made of silver:--(of) silver. see GREEK for 696

G694.text: ἀργύριον ajrguvrion argurion {ar-goo'-ree-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of 696; silvery, i.e. (by implication) cash; specially, a silverling (i.e. drachma or shekel):--money, (piece of) silver (piece). see GREEK for 696

G695.text: ἀργυροκόπος ajrgurokovpos argurokopos {ar-goo-rok-op'-os} from 696 and 2875; a beater (i.e. worker) of silver:--silversmith. see GREEK for 696 see GREEK for 2875

G696.text: ἄργυρος a[rguros arguros {ar'-goo-ros} from argos (shining); silver (the metal, in the articles or coin):--silver.

G697.text: ἄρειος ∏άγος Ἄρειος ∏άγος a[reios Pavgos A[reios Pavgos Areios Pagos {ar'-i-os pag'-os} from Ares (the name of the Greek deity of war) and a derivative of 4078; rock of Ares, a place in Athens:--Areopagus, Mars' Hill. see GREEK for 4078

G698.text: Ἀρεοπαγίτης Ajreopagivths Areopagites {ar-eh-op-ag-ee'-tace} from 697; an Areopagite or member of the court held on Mars' Hill:--Areopagite. see GREEK for 697

G699.text: ἀρεσκεία ajreskeiva areskeia {ar-es'-ki-ah} from a derivative of 700; complaisance:--pleasing. see GREEK for 700

G700.text: ἀρέσκω ajrevskw aresko {ar-es'-ko} probably from 142 (through the idea of exciting emotion); to be agreeable (or by implication, to seek to be so):--please. see GREEK for 142

G701.text: ἀρεστός ajrestovs arestos {ar-es-tos'} from 700; agreeable; by implication, fit:--(things that) please(-ing), reason. see GREEK for 700

G702.text: Ἁρέτας AJrevtas Aretas {ar-et'-as} of foreign origin; Aretas, an Arabian:--Aretas.

G703.text: ἀρετή ajrethv arete {ar-et'-ay} from the same as 730; properly, manliness (valor), i.e. excellence (intrinsic or attributed):--praise, virtue. see GREEK for 730

G704.text: ἀρήν ajrhvn aren {ar-ane'} perhaps the same as 730; a lamb (as a male):--lamb. see GREEK for 730

G705.text: ἀριθμέω ajriqmevw arithmeo {ar-ith-meh'-o} from 706; to enumerate or count:--number. see GREEK for 706

G706.text: ἀριθμός ajriqmovs arithmos {ar-ith-mos'} from 142; a number (as reckoned up):--number. see GREEK for 142

G707.text: Ἀριμαθαία Ajrimaqaiva Arimathaia {ar-ee-math-ah'-ee-ah} of Hebrew origin (7414); Arimathaea (or Ramah), a place in Palestine:--Arimathaea. see HEBREW for 07414

G708.text: Ἀρίσταρχος Ajrivstarcos Aristarchos {ar-is'-tar-khos} from the same as 712 and 757; best ruling; Aristarchus, a Macedonian:--Aristarchus. see GREEK for 712 see GREEK for 757

G709.text: ἀριστάω ajristavw aristao {ar-is-tah'-o} from 712; to take the principle meal:--dine. see GREEK for 712

G710.text: ἀριστερός ajristerovs aristeros {ar-is-ter-os'} apparently a comparative of the same as 712; the left hand (as second-best):--left (hand). see GREEK for 712

G711.text: Ἀριστόβουλος Ajristovboulos Aristoboulos {ar-is-tob'-oo-los} from the same as 712 and 1012; best counselling; Aristoboulus, a Christian:--Aristobulus. see GREEK for 712 see GREEK for 1012

G712.text: ἄριστον a[riston ariston {ar'-is-ton} apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as 730; the best meal (or breakfast; perhaps from eri ("early")), i.e. luncheon:--dinner. see GREEK for 730

G713.text: ἀρκετός ajrketovs arketos {ar-ket-os'} from 714; satisfactory:--enough, suffice (-ient). see GREEK for 714

G714.text: ἀρκέω ajrkevw arkeo {ar-keh'-o} apparently a primary verb (but probably akin to 142 through the idea of raising a barrier); properly, to ward off, i.e. (by implication) to avail (figuratively, be satisfactory):--be content, be enough, suffice, be sufficient. see GREEK for 142

G715.text: ἄρκος a[rkos arktos {ark'-tos} probably from 714; a bear (as obstructing by ferocity):--bear. see GREEK for 714

G716.text: ἅρμα a&rma harma {har'-mah} probably from 142 (perhaps with 1 (as a particle of union) prefixed); a chariot (as raised or fitted together (compare 719)):--chariot. see GREEK for 142 see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 719

G717.text: Ἁρμαγεδών Ἃρ Μαγεδών AJrmagedwvn A^r Magedwvn Armageddon {ar-mag-ed-dohn'} of Hebrew origin (2022 and 4023); Armageddon (or Har-Meggiddon), a symbolic name:--Armageddon. see HEBREW for 02022 see HEBREW for 04023

G718.text: ἁρμόζομαι aJrmovzomai harmozo {har-mod'-zo} from 719; to joint, i.e. (figuratively) to woo (reflexively, to betroth):--espouse. see GREEK for 719

G719.text: ἁρμός aJrmovs harmos {har-mos'} from the same as 716; an articulation (of the body):--joint. see GREEK for 716

G720.text: ἀρνέομαι ajrnevomai arneomai {ar-neh'-om-ahee} perhaps from 1 (as a negative particle) and the middle voice of 4483; to contradict, i.e. disavow, reject, abnegate:--deny, refuse. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 4483

G721.text: ἀρνίον ajrnivon arnion {ar-nee'-on} diminutive from 704; a lambkin:--lamb. see GREEK for 704

G722.text: ἀροτριάω ajrotriavw arotrioo {ar-ot-ree-o'-o} from 723; to plow:--plough. see GREEK for 723

G723.text: ἄροτρον a[rotron arotron {ar'-ot-ron} from aroo (to till); a plow:--plough.

G724.text: ἁρπαγή aJrpaghv harpage {har-pag-ay'} from 726; pillage (properly abstract):--extortion, ravening, spoiling. see GREEK for 726

G725.text: ἁρπαγμός aJrpagmovs harpagmos {har-pag-mos'} from 726; plunder (properly concrete):--robbery. see GREEK for 726

G726.text: ἁρπάζω aJrpavzw harpazo {har-pad'-zo} from a derivative of 138; to seize (in various applications):--catch (away, up), pluck, pull, take (by force). see GREEK for 138

G727.text: ἅρπαξ a&rpax harpax {har'-pax} from 726; rapacious:--extortion, ravening. see GREEK for 726

G728.text: ἀρραβών ajrrabwvn arrhabon {ar-hrab-ohn'} of Hebrew origin (6162); a pledge, i.e. part of the purchase-money or property given in advance as security for the rest:--earnest. see HEBREW for 06162

G729.text: ἄραφος a[rafos arrhaphos {ar'-hhraf-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of the same as 4476; unsewed, i.e. of a single piece:--without seam. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 4476

G730.text: ἄρσην a[rshn arrhen {ar'-hrane} or arsen {ar'-sane} or arsen ar'-sane probably from 142; male (as stronger for lifting):--male, man. see GREEK for 142

G731.text: ἄρρητος a[rrhtos arrhetos {ar'-hray-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and the same as 4490; unsaid, i.e. (by implication) inexpressible:--unspeakable. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 4490

G732.text: ἄρρωστος a[rrwstos arrhostos {ar'-hroce-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 4517; infirm:--sick (folk, -ly). see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 4517

G733.text: ἀρσενοκοίτης ajrsenokoivths arsenokoites {ar-sen-ok-oy'-tace} from 730 and 2845; a sodomite:--abuser of (that defile) self with mankind. see GREEK for 730 see GREEK for 2845
