G853.text: ἀφανίζω ajfanivzw aphanizo {af-an-id'-zo} from 852; to render unapparent, i.e. (actively) consume (becloud), or (passively) disappear (be destroyed):-- corrupt, disfigure, perish, vanish away. see GREEK for 852

G854.text: ἀφανισμός ajfanismovs aphanismos {af-an-is-mos'} from 853; disappearance, i.e. (figuratively) abrogation:--vanish away. see GREEK for 853

G855.text: ἄφαντος a[fantos aphantos {af'-an-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 5316; non-manifested, i.e. invisible:--vanished out of sight. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5316

G856.text: ἀφεδρών ajfedrwvn aphedron {af-ed-rone'} from a compound of 575 and the base of 1476; a place of sitting apart, i.e. a privy:--draught. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 1476

G857.text: ἀφειδία ajfeidiva apheidia {af-i-dee'-ah} from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and 5339; unsparingness, i.e. austerity (asceticism):--neglecting. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5339

G858.text: ἀφελότης ajfelovths aphelotes {af-el-ot'-ace} from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and phellos (in the sense of a stone as stubbing the foot); smoothness, i.e. (figuratively) simplicity:--singleness. see GREEK for 1

G859.text: ἄφεσις a[fesis aphesis {af'-es-is} from 863; freedom; (figuratively) pardon:--deliverance, forgiveness, liberty, remission. see GREEK for 863

G860.text: ἁφή aJfhv haphe {haf-ay'} from 680; probably a ligament (as fastening):--joint. see GREEK for 680

G861.text: ἀφθαρσία ajfqarsiva aphtharsia {af-thar-see'-ah} from 862; incorruptibility; genitive, unending existence; (figuratively) genuineness:--immortality, incorruption, sincerity. see GREEK for 862

G862.text: ἄφθαρτος a[fqartos aphthartos {af'-thar-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 5351; undecaying (in essence or continuance):--not (in-, un-)corruptible, immortal. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5351

G863.text: ἀφίημι ajfivhmi aphiemi {af-ee'-ay-mee} from 575 and hiemi (to send; an intensive form of eimi, to go); to send forth, in various applications (as follow):--cry, forgive, forsake, lay aside, leave, let (alone, be, go, have), omit, put (send) away, remit, suffer, yield up. see GREEK for 575

G864.text: ἀφικνέομαι ajfiknevomai aphikneomai {af-ik-neh'-om-ahee} from 575 and the base of 2425; to go (i.e. spread) forth (by rumor):--come abroad. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 2425

G865.text: ἀφιλάγαθος ajfilavgaqos aphilagathos {af-il-ag'-ath-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5358; hostile to virtue:--despiser of those that are good. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5358

G866.text: ἀφιλάργυρος ajfilavrguros aphilarguros {af-il-ar'-goo-ros} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5366; unavaricious:--without covetousness, not greedy of filthy lucre. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5366

G867.text: ἄφιξις a[fixis aphixis {af'-ix-is} from 864; properly, arrival, i.e. (by implication) departure:--departing. see GREEK for 864

G868.text: ἀφίστημι ajfivsthmi aphistemi {af-is'-tay-mee} from 575 and 2476; to remove, i.e. (actively) instigate to revolt; usually (reflexively) to desist, desert, etc.:--depart, draw (fall) away, refrain, withdraw self. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 2476

G869.text: ἄφνω a[fnw aphno {af'-no} adverb from 852 (contraction); unawares, i.e. unexpectedly:--suddenly. see GREEK for 852

G870.text: ἀφόβως ajfovbws aphobos {af-ob'-oce} adverb from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and 5401; fearlessly:--without fear. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5401

G871.text: ἀφομοιόω ajfomoiovw aphomoioo {af-om-oy-o'-o} from 575 and 3666; to assimilate closely:--make like. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 3666

G872.text: ἀφοράω ajforavw aphorao {af-or-ah'-o} from 575 and 3708; to consider attentively:--look. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 3708

G873.text: ἀφορίζω ajforivzw aphorizo {af-or-id'-zo} from 575 and 3724; to set off by boundary, i.e. (figuratively) limit, exclude, appoint, etc.:--divide, separate, sever. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 3724

G874.text: ἀφορμή ajformhv aphorme {af-or-may'} from a compound of 575 and 3729; a starting-point, i.e. (figuratively) an opportunity:--occasion. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 3729

G875.text: ἀφρίζω ajfrivzw aphrizo {af-rid'-zo} from 876; to froth at the mouth (in epilepsy):--foam. see GREEK for 876

G876.text: ἀφρός ajfrovs aphros {af-ros'} apparently a primary word; froth, i.e. slaver:--foaming.

G877.text: ἀφροσύνη ajfrosuvnh aphrosune {af-ros-oo'-nay} from 878; senselessness, i.e. (euphemistically) egotism; (morally) recklessness:--folly, foolishly(-ness). see GREEK for 878

G878.text: ἄφρων a[frwn aphron {af'-rone} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5424; properly, mindless, i.e. stupid, (by implication) ignorant, (specially) egotistic, (practically) rash, or (morally) unbelieving:--fool(-ish), unwise. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5424

G879.text: ἀφυπνόω ajfupnovw aphupnoo {af-oop-no'-o} from a compound of 575 and 5258; properly, to become awake, i.e. (by implication) to drop (off) in slumber:--fall asleep. see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 5258

G880.text: ἄφωνος a[fwnos aphonos {af'-o-nos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5456; voiceless, i.e. mute (by nature or choice); figuratively, unmeaning:--dumb, without signification. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5456

G881.text: Ἀχάζ Ajcavz Achaz {akh-adz'} of Hebrew origin (271); Achaz, an Israelite:--Achaz. see HEBREW for 0271

G882.text: Ἀχαΐα Ajcai?a Achaia {ach-ah-ee'-ah} of uncertain derivation; Achaia (i.e. Greece), a country of Europe:--Achaia.

G883.text: Ἀχαϊκός Ajcai>kovs Achaikos {ach-ah-ee-kos'} from 882; an Achaian; Achaicus, a Christian:--Achaicus. see GREEK for 882

G884.text: ἀχάριστος ajcavristos acharistos {ach-ar'-is-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 5483; thankless, i.e. ungrateful:--unthankful. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5483

G885.text: Ἀχίμ Ajcivm Acheim {akh-ime'} probably of Hebrew origin (compare 3137); Achim, an Israelite:--Achim. see HEBREW for 03137

G886.text: ἀχειροποίητος ajceiropoivhtos acheiropoietos {akh-i-rop-oy'-ay-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5499; unmanufactured, i.e. inartificial:--made without (not made with) hands. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5499

G887.text: ἀχλύς ajcluvs achlus {akh-looce'} of uncertain derivation; dimness of sight, i.e. (probably) a cataract:--mist.

G888.text: ἀχρεῖος ajcrei'os achreios {akh-ri'-os} from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 5534 (compare 5532); useless, i.e. (euphemistically) unmeritorious:--unprofitable. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5534 see GREEK for 5532

G889.text: ἀχρειόω ajcreiovw achreioo {akh-ri-o'-o} from 888; to render useless, i.e. spoil:--become unprofitable. see GREEK for 888

G890.text: ἄχρηστος a[crhstos achrestos {akh'-race-tos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5543; inefficient, i.e. (by implication) detrimental:--unprofitable. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5543

G891.text: ἄχρι ἄχρις a[cri a[cris achri {akh'-ree} 或 achris {akh'-rece} or achris akh'-rece; akin to 206 (through the idea of a terminus); (of time) until or (of place) up to:--as far as, for, in(-to), till, (even, un-)to, until, while. Compare 3360. see GREEK for 206 see GREEK for 3360

G892.text: ἄχυρον a[curon achuron {akh'-oo-ron} perhaps remotely from cheo (to shed forth); chaff (as diffusive):--chaff.

G893.text: ἀψευδής ajyeudhvs apseudes {aps-yoo-dace'} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5579; veracious:--that cannot lie. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5579

G894.text: ἄψινθος a[yinqos apsinthos {ap'-sin-thos} of uncertain derivation; wormwood (as a type of bitterness, i.e. (figuratively) calamity):--wormwood.

G895.text: ἄψυχος a[yucos apsuchos {ap'-soo-khos} from 1 (as a negative particle) and 5590; lifeless, i.e. inanimate (mechanical):--without life. see GREEK for 1 see GREEK for 5590

G896.text: Βάαλ Baval Baal {bah'-al} of Hebrew origin (1168); Baal, a Phoenician deity (used as a symbol of idolatry):--Baal. see HEBREW for 01168

G897.text: Βαβυλών Babulwvn Babulon {bab-oo-lone'} of Hebrew origin (894); Babylon, the capitol of Chaldaea (literally or figuratively (as a type of tyranny)):-- Babylon. see HEBREW for 0894

G898.text: βαθμός baqmovs bathmos {bath-mos'} from the same as 899; a step, i.e. (figuratively) grade (of dignity):--degree. see GREEK for 899

G899.text: βάθος bavqos bathos {bath'-os} from the same as 901; profundity, i.e. (by implication) extent; (figuratively) mystery:--deep(-ness, things), depth. see GREEK for 901

G900.text: βαθύνω baquvnw bathuno {bath-oo'-no} from 901; to deepen:--deep. see GREEK for 901

G901.text: βαθύς baquvs bathus {bath-oos'} from the base of 939; profound (as going down), literally or figuratively:--deep, very early. see GREEK for 939

G902.text: βάϊον bavi>on baion {bah-ee'-on} a diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of 939; a palm twig (as going out far):--branch. see GREEK for 939

G903.text: Βαλαάμ Balaavm Balaam {bal-ah-am'} of Hebrew origin (1109); Balaam, a Mesopotamian (symbolic of a false teacher):--Balaam. see HEBREW for 01109

G904.text: Βαλάκ Balavk Balak {bal-ak'} of Hebrew origin (1111); Balak, a Moabite:--Balac. see HEBREW for 01111

G905.text: βαλλάντιον ballavntion balantion {bal-an'-tee-on} probably remotely from 906 (as a depository); a pouch (for money):--bag, purse. see GREEK for 906

G906.text: βάλλω bavllw ballo {bal'-lo} a primary verb; to throw (in various applications, more or less violent or intense):--arise, cast (out), X dung, lay, lie, pour, put (up), send, strike, throw (down), thrust. Compare 4496. see GREEK for 4496

G907.text: βαπτίζω baptivzw baptizo {bap-tid'-zo} from a derivative of 911; to immerse, submerge; to make whelmed (i.e. fully wet); used only (in the New Testament) of ceremonial ablution, especially (technically) of the ordinance of Christian baptism:--Baptist, baptize, wash. see GREEK for 911

G908.text: βάπτισμα bavptisma baptisma {bap'-tis-mah} from 907; baptism (technically or figuratively):--baptism. see GREEK for 907

G909.text: βαπτισμός baptismovs baptismos {bap-tis-mos'} from 907; ablution (ceremonial or Christian):--baptism, washing. see GREEK for 907

G910.text: βαπτιστής baptisthvs Baptistes {bap-tis-tace'} from 907; a baptizer, as an epithet of Christ's forerunner:--Baptist. see GREEK for 907

G911.text: βάπτω bavptw bapto {bap'-to} a primary verb; to whelm, i.e. cover wholly with a fluid; in the New Testament only in a qualified or special sense, i.e. (literally) to moisten (a part of one's person), or (by implication) to stain (as with dye):--dip.

G912.text: Βαραββᾶς Barabba's Barabbas {bar-ab-bas'} of Chaldee origin (1347 and 5); son of Abba; Bar-abbas, an Israelite:--Barabbas. see HEBREW for 01347 see HEBREW for 05

G913.text: Βαράκ Baravk Barak {bar-ak'} of Hebrew origin (1301); Barak, an Israelite:--Barak. see HEBREW for 01301

G914.text: Βαραχίας Baracivas Barachias {bar-akh-ee'-as} of Hebrew origin (1296); Barachias (i.e. Berechijah), an Israelite:--Barachias. see HEBREW for 01296

G915.text: βάρβαρος bavrbaros barbaros {bar'-bar-os} of uncertain derivation; a foreigner (i.e. non-Greek):--barbarian(-rous).

G916.text: βαρέω barevw bareo {bar-eh'-o} from 926; to weigh down (figuratively):--burden, charge, heavy, press. see GREEK for 926

G917.text: βαρέως barevws bareos {bar-eh'-oce} adverb from 926; heavily (figuratively):--dull. see GREEK for 926

G918.text: Βαρθολομαῖος Barqolomai'os Bartholomaios {bar-thol-om-ah'-yos} of Chaldee origin (1247 and 8526); son of Tolmai; Bar-tholomoeus, a Christian apostle:--Bartholomeus. see HEBREW for 01247 see HEBREW for 08526

G919.text: Βαριησοῦς Barihsou's Bariesous {bar-ee-ay-sooce'} of Chaldee origin (1247 and 3091); son of Jesus (or Joshua); Bar-jesus, an Israelite:--Barjesus. see HEBREW for 01247 see HEBREW for 03091

G920.text: Βαριωνᾶ Bariwna' Barionas {bar-ee-oo-nas'} of Chaldee origin (1247 and 3124); son of Jonas (or Jonah); Bar-jonas, an Israelite:--Bar-jona. see HEBREW for 01247 see HEBREW for 03124

G921.text: Βαρναβᾶς Barnaba's Barnabas {bar-nab'-as} of Chaldee origin (1247 and 5029); son of Nabas (i.e. prophecy); Barnabas, an Israelite:--Barnabas. see HEBREW for 01247 see HEBREW for 05029

G922.text: βάρος bavros baros {bar'-os} probably from the same as 939 (through the notion of going down; compare 899); weight; in the New Testament only, figuratively, a load, abundance, authority:--burden(-some), weight. see GREEK for 939 see GREEK for 899

G923.text: Βαρσαββᾶς Barsabba's Barsabas {bar-sab-as'} of Chaldee origin (1247 and probably 6634); son of Sabas (or Tsaba); Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites:--Barsabas. see HEBREW for 01247 see HEBREW for 06634

G924.text: Βαρτιμαῖος Bartimai'os Bartimaios {bar-tim-ah'-yos} of Chaldee origin (1247 and 2931); son of Timoeus (or the unclean); Bar-timoeus, an Israelite:--Bartimaeus. see HEBREW for 01247 see HEBREW for 02931

G925.text: βαρέω barevw baruno {bar-oo'-no} from 926; to burden (figuratively):--overcharge. see GREEK for 926

G926.text: βαρύς baruvs barus {bar-ooce'} from the same as 922; weighty, i.e. (fig) burdensome, grave:--grievous, heavy, weightier. see GREEK for 922

G927.text: βαρύτιμος baruvtimos barutimos {bar-oo'-tim-os} from 926 and 5092; highly valuable:--very precious. see GREEK for 926 see GREEK for 5092

G928.text: βασανίζω basanivzw basanizo {bas-an-id'-zo} from 931; to torture:--pain, toil, torment, toss, vex. see GREEK for 931

G929.text: βασανισμός basanismovs basanismos {bas-an-is-mos'} from 928; torture:--torment. see GREEK for 928

G930.text: βασανιστής basanisthvs basanistes {bas-an-is-tace'} from 928; a torturer:--tormentor. see GREEK for 928

G931.text: βάσανος bavsanos basanos {bas'-an-os} perhaps remotely from the same as 939 (through the notion of going to the bottom); a touch-stone, i.e. (by analogy) torture:--torment. see GREEK for 939

G932.text: βασιλεία basileiva basileia {bas-il-i'-ah} from 935; properly, royalty, i.e. (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a realm (literally or figuratively):--kingdom, + reign. see GREEK for 935

G933.text: βασίλειον basileion basileion {bas-il'-i-on} neuter of 934; a palace:--king's court. see GREEK for 934

G934.text: βασίλειος basivleios basileios {bas-il'-i-os} from 935; kingly (in nature):--royal. see GREEK for 935

G935.text: βασιλεύς basileuvs basileus {bas-il-yooce'} probably from 939 (through the notion of a foundation of power); a sovereign (abstractly, relatively, or figuratively):--king. see GREEK for 939

G936.text: βασιλεύω basileuvw basileuo {bas-il-yoo'-o} from 935; to rule (literally or figuratively):--king, reign. see GREEK for 935

G937.text: βασιλικός basilikovs basilikos {bas-il-ee-kos'} from 935; regal (in relation), i.e. (literally) belonging to (or befitting) the sovereign (as land, dress, or a courtier), or (figuratively) preeminent:--king's, nobleman, royal. see GREEK for 935

G938.text: βασίλισσα basivlissa basilissa {bas-il'-is-sah} feminine from 936; a queen:--queen. see GREEK for 936

G939.text: βάσις bavsis basis {bas'-ece} from baino (to walk); a pace ("base"), i.e. (by implication) the foot:--foot.

G940.text: βασκαίνω baskaivnw baskaino {bas-kah'-ee-no} akin to 5335; to malign, i.e. (by extension) to fascinate (by false representations):--bewitch. see GREEK for 5335

G941.text: βαστάζω bastavzw bastazo {bas-tad'-zo} perhaps remotely derived from the base of 939 (through the idea of removal); to lift, literally or figuratively (endure, declare, sustain, receive, etc.):--bear, carry, take up. see GREEK for 939

G942.text: βάτος bavtos batos {bat'-os} of uncertain derivation; a brier shrub:--bramble, bush.

G943.text: βάτος bavtos batos {bat'-os} of Hebrew origin (1324); a bath, or measure for liquids:--measure. see HEBREW for 01324

G944.text: βάτραχος bavtracos batrachos {bat'-rakh-os} of uncertain derivation; a frog:--frog.

G945.text: βατταλογέω battalogevw battologeo {bat-tol-og-eh'-o} from Battos (a proverbial stammerer) and 3056; to stutter, i.e. (by implication) to prate tediously:--use vain repetitions. see GREEK for 3056

G946.text: βδέλυγμα bdevlugma bdelugma {bdel'-oog-mah} from 948; a detestation, i.e. (specially) idolatry:--abomination. see GREEK for 948

G947.text: βδελυκτός bdeluktovs bdeluktos {bdel-ook-tos'} from 948; detestable, i.e. (specially) idolatrous:--abominable. see GREEK for 948

G948.text: βδελύσσομαι bdeluvssomai bdelusso {bdel-oos'-so} from a (presumed) derivative of bdeo (to stink); to be disgusted, i.e. (by implication) detest (especially of idolatry):--abhor, abominable.

G949.text: βέβαιος bevbaios bebaios {beb'-ah-yos} from the base of 939 (through the idea of basality); stable (literally or figuratively):--firm, of force, stedfast, sure. see GREEK for 939

G950.text: βεβαιόω bebaiovw bebaioo {beb-ah-yo'-o} from 949; to stabilitate (figuratively):--confirm, (e-)stablish. see GREEK for 949

G951.text: βεβαίωσις bebaivwsis bebaiosis {beb-ah'-yo-sis} from 950; stabiliment:--confirmation. see GREEK for 950

G952.text: βέβηλος bevbhlos bebelos {beb'-ay-los} from the base of 939 and belos (a threshold); accessible (as by crossing the door-way), i.e. (by implication, of Jewish notions) heathenish, wicked:--profane (person). see GREEK for 939

G953.text: βεβηλόω bebhlovw bebeloo {beb-ay-lo'-o} from 952; to desecrate:--profane. see GREEK for 952

G954.text: Βεελζεβούλ Βεεζεβούλ Beelzebouvl Beezebouvl Beelzeboul {beh-el-zeb-ool'} of Chaldee origin (by parody on 1176); dung-god; Beelzebul, a name of Satan:--Beelzebub. see HEBREW for 01176

G955.text: Βελιάρ Beliavr Belial {bel-ee'-al} or Beliar {bel-ee'-ar} of Hebrew origin (1100); worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of Satan:--Belial. see HEBREW for 01100

G956.text: βέλος bevlos belos {bel'-os} from 906; a missile, i.e. spear or arrow:--dart. see GREEK for 906

G957.text: βέλτιον bevltion beltion {bel-tee'-on} neuter of a compound of a derivative of 906 (used for the comparative of 18); better:--very well. see GREEK for 906 see GREEK for 18

G958.text: Βενιαμίν Βενιαμείν Beniamivn Beniameivn Beniamin {ben-ee-am-een'} of Hebrew origin (1144); Benjamin, an Israelite:--Benjamin. see HEBREW for 01144

G959.text: Βερνίκη Bernivkh Bernike {ber-nee'-kay} from a provincial form of 5342 and 3529; victorious; Bernice, a member of the Herodian family:--Bernice. see GREEK for 5342 see GREEK for 3529

G960.text: Βέροια Bevroia Beroia {ber'-oy-ah} perhaps a provincial from a derivative of 4008 (Peroea, i.e. the region beyond the coast-line); Beroea, a place in Macedonia:--Berea. see GREEK for 4008

G961.text: Βεροιαῖος Beroiai'os Beroiaios {ber-oy-ah'-yos} from 960; a Beroeoean or native of Beroea:--of Berea. see GREEK for 960

G962.text: Βηθαβαρά Bethabara Bethabara {bay-thab-ar-ah'} of Hebrew origin (1004 and 5679); ferry-house; Bethabara (i.e. Bethabarah), a place on the Jordan:--Bethabara. see HEBREW for 01004 see HEBREW for 05679

G963.text: Βηθανία Βηθανιά Bhqaniva Bhqaniav Bethania {bay-than-ee'-ah} of Chaldee origin; date-house; Beth-any, a place in Palestine:--Bethany.

G964.text: Βηθζαθά Bhqzaqav Bethesda {bay-thes-dah'} of Chaldee origin (compare 1004 and 2617); house of kindness; Beth-esda, a pool in Jerusalem:--Bethesda. see HEBREW for 01004 see HEBREW for 02617

G965.text: Βηθλέεμ Bhqlevem Bethleem {bayth-leh-em'} of Hebrew origin (1036); Bethleem (i.e. Beth-lechem), a place in Palestine:--Bethlehem. see HEBREW for 01036

G966.text: Βηθσαϊδά Bhqsai>dav Bethsaida {bayth-sahee-dah'} of Chaldee origin (compare 1004 and 6719); fishing-house; Bethsaida, a place in Palestine:--Bethsaida. see HEBREW for 01004 see HEBREW for 06719

G967.text: Βηθφαγή Bhqfaghv Bethphage {bayth-fag-ay'} of Chaldee origin (compare 1004 and 6291); fig-house; Beth-phage, a place in Palestine:--Bethphage. see HEBREW for 01004 see HEBREW for 06291

G968.text: βῆμα bh'ma bema {bay'-ma} from the base of 939; a step, i.e. foot-breath; by implication, a rostrum, i.e. a tribunal:--judgment-seat, set (foot) on, throne. see GREEK for 939

G969.text: βήρυλλος bhvrullos berullos {bay'-rool-los} of uncertain derivation; a "beryl":--beryl.

G970.text: βία biva bia {bee'-ah} probably akin to 970 (through the idea of vital activity); force:--violence. see GREEK for 970

G971.text: βιάζω biavzw biazo {bee-ad'-zo} from 979; to force, i.e. (reflexively) to crowd oneself (into), or (passively) to be seized:--press, suffer violence. see GREEK for 979

G972.text: βίαιος bivaios biaios {bee'-ah-yos} from 970; violent:--mighty. see GREEK for 970

G973.text: βιαστής biasthvs biastes {bee-as-tace'} from 971; a forcer, i.e. (figuratively) energetic:--violent. see GREEK for 971

G974.text: βιβλαρίδιον biblarivdion bibliaridion {bib-lee-ar-id'-ee-on} a diminutive of 975; a booklet:--little book. see GREEK for 975

G975.text: βιβλίον biblivon biblion {bib-lee'-on} a diminutive of 976; a roll:--bill, book, scroll, writing. see GREEK for 976

G976.text: βίβλος bivblos biblos {bib'-los} properly, the inner bark of the papyrus plant, i.e. (by implication) a sheet or scroll of writing:--book.

G977.text: βιβρώσκω bibrwvskw bibrosko {bib-ro'-sko} a reduplicated and prolonged form of an obsolete primary verb (perhaps causative of 1006); to eat:--eat. see GREEK for 1006

G978.text: Βιθυνία Biquniva Bithunia {bee-thoo-nee'-ah} of uncertain derivation; Bithynia, a region of Asia:--Bithynia.

G979.text: βίος bivos bios {bee'-os} a primary word; life, i.e. (literally) the present state of existence; by implication, the means of livelihood:--good, life, living.

G980.text: βιόω biovw bioo {bee-o'-o} from 979; to spend existence:--live. see GREEK for 979

G981.text: βίωσις bivwsis biosis {bee'-o-sis} from 980; living (properly, the act, by implication, the mode):--manner of life. see GREEK for 980

G982.text: βιωτικός biwtikovs biotikos {bee-o-tee-kos'} from a derivative of 980; relating to the present existence:--of (pertaining to, things that pertain to) this life. see GREEK for 980

G983.text: βλαβερός blaberovs blaberos {blab-er-os'} from 984; injurious:--hurtful. see GREEK for 984

G984.text: βλάπτω blavptw blapto {blap'-to} a primary verb; properly, to hinder, i.e. (by implication) to injure:--hurt.

G985.text: βλαστάνω blastavnw blastano {blas-tan'-o} from blastos (a sprout); to germinate; by implication, to yield fruit:--bring forth, bud, spring (up).

G986.text: Βλάστος Blavstos Blastos {blas'-tos} perhaps the same as the base of 985; Blastus, an officer of Herod Agrippa:--Blastus. see GREEK for 985

G987.text: βλασφημέω blasfhmevw blasphemeo {blas-fay-meh'-o} from 989; to vilify; specially, to speak impiously:--(speak) blaspheme(-er, -mously, -my), defame, rail on, revile, speak evil. see GREEK for 989

G988.text: βλασφημία blasfhmiva blasphemia {blas-fay-me'-ah} from 989; vilification (especially against God):--blasphemy, evil speaking, railing. see GREEK for 989

G989.text: βλάσφημος blavsfhmos blasphemos {blas'-fay-mos} from a derivative of 984 and 5345; scurrilious, i.e. calumnious (against men), or (specially) impious (against God):--blasphemer(-mous), railing. see GREEK for 984 see GREEK for 5345

G990.text: βλέμμα blevmma blemma {blem'-mah} from 991; vision (properly concrete; by implication, abstract):--seeing. see GREEK for 991

G991.text: βλέπω blevpw blepo {blep'-o} a primary verb; to look at (literally or figuratively):--behold, beware, lie, look (on, to), perceive, regard, see, sight, take heed. Compare 3700. see GREEK for 3700

G992.text: βλητέος blhtevos bleteos {blay-teh'-os} from 906; fit to be cast (i.e. applied):--must be put. see GREEK for 906

G993.text: Βοανηργές Boanhrgevs Boanerges {bo-an-erg-es'} of Chaldee origin (1123 and 7266); sons of commotion; Boanerges, an epithet of two of the apostles:--Boanerges. see HEBREW for 01123 see HEBREW for 07266

G994.text: βοάω boavw boao {bo-ah'-o} apparently a prolonged form of a primary verb; to halloo, i.e. shout (for help or in a tumultuous way):--cry.

G995.text: βοή bohv boe {bo-ay'} from 994; a halloo, i.e. call (for aid, etc.):--cry. see GREEK for 994

G996.text: βοήθεια bohvqeia boetheia {bo-ay'-thi-ah} from 998; aid; specially, a rope or chain for frapping a vessel:--help. see GREEK for 998

G997.text: βοηθέω bohqevw boetheo {bo-ay-theh'-o} from 998; to aid or relieve:--help, succor. see GREEK for 998

G998.text: βοηθός bohqovs boethos {bo-ay-thos'} from 995 and theo (to run); a succorer:--helper. see GREEK for 995

G999.text: βόθυνος bovqunos bothunos {both'-oo-nos} akin to 900; a hole (in the ground); specially, a cistern:--ditch, pit. see GREEK for 900

G1000.text: βολή bolhv bole {bol-ay'} from 906; a throw (as a measure of distance):--cast. see GREEK for 906

G1001.text: βολίζω bolivzw bolizo {bol-id'-zo} from 1002; to heave the lead:--sound. see GREEK for 1002

G1002.text: βολίς bolis bolis {bol-ece'} from 906; a missile, i.e. javelin:--dart. see GREEK for 906

G1003.text: Βόες Βόος Boves Bovos Booz {bo-oz'} of Hebrew origin (1162); Booz, (i.e. Boaz), an Israelite:--Booz. see HEBREW for 01162

G1004.text: βόρβορος bovrboros borboros {bor'-bor-os} of uncertain derivation; mud:--mire.

G1005.text: βορρᾶς borra's borrhas {bor-hras'} of uncertain derivation; the north (properly, wind):--north.

G1006.text: βόσκω bovskw bosko {bos'-ko} a prolonged form of a primary verb (compare 977, 1016); to pasture; by extension to, fodder; reflexively, to graze:--feed, keep. see GREEK for 977 see GREEK for 1016

G1007.text: Βοσόρ Bosovr Bosor {bos-or'} of Hebrew origin (1160); Bosor (i.e. Beor), a Moabite:--Bosor. see HEBREW for 01160

G1008.text: βοτάνη botavnh botane {bot-an'-ay} from 1006; herbage (as if for grazing):--herb. see GREEK for 1006

G1009.text: βότρυς bovtrus botrus {bot'-rooce} of uncertain derivation; a bunch (of grapes):--(vine) cluster (of the vine).

G1010.text: βουλευτής bouleuthvs bouleutes {bool-yoo-tace'} from 1011; an adviser, i.e. (specially) a councillor or member of the Jewish Sanhedrin:--counsellor. see GREEK for 1011

G1011.text: βουλεύω bouleuvw bouleuo {bool-yoo'-o} from 1012; to advise, i.e. (reflexively) deliberate, or (by implication) resolve:--consult, take counsel, determine, be minded, purpose. see GREEK for 1012

G1012.text: βουλή boulhv boule {boo-lay'} from 1014; volition, i.e. (objectively) advice, or (by implication) purpose:--+ advise, counsel, will. see GREEK for 1014

G1013.text: βούλημα bouvlhma boulema {boo'-lay-mah} from 1014; a resolve:--purpose, will. see GREEK for 1014

G1014.text: βούλομαι bouvlomai boulomai {boo'-lom-ahee} middle voice of a primary verb; to "will," i.e. (reflexively) be willing:--be disposed, minded, intend, list, (be, of own) will (-ing). Compare 2309. see GREEK for 2309

G1015.text: βουνός bounovs bounos {boo-nos'} probably of foreign origin; a hillock:--hill.

G1016.text: βοῦς bou's bous {booce} probably from the base of 1006; an ox (as grazing), i.e. an animal of that species ("beef"):--ox. see GREEK for 1006

G1017.text: βραβεῖον brabei'on brabeion {brab-i'-on} from brabeus (an umpire of uncertain derivation); an award (of arbitration), i.e. (specially) a prize in the public games:--prize.

G1018.text: βραβεύω brabeuvw brabeuo {brab-yoo'-o} from the same as 1017; to arbitrate, i.e. (genitive case) to govern (figuratively, prevail):--rule. see GREEK for 1017

G1019.text: βραδύνω braduvnw braduno {brad-oo'-no} from 1021; to delay:--be slack, tarry. see GREEK for 1021

G1020.text: βραδυπλοέω braduploevw braduploeo {brad-oo-plo-eh'-o} from 1021 and a prolonged form of 4126; to sail slowly:--sail slowly. see GREEK for 1021 see GREEK for 4126

G1021.text: βραδύς braduvs bradus {brad-ooce'} of uncertain affinity; slow; figuratively, dull:--slow.

G1022.text: βραδύτης braduvths bradutes {brad-oo'-tace} from 1021; tardiness:--slackness. see GREEK for 1021

G1023.text: βραχίων bracivwn brachion {brakh-ee'-own} properly, comparative of 1024, but apparently in the sense of brasso (to wield); the arm, i.e. (figuratively) strength:--arm. see GREEK for 1024

G1024.text: βραχύς bracuvs brachus {brakh-ooce'} of uncertain affinity; short (of time, place, quantity, or number):--few words, little (space, while).

G1025.text: βρέφος brevfos brephos {bref'-os} of uncertain affinity; an infant (properly, unborn) literally or figuratively:--babe, (young) child, infant.

G1026.text: βρέχω brevcw brecho {brekh'-o} a primary verb; to moisten (especially by a shower):--(send) rain, wash.

G1027.text: βροντή bronthv bronte {bron-tay'} akin to bremo (to roar); thunder:--thunder(-ing).

G1028.text: βροχή brochv broche {brokh-ay'} from 1026; rain:--rain. see GREEK for 1026

G1029.text: βρόχος brovcos brochos {brokh'-os} of uncertain derivation; a noose:--snare.

G1030.text: βρυγμός brugmovs brugmos {broog-mos'} from 1031; a grating (of the teeth):--gnashing. see GREEK for 1031

G1031.text: βρύχω bruvcw brucho {broo'-kho} a primary verb; to grate the teeth (in pain or rage):--gnash.

G1032.text: βρύω bruvw bruo {broo'-o} a primary verb; to swell out, i.e. (by implication) to gush:--send forth.

G1033.text: βρῶμα brw'ma broma {bro'-mah} from the base of 977; food (literally or figuratively), especially (ceremonially) articles allowed or forbidden by the Jewish law:--meat, victuals. see GREEK for 977

G1034.text: βρώσιμος brwvsimos brosimos {bro'-sim-os} from 1035; eatable:--meat. see GREEK for 1035

G1035.text: βρῶσις brw'sis brosis {bro'-sis} from the base of 977; (abstractly) eating (literally or figuratively); by extension (concretely) food (literally or figuratively):--eating, food, meat. see GREEK for 977

G1036.text: βυθίζω buqivzw buthizo {boo-thid'-zo} from 1037; to sink; by implication, to drown:--begin to sink, drown. see GREEK for 1037

G1037.text: βυθός buqovs buthos {boo-thos'} a variation of 899; depth, i.e. (by implication) the sea:--deep. see GREEK for 899

G1038.text: βυρσεύς burseuvs burseus {boorce-yooce'} from bursa (a hide); a tanner:--tanner.

G1039.text: βύσσινος buvssinos bussinos {boos'-see-nos} from 1040; made of linen (neuter a linen cloth):--fine linen. see GREEK for 1040

G1040.text: βύσσος buvssos bussos {boos'-sos} of Hebrew origin (948); white linen:--fine linen. see HEBREW for 0948

G1041.text: βωμός bwmovs bomos {bo'-mos} from the base of 939; properly, a stand, i.e. (specially) an altar:--altar. see GREEK for 939

G1042.text: Γαββαθα Gabbaqa gabbatha {gab-bath-ah'} of Chaldee origin (compare 1355); the knoll; gabbatha, a vernacular term for the Roman tribunal in Jerusalem:-- Gabbatha. see HEBREW for 01355

G1043.text: Γαβριήλ Gabrihvl Gabriel {gab-ree-ale'} of Hebrew origin (1403); Gabriel, an archangel:--Gabriel. see HEBREW for 01403

G1044.text: γάγγραινα gavggraina gaggraina {gang'-grahee-nah} from graino (to gnaw); an ulcer ("gangrene"):--canker.

G1045.text: Γάδ Gavd Gad {gad} of Hebrew origin (1410); Gad, a tribe of Israelites:--Gad. see HEBREW for 01410

G1046.text: Γαδαρηνός Gadarhnovs Gadarenos {gad-ar-ay-nos'} from Gadara (a town east of the Jordan); a Gadarene or inhabitant of Gadara:--Gadarene.

G1047.text: Γάζα Gavza gaza {gad'-zah} of foreign origin; a treasure:--treasure.

G1048.text: Γάζα Gavza Gaza {gad'-zah} of Hebrew origin (5804); Gazah (i.e. Azzah), a place in Palestine:--Gaza. see HEBREW for 05804

G1049.text: γαζοφυλάκιον gazofulavkion gazophulakion {gad-zof-oo-lak'-ee-on} from 1047 and 5438; a treasure-house, i.e. a court in the temple for the collection-boxes:--treasury. see GREEK for 1047 see GREEK for 5438

G1050.text: Γάϊος Gavi>os Gaios {gah'-ee-os} of Latin origin; Gaius (i.e. Caius), a Christian:--Gaius.

G1051.text: γάλα gavla gala {gal'-ah} of uncertain affinity; milk (figuratively):--milk.

G1052.text: Γαλάτης Galavths Galates {gal-at'-ace} from 1053; a Galatian or inhabitant of Galatia:--Galatian. see GREEK for 1053

G1053.text: Γαλατία Galativa Galatia {gal-at-ee'-ah} of foreign origin; Galatia, a region of Asia:--Galatia.

G1054.text: Γαλατικός Galatikovs Galatikos {gal-at-ee-kos'} from 1053; Galatic or relating to Galatia:--of Galatia. see GREEK for 1053

G1055.text: γαλήνη galhvnh galene {gal-ay'-nay} of uncertain derivation; tranquillity:--calm.

G1056.text: Γαλιλαία Galilaiva Galilaia {gal-il-ah'-yah} of Hebrew origin (1551); Galiloea (i.e. the heathen circle), a region of Palestine:--Galilee. see HEBREW for 01551

G1057.text: Γαλιλαῖος Galilai'os Galilaios {gal-ee-lah'-yos} from 1056; Galilean or belonging to Galilea:--Galilean, of Galilee. see GREEK for 1056

G1058.text: Γαλλίων Gallivwn Gallion {gal-lee'-own} of Latin origin; Gallion (i.e. Gallio), a Roman officer:--Gallio.

G1059.text: Γαμαλιήλ Gamalihvl Gamaliel {gam-al-ee-ale'} of Hebrew origin (1583); Gamaliel (i.e. Gamliel), an Israelite:--Gamaliel. see HEBREW for 01583

G1060.text: γαμέω gamevw gameo {gam-eh'-o} from 1062; to wed (of either sex):--marry (a wife). see GREEK for 1062

G1061.text: γαμίσκω gamivskw gamisko {gam-is'-ko} from 1062; to espouse (a daughter to a husband):--give in marriage. see GREEK for 1062

G1062.text: γάμος gavmos gamos {gam'-os} of uncertain affinity; nuptials:--marriage, wedding.

G1063.text: γάρ gavr gar {gar} a primary particle; properly, assigning a reason (used in argument, explanation or intensification; often with other particles):--and, as, because (that), but, even, for, indeed, no doubt, seeing, then, therefore, verily, what, why, yet.

G1064.text: γαστήρ gasthvr gaster {gas-tare'} of uncertain derivation; the stomach; by analogy, the matrix; figuratively, a gourmand:--belly, + with child, womb.

G1065.text: γέ gev ge {gheh} a primary particle of emphasis or qualification (often used with other particles prefixed):--and besides, doubtless, at least, yet.

G1066.text: Γεδεών Gedewvn Gedeon {ghed-eh-own'} of Hebrew origin (1439); Gedeon (i.e. Gid(e)on), an Israelite:--Gedeon (in the King James Version). see HEBREW for 01439

G1067.text: γέεννα gevenna geenna {gheh'-en-nah} of Hebrew origin (1516 and 2011); valley of (the son of) Hinnom; ge-henna (or Ge-Hinnom), a valley of Jerusalem, used (figuratively) as a name for the place (or state) of everlasting punishment:--hell. see HEBREW for 01516 see HEBREW for 02011

G1068.text: Γεθσημανί Geqshmaniv Gethsemane {gheth-say-man-ay'} of Chaldee origin (compare 1660 and 8081); oil-press; Gethsemane, a garden near Jerusalem:--Gethsemane. see HEBREW for 01660 see HEBREW for 08081

G1069.text: γείτων geivtwn geiton {ghi'-tone} from 1093; a neighbour (as adjoining one's ground); by implication, a friend:--neighbour. see GREEK for 1093

G1070.text: γελάω gelavw gelao {ghel-ah'-o} of uncertain affinity; to laugh (as a sign of joy or satisfaction):--laugh.

G1071.text: γέλως gevlws gelos {ghel'-os} from 1070; laughter (as a mark of gratification):--laughter. see GREEK for 1070

G1072.text: γεμίζω gemivzw gemizo {ghem-id'-zo} transitive from 1073; to fill entirely:--fill (be) full. see GREEK for 1073

G1073.text: γέμω gevmw gemo {ghem'-o} a primary verb; to swell out, i.e. be full:--be full.

G1074.text: γενεά geneav genea {ghen-eh-ah'} from (a presumed derivative of) 1085; a generation; by implication, an age (the period or the persons):--age, generation, nation, time. see GREEK for 1085

G1075.text: γενεαλογέομαι genealogevomai genealogeo {ghen-eh-al-og-eh'-o} from 1074 and 3056; to reckon by generations, i.e. trace in genealogy:--count by descent. see GREEK for 1074 see GREEK for 3056

G1076.text: γενεαλογία genealogiva genealogia {ghen-eh-al-og-ee'-ah} from the same as 1075; tracing by generations, i.e. "genealogy":--genealogy. see GREEK for 1075

G1077.text: γενέσια genevsia genesia {ghen-es'-ee-ah} neuter plural of a derivative of 1078; birthday ceremonies:--birthday. see GREEK for 1078

G1078.text: γένεσις gevnesis genesis {ghen'-es-is} from the same as 1074; nativity; figuratively, nature:--generation, nature(-ral). see GREEK for 1074

G1079.text: γενετή genethv genete {ghen-et-ay} feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of 1074; birth:--birth. see GREEK for 1074

G1080.text: γεννάω gennavw gennao {ghen-nah'-o} from a variation of 1085; to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate:--bear, beget, be born, bring forth, conceive, be delivered of, gender, make, spring. see GREEK for 1085

G1081.text: γένημα γέννημα gevnhma gevnnhma gennema {ghen'-nay-mah} from 1080; offspring; by analogy, produce (literally or figuratively):--fruit, generation. see GREEK for 1080

G1082.text: Γεννησαρέτ Gennhsarevt Gennesaret {ghen-nay-sar-et'} of Hebrew origin (compare 3672); Gennesaret (i.e. Kinnereth), a lake and plain in Palestine:--Gennesaret. see HEBREW for 03672

G1083.text: γέννησις εως ἡ gennesis gennesis {ghen'-nay-sis} from 1080; nativity:--birth. see GREEK for 1080

G1084.text: γεννητός gennhtovs gennetos {ghen-nay-tos'} from 1080; born:--they that are born. see GREEK for 1080

G1085.text: γένος gevnos genos {ghen'-os} from 1096; "kin" (abstract or concrete, literal or figurative, individual or collective):--born, country(-man), diversity, generation, kind(-red), nation, offspring, stock. see GREEK for 1096

G1086.text: Γαδαρηνός Gadarhnovs Gergesenos {gher-ghes-ay-nos'} of Hebrew origin (1622); a Gergesene (i.e. Girgashite) or one of the aborigines of Palestine:--Gergesene. see HEBREW for 01622

G1087.text: γερουσία gerousiva gerousia {gher-oo-see'-ah} from 1088; the eldership, i.e. (collectively) the Jewish Sanhedrin:--senate. see GREEK for 1088

G1088.text: γέρων gevrwn geron {gher'-own} of uncertain affinity (compare 1094); aged:--old. see GREEK for 1094

G1089.text: γεύομαι geuvomai geuomai {ghyoo'-om-ahee} a primary verb; to taste; by implication, to eat; figuratively, to experience (good or ill):--eat, taste.

G1090.text: γεωργέω gewrgevw georgeo {gheh-or-gheh'-o} from 1092; to till (the soil):--dress. see GREEK for 1092

G1091.text: γεώργιον gewvrgion georgion {gheh-ore'-ghee-on} neuter of a (presumed) derivative of 1092; cultivable, i.e. a farm:--husbandry. see GREEK for 1092

G1092.text: γεωργός gewrgovs georgos {gheh-ore-gos'} from 1093 and the base of 2041; a land-worker, i.e. farmer:--husbandman. see GREEK for 1093 see GREEK for 2041

G1093.text: γῆ gh' ge {ghay} contracted from a primary word; soil; by extension a region, or the solid part or the whole of the terrene globe (including the occupants in each application):--country, earth(-ly), ground, land, world.

G1094.text: γῆρας gh'ras geras {ghay'-ras} akin to 1088; senility:--old age. see GREEK for 1088

G1095.text: γηράσκω ghravskw gerasko {ghay-ras'-ko} from 1094; to be senescent:--be (wax) old. see GREEK for 1094

G1096.text: γίνομαι givnomai ginomai {ghin'-om-ahee} a prolongation and middle voice form of a primary verb; to cause to be ("gen"-erate), i.e. (reflexively) to become (come into being), used with great latitude (literal, figurative, intensive, etc.):--arise, be assembled, be(-come, -fall, -have self), be brought (to pass), (be) come (to pass), continue, be divided, draw, be ended, fall, be finished, follow, be found, be fulfilled, + God forbid, grow, happen, have, be kept, be made, be married, be ordained to be, partake, pass, be performed, be published, require, seem, be showed, X soon as it was, sound, be taken, be turned, use, wax, will, would, be wrought.

G1097.text: γινώσκω ginwvskw ginosko {ghin-oce'-ko} a prolonged form of a primary verb; to "know" (absolutely) in a great variety of applications and with many implications (as follow, with others not thus clearly expressed):--allow, be aware (of), feel, (have) know(-ledge), perceived, be resolved, can speak, be sure, understand.

G1098.text: γλεῦκος gleu'kos gleukos {glyoo'-kos} akin to 1099; sweet wine, i.e. (properly) must (fresh juice), but used of the more saccharine (and therefore highly inebriating) fermented wine:--new wine. see GREEK for 1099

G1099.text: γλυκύς glukuvs glukus {gloo-koos'} of uncertain affinity; sweet (i.e. not bitter nor salt):--sweet, fresh.

G1100.text: γλῶσσα glw'ssa glossa {gloce-sah'} of uncertain affinity; the tongue; by implication, a language (specially, one naturally unacquired):--tongue.

G1101.text: γλωσσόκομον glwssovkomon glossokomon {gloce-sok'-om-on} from 1100 and the base of 2889; properly, a case (to keep mouthpieces of wind-instruments in) i.e. (by extension) a casket or (specially) purse:--bag. see GREEK for 1100 see GREEK for 2889

G1102.text: γναφεύς gnafeuvs gnapheus {gnaf-yuce'} by variation for a derivative from knapto (to tease cloth); a cloth-dresser:--fuller.

G1103.text: γνήσιος gnhvsios gnesios {gnay'-see-os} from the same as 1077; legitimate (of birth), i.e. genuine:--own, sincerity, true. see GREEK for 1077

G1104.text: γνησίως gnhsivws gnesios {gnay-see'-ose} adverb from 1103; genuinely, i.e. really:--naturally. see GREEK for 1103

G1105.text: γνόφος gnovfos gnophos {gnof'-os} akin to 3509; gloom (as of a storm):--blackness. see GREEK for 3509

G1106.text: γνώμη gnwvmh gnome {gno'-may} from 1097; cognition, i.e. (subjectively) opinion, or (objectively) resolve (counsel, consent, etc.):--advice, + agree, judgment, mind, purpose, will. see GREEK for 1097

G1107.text: γνωρίζω gnwrivzw gnorizo {gno-rid'-zo} from a derivative of 1097; to make known; subjectively, to know:--certify, declare, make known, give to understand, do to wit, wot. see GREEK for 1097

G1108.text: γνῶσις gnw'sis gnosis {gno'-sis} from 1097; knowing (the act), i.e. (by implication) knowledge:--knowledge, science. see GREEK for 1097

G1109.text: γνώστης gnwvsths gnostes {gnoce'-tace} from 1097; a knower:--expert. see GREEK for 1097

G1110.text: γνωστός gnwstovs gnostos {gnoce-tos'} from 1097; well-known:--acquaintance, (which may be) known, notable. see GREEK for 1097

G1111.text: γογγύζω gogguvzw gogguzo {gong-good'-zo} of uncertain derivation; to grumble:--murmur.

G1112.text: γογγυσμός goggusmovs goggusmos {gong-goos-mos'} from 1111; a grumbling:--grudging, murmuring. see GREEK for 1111

G1113.text: γογγύστης gogguvsths goggustes {gong-goos-tace'} from 1111; a grumbler:--murmurer. see GREEK for 1111

G1114.text: γόης govhs goes {go'-ace} from goao (to wail); properly, a wizard (as muttering spells), i.e. (by implication) an imposter:--seducer.

G1115.text: Γολγοθᾶ Golgoqa' Golgotha {gol-goth-ah'} of Chaldee origin (compare 1538); the skull; Golgotha, a knoll near Jerusalem:--Golgotha. see HEBREW for 01538

G1116.text: Γόμορρα Govmorra Gomorrha {gom'-or-hrhah} of Hebrew origin (6017); Gomorrha (i.e. Amorah), a place near the Dead Sea:--Gomorrha. see HEBREW for 06017

G1117.text: γόμος govmos gomos {gom'-os} from 1073; a load (as filling), i.e. (specially) a cargo, or (by extension) wares:--burden, merchandise. see GREEK for 1073

G1118.text: γονεύς goneuvs goneus {gon-yooce'} from the base of 1096; a parent:--parent. see GREEK for 1096

G1119.text: γόνυ govnu gonu {gon-oo'} of uncertain affinity; the "knee":--knee(X -l).

G1120.text: γονυπετέω gonupetevw gonupeteo {gon-oo-pet-eh'-o} from a compound of 1119 and the alternate of 4098; to fall on the knee:--bow the knee, kneel down. see GREEK for 1119 see GREEK for 4098

G1121.text: γράμμα gravmma gramma {gram'-mah} from 1125; a writing, i.e. a letter, note, epistle, book, etc.; plural learning:--bill, learning, letter, scripture, writing, written. see GREEK for 1125

G1122.text: γραμματεύς grammateuvs grammateus {gram-mat-yooce'} from 1121. a writer, i.e. (professionally) scribe or secretary:--scribe, town-clerk. see GREEK for 1121

G1123.text: γραπτός graptovs graptos {grap-tos'} from 1125; inscribed (figuratively):--written. see GREEK for 1125

G1124.text: γραφή grafhv graphe {graf-ay'} a document, i.e. holy Writ (or its contents or a statement in it):--scripture.

G1125.text: γράφω gravfw grapho {graf'-o} a primary verb; to "grave", especially to write; figuratively, to describe:--describe, write(-ing, -ten).

G1126.text: γραώδης grawvdhs graodes {grah-o'-dace} from graus (an old woman) and 1491; crone-like, i.e. silly:--old wives'. see GREEK for 1491

G1127.text: γρηγορέω grhgorevw gregoreuo {gray-gor-yoo'-o} from 1453; to keep awake, i.e. watch (literally or figuratively):--be vigilant, wake, (be) watch(-ful). see GREEK for 1453

G1128.text: γυμνάζω gumnavzw gumnazo {goom-nad'-zo} from 1131; to practise naked (in the games), i.e. train (figuratively):--exercise. see GREEK for 1131

G1129.text: γυμνασία gumnasiva gumnasia {goom-nas-ee'-ah} from 1128; training, i.e. (figuratively) asceticism:--exercise. see GREEK for 1128

G1130.text: γυμνιτεύω gumniteuvw gumneteuo {goom-nayt-yoo'-o} from a derivative of 1131; to strip, i.e. (reflexively) go poorly clad:--be naked. see GREEK for 1131

G1131.text: γυμνός gumnovs gumnos {goom-nos'} of uncertain affinity; nude (absolute or relative, literal or figurative):--naked.

G1132.text: γυμνότης gumnovths gumnotes {goom-not'-ace} from 1131; nudity (absolute or comparative):--nakedness. see GREEK for 1131

G1133.text: γυναικάριον gunaikavrion gunaikarion {goo-nahee-kar'-ee-on} a diminutive from 1135; a little (i.e. foolish) woman:--silly woman. see GREEK for 1135

G1134.text: γυναικεῖος gunaikei'os gunaikeios {goo-nahee-ki'-os} from 1135; feminine:--wife. see GREEK for 1135

G1135.text: γυνή gunhv gune {goo-nay'} probably from the base of 1096; a woman; specially, a wife:--wife, woman. see GREEK for 1096

G1136.text: Γώγ Gwvg Gog {gogue} of Hebrew origin (1463); Gog, a symbolic name for some future Antichrist:--Gog. see HEBREW for 01463

G1137.text: γωνία gwniva gonia {go-nee'-ah} probably akin to 1119; an angle:--corner, quarter. see GREEK for 1119

G1138.text: Δαυίδ Dauivd Dabid {dab-eed'} of Hebrew origin (1732); Dabid (i.e. David), the Israelite king:--David. see HEBREW for 01732

G1139.text: δαιμονίζομαι daimonivzomai daimonizomai {dahee-mon-id'-zom-ahee} middle voice from 1142; to be exercised by a dæmon:--have a (be vexed with, be possessed with) devil(-s). see GREEK for 1142

G1140.text: δαιμόνιον daimovnion daimonion {dahee-mon'-ee-on} neuter of a derivative of 1142; a dæmonic being; by extension a deity:--devil, god. see GREEK for 1142

G1141.text: δαιμονιώδης daimoniwvdhs daimoniodes {dahee-mon-ee-o'-dace} from 1140 and 1142; dæmon-like:--devilish. see GREEK for 1140 see GREEK for 1142

G1142.text: δαίμων daivmwn daimon {dah'-ee-mown} from daio (to distribute fortunes); a dæmon or supernatural spirit (of a bad nature):--devil.

G1143.text: δάκνω davknw dakno {dak'-no} a prolonged form of a primary root; to bite, i.e. (figuratively) thwart:--bite.

G1144.text: δάκρυον davkruon dakru {dak'-roo} or dakruon {dak'-roo-on} or dakruon dak'-roo-on of uncertain affinity; a tear:--tear.

G1145.text: δακρύω dakruvw dakruo {dak-roo'-o} from 1144; to shed tears:--weep. Compare 2799. see GREEK for 1144 see GREEK for 2799

G1146.text: δακτύλιος daktuvlios daktulios {dak-too'-lee-os} from 1147; a finger-ring:--ring. see GREEK for 1147

G1147.text: δάκτυλος davktulos daktulos {dak'-too-los} probably from 1176; a finger:--finger. see GREEK for 1176

G1148.text: Δαλμανουθά Dalmanouqav Dalmanoutha {dal-man-oo-thah'} probably of Chaldee origin; Dalmanutha, a place in Palestine:--Dalmanutha.

G1149.text: Δαλματία Dalmativa Dalmatia {dal-mat-ee'-ah} probably of foreign derivation; Dalmatia, a region of Europe:--Dalmatia.

G1150.text: δαμάζω damavzw damazo {dam-ad'-zo} a variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to tame:--tame.

G1151.text: δάμαλις davmalis damalis {dam'-al-is} probably from the base of 1150; a heifer (as tame):--heifer. see GREEK for 1150

G1152.text: Δάμαρις Davmaris Damaris {dam'-ar-is} probably from the base of 1150; perhaps gentle; Damaris, an Athenian woman:--Damaris. see GREEK for 1150

G1153.text: Δαμασκηνός Damaskhnovs Damaskenos {dam-as-kay-nos'} from 1154; a Damascene or inhabitant of Damascus:--Damascene. see GREEK for 1154

G1154.text: Δαμασκός Damaskovs Damaskos {dam-as-kos'} of Hebrew origin (1834); Damascus, a city of Syria:--Damascus. see HEBREW for 01834

G1155.text: δανείζω daneivzw daneizo {dan-ide'-zo} from 1156; to loan on interest; reflexively, to borrow:--borrow, lend. see GREEK for 1156

G1156.text: δάνειον davneion daneion {dan'-i-on} from danos (a gift); probably akin to the base of 1325; a loan:--debt. see GREEK for 1325

G1157.text: δανιστής danisthvs daneistes {dan-ice-tace'} from 1155; a lender:--creditor. see GREEK for 1155

G1158.text: Δανιήλ Danihvl Daniel {dan-ee-ale'} of Hebrew origin (1840); Daniel, an Israelite:--Daniel. see HEBREW for 01840

G1159.text: δαπανάω dapanavw dapanao {dap-an-ah'-o} from 1160; to expend, i.e. (in a good sense) to incur cost, or (in a bad one) to waste:--be at charges, consume, spend. see GREEK for 1160

G1160.text: δαπάνη dapavnh dapane {dap-an'-ay} from dapto (to devour); expense (as consuming):--cost.

G1161.text: δέ dev de {deh} a primary particle (adversative or continuative); but, and, etc.:--also, and, but, moreover, now (often unexpressed in English).

G1162.text: δέησις devhsis deesis {deh'-ay-sis} from 1189; a petition:--prayer, request, supplication. see GREEK for 1189

G1163.text: δεῖ dei' dei {die} 3d person singular active present of 1210; also deon deh-on'; neuter active participle of the same; both used impersonally; it is (was, etc.) necessary (as binding):--behoved, be meet, must (needs), (be) need(-ful), ought, should. see GREEK for 1210

G1164.text: δεῖγμα dei'gma deigma {digh'-mah} from the base of 1166; a specimen (as shown):--example. see GREEK for 1166

G1165.text: δειγματίζω deigmativzw deigmatizo {digh-mat-id'-zo} from 1164; to exhibit:--make a shew. see GREEK for 1164

G1166.text: δείκνυμι deivknumi deiknuo {dike-noo'-o} a prolonged form of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to show (literally or figuratively):--shew.

G1167.text: δειλία deiliva deilia {di-lee'-ah} from 1169; timidity:--fear. see GREEK for 1169

G1168.text: δειλιάω deiliavw deiliao {di-lee-ah'-o} from 1167; to be timid:--be afraid. see GREEK for 1167

G1169.text: δειλός deilovs deilos {di-los'} from deos (dread); timid, i.e. (by implication) faithless:--fearful.

G1170.text: δεῖνα dei'na deina {di'-nah} probably from the same as 1171 (through the idea of forgetting the name as fearful, i.e. strange); so and so (when the person is not specified):--such a man. see GREEK for 1171

G1171.text: δεινῶς deinw's deinos {di-noce'} adverb from a derivative of the same as 1169; terribly, i.e. excessively:--grievously, vehemently. see GREEK for 1169

G1172.text: δειπνέω deipnevw deipneo {dipe-neh'-o} from 1173; to dine, i.e. take the principle (or evening) meal:--sup (X -er). see GREEK for 1173

G1173.text: δεῖπνον dei'pnon deipnon {dipe'-non} from the same as 1160; dinner, i.e. the chief meal (usually in the evening):--feast, supper. see GREEK for 1160

G1174.text: δεισιδαίμων deisidaivmwn deisidaimonesteros {dice-ee-dahee-mon-es'-ter-os} the compound of a derivative of the base of 1169 and 1142; more religious than others:--too superstitious. see GREEK for 1169 see GREEK for 1142

G1175.text: δεισιδαιμονία deisidaimoniva deisidaimonia {dice-ee-dahee-mon-ee'-ah} from the same as 1174; religion:--superstition. see GREEK for 1174

G1176.text: δέκα devka deka {dek'-ah} a primary number; ten:--(eight-)een, ten.

G1177.text: δεκαδύο dekaduo dekaduo {dek-ad-oo'-o} from 1176 and 1417; two and ten, i.e. twelve:--twelve. see GREEK for 1176 see GREEK for 1417

G1178.text: δεκαπέντε dekapevnte dekapente {dek-ap-en'-teh} from 1176 and 4002; ten and five, i.e. fifteen:--fifteen. see GREEK for 1176 see GREEK for 4002

G1179.text: Δεκάπολις Dekavpolis Dekapolis {dek-ap'-ol-is} from 1176 and 4172; the ten-city region; the Decapolis, a district in Syria:--Decapolis. see GREEK for 1176 see GREEK for 4172

G1180.text: δεκατέσσαρες dekatevssares dekatessares {dek-at-es'-sar-es} from 1176 and 5064; ten and four, i.e. fourteen:--fourteen. see GREEK for 1176 see GREEK for 5064

G1181.text: δέκατος devkatos dekate {dek-at'-ay} feminine of 1182; a tenth, i.e. as a percentage or (technically) tithe:--tenth (part), tithe. see GREEK for 1182

G1182.text: δέκατος devkatos dekatos {dek'-at-os} ordinal from 1176; tenth:--tenth. see GREEK for 1176

G1183.text: δεκατόω dekatovw dekatoo {dek-at-o'-o} from 1181; to tithe, i.e. to give or take a tenth:--pay (receive) tithes. see GREEK for 1181

G1184.text: δεκτός dektovs dektos {dek-tos'} from 1209; approved; (figuratively) propitious:-- accepted(-table). see GREEK for 1209

G1185.text: δελεάζω deleavzw deleazo {del-eh-ad'-zo} from the base of 1388; to entrap, i.e. (figuratively) delude:--allure, beguile, entice. see GREEK for 1388

G1186.text: δένδρον devndron dendron {den'-dron} probably from drus (an oak); a tree:--tree.

G1187.text: δεξιολάβος dexiolavbos dexiolabos {dex-ee-ol-ab'-os} from 1188 and 2983; a guardsman (as if taking the right) or light-armed soldier:--spearman. see GREEK for 1188 see GREEK for 2983

G1188.text: δεξιός dexiovs dexios {dex-ee-os'} from 1209; the right side or (feminine) hand (as that which usually takes):--right (hand, side). see GREEK for 1209

G1189.text: δέομαι devomai deomai {deh'-om-ahee} middle voice of 1210; to beg (as binding oneself), i.e. petition:--beseech, pray (to), make request. Compare 4441. see GREEK for 1210 see GREEK for 4441

G1190.text: Δερβαῖος Derbai'os Derbaios {der-bah'-ee-os} from 1191; a Derbæan or inhabitant of Derbe:--of Derbe. see GREEK for 1191

G1191.text: Δέρβη Devrbh Derbe {der-bay'} of foreign origin; Derbe, a place in Asia Minor:--Derbe.

G1192.text: δέρμα devrma derma {der'-mah} from 1194; a hide:--skin. see GREEK for 1194

G1193.text: δερμάτινος dermavtinos dermatinos {der-mat'-ee-nos} from 1192; made of hide:--leathern, of a skin. see GREEK for 1192

G1194.text: δέρω devrw dero {der'-o} a primary verb; properly, to flay, i.e. (by implication) to scourge, or (by analogy) to thrash:--beat, smite.

G1195.text: δεσμεύω desmeuvw desmeuo {des-myoo'-o} from a (presumed) derivative of 1196; to be a binder (captor), i.e. to enchain (a prisoner), to tie on (a load):-- bind. see GREEK for 1196

G1196.text: δεσμέω desmeo desmeo {des-meh'-o} from 1199; to tie, i.e. shackle:--bind. see GREEK for 1199

G1197.text: δέσμη devsmh desme {des-may'} from 1196; a bundle:--bundle. see GREEK for 1196

G1198.text: δέσμιος devsmios desmios {des'-mee-os} from 1199; a captive (as bound):--in bonds, prisoner. see GREEK for 1199

G1199.text: δεσμός desmovs desmon {des-mon'} 或 desmos {des-mos'} or desmos des-mos' neuter and masculine respectively from 1210; a band, i.e. ligament (of the body) or shackle (of a prisoner); figuratively, an impediment or disability:--band, bond, chain, string. see GREEK for 1210

G1200.text: δεσμοφύλαξ desmofuvlax desmophulax {des-mof-oo'-lax} from 1199 and 5441; a jailer (as guarding the prisoners):--jailor, keeper of the prison. see GREEK for 1199 see GREEK for 5441

G1201.text: δεσμωτήριον desmwthvrion desmoterion {des-mo-tay'-ree-on} from a derivative of 1199 (equivalent to 1196); a place of bondage, i.e. a dungeon:--prison. see GREEK for 1199 see GREEK for 1196

G1202.text: δεσμώτης desmwvths desmotes {des-mo'-tace} from the same as 1201; (passively) a captive:--prisoner. see GREEK for 1201

G1203.text: δεσπότης despovths despotes {des-pot'-ace} perhaps from 1210 and posis (a husband); an absolute ruler ("despot"):--Lord, master. see GREEK for 1210

G1204.text: δεῦρο deu'ro deuro {dyoo'-ro} of uncertain affinity; here; used also imperative hither!; and of time, hitherto:--come (hither), hither(-to).

G1205.text: δεῦτε deu'te deute {dyoo'-teh} from 1204 and an imperative form of eimi (to go); come hither!:--come, X follow. see GREEK for 1204

G1206.text: δευτεραῖος deuterai'os deuteraios {dyoo-ter-ah'-yos} from 1208; secondary, i.e. (specially) on the second day:--next day. see GREEK for 1208

G1207.text: δευτερόπρωτος ον deuteroprotos deuteroprotos {dyoo-ter-op'-ro-tos} from 1208 and 4413; second-first, i.e. (specially) a designation of the Sabbath immediately after the Paschal week (being the second after Passover day, and the first of the seven Sabbaths intervening before Pentecost):--second ... after the first. see GREEK for 1208 see GREEK for 4413

G1208.text: δεύτερος deuvteros deuteros {dyoo'-ter-os} as the compare of 1417; (ordinal) second (in time, place, or rank; also adverb):--afterward, again, second(-arily, time). see GREEK for 1417

G1209.text: δέχομαι devcomai dechomai {dekh'-om-ahee} middle voice of a primary verb; to receive (in various applications, literally or figuratively):--accept, receive, take. Compare 2983. see GREEK for 2983

G1210.text: δέω devw deo {deh'-o} a primary verb; to bind (in various applications, literally or figuratively):--bind, be in bonds, knit, tie, wind. See also 1163, 1189. see GREEK for 1163 see GREEK for 1189

G1211.text: δή dhv de {day} probably akin to 1161; a particle of emphasis or explicitness; now, then, etc.:--also, and, doubtless, now, therefore. see GREEK for 1161

G1212.text: δῆλος dh'los delos {day'-los} of uncertain derivation; clear:--+ bewray, certain, evident, manifest.

G1213.text: δηλόω dhlovw deloo {day-lo'-o} from 1212; to make plain (by words):--declare, shew, signify. see GREEK for 1212

G1214.text: Δημᾶς Dhma's Demas {day-mas'} probably for 1216; Demas, a Christian:--Demas. see GREEK for 1216

G1215.text: δημηγορέω dhmhgorevw demegoreo {day-may-gor-eh'-o} from a compound of 1218 and 58; to be a people-gatherer, i.e. to address a public assembly:--make an oration. see GREEK for 1218 see GREEK for 58

G1216.text: Δημήτριος Dhmhvtrios Demetrios {day-may'-tree-os} from Demeter (Ceres); Demetrius, the name of an Ephesian and of a Christian:--Demetrius.

G1217.text: δημιουργός dhmiourgovs demiourgos {day-me-oor-gos'} from 1218 and 2041; a worker for the people, i.e. mechanic (spoken of the Creator):--maker. see GREEK for 1218 see GREEK for 2041

G1218.text: δῆμος dh'mos demos {day'-mos} from 1210; the public (as bound together socially):--people. see GREEK for 1210

G1219.text: δημόσιος dhmovsios demosios {day-mos'ee-os} from 1218; public; (feminine singular dative case as adverb) in public:--common, openly, publickly. see GREEK for 1218

G1220.text: δηνάριον dhnavrion denarion {day-nar'-ee-on} of Latin origin; a denarius (or ten asses):--pence, penny(-worth).

G1221.text: δήποτε depote depote {day'-pot-eh} from 1211 and 4218; a particle of generalization; indeed, at any time:--(what-)soever. see GREEK for 1211 see GREEK for 4218

G1222.text: δήπου dhvpou depou {day'-poo} from 1211 and 4225; a particle of asseveration; indeed doubtless:--verily. see GREEK for 1211 see GREEK for 4225

G1223.text: διά diav dia {dee-ah'} a primary preposition denoting the channel of an act; through (in very wide applications, local, causal, or occasional):--after, always, among, at, to avoid, because of (that), briefly, by, for (cause) ... fore, from, in, by occasion of, of, by reason of, for sake, that, thereby, therefore, X though, through(-out), to, wherefore, with (-in). In composition it retains the same general importance.

G1224.text: διαβαίνω diabaivnw diabaino {dee-ab-ah'-ee-no} from 1223 and the base of 939; to cross:--come over, pass (through). see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 939

G1225.text: διαβάλλω diabavllw diaballo {dee-ab-al'-lo} from 1223 and 906; (figuratively) to traduce:--accuse. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 906

G1226.text: διαβεβαιόομαι diabebaiovomai diabebaioomai {dee-ab-eb-ahee-o'-om-ahee} middle voice of a compound of 1223 and 950; to confirm thoroughly (by words), i.e. asseverate:--affirm constantly. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 950

G1227.text: διαβλέπω diablevpw diablepo {dee-ab-lep'-o} from 1223 and 991; to look through, i.e. recover full vision:--see clearly. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 991

G1228.text: διάβολος diavbolos diabolos {dee-ab'-ol-os} from 1225; a traducer; specially, Satan (compare 7854):--false accuser, devil, slanderer. see GREEK for 1225 see HEBREW for 07854

G1229.text: διαγγέλλω diaggevllw diaggello {de-ang-gel'-lo} from 1223 and the base of 32; to herald thoroughly:--declare, preach, signify. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 32

G1230.text: διαγίνομαι diagivnomai diaginomai {dee-ag-in'-om-ahee} from 1223 and 1096; to elapse meanwhile:--X after, be past, be spent. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 1096

G1231.text: διαγινώσκω diaginwvskw diaginosko {dee-ag-in-o'-sko} from 1223 and 1097; to know thoroughly, i.e. ascertain exactly:--(would) enquire, know the uttermost. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 1097

G1232.text: διαγνωρίζω diagnorizo diagnorizo {dee-ag-no-rid'-zo} from 1123 and 1107; to tell abroad:--make known. see GREEK for 1123 see GREEK for 1107

G1233.text: διάγνωσις diavgnwsis diagnosis {dee-ag'-no-sis} from 1231; (magisterial) examination ("diagnosis"):--hearing. see GREEK for 1231

G1234.text: διαγογγύζω diagogguvzw diagogguzo {dee-ag-ong-good'-zo} from 1223 and 1111; to complain throughout a crowd:--murmur. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 1111

G1235.text: διαγρηγορέω diagrhgorevw diagregoreo {dee-ag-ray-gor-eh'-o} from 1223 and 1127; to waken thoroughly:--be awake. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 1127

G1236.text: διάγω diavgw diago {dee-ag'-o} from 1223 and 71; to pass time or life:--lead life, living. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 71

G1237.text: διαδέχομαι diadevcomai diadechomai {dee-ad-ekh'-om-ahee} from 1223 and 1209; to receive in turn, i.e. (figuratively) succeed to:--come after. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 1209

G1238.text: διάδημα diavdhma diadema {dee-ad'-ay-mah} from a compound of 1223 and 1210; a "diadem" (as bound about the head):--crown. Compare 4735. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 1210 see GREEK for 4735

G1239.text: διαδίδωμι diadivdwmi diadidomai {dee-ad-id'-o-mee} from 1223 and 1325; to give throughout a crowd, i.e. deal out; also to deliver over (as to a successor):--(make) distribute(-ion), divide, give. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 1325

G1240.text: διάδοχος diavdocos diadochos {dee-ad'-okh-os} from 1237; a successor in office:--room. see GREEK for 1237

G1241.text: διαζώννυμι diazwvnnumi diazonnumi {dee-az-own'-noo-mee} from 1223 and 2224; to gird tightly:--gird. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 2224

G1242.text: διαθήκη diaqhvkh diatheke {dee-ath-ay'-kay} from 1303; properly, a disposition, i.e. (specially) a contract (especially a devisory will):--covenant, testament. see GREEK for 1303

G1243.text: διαίρεσις diaivresis diairesis {dee-ah'-ee-res-is} from 1244; a distinction or (concretely) variety:--difference, diversity. see GREEK for 1244

G1244.text: διαιρέω diairevw diaireo {dee-ahee-reh'-o} from 1223 and 138; to separate, i.e. distribute:--divide. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 138

G1245.text: διακαθαρίζω διακαθαίρω diakaqarivzw diakaqaivrw diakatharizo {dee-ak-ath-ar-id'-zo} from 1223 and 2511; to cleanse perfectly, i.e. (specially) winnow:--thoroughly purge. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 2511

G1246.text: διακατελέγχομαι diakatelevgcomai diakatelegchomai {dee-ak-at-el-eng'-khom-ahee} middle voice from 1223 and a compound of 2596 and 1651; to prove downright, i.e. confute:--convince. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 1651

G1247.text: διακονέω diakonevw diakoneo {dee-ak-on-eh'-o} from 1249; to be an attendant, i.e. wait upon (menially or as a host, friend, or (figuratively) teacher); technically, to act as a Christian deacon:--(ad-)minister (unto), serve, use the office of a deacon. see GREEK for 1249
