G1358.text: διορύσσω dioruvssw diorusso {dee-or-oos'-so} from 1223 and 3736; to penetrate burglariously:--break through (up). see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 3736

G1359.text: Διόσκουροι Diovskouroi Dioskouroi {dee-os'-koo-roy} from the alternate of 2203 and a form of the base of 2877; sons of Jupiter, i.e. the twins Dioscuri:--Castor and Pollux. see GREEK for 2203 see GREEK for 2877

G1360.text: διότι diovti dioti {dee-ot'-ee} from 1223 and 3754; on the very account that, or inasmuch as:--because (that), for, therefore. see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 3754

G1361.text: Διοτρέφης Diotrevfhs Diotrephes {dee-ot-ref-ace'} from the alternate of 2203 and 5142; Jove-nourished; Diotrephes, an opponent of Christianity:--Diotrephes. see GREEK for 2203 see GREEK for 5142

G1362.text: διπλοῦς diplou's diplous {dip-looce'} from 1364 and (probably) the base of 4119; two-fold:--double, two-fold more. see GREEK for 1364 see GREEK for 4119

G1363.text: διπλόω diplovw diploo {dip-lo'-o} from 1362; to render two-fold:--double. see GREEK for 1362

G1364.text: δίς divs dis {dece} adverb from 1417; twice:--again, twice. see GREEK for 1417

G1365.text: διστάζω distavzw distazo {dis-tad'-zo} from 1364; properly, to duplicate, i.e. (mentally) to waver (in opinion):--doubt. see GREEK for 1364

G1366.text: δίστομος divstomos distomos {dis'-tom-os} from 1364 and 4750; double-edged:--with two edges, two-edged. see GREEK for 1364 see GREEK for 4750

G1367.text: δισχίλιοι discivlioi dischilioi {dis-khil'-ee-oy} from 1364 and 5507; two thousand:--two thousand. see GREEK for 1364 see GREEK for 5507

G1368.text: διϋλίζω diu>livzw diulizo {dee-oo-lid'-zo} from 1223 and hulizo hoo-lid'-zo (to filter); to strain out:--strain at (probably by misprint). see GREEK for 1223

G1369.text: διχάζω dicavzw dichazo {dee-khad'-zo} from a derivative of 1364; to make apart, i.e. sunder (figuratively, alienate):--set at variance. see GREEK for 1364

G1370.text: διχοστασία dicostasiva dichostasia {dee-khos-tas-ee'-ah} from a derivative of 1364 and 4714; disunion, i.e. (figuratively) dissension:--division, sedition. see GREEK for 1364 see GREEK for 4714

G1371.text: διχοτομέω dicotomevw dichotomeo {dee-khot-om-eh'-o} from a compound of a derivative of 1364 and a derivative of temno (to cut); to bisect, i.e. (by extension) to flog severely:--cut asunder (in sunder). see GREEK for 1364

G1372.text: διψάω diyavw dipsao {dip-sah'-o} from a variation of 1373; to thirst for (literally or figuratively):--(be, be a-)thirst(-y). see GREEK for 1373

G1373.text: δίψος divyos dipsos {dip'-sos} of uncertain affinity; thirst:--thirst.

G1374.text: δίψυχος divyucos dipsuchos {dip'-soo-khos} from 1364 and 5590; two-spirited, i.e. vacillating (in opinion or purpose):--double minded. see GREEK for 1364 see GREEK for 5590

G1375.text: διωγμός diwgmovs diogmos {dee-ogue-mos'} from 1377; persecution:--persecution. see GREEK for 1377

G1376.text: διώκτης diwvkths dioktes {dee-oke'-tace} from 1377; a persecutor:--persecutor. see GREEK for 1377

G1377.text: διώκω diwvkw dioko {dee-o'-ko} a prolonged (and causative) form of a primary verb dio (to flee; compare the base of 1169 and 1249); to pursue (literally or figuratively); by implication, to persecute:--ensue, follow (after), given to, (suffer) persecute(-ion), press forward. see GREEK for 1169 see GREEK for 1249

G1378.text: δόγμα dovgma dogma {dog'-mah} from the base of 1380; a law (civil, ceremonial or ecclesiastical):--decree, ordinance. see GREEK for 1380

G1379.text: δογματίζομαι dogmativzomai dogmatizo {dog-mat-id'-zo} from 1378; to prescribe by statute, i.e. (reflexively) to submit to, ceremonially rule:--be subject to ordinances. see GREEK for 1378

G1380.text: δοκέω dokevw dokeo {dok-eh'-o} a prolonged form of a primary verb, doko dok'-o (used only in an alternate in certain tenses; compare the base of 1166) of the same meaning; to think; by implication, to seem (truthfully or uncertainly):--be accounted, (of own) please(-ure), be of reputation, seem (good), suppose, think, trow. see GREEK for 1166

G1381.text: δοκιμάζω dokimavzw dokimazo {dok-im-ad'-zo} from 1384; to test (literally or figuratively); by implication, to approve:--allow, discern, examine, X like, (ap-)prove, try. see GREEK for 1384

G1382.text: δοκιμή dokimhv dokime {dok-ee-may'} from the same as 1384; test (abstractly or concretely); by implication, trustiness:--experience(-riment), proof, trial. see GREEK for 1384

G1383.text: δοκίμιον dokivmion dokimion {dok-im'-ee-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of 1382; a testing; by implication, trustworthiness:--trial, trying. see GREEK for 1382

G1384.text: δόκιμος dovkimos dokimos {dok'-ee-mos} from 1380; properly, acceptable (current after assayal), i.e. approved:--approved, tried. see GREEK for 1380

G1385.text: δοκός dokovs dokos {dok-os'} from 1209 (through the idea of holding up); a stick of timber:--beam. see GREEK for 1209

G1386.text: δόλιος dovlios dolios {dol'-ee-os} from 1388; guileful:--deceitful. see GREEK for 1388

G1387.text: δολιόω doliovw dolioo {dol-ee-o'-o} from 1386; to be guileful:--use deceit. see GREEK for 1386

G1388.text: δόλος dovlos dolos {dol'-os} from an obsolete primary verb, dello (probably meaning to decoy; compare 1185); a trick (bait), i.e. (figuratively) wile:--craft, deceit, guile, subtilty. see GREEK for 1185

G1389.text: δολόω dolovw doloo {dol-o'-o} from 1388; to ensnare, i.e. (figuratively) adulterate:--handle deceitfully. see GREEK for 1388

G1390.text: δόμα dovma doma {dom'-ah} from the base of 1325; a present:--gift. see GREEK for 1325

G1391.text: δόξα dovxa doxa {dox'-ah} from the base of 1380; glory (as very apparent), in a wide application (literal or figurative, objective or subjective):--dignity, glory(-ious), honour, praise, worship. see GREEK for 1380

G1392.text: δοξάζω doxavzw doxazo {dox-ad'-zo} from 1391; to render (or esteem) glorious (in a wide application):--(make) glorify(-ious), full of (have) glory, honour, magnify. see GREEK for 1391

G1393.text: Δορκάς Dorkavs Dorkas {dor-kas'} gazelle; Dorcas, a Christian woman:--Dorcas.

G1394.text: δόσις dovsis dosis {dos'-is} from the base of 1325; a giving; by implication, (concretely) a gift:--gift, giving. see GREEK for 1325

G1395.text: δότης dovths dotes {dot'-ace} from the base of 1325; a giver:--giver. see GREEK for 1325

G1396.text: δουλαγωγέω doulagwgevw doulagogeo {doo-lag-ogue-eh'-o} from a presumed compound of 1401 and 71; to be a slave-driver, i.e. to enslave (figuratively, subdue):--bring into subjection. see GREEK for 1401 see GREEK for 71

G1397.text: δουλεία douleiva douleia {doo-li'-ah} from 1398; slavery (ceremonially or figuratively):--bondage. see GREEK for 1398

G1398.text: δουλεύω douleuvw douleuo {dool-yoo'-o} from 1401; to be a slave to (literal or figurative, involuntary or voluntary):--be in bondage, (do) serve(-ice). see GREEK for 1401

G1399.text: δούλη douvlh doule {doo'-lay} feminine of 1401; a female slave (involuntarily or voluntarily):--handmaid(-en). see GREEK for 1401

G1400.text: δοῦλον doulon doulon {doo'-lon} neuter of 1401; subservient:--servant. see GREEK for 1401

G1401.text: δοῦλος dou'los doulos {doo'-los} from 1210; a slave (literal or figurative, involuntary or voluntary; frequently, therefore in a qualified sense of subjection or subserviency):--bond(-man), servant. see GREEK for 1210

G1402.text: δουλόω doulovw douloo {doo-lo'-o} from 1401; to enslave (literally or figuratively):--bring into (be under) bondage, X given, become (make) servant. see GREEK for 1401

G1403.text: δοχή dochv doche {dokh-ay'} from 1209; a reception, i.e. convivial entertainment:--feast. see GREEK for 1209

G1404.text: δράκων dravkwn drakon {drak'-own} probably from an alternate form of derkomai (to look); a fabulous kind of serpent (perhaps as supposed to fascinate):--dragon.

G1405.text: δράσσομαι dravssomai drassomai {dras'-som-ahee} perhaps akin to the base of 1404 (through the idea of capturing); to grasp, i.e. (figuratively) entrap:--take. see GREEK for 1404

G1406.text: δραχμή dracmhv drachme {drakh-may'} from 1405; a drachma or (silver) coin (as handled):--piece (of silver). see GREEK for 1405

G1407.text: δρέπανον drevpanon drepanon {drep'-an-on} from drepo (to pluck); a gathering hook (especially for harvesting):--sickle.

G1408.text: δρόμος drovmos dromos {drom'-os} from the alternate of 5143; a race, i.e. (figuratively) career:--course. see GREEK for 5143

G1409.text: Δρούσιλλα Drouvsilla Drousilla {droo'-sil-lah} a feminine diminutive of Drusus (a Roman name); Drusilla, a member of the Herodian family:--Drusilla.

G1410.text: δύναμαι duvnamai dunamai {doo'-nam-ahee} of uncertain affinity; to be able or possible:--be able, can (do, + -not), could, may, might, be possible, be of power.

G1411.text: δύναμις duvnamis dunamis {doo'-nam-is} from 1410; force (literally or figuratively); specially, miraculous power (usually by implication, a miracle itself):--ability, abundance, meaning, might(-ily, -y, -y deed), (worker of) miracle(-s), power, strength, violence, mighty (wonderful) work. see GREEK for 1410

G1412.text: δυναμόω dunamovw dunamoo {doo-nam-o'-o} from 1411; to enable:--strengthen. see GREEK for 1411

G1413.text: δυνάστης dunavsths dunastes {doo-nas'-tace} from 1410; a ruler or officer:--of great authority, mighty, potentate. see GREEK for 1410

G1414.text: δυνατέω dunatevw dunateo {doo-nat-eh'-o} from 1415; to be efficient (figuratively):--be mighty. see GREEK for 1415

G1415.text: δυνατός dunatovs dunatos {doo-nat-os'} from 1410; powerful or capable (literally or figuratively); neuter possible:--able, could, (that is) mighty (man), possible, power, strong. see GREEK for 1410

G1416.text: δύνω δύω duvnw duvw duno {doo'-no} 或 dumi {doo'-mee} 或 duo {doo'-o} or dumi doo'-mee prolonged forms of an obsolete primary duo doo'-o (to sink) to go "down":--set.

G1417.text: δύο duvo duo {doo'-o} a primary numeral; "two":--both, twain, two.

G1419.text: δυσβάστακτος dusbavstaktos dusbastaktos {doos-bas'-tak-tos} from 1418 and a derivative of 941; oppressive:--grievous to be borne. see GREEK for 1418 see GREEK for 941

G1420.text: δυσεντέριον dusentevrion dusenteria {doos-en-ter-ee'-ah} from 1418 and a comparative of 1787 (meaning a bowel); a "dysentery":--bloody flux. see GREEK for 1418 see GREEK for 1787

G1421.text: δυσερμήνευτος dusermhvneutos dusermeneutos {doos-er-mane'-yoo-tos} from 1418 and a presumed derivative of 2059; difficult of explanation:--hard to be uttered. see GREEK for 1418 see GREEK for 2059

G1422.text: δύσκολος duvskolos duskolos {doo'-kol-os} from 1418 and kolon (food); properly, fastidious about eating (peevish), i.e. (genitive case) impracticable:--hard. see GREEK for 1418

G1423.text: δυσκόλως duskovlws duskolos {doos-kol'-oce} adverb from 1422; impracticably:--hardly. see GREEK for 1422

G1424.text: δυσμή dusmhv dusme {doos-may'} from 1416; the sun-set, i.e. (by implication) the western region:--west. see GREEK for 1416

G1425.text: δυσνόητος dusnovhtos dusnoetos {doos-no'-ay-tos} from 1418 and a derivative of 3539; difficult of perception:--hard to be understood. see GREEK for 1418 see GREEK for 3539

G1426.text: δυσφημία dusfhmiva dusphemia {doos-fay-mee'-ah} from a compound of 1418 and 5345; defamation:--evil report. see GREEK for 1418 see GREEK for 5345

G1427.text: δώδεκα dwvdeka dodeka {do'-dek-ah} from 1417 and 1176; two and ten, i.e. a dozen:--twelve. see GREEK for 1417 see GREEK for 1176

G1428.text: δωδέκατος dwdevkatos dodekatos {do-dek'-at-os} from 1427; twelfth:--twelfth. see GREEK for 1427

G1429.text: δωδεκάφυλον dwdekavfulon dodekaphulon {do-dek-af'-oo-lon} from 1427 and 5443; the commonwealth of Israel:--twelve tribes. see GREEK for 1427 see GREEK for 5443

G1430.text: δῶμα dw'ma doma {do'-mah} from demo (to build); properly, an edifice, i.e. (specially) a roof:--housetop.

G1431.text: δωρεά dwreav dorea {do-reh-ah'} from 1435; a gratuity:--gift. see GREEK for 1435

G1432.text: δωρεάν dwreavn dorean {do-reh-an'} accusative case of 1431 as adverb; gratuitously (literally or figuratively):--without a cause, freely, for naught, in vain. see GREEK for 1431

G1433.text: δωρέομαι dwrevomai doreomai {do-reh'-om-ahee} middle voice from 1435; to bestow gratuitously:--give. see GREEK for 1435

G1434.text: δώρημα dwvrhma dorema {do'-ray-mah} from 1433; a bestowment:--gift. see GREEK for 1433

G1435.text: δῶρον dw'ron doron {do'-ron} a present; specially, a sacrifice:--gift, offering.

G1436.text: ἔα e[a ea {eh'-ah} apparent imperative of 1439; properly, let it be, i.e. (as interjection) aha!:--let alone. see GREEK for 1439

G1437.text: ἐάν ἐάνπερ ejavn ejavnper ean {e-an'} from 1487 and 302; a conditional particle; in case that, provided, etc.; often used in connection with other particles to denote indefiniteness or uncertainty:--before, but, except, (and) if, (if) so, (what-, whither-)soever, though, when (-soever), whether (or), to whom, (who-)so(-ever). See 3361. see GREEK for 1487 see GREEK for 302 see GREEK for 3361

G1439.text: ἐάω ejavw eao {eh-ah'-o} of uncertain affinity; to let be, i.e. permit or leave alone:--commit, leave, let (alone), suffer. See also 1436. see GREEK for 1436

G1440.text: ἑβδομήκοντα eJbdomhvkonta hebdomekonta {heb-dom-ay'-kon-tah} from 1442 and a modified form of 1176; seventy:--seventy, three score and ten. see GREEK for 1442 see GREEK for 1176

G1441.text: ἑβδομηκοντάκις eJbdomhkontavkis hebdomekontakis {heb-dom-ay-kon-tak-is} multiple adverb from 1440; seventy times:--seventy times. see GREEK for 1440

G1442.text: ἕβδομος e&bdomos hebdomos {heb'-dom-os} ordinal from 2033; seventh:--seventh. see GREEK for 2033

G1443.text: Ἔβερ E[ber Eber {eb-er'} of Hebrew origin (5677); Eber, a patriarch:--Eber. see HEBREW for 05677

G1444.text: Ἑβραϊκός ή όν Hebraikos Hebraikos {heb-rah-ee-kos'} from 1443; Hebraic or the Jewish language:--Hebrew. see GREEK for 1443

G1445.text: Ἑβραῖος EJbrai'os Hebraios {heb-rah'-yos} from 1443; a Hebræan (i.e. Hebrew) or Jew:--Hebrew. see GREEK for 1443

G1446.text: Ἑβραΐς EJbrai?s Hebrais {heb-rah-is'} from 1443; the Hebraistic (Hebrew) or Jewish (Chaldee) language:--Hebrew. see GREEK for 1443

G1447.text: Ἑβραϊστί EJbrai>stiv Hebraisti {heb-rah-is-tee'} adverb from 1446; Hebraistically or in the Jewish (Chaldee) language:--in (the) Hebrew (tongue). see GREEK for 1446

G1448.text: ἐγγίζω ejggivzw eggizo {eng-id'-zo} from 1451; to make near, i.e. (reflexively) approach:--approach, be at hand, come (draw) near, be (come, draw) nigh. see GREEK for 1451

G1449.text: ἐγγράφω ejggravfw eggrapho {eng-graf'-o} from 1722 and 1125; to "engrave", i.e. inscribe:--write (in). see GREEK for 1722 see GREEK for 1125

G1450.text: ἔγγυος e[gguos egguos {eng'-goo-os} from 1722 and guion (a limb); pledged (as if articulated by a member), i.e. a bondsman:--surety. see GREEK for 1722

G1451.text: ἐγγύς ejgguvs eggus {eng-goos'} from a primary verb agcho (to squeeze or throttle; akin to the base of 43); near (literally or figuratively, of place or time):--from , at hand, near, nigh (at hand, unto), ready. see GREEK for 43

G1452.text: ἐγγύς ejgguvs egguteron {eng-goo'-ter-on} neuter of the comparative of 1451; nearer:--nearer. see GREEK for 1451

G1453.text: ἐγείρω ejgeivrw egeiro {eg-i'-ro} probably akin to the base of 58 (through the idea of collecting one's faculties); to waken (transitively or intransitively), i.e. rouse (literally, from sleep, from sitting or lying, from disease, from death; or figuratively, from obscurity, inactivity, ruins, nonexistence):--awake, lift (up), raise (again, up), rear up, (a-)rise (again, up), stand, take up. see GREEK for 58

G1454.text: ἔγερσις e[gersis egersis {eg'-er-sis} from 1453; a resurgence (from death):--resurrection. see GREEK for 1453

G1455.text: ἐγκάθετος ejgkavqetos egkathetos {eng-kath'-et-os} from 1722 and a derivative of 2524; subinduced, i.e. surreptitiously suborned as a lier-in-wait:--spy. see GREEK for 1722 see GREEK for 2524

G1456.text: ἐγκαίνια ejgkaivnia egkainia {eng-kah'-ee-nee-ah} neuter plural of a presumed compound from 1722 and 2537; innovatives, i.e. (specially) renewal (of religious services after the Antiochian interruption):--dedication. see GREEK for 1722 see GREEK for 2537

G1457.text: ἐγκαινίζω ejgkainivzw egkainizo {eng-kahee-nid'-zo} from 1456; to renew, i.e. inaugurate:--consecrate, dedicate. see GREEK for 1456

G1458.text: ἐγκαλέω ejgkalevw egkaleo {eng-kal-eh'-o} from 1722 and 2564; to call in (as a debt or demand), i.e. bring to account (charge, criminate, etc.):--accuse, call in question, implead, lay to the charge. see GREEK for 1722 see GREEK for 2564

G1459.text: ἐγκαταλείπω ejgkataleivpw egkataleipo {eng-kat-al-i'-po} from 1722 and 2641; to leave behind in some place, i.e. (in a good sense) let remain over, or (in a bad sense) to desert:--forsake, leave. see GREEK for 1722 see GREEK for 2641

G1460.text: ἐγκατοικέω ejgkatoikevw egkatoikeo {eng-kat-oy-keh'-o} from 1722 and 2730; to settle down in a place, i.e. reside:--dwell among. see GREEK for 1722 see GREEK for 2730

G1461.text: ἐγκεντρίζω ejgkentrivzw egkentrizo {eng-ken-trid'-zo} from 1722 and a derivative of 2759; to prick in, i.e. ingraft:--graff in(-to). see GREEK for 1722 see GREEK for 2759

G1462.text: ἔγκλημα e[gklhma egklema {eng'-klay-mah} from 1458; an accusation, i.e. offence alleged:--crime laid against, laid to charge. see GREEK for 1458

G1463.text: ἐγκομβόομαι ejgkombovomai egkomboomai {eng-kom-bo'-om-ahee} middle voice from 1722 and komboo (to gird); to engirdle oneself (for labor), i.e. figuratively (the apron as being a badge of servitude) to wear (in token of mutual deference):--be clothed with. see GREEK for 1722

G1464.text: ἐγκοπή ejgkophv egkope {eng-kop-ay'} from 1465; a hindrance:--X hinder. see GREEK for 1465

G1465.text: ἐγκόπτω ejgkovptw egkopto {eng-kop'-to} from 1722 and 2875; to cut into, i.e. (figuratively) impede, detain:--hinder, be tedious unto. see GREEK for 1722 see GREEK for 2875

G1466.text: ἐγκράτεια ejgkravteia egkrateia {eng-krat'-i-ah} from 1468; self-control (especially continence):--temperance. see GREEK for 1468

G1467.text: ἐγκρατεύομαι ejgkrateuvomai egkrateuomai {eng-krat-yoo'-om-ahee} middle voice from 1468; to exercise self-restraint (in diet and chastity):--can(-not) contain, be temperate. see GREEK for 1468

G1468.text: ἐγκρατής ejgkrathvs egkrates {eng-krat-ace'} from 1722 and 2904; strong in a thing (masterful), i.e. (figuratively and reflexively) self-controlled (in appetite, etc.):--temperate. see GREEK for 1722 see GREEK for 2904

G1469.text: ἐγκρίνω ejgkrivnw egkrino {eng-kree'-no} from 1722 and 2919; to judge in, i.e. count among:--make of the number. see GREEK for 1722 see GREEK for 2919

G1470.text: ἐγκρύπτω ejgkruvptw ekgrupto {eng-kroop'-to} from 1722 and 2928; to conceal in, i.e. incorporate with:--hid in. see GREEK for 1722 see GREEK for 2928

G1471.text: ἔγκυος e[gkuos egkuos {eng'-koo-os} from 1722 and the base of 2949; swelling inside, i.e. pregnant:--great with child. see GREEK for 1722 see GREEK for 2949

G1472.text: ἐγχρίω ejgcrivw egchrio {eng-khree'-o} from 1722 and 5548; to rub in (oil), i.e. besmear:--anoint. see GREEK for 1722 see GREEK for 5548

G1473.text: ἐγώ ejgwv ego {eg-o'} a primary pronoun of the first person I (only expressed when emphatic):--I, me. For the other cases and the plural see 1691, 1698, 1700, 2248, 2249, 2254, 2257, etc. see GREEK for 1691 see GREEK for 1698 see GREEK for 1700 see GREEK for 2248 see GREEK for 2249 see GREEK for 2254 see GREEK for 2257

G1474.text: ἐδαφίζω ejdafivzw edaphizo {ed-af-id'-zo} from 1475; to raze:--lay even with the ground. see GREEK for 1475

G1475.text: ἔδαφος e[dafos edaphos {ed'-af-os} from the base of 1476; a basis (bottom), i.e. the soil:--ground. see GREEK for 1476

G1476.text: ἑδραῖος eJdrai'os hedraios {hed-rah'-yos} from a derivative of hezomai (to sit); sedentary, i.e. (by implication) immovable:--settled, stedfast.

G1477.text: ἑδραίωμα eJdraivwma hedraioma {hed-rah'-yo-mah} from a derivative of 1476; a support, i.e. (figuratively) basis:--ground. see GREEK for 1476

G1478.text: Ἑζεκίας EJzekivas Ezekias {ed-zek-ee'-as} of Hebrew origin (2396); Ezekias (i.e. Hezekeiah), an Israelite:--Ezekias. see HEBREW for 02396

G1479.text: θρησκεία qrhskeiva ethelothreskeia {eth-el-oth-race-ki'-ah} from 2309 and 2356; voluntary (arbitrary and unwarranted) piety, i.e. sanctimony:--will worship. see GREEK for 2309 see GREEK for 2356

G1480.text: ἐθίζω ejqivzw ethizo {eth-id'-zo} from 1485; to accustom, i.e. (neuter passive participle) customary:--custom. see GREEK for 1485

G1481.text: ἐθνάρχης ejqnavrchs ethnarches {eth-nar'-khace} from 1484 and 746; the governor (not king) of a district:--ethnarch. see GREEK for 1484 see GREEK for 746

G1482.text: ἐθνικός ejqnikovs ethnikos {eth-nee-kos'} from 1484; national ("ethnic"), i.e. (specially) a Gentile:--heathen (man). see GREEK for 1484

G1483.text: ἐθνικῶς ejqnikw's ethnikos {eth-nee-koce'} adverb from 1482; as a Gentile:--after the manner of Gentiles. see GREEK for 1482

G1484.text: ἔθνος e[qnos ethnos {eth'-nos} probably from 1486; a race (as of the same habit), i.e. a tribe; specially, a foreign (non-Jewish) one (usually, by implication, pagan):--Gentile, heathen, nation, people. see GREEK for 1486

G1485.text: ἔθος e[qos ethos {eth'-os} from 1486; a usage (prescribed by habit or law):--custom, manner, be wont. see GREEK for 1486

G1486.text: εἴωθα ei[wqa etho {eth'-o} a primary verb; to be used (by habit or conventionality); neuter perfect participle usage:--be custom (manner, wont).

G1487.text: εἰ eij ei {i} a primary particle of conditionality; if, whether, that, etc.:--forasmuch as, if, that, (al-)though, whether. Often used in connection or composition with other particles, especially as in 1489, 1490, 1499, 1508, 1509, 1512, 1513, 1536, 1537. See also 1437. see GREEK for 1489 see GREEK for 1490 see GREEK for 1499 see GREEK for 1508 see GREEK for 1509 see GREEK for 1512 see GREEK for 1513 see GREEK for 1536 see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1437

G1488.text: εἰμί εἰ eijmiv eij ei {i} second person singular present of 1510; thou art:--art, be. see GREEK for 1510

G1489.text: εἰ eij eige {i'-gheh} from 1487 and 1065; if indeed, seeing that, unless, (with negative) otherwise:--if (so be that, yet). see GREEK for 1487 see GREEK for 1065

G1490.text: μήγε mhvge ei de me(ge) {i deh may'-(gheh)} from 1487, 1161, and 3361 (sometimes with 1065 added); but if not:--(or) else, if (not, otherwise), otherwise. see GREEK for 1487 see GREEK for 1161 see GREEK for 3361 see GREEK for 1065

G1491.text: εἶδος ei\\dos eidos {i'-dos} from 1492; a view, i.e. form (literally or figuratively):--appearance, fashion, shape, sight. see GREEK for 1492

G1492.text: οἶδα οιδα ὁράω oi\da oida oJravw eido {i'-do} 或 oida {oy'-da} a primary verb; used only in certain past tenses, the others being borrowed from the equivalent 3700 and 3708; properly, to see (literally or figuratively); by implication, (in the perfect tense only) to know:--be aware, behold, X can (+ not tell), consider, (have) know(-ledge), look (on), perceive, see, be sure, tell, understand, wish, wot. Compare 3700. see GREEK for 3700 see GREEK for 3708 see GREEK for 3700

G1493.text: εἰδωλεῖον eijdwlei'on eidoleion {i-do-li'-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of 1497; an image-fane:--idol's temple. see GREEK for 1497

G1494.text: εἰδωλόθυτος eijdwlovqutos eidolothuton {i-do-loth'-oo-ton} neuter of a compound of 1497 and a presumed derivative of 2380; an image-sacrifice, i.e. part of an idolatrous offering:--(meat, thing that is) offered (in sacrifice, sacrificed) to (unto) idols. see GREEK for 1497 see GREEK for 2380

G1495.text: εἰδωλολάτρία eijdwlolavtriva eidololatreia {i-do-lol-at-ri'-ah} from 1497 and 2999; image-worship (literally or figuratively):--idolatry. see GREEK for 1497 see GREEK for 2999

G1496.text: εἰδωλολάτρης eijdwlolavtrhs eidololatres {i-do-lol-at'-race} from 1497 and the base of 3000; an image- (servant or) worshipper (literally or figuratively):--idolater. see GREEK for 1497 see GREEK for 3000

G1497.text: εἴδωλον ei[dwlon eidolon {i'-do-lon} from 1491; an image (i.e. for worship); by implication, a heathen god, or (plural) the worship of such:--idol. see GREEK for 1491

G1498.text: εἰμί eijmiv eien {i'-ane} optative (i.e. English subjunctive) present of 1510 (including the other person); might (could, would, or should) be:--mean, + perish, should be, was, were. see GREEK for 1510

G1499.text: εἰ ei kai ei kai {i kahee} from 1487 and 2532; if also (or even):--if (that), though. see GREEK for 1487 see GREEK for 2532

G1500.text: εἰκῇ eijkh'/ eike {i-kay'} probably from 1502 (through the idea of failure); idly, i.e. without reason (or effect):--without a cause, (in) vain(-ly). see GREEK for 1502

G1501.text: εἴκοσι ei[kosi eikosi {i'-kos-ee} of uncertain affinity; a score:--twenty.

G1502.text: εἴκω ei[kw eiko {i'-ko} apparently a primary verb; properly, to be weak, i.e. yield:--give place.

G1503.text: ἔοικα e[oika eiko {i'-ko} apparently a primary verb (perhaps akin to 1502 through the idea of faintness as a copy); to resemble:--be like. see GREEK for 1502

G1504.text: εἰκών eijkwvn eikon {i-kone'} from 1503; a likeness, i.e. (literally) statue, profile, or (figuratively) representation, resemblance:--image. see GREEK for 1503

G1505.text: εἰλικρίνεια eijlikrivneia heilikrineia {i-lik-ree'-ni-ah} from 1506; clearness, i.e. (by implication) purity (figuratively):--sincerity. see GREEK for 1506

G1506.text: εἰλικρινής eijlikrinhvs heilikrines {i-lik-ree-nace'} from heile (the sun's ray) and 2919; judged by sunlight, i.e. tested as genuine (figuratively):--pure, sincere. see GREEK for 2919

G1507.text: εἱλίσσω heilisso heilisso {hi-lis'-so} a prolonged form of a primary but defective verb heilo (of the same meaning); to coil or wrap:--roll together. See also 1667. see GREEK for 1667

G1508.text: εἰ ei me ei me {i may} from 1487 and 3361; if not:--but, except (that), if not, more than, save (only) that, saving, till. see GREEK for 1487 see GREEK for 3361

G1509.text: εἰ ei me ti ei me ti {i may tee} from 1508 and the neuter of 5100; if not somewhat:--except. see GREEK for 1508 see GREEK for 5100

G1510.text: εἰμί eijmiv eimi {i-mee'} the first person singular present indicative; a prolonged form of a primary and defective verb; I exist (used only when emphatic):--am, have been, X it is I, was. See also 1488, 1498, 1511, 1527, 2258, 2071, 2070, 2075, 2076, 2771, 2468, 5600. see GREEK for 1488 see GREEK for 1498 see GREEK for 1511 see GREEK for 1527 see GREEK for 2258 see GREEK for 2071 see GREEK for 2070 see GREEK for 2075 see GREEK for 2076 see GREEK for 2771 see GREEK for 2468 see GREEK for 5600

G1511.text: εἰμί ἐιμί eijmiv ejimiv einai {i'-nahee} present infinitive from 1510; to exist:--am, was. come, is, X lust after, X please well, there is, to be, was. see GREEK for 1510

G1512.text: εἴπερ ei[per ei per {i per} from 1487 and 4007; if perhaps:--if so be (that), seeing, though. see GREEK for 1487 see GREEK for 4007

G1513.text: εἴ ei pos ei pos {i poce} from 1487 and 4458; if somehow:--if by any means. see GREEK for 1487 see GREEK for 4458

G1514.text: εἰρηνεύω eijrhneuvw eireneuo {i-rane-yoo'-o} from 1515; to be (act) peaceful:--be at (have, live in) peace, live peaceably. see GREEK for 1515

G1515.text: εἰρήνη eijrhvnh eirene {i-ray'-nay} probably from a primary verb eiro (to join); peace (literally or figuratively); by implication, prosperity:--one, peace, quietness, rest, + set at one again.

G1516.text: εἰρηνικός eijrhnikovs eirenikos {i-ray-nee-kos'} from 1515; pacific; by implication, salutary:--peaceable. see GREEK for 1515

G1517.text: εἰρηνοποιέω eijrhnopoievw eirenopoieo {i-ray-nop-oy-eh'-o} from 1518; to be a peace-maker, i.e. (figuratively) to harmonize:--make peace. see GREEK for 1518

G1518.text: εἰρηνοποιός eijrhnopoiovs eirenopoios {i-ray-nop-oy-os'} from 1518 and 4160; pacificatory, i.e. (subjectively) peaceable:--peacemaker. see GREEK for 1518 see GREEK for 4160

G1519.text: εἰς eijs eis {ice} a primary preposition; to or into (indicating the point reached or entered), of place, time, or (figuratively) purpose (result, etc.); also in adverbial phrases:--(abundant-)ly, against, among, as, at, (back-)ward, before, by, concerning, + continual, + far more exceeding, for (intent, purpose), fore, + forth, in (among, at, unto, -so much that, -to), to the intent that, + of one mind, + never, of, (up-)on, + perish, + set at one again, (so) that, therefore(-unto), throughout, til, to (be, the end, -ward), (here-)until(-to), ...ward, (where-)fore, with. Often used in composition with the same general import, but only with verbs (etc.) expressing motion (literally or figuratively).

G1520.text: εἷς ei|s heis {hice} (including the neuter (etc.) hen); a primary numeral; one:--a(-n, -ny, certain), + abundantly, man, one (another), only, other, some. See also 1527, 3367, 3391, 3762. see GREEK for 1527 see GREEK for 3367 see GREEK for 3391 see GREEK for 3762

G1521.text: εἰσάγω eijsavgw eisago {ice-ag'-o} from 1519 and 71; to introduce (literally or figuratively):--bring in(-to), (+ was to) lead into. see GREEK for 1519 see GREEK for 71

G1522.text: εἰσακούω eijsakouvw eisakouo {ice-ak-oo'-o} from 1519 and 191; to listen to:--hear. see GREEK for 1519 see GREEK for 191

G1523.text: εἰσδέχομαι eijsdevcomai eisdechomai {ice-dekh'-om-ahee} from 1519 and 1209; to take into one's favor:--receive. see GREEK for 1519 see GREEK for 1209

G1524.text: εἴσειμι ei[seimi eiseimi {ice'-i-mee} from 1519 and eimi (to go); to enter:--enter (go) into. see GREEK for 1519

G1525.text: εἰσέρχομαι eijsevrcomai eiserchomai {ice-er'-khom-ahee} from 1519 and 2064; to enter (literally or figuratively):--X arise, come (in, into), enter in(-to), go in (through). see GREEK for 1519 see GREEK for 2064

G1526.text: εἰμί eijmiv eisi {i-see'} 3d person plural present indicative of 1510; they are:--agree, are, be, dure, X is, were. see GREEK for 1510

G1527.text: εἷς heis kath heis heis kath heis {hice kath hice} from 1520 repeated with 2596 inserted; severally:--one by one. see GREEK for 1520 see GREEK for 2596

G1528.text: εἰσκαλέομαι eijskalevomai eiskaleo {ice-kal-eh'-o} from 1519 and 2564; to invite in:--call in. see GREEK for 1519 see GREEK for 2564

G1529.text: εἴσοδος ei[sodos eisodos {ice'-od-os} from 1519 and 3598; an entrance (literally or figuratively):--coming, enter(-ing) in (to). see GREEK for 1519 see GREEK for 3598

G1530.text: εἰσπηδάω eijsphdavw eispedao {ice-pay-dah'-o} from 1519 and pedao (to leap); to rush in:--run (spring) in. see GREEK for 1519

G1531.text: εἰσπορεύομαι eijsporeuvomai eisporeuomai {ice-por-yoo'-om-ahee} from 1519 and 4198; to enter (literally or figuratively):--come (enter) in, go into. see GREEK for 1519 see GREEK for 4198

G1532.text: εἰστρέχω eijstrevcw eistrecho {ice-trekh'-o} from 1519 and 5143; to hasten inward:--run in. see GREEK for 1519 see GREEK for 5143

G1533.text: εἰσφέρω eijsfevrw eisphero {ice-fer'-o} from 1519 and 5342; to carry inward (literally or figuratively):--bring (in), lead into. see GREEK for 1519 see GREEK for 5342

G1534.text: εἶτα εἶτεν ei\\ta ei\\ten eita {i'-tah} of uncertain affinity; a particle of succession (in time or logical enumeration), then, moreover:--after that(-ward), furthermore, then. See also 1899. see GREEK for 1899

G1535.text: εἴτε ei[te eite {i'-teh} from 1487 and 5037; if too:--if, or, whether. see GREEK for 1487 see GREEK for 5037

G1536.text: τίς ei tis {i tis} from 1487 and 5100; if any:--he that, if a(-ny) man('s thing, from any, ought), whether any, whosoever. see GREEK for 1487 see GREEK for 5100

G1537.text: ἐκ ejk ek {ek} 或 母音前用 ex {ex} or ex ex a primary preposition denoting origin (the point whence action or motion proceeds), from, out (of place, time, or cause; literal or figurative; direct or remote):--after, among, X are, at, betwixt(-yond), by (the means of), exceedingly, (+ abundantly above), for(- th), from (among, forth, up), + grudgingly, + heartily, X heavenly, X hereby, + very highly, in, ...ly, (because, by reason) of, off (from), on, out among (from, of), over, since, X thenceforth, through, X unto, X vehemently, with(-out). Often used in composition, with the same general import; often of completion.

G1538.text: ἕκαστος e&kastos hekastos {hek'-as-tos} as if a superlative of hekas (afar); each or every:--any, both, each (one), every (man, one, woman), particularly.

G1539.text: ἑκάστοτε eJkavstote hekastote {hek-as'-tot-eh} as if from 1538 and 5119; at every time:--always. see GREEK for 1538 see GREEK for 5119

G1540.text: ἑκατόν eJkatovn hekaton {hek-at-on'} of uncertain affinity; a hundred:--hundred.

G1541.text: ἑκατονταετής eJkatontaethvs hekatontaetes {hek-at-on-tah-et'-ace} from 1540 and 2094; centenarian:--hundred years old. see GREEK for 1540 see GREEK for 2094

G1542.text: ἑκατονταπλασίων eJkatontaplasivwn hekatontaplasion {hek-at-on-ta-plah-sec'-own} from 1540 and a presumed derivative of 4111; a hundred times:--hundredfold. see GREEK for 1540 see GREEK for 4111

G1543.text: ἑκατοντάρχης ἑκατοντάρχος eJkatontavrchs eJkatontavrcos hekatontarches {hek-at-on-tar'-khace} or hekatontarchos hek-at-on'-tar-khos from 1540 and 757; the captain of one hundred men:--centurion. see GREEK for 1540 see GREEK for 757

G1544.text: ἐκβάλλω ejkbavllw ekballo {ek-bal'-lo} from 1537 and 906; to eject (literally or figuratively):--bring forth, cast (forth, out), drive (out), expel, leave, pluck (pull, take, thrust) out, put forth (out), send away (forth, out). see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 906

G1545.text: ἔκβασις e[kbasis ekbasis {ek'-bas-is} from a compound of 1537 and the base of 939 (meaning to go out); an exit (literally or figuratively):--end, way to escape. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 939

G1546.text: ἐκβολή ejkbolhv ekbole {ek-bol-ay'} from 1544; ejection, i.e. (specially) a throwing overboard of the cargo:--+ lighten the ship. see GREEK for 1544

G1547.text: γαμίζω gamivzw ekgamizo {ek-gam-id'-zo} from 1537 and a form of 1061 (compare 1548); to marry off a daughter:--give in marriage. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1061 see GREEK for 1548

G1548.text: ἐκγαμίσκω ekgamisko ekgamisko {ek-gam-is'-ko} from 1537 and 1061; the same as 1547:--give in marriage. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1061

G1549.text: ἔκγονον e[kgonon ekgonon {ek'-gon-on} neuter of a derivative of a compound of 1537 and 1096; a descendant, i.e. (specially) grandchild:--nephew. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1096

G1550.text: ἐκδαπανάομαι ejkdapanavomai ekdapanao {ek-dap-an-ah'-o} from 1537 and 1159; to expend (wholly), i.e. (figuratively) exhaust:--spend. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1159

G1551.text: ἐκδέχομαι ejkdevcomai ekdechomai {ek-dekh'-om-ahee} from 1537 and 1209; to accept from some source, i.e. (by implication) to await:--expect, look (tarry) for, wait (for). see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1209

G1552.text: ἔκδηλος e[kdhlos ekdelos {ek'-day-los} from 1537 and 1212; wholly evident:--manifest. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1212

G1553.text: ἐκδημέω ejkdhmevw ekdemeo {ek-day-meh'-o} from a compound of 1537 and 1218; to emigrate, i.e. (figuratively) vacate or quit:--be absent. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1218

G1554.text: ἐκδίδομαι ejkdivdomai ekdidomi {ek-did-o'-mee} from 1537 and 1325; to give forth, i.e. (specially) to lease:--let forth (out). see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1325

G1555.text: ἐκδιηγέομαι ejkdihgevomai ekdiegeomai {ek-dee-ayg-eh'-om-ahee} from 1537 and a compound of 1223 and 2233; to narrate through wholly:--declare. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1223 see GREEK for 2233

G1556.text: ἐκδικέω ejkdikevw ekdikeo {ek-dik-eh'-o} from 1558; to vindicate, retaliate, punish:--a (re-)venge. see GREEK for 1558

G1557.text: ἐκδίκησις ejkdivkhsis ekdikesis {ek-dik'-ay-sis} from 1556; vindication, retribution:--(a-, re-)venge(-ance), punishment. see GREEK for 1556

G1558.text: ἔκδικος e[kdikos ekdikos {ek'-dik-os} from 1537 and 1349; carrying justice out, i.e. a punisher:--a (re-)venger. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1349

G1559.text: ἐκδιώκω ejkdiwvkw ekdioko {ek-dee-o'-ko} from 1537 and 1377; to pursue out, i.e. expel or persecute implacably:--persecute. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1377

G1560.text: ἔκδοτος e[kdotos ekdotos {ek'-dot-os} from 1537 and a derivative of 1325; given out or over, i.e. surrendered:--delivered. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1325

G1561.text: ἐκδοχή ejkdochv ekdoche {ek-dokh-ay'} from 1551; expectation:--looking foreign see GREEK for 1551

G1562.text: ἐκδύω ejkduvw ekduo {ek-doo'-o} from 1537 and the base of 1416; to cause to sink out of, i.e. (specially as of clothing) to divest:--strip, take off from, unclothe. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1416

G1563.text: ἐκεῖ ejkei' ekei {ek-i'} of uncertain affinity; there; by extension, thither:--there, thither(-ward), (to) yonder (place).

G1564.text: ἐκεῖθεν ejkei'qen ekeithen {ek-i'-then} from 1563; thence:--from that place, (from) thence, there. see GREEK for 1563

G1565.text: ἐκεῖνος ejkei'nos ekeinos {ek-i'-nos} from 1563; that one (or (neuter) thing); often intensified by the article prefixed:--he, it, the other (same), selfsame, that (same, very), X their, X them, they, this, those. See also 3778. see GREEK for 1563 see GREEK for 3778

G1566.text: ἐκεῖσε ejkei'se ekeise {ek-i'-seh} from 1563; thither:--there. see GREEK for 1563

G1567.text: ἐκζητέω ejkzhtevw ekzeteo {ek-zay-teh'-o} from 1537 and 2212; to search out, i.e. (figuratively)investigate, crave, demand, (by Hebraism) worship:--en- (re-)quire, seek after (carefully, diligently). see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2212

G1568.text: ἐκθαμβεω ejkqambew ekthambeo {ek-tham-beh'-o} from 1569; to astonish utterly:--affright, greatly (sore) amaze. see GREEK for 1569

G1569.text: ἔκθαμβος e[kqambos ekthambos {ek'-tham-bos} from 1537 and 2285; utterly astounded:--greatly wondering. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2285

G1570.text: ἔκθετος e[kqetos ekthetos {ek'-thet-os} from 1537 and a derivative of 5087; put out, i.e. exposed to perish:--cast out. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 5087

G1571.text: ἐκκαθαίρω ejkkaqaivrw ekkathairo {ek-kath-ah'-ee-ro} from 1537 and 2508; to cleanse thoroughly:--purge (out). see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2508

G1572.text: ἐκκαίομαι ejkkaivomai ekkaio {ek-kah'-yo} from 1537 and 2545; to inflame deeply:--burn. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2545

G1573.text: ἐγκακέω ejgkakevw ekkakeo {ek-kak-eh'-o} or egkakeo {eng-kak-eh'-o} from 1537 and 2556; to be (bad or) weak, i.e. (by implication) to fail (in heart):--faint, be weary. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2556

G1574.text: ἐκκεντέω ejkkentevw ekkenteo {ek-ken-teh'-o} from 1537 and the base of 2759; to transfix:--pierce. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2759

G1575.text: ἐκκλάω ejkklavw ekklao {ek-klah'-o} from 1537 and 2806; to exscind:--break off. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2806

G1576.text: ἐκκλείω ejkkleivw ekkleio {ek-kli'-o} from 1537 and 2808; to shut out (literally or figuratively):--exclude. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2808

G1577.text: ἐκκλησία ejkklhsiva ekklesia {ek-klay-see'-ah} from a compound of 1537 and a derivative of 2564; a calling out, i.e. (concretely) a popular meeting, especially a religious congregation (Jewish synagogue, or Christian community of members on earth or saints in heaven or both):--assembly, church. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2564

G1578.text: ἐκκλίνω ejkklivnw ekklino {ek-klee'-no} from 1537 and 2827; to deviate, i.e. (absolutely) to shun (literally or figuratively), or (relatively) to decline (from piety):--avoid, eschew, go out of the way. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2827

G1579.text: ἐκκολυμβάω ejkkolumbavw ekkolumbao {ek-kol-oom-bah'-o} from 1537 and 2860; to escape by swimming:--swim out. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2860

G1580.text: ἐκκομίζω ejkkomivzw ekkomizo {ek-kom-id'-zo} from 1537 and 2865; to bear forth (to burial):--carry out. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2865

G1581.text: ἐκκόπτω ejkkovptw ekkopto {ek-kop'-to} from 1537 and 2875; to exscind; figuratively, to frustrate:--cut down (off, out), hew down, hinder. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2875

G1582.text: ἐκκρεμάννυμι ejkkremavnnumi ekkremamai {ek-krem'-am-ahee} middle voice from 1537 and 2910; to hang upon the lips of a speaker, i.e. listen closely:--be very attentive. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2910

G1583.text: ἐκλαλέω ejklalevw eklaleo {ek-lal-eh'-o} from 1537 and 2980; to divulge:--tell. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2980

G1584.text: ἐκλάμπω ejklavmpw eklampo {ek-lam'-po} from 1537 and 2989; to be resplendent:--shine forth. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2989

G1585.text: ἐκλέγομαι ejklevgomai eklanthanomai {ek-lan-than'-om-ahee} middle voice from 1537 and 2990; to be utterly oblivious of:--forget. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 2990

G1586.text: ἐκλέγω ejklevgw eklegomai {ek-leg'-om-ahee} middle voice from 1537 and 3004 (in its primary sense); to select:--make choice, choose (out), chosen. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 3004

G1587.text: ἐκλείπω ejkleivpw ekleipo {ek-li'-po} from 1537 and 3007; to omit, i.e. (by implication) cease (die):--fail. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 3007

G1588.text: ἐκλεκτός ejklektovs eklektos {ek-lek-tos'} from 1586; select; by implication, favorite:--chosen, elect. see GREEK for 1586

G1589.text: ἐκλογή ejkloghv ekloge {ek-log-ay'} from 1586; (divine) selection (abstractly or concretely):--chosen, election. see GREEK for 1586

G1590.text: ἐκλύω ejkluvw ekluo {ek-loo'-o} from 1537 and 3089; to relax (literally or figuratively):--faint. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 3089

G1591.text: ἐκμάσσω ejkmavssw ekmasso {ek-mas'-so} from 1537 and the base of 3145; to knead out, i.e. (by analogy) to wipe dry:--wipe. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 3145

G1592.text: ἐκμυκτηρίζω ejkmukthrivzw ekmukterizo {ek-mook-ter-id'-zo} from 1537 and 3456; to sneer outright at:--deride. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 3456

G1593.text: ἐκνεύω ejkneuvw ekneuo {ek-nyoo'-o} from 1537 and 3506; (by analogy) to slip off, i.e. quietly withdraw:--convey self away. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 3506

G1594.text: ἐκνήφω ejknhvfw eknepho {ek-nay'-fo} from 1537 and 3525; (figuratively) to rouse (oneself) out of stupor:--awake. see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 3525

G1614.text: ἐκτείνω ejkteivnw ekteino {ek-ti'-no} from 1537 and teino (to stretch); to extend:--cast, put forth, stretch forth (out). see GREEK for 1537

G1942.text: ἐπικάλυμμα ejpikavlumma epikaluma {ep-ee-kal'-oo-mah} from 1943; a covering, i.e. (figuratively) pretext:--cloke. see GREEK for 1943

G1943.text: ἐπικαλύπτω ejpikaluvptw epikalupto {ep-ee-kal-oop'-to} from 1909 and 2572; to conceal, i.e. (figuratively) forgive:--cover. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 2572

G1944.text: ἐπικατάρατος ejpikatavratos epikataratos {ep-ee-kat-ar'-at-os} from 1909 and a derivative of 2672; imprecated, i.e. execrable:--accursed. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 2672

G1945.text: ἐπίκειμαι ejpivkeimai epikeimai {ep-ik'-i-mahee} from 1909 and 2749; to rest upon (literally or figuratively):--impose, be instant, (be) laid (there-, up-)on, (when) lay (on), lie (on), press upon. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 2749

G1946.text: Ἐπικούρειος Ejpikouvreios Epikoureios {ep-ee-koo'-ri-os} from Epikouros (compare 1947) (a noted philosopher); an Epicurean or follower of Epicurus:--Epicurean. see GREEK for 1947

G1947.text: ἐπικουρία ejpikouriva epikouria {ep-ee-koo-ree'-ah} from a compound of 1909 and a (prolonged) form of the base of 2877 (in the sense of servant); assistance:--help. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 2877

G1948.text: ἐπικρίνω ejpikrivnw epikrino {ep-ee-kree'-no} from 1909 and 2919; to adjudge:--give sentence. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 2919

G1949.text: ἐπιλαμβάνομαι ejpilambavnomai epilambanomai {ep-ee-lam-ban'-om-ahee} middle voice from 1909 and 2983; to seize (for help, injury, attainment, or any other purpose; literally or figuratively):--catch, lay hold (up-)on, take (by, hold of, on). see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 2983

G1950.text: ἐπιλανθάνομαι ejpilanqavnomai epilanthanomai {ep-ee-lan-than'-om-ahee} middle voice from 1909 and 2990; to lose out of mind; by implication, to neglect:--(be) forget(-ful of). see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 2990

G1951.text: ἐπιλέγω ejpilevgw epilegomai {ep-ee-leg'-om-ahee} middle voice from 1909 and 3004; to surname, select:--call, choose. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3004

G1952.text: ἐπιλείπω ejpileivpw epileipo {ep-ee-li'-po} from 1909 and 3007; to leave upon, i.e. (figuratively) to be insufficient for:--fail. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3007

G1953.text: ἐπιλησμονή ejpilhsmonhv epilesmone {ep-ee-lace-mon-ay'} from a derivative of 1950; negligence:--X forgetful. see GREEK for 1950

G1954.text: ἐπίλοιπος ejpivloipos epiloipos {ep-il'-oy-pos} from 1909 and 3062; left over, i.e. remaining:--rest. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3062

G1955.text: ἐπίλυσις ejpivlusis epilusis {ep-il'-oo-sis} from 1956; explanation, i.e. application:--interpretation. see GREEK for 1956

G1956.text: ἐπιλύω ejpiluvw epiluo {ep-ee-loo'-o} from 1909 and 3089; to solve further, i.e. (figuratively) to explain, decide:--determine, expound. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3089

G1957.text: ἐπιμαρτυρέω ejpimarturevw epimartureo {ep-ee-mar-too-reh'-o} from 1909 and 3140; to attest further, i.e. corroborate:--testify. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3140

G1958.text: ἐπιμέλεια ejpimevleia epimeleia {ep-ee-mel'-i-ah} from 1959; carefulness, i.e. kind attention (hospitality):--+ refresh self. see GREEK for 1959

G1959.text: ἐπιμελέομαι ejpimelevomai epimeleomai {ep-ee-mel-eh'-om-ahee} middle voice from 1909 and the same as 3199; to care for (physically or otherwise):--take care of. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3199

G1960.text: ἐπιμελῶς ejpimelw's epimelos {ep-ee-mel-oce'} adverb from a derivative of 1959; carefully:--diligently. see GREEK for 1959

G1961.text: ἐπιμένω ejpimevnw epimeno {ep-ee-men'-o} from 1909 and 3306; to stay over, i.e. remain (figuratively, persevere):--abide (in), continue (in), tarry. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3306

G1962.text: ἐπινεύω ejpineuvw epineuo {ep-een-yoo'-o} from 1909 and 3506; to nod at, i.e. (by implication) to assent:--consent. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3506

G1963.text: ἐπίνοια ejpivnoia epinoia {ep-in'-oy-ah} from 1909 and 3563; attention of the mind, i.e. (by implication) purpose:--thought. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3563

G1964.text: ἐπιορκέω ejpiorkevw epiorkeo {ep-ee-or-keh'-o} from 1965; to commit perjury:--forswear self. see GREEK for 1965

G1965.text: ἐπίορκος ejpivorkos epiorkos {ep-ee'-or-kos} from 1909 and 3727; on oath, i.e. (falsely) a forswearer:--perjured person. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3727

G1966.text: ἔπειμι e[peimi epiousa {ep-ee-oo'-sah} feminine singular participle of a comparative of 1909 and heimi (to go); supervening, i.e. (2250 or 3571 being expressed or implied) the ensuing day or night:--following, next. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 2250 see GREEK for 3571

G1967.text: ἐπιούσιος ejpiouvsios epiousios {ep-ee-oo'-see-os} perhaps from the same as 1966; tomorrow's; but more probably from 1909 and a derivative of the present participle feminine of 1510; for subsistence, i.e. needful:--daily. see GREEK for 1966 see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 1510

G1968.text: ἐπιπίπτω ejpipivptw epipipto {ep-ee-pip'-to} from 1909 and 4098; to embrace (with affection) or seize (with more or less violence; literally or figuratively):--fall into (on, upon) lie on, press upon. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4098

G1969.text: ἐπιπλήσσω ejpiplhvssw epiplesso {ep-ee-place'-so} from 1909 and 4141; to chastise, i.e. (with words) to upbraid:--rebuke. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4141

G1970.text: ἐπιβοάω epiboao epipnigo {ep-ee-pnee'-go} from 1909 and 4155; to throttle upon, i.e. (figuratively) overgrow:--choke. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4155

G1971.text: ἐπιποθέω ejpipoqevw epipotheo {ep-ee-poth-eh'-o} from 1909 and potheo (to yearn); to dote upon, i.e. intensely crave possession (lawfully or wrongfully):--(earnestly) desire (greatly), (greatly) long (after), lust. see GREEK for 1909

G1972.text: ἐπιπόθησις ejpipovqhsis epipothesis {ep-ee-poth'-ay-sis} from 1971; a longing for:--earnest (vehement) desire. see GREEK for 1971

G1973.text: ἐπιπόθητος ejpipovqhtos epipothetos {ep-ee-poth'-ay-tos} from 1909 and a derivative of the latter part of 1971; yearned upon, i.e. greatly loved:--longed foreign see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 1971

G1974.text: ἐπιποθία ejpipoqiva epipothia {ep-ee-poth-ee'-ah} from 1971; intense longing:--great desire. see GREEK for 1971

G1975.text: ἐπιπορεύομαι ejpiporeuvomai epiporeuomai {ep-ee-por-yoo'-om-ahee} from 1909 and 4198; to journey further, i.e. travel on (reach):--come. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4198

G1976.text: ἐπιράπτω ejpiravptw epirrhapto {ep-ir-hrap'-to} from 1909 and the base of 4476; to stitch upon, i.e. fasten with the needle:--sew on. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4476

G1977.text: ἐπιρίπτω ejpirivptw epirrhipto {ep-ir-hrip'-to} from 1909 and 4496; to throw upon (literally or figuratively):--cast upon. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4496

G1978.text: ἐπίσημος ejpivshmos episemos {ep-is'-ay-mos} from 1909 and some form of the base of 4591; remarkable, i.e. (figuratively) eminent:--notable, of note. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4591

G1979.text: ἐπισιτισμός ejpisitismovs episitismos {ep-ee-sit-is-mos'} from a compound of 1909 and a derivative of 4621; a provisioning, i.e. (concretely) food:--victuals. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4621

G1980.text: ἐπισκέπτομαι ejpiskevptomai episkeptomai {ep-ee-skep'-tom-ahee} middle voice from 1909 and the base of 4649; to inspect, i.e. (by implication) to select; by extension, to go to see, relieve:--look out, visit. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4649

G1981.text: ἐπισκηνόω ejpiskhnovw episkenoo {ep-ee-skay-no'-o} from 1909 and 4637; to tent upon, i.e. (figuratively) abide with :--rest upon. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4637

G1982.text: ἐπισκιάζω ejpiskiavzw episkiazo {ep-ee-skee-ad'-zo} from 1909 and a derivative of 4639; to cast a shade upon, i.e. (by analogy) to envelop in a haze of brilliancy; figuratively, to invest with preternatural influence:--overshadow. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4639

G1983.text: ἐπισκοπέω ejpiskopevw episkopeo {ep-ee-skop-eh'-o} from 1909 and 4648; to oversee; by implication, to beware:--look diligently, take the oversight. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4648

G1984.text: ἐπισκοπή ejpiskophv episkope {ep-is-kop-ay'} from 1980; inspection (for relief); by implication, superintendence; specially, the Christian "episcopate":--the office of a "bishop", bishoprick, visitation. see GREEK for 1980

G1985.text: ἐπίσκοπος ejpivskopos episkopos {ep-is'-kop-os} from 1909 and 4649 (in the sense of 1983); a superintendent, i.e. Christian officer in genitive case charge of a (or the) church (literally or figuratively):--bishop, overseer. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4649 see GREEK for 1983

G1986.text: ἐπισπάομαι ejpispavomai epispaomai {ep-ee-spah'-om-ahee} from 1909 and 4685; to draw over, i.e. (with 203 implied) efface the mark of circumcision (by recovering with the foreskin):--become uncircumcised. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4685 see GREEK for 203

G1987.text: ἐπίσταμαι ejpivstamai epistamai {ep-is'-tam-ahee} apparently a middle voice of 2186 (with 3563 implied); to put the mind upon, i.e. comprehend, or be acquainted with:--know, understand. see GREEK for 2186 see GREEK for 3563

G1988.text: ἐπιστάτης ejpistavths epistates {ep-is-tat'-ace} from 1909 and a presumed derivative of 2476; an appointee over, i.e. commander (teacher):--master. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 2476

G1989.text: ἐπιστέλλω ejpistevllw epistello {ep-ee-stel'-lo} from 1909 and 4724; to enjoin (by writing), i.e. (genitive case) to communicate by letter (for any purpose):--write (a letter, unto). see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4724

G1990.text: ἐπιστήμων ejpisthvmwn epistemon {ep-ee-stay'-mone} from 1987; intelligent:--endued with knowledge. see GREEK for 1987

G1991.text: ἐπιστηρίζω ejpisthrivzw episterizo {ep-ee-stay-rid'-zo} from 1909 and 4741; to support further, i.e. reestablish:--confirm, strengthen. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4741

G1992.text: ἐπιστολή ejpistolhv epistole {ep-is-tol-ay'} from 1989; a written message:--"epistle," letter. see GREEK for 1989

G1993.text: ἐπιστομίζω ejpistomivzw epistomizo {ep-ee-stom-id'-zo} from 1909 and 4750; to put something over the mouth, i.e. (figuratively) to silence:--stop mouths. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4750

G1994.text: ἐπιστρέφω ejpistrevfw epistrepho {ep-ee-stref'-o} from 1909 and 4762; to revert (literally, figuratively or morally):--come (go) again, convert, (re-)turn (about, again). see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4762

G1995.text: ἐπιστροφή ejpistrofhv epistrophe {ep-is-trof-ay'} from 1994; reversion, i.e. morally, revolution:--conversion. see GREEK for 1994

G1996.text: ἐπισυνάγω ejpisunavgw episunago {ep-ee-soon-ag'-o} from 1909 and 4863; to collect upon the same place:--gather (together). see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4863

G1997.text: ἐπισυναγωγή ejpisunagwghv episunagoge {ep-ee-soon-ag-o-gay'} from 1996; a complete collection; especially a Christian meeting (for worship):--assembling (gathering) together. see GREEK for 1996

G1998.text: ἐπισυντρέχω ejpisuntrevcw episuntrecho {ep-ee-soon-trekh'-o} from 1909 and 4936; to hasten together upon one place (or a particular occasion):--come running together. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4936

G1999.text: ἐπίστασις ejpivstasis episustasis {ep-ee-soo'-stas-is} from the middle voice of a compound of 1909 and 4921; a conspiracy, i.e. concourse (riotous or friendly):--that which cometh upon, + raising up. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4921

G2000.text: ἐπισφαλής ejpisfalhvs episphales {ep-ee-sfal-ace'} from a compound of 1909 and sphallo (to trip); figuratively, insecure:--dangerous. see GREEK for 1909

G2001.text: ἐπισχύω ejpiscuvw epischo {ep-is-khoo'-o} from 1909 and 2480; to avail further, i.e. (figuratively) insist stoutly:--be the more fierce. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 2480

G2002.text: ἐπισωρεύω ejpiswreuvw episoreuo {ep-ee-so-ryoo'-o} from 1909 and 4987; to accumulate further, i.e. (figuratively) seek additionally:--heap. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 4987

G2003.text: ἐπιταγή ejpitaghv epitage {ep-ee-tag-ay'} from 2004; an injunction or decree; by implication, authoritativeness:--authority, commandment. see GREEK for 2004

G2004.text: ἐπιτάσσω ejpitavssw epitasso {ep-ee-tas'-so} from 1909 and 5021; to arrange upon, i.e. order:--charge, command, injoin. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 5021

G2005.text: ἐπιτελέω ejpitelevw epiteleo {ep-ee-tel-eh'-o} from 1909 and 5055; to fulfill further (or completely), i.e. execute; by implication, to terminate, undergo:--accomplish, do, finish, (make) (perfect), perform(X -ance). see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 5055

G2006.text: ἐπιτήδειος ejpithvdeios epitedeios {ep-ee-tay'-di-os} from epitedes (enough); serviceable, i.e. (by implication) requisite:--things which are needful.

G2007.text: ἐπιτίθημι ejpitivqhmi epitithemi {ep-ee-tith'-ay-mee} from 1909 and 5087; to impose (in a friendly or hostile sense):--add unto, lade, lay upon, put (up) on, set on (up), + surname, X wound. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 5087

G2008.text: ἐπιτιμάω ejpitimavw epitimao {ep-ee-tee-mah'-o} from 1909 and 5091; to tax upon, i.e. censure or admonish; by implication, forbid:--(straitly) charge, rebuke. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 5091

G2009.text: ἐπιτιμία ejpitimiva epitimia {ep-ee-tee-mee'-ah} from a compound of 1909 and 5092; properly, esteem, i.e. citizenship; used (in the sense of 2008) of a penalty:--punishment. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 5092 see GREEK for 2008

G2010.text: ἐπιτρέπω ejpitrevpw epitrepo {ep-ee-trep'-o} from 1909 and the base of 5157; to turn over (transfer), i.e. allow:--give leave (liberty, license), let, permit, suffer. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 5157

G2011.text: ἐπιτροπή ejpitrophv epitrope {ep-ee-trop-ay'} from 2010; permission, i.e. (by implication) full power:--commission. see GREEK for 2010

G2012.text: ἐπίτροπος ejpivtropos epitropos {ep-it'-rop-os} from 1909 and 5158 (in the sense of 2011); a commissioner, i.e. domestic manager, guardian:--steward, tutor. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 5158 see GREEK for 2011

G2013.text: ἐπιτυγχάνω ejpitugcavnw epitugchano {ep-ee-toong-khan'-o} from 1909 and 5177; to chance upon, i.e. (by implication) to attain:--obtain. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 5177

G2014.text: ἐπιφαίνω ejpifaivnw epiphaino {ep-ee-fah'-ee-no} from 1909 and 5316; to shine upon, i.e. become (literally) visible or (figuratively) known:--appear, give light. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 5316

G2015.text: ἐπιφάνεια ejpifavneia epiphaneia {ep-if-an'-i-ah} from 2016; a manifestation, i.e. (specially) the advent of Christ (past or future):--appearing, brightness. see GREEK for 2016

G2016.text: ἐπιφανής ejpifanhvs epiphanes {ep-if-an-ace'} from 2014; conspicuous, i.e. (figuratively) memorable:--notable. see GREEK for 2014

G2017.text: ἐπιφαύσκω ejpifauvskw epiphausko {ep-ee-fows'-ko} a form of 2014; to illuminate (figuratively):--give light. see GREEK for 2014

G2018.text: ἐπιφέρω ejpifevrw epiphero {ep-ee-fer'-o} from 1909 and 5342; to bear upon (or further), i.e. adduce (personally or judicially (accuse, inflict)), superinduce:--add, bring (against), take. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 5342

G2019.text: ἐπιφωνέω ejpifwnevw epiphoneo {ep-ee-fo-neh'-o} from 1909 and 5455; to call at something, i.e. exclaim:--cry (against), give a shout. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 5455

G2020.text: ἐπιφώσκω ejpifwvskw epiphosko {ep-ee-foce'-ko} a form of 2017; to begin to grow light:--begin to dawn, X draw on. see GREEK for 2017

G2021.text: ἐπιχειρέω ejpiceirevw epicheireo {ep-ee-khi-reh'-o} from 1909 and 5495; to put the hand upon, i.e. undertake:--go about, take in hand (upon). see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 5495

G2022.text: ἐπιχέω ejpicevw epicheo {ep-ee-kheh'-o} from 1909 and cheo (to pour); --to pour upon:--pour in. see GREEK for 1909

G2023.text: ἐπιχορηγέω ejpicorhgevw epichoregeo {ep-ee-khor-ayg-eh'-o} from 1909 and 5524; to furnish besides, i.e. fully supply, (figuratively) aid or contribute:--add, minister (nourishment, unto). see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 5524

G2024.text: ἐπιχορηγία ejpicorhgiva epichoregia {ep-ee-khor-ayg-ee'-ah} from 2023; contribution:--supply. see GREEK for 2023

G2025.text: ἐπιχρίω ejpicrivw epichrio {ep-ee-khree'-o} from 1909 and 5548; to smear over:--anoint. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 5548

G2026.text: ἐποικοδομέω ejpoikodomevw epoikodomeo {ep-oy-kod-om-eh'-o} from 1909 and 3618; to build upon, i.e. (figuratively) to rear up:--build thereon (thereupon, on, upon). see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3618

G2027.text: ἐπικέλλω ejpikevllw epokello {ep-ok-el'-lo} from 1909 and okello (to urge); to drive upon the shore, i.e. to beach a vessel:--run aground. see GREEK for 1909

G2028.text: ἐπονομάζω ejponomavzw eponomazo {ep-on-om-ad'-zo} from 1909 and 3687; to name further, i.e. denominate:--call. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3687

G2029.text: ἐποπτεύω ejpopteuvw epopteuo {ep-opt-yoo'-o} from 1909 and a derivative of 3700; to inspect, i.e. watch:--behold. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3700

G2030.text: ἐπόπτης ejpovpths epoptes {ep-op'-tace} from 1909 and a presumed derivative of 3700; a looker-on:--eye-witness. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3700

G2031.text: ἔπος e[pos epos {ep'-os} from 2036; a word:--X say. see GREEK for 2036

G2032.text: ἐπουράνιος ejpouravnios epouranios {ep-oo-ran'-ee-os} from 1909 and 3772; above the sky:--celestial, (in) heaven(-ly), high. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 3772

G2033.text: ἑπτά eJptav hepta {hep-tah'} a primary number; seven:--seven.

G2034.text: ἑπτάκις eJptavkis heptakis {hep-tak-is'} adverb from 2033; seven times:--seven times. see GREEK for 2033

G2035.text: ἑπτακισχίλιοι eJptakiscivlioi heptakischilioi {hep-tak-is-khil'-ee-oy} from 2034 and 5507; seven times a thousand:--seven thousand. see GREEK for 2034 see GREEK for 5507

G2036.text: λέγω levgw epo {ep'-o} a primary verb (used only in the definite past tense, the others being borrowed from 2046, 4483, and 5346); to speak or say (by word or writing):--answer, bid, bring word, call, command, grant, say (on), speak, tell. Compare 3004. see GREEK for 2046 see GREEK for 4483 see GREEK for 5346 see GREEK for 3004

G2037.text: Ἔραστος E[rastos Erastos {er'-as-tos} from erao (to love); beloved; Erastus, a Christian:--Erastus.

G2038.text: ἐργάζομαι ejrgavzomai ergazomai {er-gad'-zom-ahee} middle voice from 2041; to toil (as a task, occupation, etc.), (by implication) effect, be engaged in or with, etc.:--commit, do, labor for, minister about, trade (by), work. see GREEK for 2041

G2039.text: ἐργασία ejrgasiva ergasia {er-gas-ee'-ah} from 2040; occupation; by implication, profit, pains:--craft, diligence, gain, work. see GREEK for 2040

G2040.text: ἐργάτης ejrgavths ergates {er-gat'-ace} from 2041; a toiler; figuratively, a teacher:--labourer, worker(-men). see GREEK for 2041

G2041.text: ἔργον e[rgon ergon {er'-gon} from a primary (but obsolete) ergo (to work); toil (as an effort or occupation); by implication, an act:--deed, doing, labour, work.

G2042.text: ἐρεθίζω ejreqivzw erethizo {er-eth-id'-zo} from a presumed prolonged form of 2054; to stimulate (especially to anger):--provoke. see GREEK for 2054

G2043.text: ἐρείδω ejreivdw ereido {er-i'-do} of obscure affinity; to prop, i.e. (reflexively) get fast:--stick fast.

G2044.text: ἐρεύγομαι ejreuvgomai ereugomai {er-yoog'-om-ahee} of uncertain affinity; to belch, i.e. (figuratively) to speak out:--utter.

G2045.text: ἐραυνάω ejraunavw ereunao {er-yoo-nah'-o} apparently from 2046 (through the idea of inquiry); to seek, i.e. (figuratively) to investigate:--search. see GREEK for 2046

G2046.text: λέγω levgw ereo {er-eh'-o} probably a fuller form of 4483; an alternate for 2036 in certain tenses; to utter, i.e. speak or say:--call, say, speak (of), tell. see GREEK for 4483 see GREEK for 2036

G2047.text: ἐρημία ejrhmiva eremia {er-ay-mee'-ah} from 2048; solitude (concretely):--desert, wilderness. see GREEK for 2048

G2048.text: ἔρημος e[rhmos eremos {er'-ay-mos} of uncertain affinity; lonesome, i.e. (by implication) waste (usually as a noun, 5561 being implied):--desert, desolate, solitary, wilderness. see GREEK for 5561

G2049.text: ἐρημόω ejrhmovw eremoo {er-ay-mo'-o} from 2048; to lay waste (literally or figuratively):--(bring to, make) desolate(-ion), come to nought. see GREEK for 2048

G2050.text: ἐρήμωσις ejrhvmwsis eremosis {er-ay'-mo-sis} from 2049; despoliation:--desolation. see GREEK for 2049

G2051.text: ἐρίζω ejrivzw erizo {er-id'-zo} from 2054; to wrangle:--strive. see GREEK for 2054

G2052.text: ἐριθεία ejriqeiva eritheia {er-ith-i'-ah} perhaps as the same as 2042; properly, intrigue, i.e. (by implication) faction:--contention(-ious), strife. see GREEK for 2042

G2053.text: ἔριον e[rion erion {er'-ee-on} of obscure affinity; wool:--wool.

G2054.text: ἔρις e[ris eris {er'-is} of uncertain affinity; a quarrel, i.e. (by implication) wrangling:--contention, debate, strife, variance.

G2055.text: ἐρίφιον ejrivfion eriphion {er-if'-ee-on} from 2056; a kidling, i.e. (genitive case) goat (symbolically, wicked person):--goat. see GREEK for 2056

G2056.text: ἔριφος e[rifos eriphos {er'-if-os} perhaps from the same as 2053 (through the idea of hairiness); a kid or (genitive case) goat:--goat, kid. see GREEK for 2053

G2057.text: Ἑρμᾶς EJrma's Hermas {her-mas'} probably from 2060; Hermas, a Christian:--Hermas. see GREEK for 2060

G2058.text: ἑρμηνεία eJrmhneiva hermeneia {her-may-ni'-ah} from the same as 2059; translation:--interpretation. see GREEK for 2059

G2059.text: ἑρμηνεύω eJrmhneuvw hermeneuo {her-mayn-yoo'-o} from a presumed derivative of 2060 (as the god of language); to translate:--interpret. see GREEK for 2060

G2060.text: Ἑρμῆς EJrmh's Hermes {her-mace'} perhaps from 2046; Hermes, the name of the messenger of the Greek deities; also of a Christian:--Hermes, Mercury. see GREEK for 2046

G2061.text: Ἑρμογένης EJrmogevnhs Hermogenes {her-mog-en'-ace} from 2060 and 1096; born of Hermes; Hermogenes, an apostate Christian:--Hermogenes. see GREEK for 2060 see GREEK for 1096

G2062.text: ἑρπετόν eJrpetovn herpeton {her-pet-on'} neuter of a derivative of herpo (to creep); a reptile, i.e. (by Hebraism (compare 7431)) a small animal:--creeping thing, serpent. see HEBREW for 07431

G2063.text: ἐρυθρός ejruqrovs eruthros {er-oo-thros'} of uncertain affinity; red, i.e. (with 2281) the Red Sea:--red. see GREEK for 2281

G2064.text: ἔρχομαι e[rcomai erchomai {er'-khom-ahee} middle voice of a primary verb (used only in the present and imperfect tenses, the others being supplied by a kindred (middle voice) eleuthomai el-yoo'-thom-ahee, or (active) eltho el'-tho, which do not otherwise occur) to come or go (in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively):--accompany, appear, bring, come, enter, fall out, go, grow, X light, X next, pass, resort, be set.

G2065.text: ἐρωτάω ejrwtavw erotao {er-o-tah'-o} apparently from 2046 (compare 2045); to interrogate; by implication, to request:--ask, beseech, desire, intreat, pray. Compare 4441. see GREEK for 2046 see GREEK for 2045 see GREEK for 4441

G2066.text: ἐσθής ejsqhvs esthes {es-thace'} from hennumi (to clothe); dress:--apparel, clothing, raiment, robe.

G2067.text: ἔσθησις εως ἡ esthesis esthesis {es'-thay-sis} from a derivative of 2066; clothing (concretely):--government. see GREEK for 2066

G2068.text: ἐσθίω ejsqivw esthio {es-thee'-o} strengthened for a primary edo (to eat); used only in certain tenses, the rest being supplied by 5315; to eat (usually literal):--devour, eat, live. see GREEK for 5315

G2069.text: Ἑσλί EJsliv Esli {es-lee'} of Hebrew origin (probably for 454); Esli, an Israelite:--Esli. see HEBREW for 0454

G2070.text: εἰμί eijmiv esmen {es-men'} first person plural indicative of 1510; we are:--are, be, have our being, X have hope, + (the gospel) was (preached unto) us. see GREEK for 1510

G2071.text: εἰμί eijmiv esomai {es'-om-ahee} future of 1510; will be:--shall (should) be (have), (shall) come (to pass), X may have, X fall, what would follow, X live long, X sojourn. see GREEK for 1510

G2072.text: ἔσοπτρον e[soptron esoptron {es'-op-tron} from 1519 and a presumed derivative of 3700; a mirror (for looking into):--glass. Compare 2734. see GREEK for 1519 see GREEK for 3700 see GREEK for 2734

G2073.text: ἑσπέρα eJspevra hespera {hes-per'-ah} feminine of an adjective hesperos (evening); the eve (5610 being implied):--evening(-tide). see GREEK for 5610

G2074.text: Ἑσρώμ EJsrwvm Esrom {es-rome} of Hebrew origin (2696); Esrom (i.e. Chetsron), an Israelite:--Esrom. see HEBREW for 02696

G2075.text: εἰμί eijmiv este {es-teh'} second person plural present indicative of 1510; ye are:--be, have been, belong. see GREEK for 1510

G2076.text: εἰμί eijmiv esti {es-tee'} third person singular present indicative of 1510; he (she or it) is; also (with neuter plural) they are:--are, be(-long), call, X can(-not), come, consisteth, X dure for a while, + follow, X have, (that) is (to say), make, meaneth, X must needs, + profit, + remaineth, + wrestle. see GREEK for 1510

G2077.text: εἰμί eijmiv esto {es'-to} second person singular present imperative of 1510; be thou; also estosan es'-to-san, third person of the same let them be:--be. see GREEK for 1510

G2078.text: ἔσχατος e[scatos eschatos {es'-khat-os} a superlative probably from 2192 (in the sense of contiguity); farthest, final (of place or time):--ends of, last, latter end, lowest, uttermost. see GREEK for 2192

G2079.text: ἐσχάτως ejscavtws eschatos {es-khat'-oce} adverb from 2078; finally, i.e. (with 2192) at the extremity of life:--point of death. see GREEK for 2078 see GREEK for 2192

G2080.text: ἔσω e[sw eso {es'-o} from 1519; inside (as preposition or adjective):-- (with-)in(-ner, -to, -ward). see GREEK for 1519

G2081.text: ἔσωθεν e[swqen esothen {es'-o-then} from 2080; from inside; also used as equivalent to 2080 (inside):--inward(-ly), (from) within, without. see GREEK for 2080 see GREEK for 2080

G2082.text: ἐσώτερος ejswvteros esoteros {es-o'-ter-os} comparative of 2080; interior:--inner, within. see GREEK for 2080

G2083.text: ἑταῖρος eJtai'ros hetairos {het-ah'-ee-ros} from etes (a clansman); a comrade:--fellow, friend.

G2084.text: ἑτερόγλωσσος eJterovglwssos heteroglossos {het-er-og'-loce-sos} from 2087 and 1100; other- tongued, i.e. a foreigner:--man of other tongue. see GREEK for 2087 see GREEK for 1100

G2085.text: ἑτεροδιδασκαλέω eJterodidaskalevw heterodidaskaleo {het-er-od-id-as-kal-eh'-o} from 2087 and 1320; to instruct differently:--teach other doctrine(-wise). see GREEK for 2087 see GREEK for 1320

G2086.text: ἑτεροζυγέω eJterozugevw heterozugeo {het-er-od-zoog-eh'-o} from a compound of 2087 and 2218; to yoke up differently, i.e. (figuratively) to associate discordantly:--unequally yoke together with. see GREEK for 2087 see GREEK for 2218

G2088.text: ἑτέρως eJtevrws heteros {het-er'-oce} adverb from 2087; differently:--otherwise. see GREEK for 2087

G2089.text: ἔτι e[ti eti {et'-ee} perhaps akin to 2094; "yet," still (of time or degree):--after that, also, ever, (any) further, (t-)henceforth (more), hereafter, (any) longer, (any) more(-one), now, still, yet. see GREEK for 2094

G2090.text: ἑτοιμάζω eJtoimavzw hetoimazo {het-oy-mad'-zo} from 2092; to prepare:--prepare, provide, make ready. Compare 2680. see GREEK for 2092 see GREEK for 2680

G2091.text: ἑτοιμασία eJtoimasiva hetoimasia {het-oy-mas-ee'-ah} from 2090; preparation:--preparation. see GREEK for 2090

G2092.text: ἕτοιμος e&toimos hetoimos {het-oy'-mos} from an old noun heteos (fitness); adjusted, i.e. ready:--prepared, (made) ready(-iness, to our hand).

G2093.text: ἑτοίμως eJtoivmws hetoimos {het'-oy-moce} adverb from 2092; in readiness:--ready. see GREEK for 2092

G2094.text: ἔτος e[tos etos {et'-os} apparently a primary word; a year:--year.

G2095.text: εὖγε εὖ eu\\ge eu\\ eu {yoo} neuter of a primary eus (good); (adverbially) well:--good, well (done).

G2096.text: Εὕα Eu&a Eua {yoo'-ah} of Hebrew origin (2332); Eua (or Eva, i.e. Chavvah), the first woman:--Eve. see HEBREW for 02332

G2097.text: εὐαγγελίζω eujaggelivzw euaggelizo {yoo-ang-ghel-id'-zo} from 2095 and 32; to announce good news ("evangelize") especially the gospel:--declare, bring (declare, show) glad (good) tidings, preach (the gospel). see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 32

G2098.text: εὐαγγέλιον eujaggevlion euaggelion {yoo-ang-ghel'-ee-on} from the same as 2097; a good message, i.e. the gospel:--gospel. see GREEK for 2097

G2099.text: εὐαγγελιστής eujaggelisthvs euaggelistes {yoo-ang-ghel-is-tace'} from 2097; a preacher of the gospel:--evangelist. see GREEK for 2097

G2100.text: εὐαρεστέω eujarestevw euaresteo {yoo-ar-es-teh'-o} from 2101; to gratify entirely:--please (well). see GREEK for 2101

G2101.text: εὐάρεστος eujavrestos euarestos {yoo-ar'-es-tos} from 2095 and 701; fully agreeable:--acceptable(-ted), wellpleasing. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 701

G2102.text: εὐαρέστως eujarevstws euarestos {yoo-ar-es'-toce} adverb from 2101; quite agreeably:--acceptably, + please well. see GREEK for 2101

G2103.text: Εὔβουλος Eu[boulos Euboulos {yoo'-boo-los} from 2095 and 1014; good-willer; Eubulus, a Christian:--Eubulus. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 1014

G2104.text: εὐγενής eujgenhvs eugenes {yoog-en'-ace} from 2095 and 1096; well born, i.e. (literally) high in rank, or (figuratively) generous:--more noble, nobleman. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 1096

G2105.text: εὐδία eujdiva eudia {yoo-dee'-ah} feminine from 2095 and the alternate of 2203 (as the god of the weather); a clear sky, i.e. fine weather:--fair weather. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 2203

G2106.text: εὐδοκέω eujdokevw eudokeo {yoo-dok-eh'-o} from 2095 and 1380; to think well of, i.e. approve (an act); specially, to approbate (a person or thing):--think good, (be well) please(-d), be the good (have, take) pleasure, be willing. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 1380

G2107.text: εὐδοκία eujdokiva eudokia {yoo-dok-ee'-ah} from a presumed compound of 2095 and the base of 1380; satisfaction, i.e. (subjectively) delight, or (objectively) kindness, wish, purpose:--desire, good pleasure (will), X seem good. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 1380

G2108.text: εὐεργεσία eujergesiva euergesia {yoo-erg-es-ee'-ah} from 2110; beneficence (genitive case or specially):--benefit, good deed done. see GREEK for 2110

G2109.text: εὐεργετέω eujergetevw euergeteo {yoo-erg-et-eh'-o} from 2110; to be philanthropic:--do good. see GREEK for 2110

G2110.text: εὐεργέτης eujergevths euergetes {yoo-erg-et'-ace} from 2095 and the base of 2041; a worker of good, i.e. (specially) a philanthropist:--benefactor. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 2041

G2111.text: εὔθετος eu[qetos euthetos {yoo'-thet-os} from 2095 and a derivative of 5087; well placed, i.e. (figuratively) appropriate:--fit, meet. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 5087

G2112.text: εὐθέως eujqevws eutheos {yoo-theh'-oce} adverb from 2117; directly, i.e. at once or soon:--anon, as soon as, forthwith, immediately, shortly, straightway. see GREEK for 2117

G2113.text: εὐθυδρομέω eujqudromevw euthudromeo {yoo-thoo-drom-eh'-o} from 2117 and 1408; to lay a straight course, i.e. sail direct:--(come) with a straight course. see GREEK for 2117 see GREEK for 1408

G2114.text: εὐθυμέω eujqumevw euthumeo {yoo-thoo-meh'-o} from 2115; to cheer up, i.e. (intransitively) be cheerful; neuter comparative (adverbially) more cheerfully:--be of good cheer (merry). see GREEK for 2115

G2115.text: εὔθυμος eu[qumos euthumos {yoo'-thoo-mos} from 2095 and 2372; in fine spirits, i.e. cheerful:--of good cheer, the more cheerfully. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 2372

G2116.text: εὐθύνω eujquvnw euthuno {yoo-thoo'-no} from 2117; to straighten (level); technically, to steer:--governor, make straight. see GREEK for 2117

G2117.text: εὐθύς eujquvs euthus {yoo-thoos'} perhaps from 2095 and 5087; straight, i.e. (literally) level, or (figuratively) true; adverbially (of time) at once:--anon, by and by, forthwith, immediately, straightway. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 5087

G2118.text: εὐθύτης eujquvths euthutes {yoo-thoo'-tace} from 2117; rectitude:--righteousness. see GREEK for 2117

G2119.text: εὐκαιρέω eujkairevw eukaireo {yoo-kahee-reh'-o} from 2121; to have good time, i.e. opportunity or leisure:--have leisure (convenient time), spend time. see GREEK for 2121

G2120.text: εὐκαιρία eujkairiva eukairia {yoo-kahee-ree'-ah} from 2121; a favorable occasion:--opportunity. see GREEK for 2121

G2121.text: εὔκαιρος eu[kairos eukairos {yoo'-kahee-ros} from 2095 and 2540; well-timed, i.e. opportune:--convenient, in time of need. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 2540

G2122.text: εὐκαίρως eujkaivrws eukairos {yoo-kah'-ee-roce} adverb from 2121; opportunely:--conveniently, in season. see GREEK for 2121

G2123.text: εὐκοπώτερος eujkopwvteros eukopoteros {yoo-kop-o'-ter-os} comparative of a compound of 2095 and 2873; better for toil, i.e. more facile:--easier. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 2873

G2124.text: εὐλάβεια eujlavbeia eulabeia {yoo-lab'-i-ah} from 2126; properly, caution, i.e. (religiously) reverence (piety); by implication, dread (concretely):--fear(-ed). see GREEK for 2126

G2125.text: εὐλαβέομαι eujlabevomai eulabeomai {yoo-lab-eh'-om-ahee} middle voice from 2126; to be circumspect, i.e. (by implication) to be apprehensive; religiously, to reverence:--(moved with) fear. see GREEK for 2126

G2126.text: εὐλαβής eujlabhvs eulabes {yoo-lab-ace'} from 2095 and 2983; taking well (carefully), i.e. circumspect (religiously, pious):--devout. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 2983

G2127.text: εὐλογέω eujlogevw eulogeo {yoo-log-eh'-o} from a compound of 2095 and 3056; to speak well of, i.e. (religiously) to bless (thank or invoke a benediction upon, prosper):--bless, praise. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 3056

G2128.text: εὐλογητός eujloghtovs eulogetos {yoo-log-ay-tos'} from 2127; adorable:--blessed. see GREEK for 2127

G2129.text: εὐλογία eujlogiva eulogia {yoo-log-ee'-ah} from the same as 2127; fine speaking, i.e. elegance of language; commendation ("eulogy"), i.e. (reverentially) adoration; religiously, benediction; by implication, consecration; by extension, benefit or largess:--blessing (a matter of) bounty (X -tifully), fair speech. see GREEK for 2127

G2130.text: εὐμετάδοτος eujmetavdotos eumetadotos {yoo-met-ad'-ot-os} from 2095 and a presumed derivative of 3330; good at imparting, i.e. liberal:--ready to distribute. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 3330

G2131.text: Εὐνίκη Eujnivkh Eunike {yoo-nee'-kay} from 2095 and 3529; victorious; Eunice, a Jewess:--Eunice. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 3529

G2132.text: εὐνοέω eujnoevw eunoeo {yoo-no-eh'-o} from a compound of 2095 and 3563; to be well- minded, i.e. reconcile:--agree. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 3563

G2133.text: εὔνοια eu[noia eunoia {yoo'-noy-ah} from the same as 2132; kindness; euphemistically, conjugal duty:--benevolence, good will. see GREEK for 2132

G2134.text: εὐνουχίζω eujnoucivzw eunouchizo {yoo-noo-khid'-zo} from 2135; to castrate (figuratively, live unmarried):--make...eunuch. see GREEK for 2135

G2135.text: εὐνοῦχος eujnou'cos eunouchos {yoo-noo'-khos} from eune (a bed) and 2192; a castrated person (such being employed in Oriental bed-chambers); by extension an impotent or unmarried man; by implication, a chamberlain (state-officer):--eunuch. see GREEK for 2192

G2136.text: Εὐοδία Eujodiva Euodia {yoo-od-ee'-ah} from the same as 2137; fine travelling; Euodia, a Christian woman:--Euodias. see GREEK for 2137

G2137.text: εὐοδόομαι eujodovomai euodoo {yoo-od-o'-o} from a compound of 2095 and 3598; to help on the road, i.e. (passively) succeed in reaching; figuratively, to succeed in business affairs:--(have a) prosper(-ous journey). see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 3598

G2138.text: εὐπειθής eujpeiqhvs eupeithes {yoo-pi-thace'} from 2095 and 3982; good for persuasion, i.e. (intransitively) complaint:--easy to be intreated. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 3982

G2139.text: εὐπερίστατος eujperivstatos euperistatos {yoo-per-is'-tat-os} from 2095 and a derivative of a presumed compound of 4012 and 2476; well standing around, i.e. (a competitor) thwarting (a racer) in every direction (figuratively, of sin in genitive case):--which doth so easily beset. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2476

G2140.text: εὐποιΐα eujpoii?a eupoiia {yoo-poy-ee'-ah} from a compound of 2095 and 4160; well-doing, i.e. beneficence:--to do good. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 4160

G2141.text: εὐπορέω eujporevw euporeo {yoo-por-eh'-o} from a compound of 2090 and the base of 4197; (intransitively) to be good for passing through, i.e. (figuratively) have pecuniary means:--ability. see GREEK for 2090 see GREEK for 4197

G2142.text: εὐπορία eujporiva euporia {yoo-por-ee'-ah} from the same as 2141; pecuniary resources:--wealth. see GREEK for 2141

G2143.text: εὐπρέπεια eujprevpeia euprepeia {yoo-prep'-i-ah} from a compound of 2095 and 4241; good suitableness, i.e. gracefulness:--grace. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 4241

G2144.text: εὐπρόσδεκτος eujprovsdektos euprosdektos {yoo-pros'-dek-tos} from 2095 and a derivative of 4327; well-received, i.e. approved, favorable:--acceptable(-ted). see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 4327
