G2145.text: εὐπάρεδρον eujpavredron euprosedros {yoo-pros'-ed-ros} from 2095 and the same as 4332; sitting well towards, i.e. (figuratively) assiduous (neuter, diligent service):--X attend upon. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 4332

G2146.text: εὐπροσωπέω eujproswpevw euprosopeo {yoo-pros-o-peh'-o} from a compound of 2095 and 4383; to be of good countenance, i.e. (figuratively) to make a display:--make a fair show. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 4383

G2147.text: εὑρίσκω euJrivskw heurisko {hyoo-ris'-ko} heuro hyoo'-ro, which (together with another cognate form) heureo hyoo-reh'-o is used for it in all the tenses except the present and imperfect to find (literally or figuratively):--find, get, obtain, perceive, see.

G2149.text: εὐρύχωρος eujruvcwros euruchoros {yoo-roo'-kho-ros} from eurus (wide) and 5561; spacious:--broad. see GREEK for 5561

G2150.text: εὐσέβεια eujsevbeia eusebeia {yoo-seb'-i-ah} from 2152; piety; specially, the gospel scheme:--godliness, holiness. see GREEK for 2152

G2151.text: εὐσεβέω eujsebevw eusebeo {yoo-seb-eh'-o} from 2152; to be pious, i.e. (towards God) to worship, or (towards parents) to respect (support):--show piety, worship. see GREEK for 2152

G2152.text: εὐσεβής eujsebhvs eusebes {yoo-seb-ace'} from 2095 and 4576; well-reverent, i.e. pious:--devout, godly. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 4576

G2153.text: εὐσεβῶς eujsebw's eusebos {yoo-seb-oce'} adverb from 2152; piously:--godly. see GREEK for 2152

G2154.text: εὔσημος eu[shmos eusemos {yoo'-say-mos} from 2095 and the base of 4591; well indicated, i.e. (figuratively) significant:--easy to be understood. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 4591

G2155.text: εὔσπλαγχνος eu[splagcnos eusplagchnos {yoo'-splangkh-nos} from 2095 and 4698; well compassioned, i.e. sympathetic:--pitiful, tender-hearted. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 4698

G2156.text: εὐσχημόνως eujschmovnws euschemonos {yoo-skhay-mon'-ose} adverb from 2158; decorously:--decently, honestly. see GREEK for 2158

G2157.text: εὐσχημοσύνη eujschmosuvnh eushemosune {yoo-skhay-mos-oo'-nay} from 2158; decorousness:--comeliness. see GREEK for 2158

G2158.text: εὐσχήμων eujschvmwn euschemon {yoo-skhay'-mone} from 2095 and 4976; well-formed, i.e. (figuratively) decorous, noble (in rank):--comely, honourable. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 4976

G2159.text: εὐτόνως eujtovnws eutonos {yoo-ton'-oce} adverb from a compound of 2095 and a derivative of teino (to stretch); in a well-strung manner, i.e. (figuratively) intensely (in a good sense, cogently; in a bad one, fiercely):--mightily, vehemently. see GREEK for 2095

G2160.text: εὐτραπελία eujtrapeliva eutrapelia {yoo-trap-el-ee'-ah} from a compound of 2095 and a derivative of the base of 5157 (meaning well-turned, i.e. ready at repartee, jocose); witticism, i.e. (in a vulgar sense) ribaldry:--jesting. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 5157

G2161.text: Εὔτυχος Eu[tucos Eutuchos {yoo'-too-khos} from 2095 and a derivative of 5177; well- fated, i.e. fortunate; Eutychus, a young man:--Eutychus. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 5177

G2162.text: εὐφημία eujfhmiva euphemia {yoo-fay-mee'-ah} from 2163; good language ("euphemy"), i.e. praise (repute):--good report. see GREEK for 2163

G2163.text: εὔφημος eu[fhmos euphemos {yoo'-fay-mos} from 2095 and 5345; well spoken of, i.e. reputable:--of good report. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 5345

G2164.text: εὐφορέω eujforevw euphoreo {yoo-for-eh'-o} from 2095 and 5409; to bear well, i.e. be fertile:--bring forth abundantly. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 5409

G2165.text: εὐφραίνω eujfraivnw euphraino {yoo-frah'-ee-no} from 2095 and 5424; to put (middle voice or passively, be) in a good frame of mind, i.e. rejoice:--fare, make glad, be (make) merry, rejoice. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 5424

G2166.text: Εὐφράτης Eujfravths Euphrates {yoo-frat'-ace} of foreign origin (compare 6578); Euphrates, a river of Asia:--Euphrates. see HEBREW for 06578

G2167.text: εὐφροσύνη eujfrosuvnh euphrosune {yoo-fros-oo'-nay} from the same as 2165; joyfulness:--gladness, joy. see GREEK for 2165

G2168.text: εὐχαριστέω eujcaristevw eucharisteo {yoo-khar-is-teh'-o} from 2170; to be grateful, i.e. (actively) to express gratitude (towards); specially, to say grace at a meal:--(give) thank(-ful, -s). see GREEK for 2170

G2169.text: εὐχαριστία eujcaristiva eucharistia {yoo-khar-is-tee'-ah} from 2170; gratitude; actively, grateful language (to God, as an act of worship):--thankfulness, (giving of) thanks(-giving). see GREEK for 2170

G2170.text: εὐχάριστος eujcavristos eucharistos {yoo-khar'-is-tos} from 2095 and a derivative of 5483; well favored, i.e. (by implication) grateful:--thankful. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 5483

G2171.text: εὐχή eujchv euche {yoo-khay'} from 2172; properly, a wish, expressed as a petition to God, or in votive obligation:--prayer, vow. see GREEK for 2172

G2172.text: εὔχομαι eu[comai euchomai {yoo'-khom-ahee} middle voice of a primary verb; to wish; by implication, to pray to God:--pray, will, wish.

G2173.text: εὔχρηστος eu[crhstos euchrestos {yoo'-khrays-tos} from 2095 and 5543; easily used, i.e. useful:--profitable, meet for use. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 5543

G2174.text: εὐψυχέω eujyucevw eupsucheo {yoo-psoo-kheh'-o} from a compound of 2095 and 5590; to be in good spirits, i.e. feel encouraged:--be of good comfort. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 5590

G2175.text: εὐωδία eujwdiva euodia {yoo-o-dee'-ah} from a compound of 2095 and a derivative of 3605; good-scentedness, i.e. fragrance:--sweet savour (smell, -smelling). see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 3605

G2176.text: εὐώνυμος eujwvnumos euonumos {yoo-o'-noo-mos} from 2095 and 3686; properly, well-named (good-omened), i.e. the left (which was the lucky side among the pagan Greeks); neuter as adverbial, at the left hand:--(on the) left. see GREEK for 2095 see GREEK for 3686

G2177.text: ἐφάλλομαι ejfavllomai ephallomai {ef-al'-lom-ahee} from 1909 and 242; to spring upon:--leap on. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 242

G2178.text: ἐφάπαξ ejfavpax ephapax {ef-ap'-ax} from 1909 and 530; upon one occasion (only):--(at) once (for all). see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 530

G2179.text: Ἐφεσῖνος Ephesinos Ephesinos {ef-es-ee'-nos} from 2181; Ephesine, or situated at Ephesus:--of Ephesus. see GREEK for 2181

G2180.text: Ἐφέσιος Ejfevsios Ephesios {ef-es'-ee-os} from 2181; an Ephesian or inhabitant of Ephesus:--Ephesian, of Ephesus. see GREEK for 2181

G2181.text: Ἔφεσος E[fesos Ephesos {ef'-es-os} probably of foreign origin; Ephesus, a city of Asia Minor:--Ephesus.

G2182.text: ἐφευρετής ejfeurethvs epheuretes {ef-yoo-ret'-ace} from a compound of 1909 and 2147; a discoverer, i.e. contriver:--inventor. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 2147

G2183.text: ἐφημερία ejfhmeriva ephemeria {ef-ay-mer-ee'-ah} from 2184; diurnality, i.e. (specially) the quotidian rotation or class of the Jewish priests' service at the Temple, as distributed by families:--course. see GREEK for 2184

G2184.text: ἐφήμερος ejfhvmeros ephemeros {ef-ay'-mer-os} from 1909 and 2250; for a day ("ephemeral"), i.e. diurnal:--daily. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 2250

G2185.text: ἐφικνέομαι ejfiknevomai ephikneomai {ef-ik-neh'-om-ahee} from 1909 and a cognate of 2240; to arrive upon, i.e. extend to:--reach. see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 2240

G2186.text: ἐφίστημι ejfivsthmi ephistemi {ef-is'-tay-mee} from 1909 and 2476; to stand upon, i.e. be present (in various applications, friendly or otherwise, usually literal); --assault, come (in, to, unto, upon), be at hand (instant), present, stand (before, by, over). see GREEK for 1909 see GREEK for 2476

G2187.text: Ἐφραίμ Ejfraivm Ephraim {ef-rah-im'} of Hebrew origin (669 or better 6085); Ephraim, a place in Palestine:--Ephraim. see HEBREW for 0669 see HEBREW for 06085

G2188.text: εφφαθα effaqa ephphatha {ef-fath-ah'} of Chaldee origin (6606); be opened!:--Ephphatha. see HEBREW for 06606

G2189.text: ἔχθρα e[cqra echthra {ekh'-thrah} feminine of 2190; hostility; by implication, a reason for opposition:--enmity, hatred. see GREEK for 2190

G2190.text: ἐχθρός ejcqrovs echthros {ech-thros'} from a primary echtho (to hate); hateful (passively, odious, or actively, hostile); usually as a noun, an adversary (especially Satan):--enemy, foe.

G2191.text: ἔχιδνα e[cidna echidna {ekh'-id-nah} of uncertain origin; an adder or other poisonous snake (literally or figuratively):--viper.

G2192.text: ἔχω e[cw echo {ekh'-o} scheo skheh'-o; (used in certain tenses only) a primary verb; to hold (used in very various applications, literally or figuratively, direct or remote; such as possession; ability, contiuity, relation, or condition):--be (able, X hold, possessed with), accompany, + begin to amend, can(+ -not), X conceive, count, diseased, do + eat, + enjoy, + fear, following, have, hold, keep, + lack, + go to law, lie, + must needs, + of necessity, + need, next, + recover, + reign, + rest, + return, X sick, take for, + tremble, + uncircumcised, use.

G2193.text: ἕως e&ws heos {heh'-oce} of uncertain affinity; a conjunction, preposition and adverb of continuance, until (of time and place):--even (until, unto), (as) far (as), how long, (un-)til(-l), (hither-, un-, up) to, while(-s).

G2194.text: Ζαβουλών Zaboulwvn Zaboulon {dzab-oo-lone'} of Hebrew origin (2074); Zabulon (i.e. Zebulon), a region of Palestine:--Zabulon. see HEBREW for 02074

G2195.text: Ζακχαῖος Zakcai'os Zakchaios {dzak-chah'-ee-yos} of Hebrew origin (compare 2140); Zacchaeus, an Israelite:--Zacchaeus. see HEBREW for 02140

G2196.text: Ζάρα Zavra Zara {dzar-ah'} of Hebrew origin (2226); Zara, (i.e. Zerach), an Israelite:--Zara. see HEBREW for 02226

G2197.text: Ζαχαρίας Zacarivas Zacharias {dzakh-ar-ee'-as} of Hebrew origin (2148); Zacharias (i.e. Zechariah), the name of two Israelites:--Zacharias. see HEBREW for 02148

G2198.text: ζάω zavw zao {dzah'-o} a primary verb; to live (literally or figuratively):--life(-time), (a-)live(-ly), quick.

G2199.text: Ζεβεδαῖος Zebedai'os Zebedaios {dzeb-ed-ah'-yos} of Hebrew origin (compare 2067); Zebedaeus, an Israelite:--Zebedee. see HEBREW for 02067

G2200.text: ζεστός zestovs zestos {dzes-tos'} from 2204; boiled, i.e. (by implication) calid (figuratively, fervent):--hot. see GREEK for 2204

G2201.text: ζεῦγος zeu'gos zeugos {dzyoo'-gos} from the same as 2218; a couple, i.e. a team (of oxen yoked together) or brace (of birds tied together):--yoke, pair. see GREEK for 2218

G2202.text: ζευκτηρία zeukthriva zeukteria {dzook-tay-ree'-ah} feminine of a derivative (at the second stage) from the same as 2218; a fastening (tiller-rope):--band. see GREEK for 2218

G2203.text: Ζεύς Zeuvs Zeus {dzyooce} of uncertain affinity; in the oblique cases there is used instead of it a (probably cognate) name Dis deece, which is otherwise obsolete Zeus or Dis (among the Latins, Jupiter or Jove), the supreme deity of the Greeks:--Jupiter.

G2204.text: ζέω zevw zeo {dzeh'-o} a primary verb; to be hot (boil, of liquids; or glow, of solids), i.e. (figuratively) be fervid (earnest):--be fervent.

G2205.text: ζῆλος zh'los zelos {dzay'-los} from 2204; properly, heat, i.e. (figuratively) "zeal" (in a favorable sense, ardor; in an unfavorable one, jealousy, as of a husband (figuratively, of God), or an enemy, malice):--emulation, envy(-ing), fervent mind, indignation, jealousy, zeal. see GREEK for 2204

G2206.text: ζηλόω ζηλεύω zhlovw zhleuvw zeloo {dzay-lo'-o} from 2205; to have warmth of feeling for or against:--affect, covet (earnestly), (have) desire, (move with) envy, be jealous over, (be) zealous(-ly affect). see GREEK for 2205

G2207.text: ζηλωτής zhlwthvs zelotes {dzay-lo-tace'} from 2206; a "zealot":--zealous. see GREEK for 2206

G2208.text: ζηλωτής zhlwthvs Zelotes {dzay-lo-tace'} the same as 2208; a Zealot, i.e. (specially) partisan for Jewish political independence:--Zelotes. see GREEK for 2208

G2209.text: ζημία zhmiva zemia {dzay-mee'-ah} probably akin to the base of 1150 (through the idea of violence); detriment:--damage, loss. see GREEK for 1150

G2210.text: ζημιόω zhmiovw zemioo {dzay-mee-o'-o} from 2209; to injure, i.e. (reflexively or passively) to experience detriment:--be cast away, receive damage, lose, suffer loss. see GREEK for 2209

G2211.text: Ζηνᾶς Zhna's Zenas {dzay-nas'} probably contracted from a poetic form of 2203 and 1435; Jove-given; Zenas, a Christian:--Zenas. see GREEK for 2203 see GREEK for 1435

G2212.text: ζητέω zhtevw zeteo {dzay-teh'-o} of uncertain affinity; to seek (literally or figuratively); specially, (by Hebraism) to worship (God), or (in a bad sense) to plot (against life):--be (go) about, desire, endeavour, enquire (for), require, (X will) seek (after, for, means). Compare 4441. see GREEK for 4441

G2213.text: ζήτημα zhvthma zetema {dzay'-tay-mah} from 2212; a search (properly concretely), i.e. (in words) a debate:--question. see GREEK for 2212

G2214.text: ζήτησις zhvthsis zetesis {dzay'-tay-sis} from 2212; a searching (properly, the act), i.e. a dispute or its theme:--question. see GREEK for 2212

G2215.text: ζιζάνιον zizavnion zizanion {dziz-an'-ee-on} of uncertain origin; darnel or false grain:--tares.

G2216.text: Ζοροβαβέλ Zorobabevl Zorobabel {dzor-ob-ab'-el} of Hebrew origin (2216); Zorobabel (i.e. Zerubbabel), an Israelite:--Zorobabel. see HEBREW for 02216

G2217.text: ζόφος zovfos zophos {dzof'-os} akin to the base of 3509; gloom (as shrouding like a cloud):--blackness, darkness, mist. see GREEK for 3509

G2218.text: ζυγός zugovs zugos {dzoo-gos'} from the root of zeugnumi (to join, especially by a "yoke"); a coupling, i.e. (figuratively) servitude (a law or obligation); also (literally) the beam of the balance (as connecting the scales):--pair of balances, yoke.

G2219.text: ζύμη zuvmh zume {dzoo'-may} probably from 2204; ferment (as if boiling up):--leaven. see GREEK for 2204

G2220.text: ζυμόω zumovw zumoo {dzoo-mo'-o} from 2219; to cause to ferment:--leaven. see GREEK for 2219

G2221.text: ζωγρέω zwgrevw zogreo {dzogue-reh'-o} from the same as 2226 and 64; to take alive (make a prisoner of war), i.e. (figuratively) to capture or ensnare:--take captive, catch. see GREEK for 2226 see GREEK for 64

G2222.text: ζωή zwhv zoe {dzo-ay'} from 2198; life (literally or figuratively):--life(-time). Compare 5590. see GREEK for 2198 see GREEK for 5590

G2223.text: ζώνη zwvnh zone {dzo'-nay} probably akin to the base of 2218; a belt; by implication, a pocket:--girdle, purse. see GREEK for 2218

G2224.text: ζώννυμι ζωννύω zwvnnumi zwnnuvw zonnumi {dzone'-noo-mi} or zonnuo {dzone-noo'-o} from 2223; to bind about (especially with a belt):--gird. see GREEK for 2223

G2225.text: ζῳογονέω zw/ogonevw zoogoneo {dzo-og-on-eh'-o} from the same as 2226 and a derivative of 1096; to engender alive, i.e. (by analogy) to rescue (passively, be saved) from death:--live, preserve. see GREEK for 2226 see GREEK for 1096

G2226.text: ζῷον zw'/on zoon {dzo'-on} neuter of a derivative of 2198; a live thing, i.e. an animal:--beast. see GREEK for 2198

G2227.text: ζῳοποιέω zw/opoievw zoopoieo {dzo-op-oy-eh'-o} from the same as 2226 and 4160; to (re-)vitalize (literally or figuratively):--make alive, give life, quicken. see GREEK for 2226 see GREEK for 4160

G2228.text: ἤ h[ e {ay} a primary particle of distinction between two connected terms; disjunctive, or; comparative, than:--and, but (either), (n-)either, except it be, (n-)or (else), rather, save, than, that, what, yea. Often used in connection with other particles. Compare especially 2235, 2260, 2273. see GREEK for 2235 see GREEK for 2260 see GREEK for 2273

G2229.text: εἰ eij e {ay} an adverb of confirmation; perhaps intensive of 2228; used only (in the New Testament) before 3303; assuredly:--surely. see GREEK for 2228 see GREEK for 3303

G2230.text: ἡγεμονεύω hJgemoneuvw hegemoneuo {hayg-em-on-yoo'-o} from 2232; to act as ruler:--be governor. see GREEK for 2232

G2231.text: ἡγεμονία hJgemoniva hegemonia {hayg-em-on-ee'-ah} from 2232; government, i.e. (in time) official term:--reign. see GREEK for 2232

G2232.text: ἡγεμών hJgemwvn hegemon {hayg-em-ohn'} from 2233; a leader, i.e. chief person (or figuratively, place) of a province:--governor, prince, ruler. see GREEK for 2233

G2233.text: ἡγέομαι hJgevomai hegeomai {hayg-eh'-om-ahee} middle voice of a (presumed) strengthened form of 71; to lead, i.e. command (with official authority); figuratively, to deem, i.e. consider:--account, (be) chief, count, esteem, governor, judge, have the rule over, suppose, think. see GREEK for 71

G2234.text: ἡδέως hJdevws hedeos {hay-deh'-oce} adverb from a derivative of the base of 2237; sweetly, i.e. (figuratively) with pleasure:--gladly. see GREEK for 2237

G2235.text: ἤδη h[dh ede {ay'-day} apparently from 2228 (or possibly 2229) and 1211; even now:--already, (even) now (already), by this time. see GREEK for 2228 see GREEK for 2229 see GREEK for 1211

G2236.text: ἡδέως hJdevws hedista {hay'-dis-tah} neuter plural of the superlative of the same as 2234; with great pleasure:--most (very) gladly. see GREEK for 2234

G2237.text: ἡδονή hJdonhv hedone {hay-don-ay'} from handano (to please); sensual delight; by implication, desire:--lust, pleasure.

G2238.text: ἡδύοσμον hJduvosmon heduosmon {hay-doo'-os-mon} neuter of the compound of the same as 2234 and 3744; a sweet-scented plant, i.e. mint:--mint. see GREEK for 2234 see GREEK for 3744

G2239.text: ἦθος h\\qos ethos {ay'-thos} a strengthened form of 1485; usage, i.e. (plural) moral habits:--manners. see GREEK for 1485

G2240.text: ἥκω h&kw heko {hay'-ko} a primary verb; to arrive, i.e. be present (literally or figuratively):--come.

G2241.text: Ἠλί Hjliv eli {ay-lee'} of Hebrew origin (410 with pronominal suffix); my God:-- Eli. see HEBREW for 0410

G2242.text: Ἠλί Hjliv Heli {hay-lee'} of Hebrew origin (5941); Heli (i.e. Eli), an Israelite:--Heli. see HEBREW for 05941

G2243.text: Ἠλίας Hjlivas Helias {hay-lee'-as} of Hebrew origin (452); Helias (i.e. Elijah), an Israelite:--Elias. see HEBREW for 0452

G2244.text: ἡλικία hJlikiva helikia {hay-lik-ee'-ah} from the same as 2245; maturity (in years or size):--age, stature. see GREEK for 2245

G2245.text: ἡλίκος hJlivkos helikos {hay-lee'-kos} from helix (a comrade, i.e. one of the same age); as big as, i.e. (interjectively) how much:--how (what) great.

G2246.text: ἥλιος h&lios helios {hay'-lee-os} from hele (a ray; perhaps akin to the alternate of 138); the sun; by implication, light:--+ east, sun. see GREEK for 138

G2247.text: ἧλος h|los helos {hay'-los} of uncertain affinity; a stud, i.e. spike:--nail.

G2248.text: ἐγώ ejgwv hemas {hay-mas'} accusative case plural of 1473; us:--our, us, we. see GREEK for 1473

G2249.text: ἐγώ ejgwv hemeis {hay-mice'} nominative plural of 1473; we (only used when emphatic):--us, we (ourselves). see GREEK for 1473

G2250.text: ἡμέρα hJmevra hemera {hay-mer'-ah} feminine (with 5610 implied) of a derivative of hemai (to sit; akin to the base of 1476) meaning tame, i.e. gentle; day, i.e. (literally) the time space between dawn and dark, or the whole 24 hours (but several days were usually reckoned by the Jews as inclusive of the parts of both extremes); figuratively, a period (always defined more or less clearly by the context):--age, + alway, (mid-)day (by day, (-ly)), + for ever, judgment, (day) time, while, years. see GREEK for 5610 see GREEK for 1476

G2251.text: ἡμέτερος hJmevteros hemeteros {hay-met'-er-os} from 2349; our:--our, your (by a different reading). see GREEK for 2349

G2252.text: εἰμί eijmiv emen {ay'-mane} a prolonged form of 2358; I was:--be, was. (Sometimes unexpressed). see GREEK for 2358

G2253.text: ἡμιθανής hJmiqanhvs hemithanes {hay-mee-than-ace'} from a presumed compound of the base of 2255 and 2348; half dead, i.e. entirely exhausted:--half dead. see GREEK for 2255 see GREEK for 2348

G2254.text: ἐγώ ejgwv hemin {hay-meen'} dative case plural of 1473; to (or for, with, by) us:--our, (for) us, we. see GREEK for 1473

G2255.text: ἥμισυς h&misus hemisu {hay'-mee-soo} neuter of a derivative from an inseparable prefix akin to 260 (through the idea of partition involved in connection) and meaning semi-; (as noun) half:--half. see GREEK for 260

G2256.text: "ἡμίωρον, ἡμίωριον","hJmivwron hJmivwrion" hemiorion {hay-mee-o'-ree-on} from the base of 2255 and 5610; a half-hour:--half an hour. see GREEK for 2255 see GREEK for 5610

G2257.text: ἐγώ ejgwv hemon {hay-mone'} genitive case plural of 1473; of (or from) us:--our (company), us, we. see GREEK for 1473

G2258.text: εἰμί eijmiv en {ane} imperfect of 1510; I (thou, etc.) was (wast or were):--+ agree, be, X have (+ charge of), hold, use, was(-t), were. see GREEK for 1510

G2259.text: ἡνίκα hJnivka henika {hay-nee'-kah} of uncertain affinity; at which time:--when.

G2260.text: ἤπερ h[per eper {ay'-per} from 2228 and 4007; than at all (or than perhaps, than indeed):--than. see GREEK for 2228 see GREEK for 4007

G2261.text: ἤπιος h[pios epios {ay'-pee-os} probably from 2031; properly, affable, i.e. mild or kind:--gentle. see GREEK for 2031

G2262.text: Ἤρ H[r Er {ayr} of Hebrew origin (6147); Er, an Israelite:--Er. see HEBREW for 06147

G2263.text: ἤρεμος h[remos eremos {ay'-rem-os} perhaps by transposition from 2048 (through the idea of stillness); tranquil:--quiet. see GREEK for 2048

G2264.text: Ἡρῴδης HJrwv/dhs Herodes {hay-ro'-dace} compound of heros (a "hero") and 1491; heroic; Herod, the name of four Jewish kings:--Herod. see GREEK for 1491

G2265.text: Ἡρῳδιανοί HJrw/dianoiv Herodianoi {hay-ro-dee-an-oy'} plural of a derivative of 2264; Herodians, i.e. partisans of Herod:--Herodians. see GREEK for 2264

G2266.text: Ἡρῳδιάς HJrw/diavs Herodias {hay-ro-dee-as'} from 2264; Herodias, a woman of the Heodian family:--Herodias. see GREEK for 2264

G2267.text: Ἡρῳδίων HJrw/divwn Herodion {hay-ro-dee'-ohn} from 2264; Herodion, a Christian:--Herodion. see GREEK for 2264

G2268.text: Ἠσαΐας Hjsai?as Hesaias {hay-sah-ee'-as} of Hebrew origin (3470); Hesaias (i.e. Jeshajah), an Israelite:--Esaias. see HEBREW for 03470

G2269.text: Ἠσαῦ Hjsau' Esau {ay-sow'} of Hebrew origin (6215); Esau, an Edomite:--Esau. see HEBREW for 06215

G2270.text: ἡσυχάζω hJsucavzw hesuchazo {hay-soo-khad'-zo} from the same as 2272; to keep still (intransitively), i.e. refrain from labor, meddlesomeness or speech:--cease, hold peace, be quiet, rest. see GREEK for 2272

G2271.text: ἡσυχία hJsuciva hesuchia {hay-soo-khee'-ah} feminine of 2272; (as noun) stillness, i.e. desistance from bustle or language:--quietness, silence. see GREEK for 2272

G2272.text: ἡσύχιος hJsuvcios hesuchios {hay-soo'-khee-os} a prolonged form of a compound probably of a derivative of the base of 1476 and perhaps 2192; properly, keeping one's seat (sedentary), i.e. (by implication) still (undisturbed, undisturbing):--peaceable, quiet. see GREEK for 1476 see GREEK for 2192

G2273.text: ἤτοι h[toi etoi {ay'-toy} from 2228 and 5104; either indeed:--whether. see GREEK for 2228 see GREEK for 5104

G2274.text: ἡττάομαι hJttavomai hettao {hayt-tah'-o} from the same as 2276; to make worse, i.e. vanquish (literally or figuratively); by implication, to rate lower:--be inferior, overcome. see GREEK for 2276

G2275.text: ἥττημα h&tthma hettema {hayt'-tay-mah} from 2274; a deterioration, i.e. (objectively) failure or (subjectively) loss:--diminishing, fault. see GREEK for 2274

G2276.text: ἥσσων h&sswn hetton {hate'-ton} neuter of comparative of heka (slightly) used for that of 2556; worse (as noun); by implication, less (as adverb):--less, worse. see GREEK for 2556

G2277.text: ἤτω eto eto {ay'-to} third person singular imperative of 1510; let him (or it) be:--let ... be. see GREEK for 1510

G2278.text: ἠχέω hjcevw echeo {ay-kheh'-o} from 2279; to make a loud noise, i.e. reverberate:--roar, sound. see GREEK for 2279

G2279.text: ἦχος h\\cos echos {ay'-khos} of uncertain affinity; a loud or confused noise ("echo"), i.e. roar; figuratively, a rumor:--fame, sound.

G2280.text: Θαδδαῖος Qaddai'os Thaddaios {thad-dah'-yos} of uncertain origin; Thaddaeus, one of the Apostles:--Thaddaeus.

G2281.text: θάλασσα qavlassa thalassa {thal'-as-sah} probably prolonged from 251; the sea (genitive case or specially):--sea. see GREEK for 251

G2282.text: θάλπω qavlpw thalpo {thal'-po} probably akin to thallo (to warm); to brood, i.e. (figuratively) to foster:--cherish.

G2283.text: Θαμάρ Qamavr Thamar {tham'-ar} of Hebrew origin (8559); Thamar (i.e. Tamar), an Israelitess:--Thamar. see HEBREW for 08559

G2284.text: θαμβέω qambevw thambeo {tham-beh'-o} from 2285; to stupefy (with surprise), i.e. astound:--amaze, astonish. see GREEK for 2285

G2285.text: θάμβος qavmbos thambos {tham'-bos} akin to an obsolete tapho (to dumbfound); stupefaction (by surprise), i.e. astonishment:--X amazed, + astonished, wonder.

G2286.text: θανάσιμον qanavsimon thanasimos {than-as'-ee-mos} from 2288; fatal, i.e. poisonous:--deadly. see GREEK for 2288

G2287.text: θανατηφόρος qanathfovros thanatephoros {than-at-ay'-for-os} from (the feminine form of) 2288 and 5342; death-bearing, i.e. fatal:--deadly. see GREEK for 2288 see GREEK for 5342

G2288.text: θάνατος qavnatos thanatos {than'-at-os} from 2348; (properly, an adjective used as a noun) death (literally or figuratively):--X deadly, (be...) death. see GREEK for 2348

G2289.text: θανατόω qanatovw thanatoo {than-at-o'-o} from 2288 to kill (literally or figuratively):--become dead, (cause to be) put to death, kill, mortify. see GREEK for 2288

G2290.text: θάπτω qavptw thapto {thap'-to} a primary verb; to celebrate funeral rites, i.e. inter:--bury.

G2291.text: Θάρα Qavra Thara {thar'-ah} of Hebrew origin (8646); Thara (i.e. Terach), the father of Abraham:--Thara. see HEBREW for 08646

G2292.text: θαρρέω qarrevw tharrheo {thar-hreh'-o} another form for 2293; to exercise courage:--be bold, X boldly, have confidence, be confident. Compare 5111. see GREEK for 2293 see GREEK for 5111

G2293.text: θαρσέω qarsevw tharseo {thar-seh'-o} from 2294; to have courage:--be of good cheer (comfort). Compare 2292. see GREEK for 2294 see GREEK for 2292

G2294.text: θάρσος qavrsos tharsos {thar'-sos} akin (by transposition) to thrasos (daring); boldness (subjectively):--courage.

G2295.text: θαῦμα qau'ma thauma {thos'-mah} apparently from a form of 2300; wonder (properly concrete; but by implication, abstract):--admiration. see GREEK for 2300

G2296.text: θαυμάζω qaumavzw thaumazo {thou-mad'-zo} from 2295; to wonder; by implication, to admire:--admire, have in admiration, marvel, wonder. see GREEK for 2295

G2297.text: θαυμάσιος qaumavsios thaumasios {thow-mas'-ee-os} from 2295; wondrous, i.e. (neuter as noun) a miracle:--wonderful thing. see GREEK for 2295

G2298.text: θαυμαστός qaumastovs thaumastos {thow-mas-tos'} from 2296; wondered at, i.e. (by implication) wonderful:--marvel(-lous). see GREEK for 2296

G2299.text: θεά qeav thea {theh-ah'} feminine of 2316; a female deity:--goddess. see GREEK for 2316

G2300.text: θεάομαι qeavomai theaomai {theh-ah'-om-ahee} a prolonged form of a primary verb; to look closely at, i.e. (by implication) perceive (literally or figuratively); by extension to visit:--behold, look (upon), see. Compare 3700. see GREEK for 3700

G2301.text: θεατρίζω qeatrivzw theatrizo {theh-at-rid'-zo} from 2302; to expose as a spectacle:--make a gazing stock. see GREEK for 2302

G2302.text: θέατρον qevatron theatron {theh'-at-ron} from 2300; a place for public show ("theatre"), i.e. general audience-room; by implication, a show itself (figuratively):--spectacle, theatre. see GREEK for 2300

G2303.text: θεῖον qei'on theion {thi'-on} probably neuter of 2304 (in its original sense of flashing); sulphur:--brimstone. see GREEK for 2304

G2304.text: θεῖος qei'os theios {thi'-os} from 2316; godlike (neuter as noun, divinity): - divine, godhead. see GREEK for 2316

G2305.text: θειότης qeiovths theiotes {thi-ot'-ace} from 2304; divinity (abstractly):--godhead. see GREEK for 2304

G2306.text: θειώδης qeiwvdhs theiodes {thi-o'-dace} from 2303 and 1491; sulphur-like, i.e. sulphurous:--brimstone. see GREEK for 2303

G2307.text: θέλημα qevlhma thelema {thel'-ay-mah} from the prolonged form of 2309; a determination (properly, the thing), i.e. (actively) choice (specially, purpose, decree; abstractly, volition) or (passively) inclination:-- desire, pleasure, will. see GREEK for 2309

G2308.text: θέλησις qevlhsis thelesis {thel'-ay-sis} from 2309; determination (properly, the act), i.e. option:--will. see GREEK for 2309

G2310.text: θεμέλιος θεμέλιον qemevlios qemevlion themelios {them-el'-ee-os} 或 themelion {them-el'-ee-on} from a derivative of 5087; something put down, i.e. a substruction (of a building, etc.), (literally or figuratively):--foundation. see GREEK for 5087

G2311.text: θεμελιόω qemeliovw themelioo {them-el-ee-o'-o} from 2310; to lay a basis for, i.e. (literally) erect, or (figuratively) consolidate:--(lay the) found(- ation), ground, settle. see GREEK for 2310

G2312.text: θεοδίδακτος qeodivdaktos theodidaktos {theh-od-id'-ak-tos} from 2316 and 1321; divinely instructed:--taught of God. see GREEK for 2316 see GREEK for 1321

G2313.text: εὔνοια ας ἡ eunoia theomacheo {theh-o-makh-eh'-o} from 2314; to resist deity:--fight against God. see GREEK for 2314

G2314.text: θεομάχος qeomavcos theomachos {theh-om'-akh-os} from 2316 and 3164; an opponent of deity:--to fight against God. see GREEK for 2316 see GREEK for 3164

G2315.text: θεόπνευστος qeovpneustos theopneustos {theh-op'-nyoo-stos} from 2316 and a presumed derivative of 4154; divinely breathed in:--given by inspiration of God. see GREEK for 2316 see GREEK for 4154

G2316.text: θεός qeovs theos {theh'-os} of uncertain affinity; a deity, especially (with 3588) the supreme Divinity; figuratively, a magistrate; by Hebraism, very:--X exceeding, God, god(-ly, -ward). see GREEK for 3588

G2317.text: θεοσέβεια qeosevbeia theosebeia {theh-os-eb'-i-ah} from 2318; devoutness, i.e. piety:--godliness. see GREEK for 2318

G2318.text: θεοσεβής qeosebhvs theosebes {theh-os-eb-ace'} from 2316 and 4576; reverent of God, i.e. pious:--worshipper of God. see GREEK for 2316 see GREEK for 4576

G2319.text: θεοστυγής qeostughvs theostuges {theh-os-too-gace'} from 2316 and the base of 4767; hateful to God, i.e. impious:--hater of God. see GREEK for 2316 see GREEK for 4767

G2320.text: θεότης qeovths theotes {theh-ot'-ace} from 2316; divinity (abstractly):--godhead. see GREEK for 2316

G2321.text: Θεόφιλος Qeovfilos Theophilos {theh-of'-il-os} from 2316 and 5384; friend of God; Theophilus, a Christian:--Theophilus. see GREEK for 2316 see GREEK for 5384

G2322.text: θεραπεία qerapeiva therapeia {ther-ap-i'-ah} from 2323; attendance (specially, medical, i.e. cure); figuratively and collectively, domestics:--healing, household. see GREEK for 2323

G2323.text: θεραπεύω qerapeuvw therapeuo {ther-ap-yoo'-o} from the same as 2324; to wait upon menially, i.e. (figuratively) to adore (God), or (specially) to relieve (of disease):--cure, heal, worship. see GREEK for 2324

G2324.text: θεράπων qeravpwn therapon {ther-ap'-ohn} apparently a participle from an otherwise obsolete derivative of the base of 2330; a menial attendant (as if cherishing):--servant. see GREEK for 2330

G2325.text: θερίζω qerivzw therizo {ther-id'-zo} from 2330 (in the sense of the crop); to harvest:--reap. see GREEK for 2330

G2326.text: θερισμός qerismovs therismos {ther-is-mos'} from 2325; reaping, i.e. the crop:--harvest. see GREEK for 2325

G2327.text: θεριστής qeristhvs theristes {ther-is-tace'} from 2325; a harvester:--reaper. see GREEK for 2325

G2328.text: θερμαίνω qermaivnw thermaino {ther-mah'-ee-no} from 2329; to heat (oneself):--(be) warm(-ed, self). see GREEK for 2329

G2329.text: θέρμη qevrmh therme {ther'-may} from the base of 2330; warmth:--heat. see GREEK for 2330

G2330.text: θέρος qevros theros {ther'-os} from a primary thero (to heat); properly, heat, i.e. summer:--summer.

G2331.text: Θεσσαλονικεύς Qessalonikeuvs Thessalonikeus {thes-sal-on-ik-yoos'} from 2332; a Thessalonican, i.e. inhabitant of Thessalonice:--Thessalonian. see GREEK for 2332

G2332.text: Θεσσαλονίκη Qessalonivkh Thessalonike {thes-sal-on-ee'-kay} from Thessalos (a Thessalian) and 3529; Thessalonice, a place in Asia Minor:--Thessalonica. see GREEK for 3529

G2333.text: Θευδᾶς Qeuda's Theudas {thyoo-das'} of uncertain origin; Theudas, an Israelite:--Theudas.

G2334.text: θεωρέω qewrevw theoreo {theh-o-reh'-o} from a derivative of 2300 (perhaps by addition of 3708); to be a spectator of, i.e. discern, (literally, figuratively (experience) or intensively (acknowledge)):--behold, consider, look on, perceive, see. Compare 3700. see GREEK for 2300 see GREEK for 3708 see GREEK for 3700

G2335.text: θεωρία qewriva theoria {theh-o-ree'-ah} from the same as 2334; spectatorship, i.e. (concretely) a spectacle:--sight. see GREEK for 2334

G2336.text: θήκη qhvkh theke {thay'-kay} from 5087; a receptacle, i.e. scabbard:--sheath. see GREEK for 5087

G2337.text: θηλάζω qhlavzw thelazo {thay-lad'-zo} from thele (the nipple); to suckle, (by implication) to suck:--(give) suck(-ling).

G2338.text: θῆλυς qh'lus thelus {thay'-loos} from the same as 2337; female:--female, woman. see GREEK for 2337

G2339.text: θήρα qhvra thera {thay'-rah} from ther (a wild animal, as game); hunting, i.e. (figuratively) destruction:--trap.

G2340.text: θηρεύω qhreuvw thereuo {thay-ryoo'-o} from 2339; to hunt (an animal), i.e. (figuratively) to carp at:--catch. see GREEK for 2339

G2341.text: θηριομαχέω qhriomacevw theriomacheo {thay-ree-om-akh-eh'-o} from a compound of 2342 and 3164; to be a beast-fighter (in the gladiatorial show), i.e. (figuratively) to encounter (furious men):--fight with wild beasts. see GREEK for 2342 see GREEK for 3164

G2342.text: θηρίον qhrivon therion {thay-ree'-on} diminutive from the same as 2339; a dangerous animal:--(venomous, wild) beast. see GREEK for 2339

G2343.text: θησαυρίζω qhsaurivzw thesaurizo {thay-sow-rid'-zo} from 2344; to amass or reserve (literally or figuratively):--lay up (treasure), (keep) in store, (heap) treasure (together, up). see GREEK for 2344

G2344.text: θησαυρός qhsaurovs thesauros {thay-sow-ros'} from 5087; a deposit, i.e. wealth (literally or figuratively):--treasure. see GREEK for 5087

G2345.text: θιγγάνω qiggavnw thiggano {thing-gan'-o} a prolonged form of an obsolete primary thigo (to finger); to manipulate, i.e. have to do with; by implication, to injure:--handle, touch.

G2346.text: θλίβω qlivbw thlibo {thlee'-bo} akin to the base of 5147; to crowd (literally or figuratively):--afflict, narrow, throng, suffer tribulation, trouble. see GREEK for 5147

G2347.text: θλῖψις qli'yis thlipsis {thlip'-sis} from 2346; pressure (literally or figuratively):--afflicted(-tion), anguish, burdened, persecution, tribulation, trouble. see GREEK for 2346

G2348.text: θνῄσκω qnhv/skw thnesko {thnay'-sko} a strengthened form of a simpler primary thano than'-o (which is used for it only in certain tenses); to die (literally or figuratively):--be dead, die.

G2349.text: θνητός qnhtovs thnetos {thnay-tos'} from 2348; liable to die:--mortal(-ity). see GREEK for 2348

G2350.text: θορυβέω qorubevw thorubeo {thor-oo-beh'-o} from 2351; to be in tumult, i.e. disturb, clamor:--make ado (a noise), trouble self, set on an uproar. see GREEK for 2351

G2351.text: θόρυβος qovrubos thorubos {thor'-oo-bos} from the base of 2360; a disturbance:--tumult, uproar. see GREEK for 2360

G2352.text: θραύω qrauvw thrauo {throw'-o} a primary verb; to crush:--bruise. Compare 4486. see GREEK for 4486

G2353.text: θρέμμα qrevmma thremma {threm'-mah} from 5142; stock (as raised on a farm):--cattle. see GREEK for 5142

G2354.text: θρηνέω qrhnevw threneo {thray-neh'-o} from 2355; to bewail:--lament, mourn. see GREEK for 2355

G2355.text: κλαυθμός klauqmovs threnos {thray'-nos} from the base of 2360; wailing:--lamentation. see GREEK for 2360

G2356.text: θρησκεία qrhskeiva threskeia {thrace-ki'-ah} from a derivative of 2357; ceremonial observance:--religion, worshipping. see GREEK for 2357

G2357.text: θρησκός qrhskovs threskos {thrace'-kos} probably from the base of 2360; ceremonious in worship (as demonstrative), i.e. pious:--religious. see GREEK for 2360

G2358.text: θριαμβεύω qriambeuvw thriambeuo {three-am-byoo'-o} from a prolonged compound of the base of 2360; and a derivative of 680 (meaning a noisy iambus, sung in honor of Bacchus); to make an acclamatory procession, i.e. (figuratively) to conquer or (by Hebraism) to give victory:--(cause) to triumph (over). see GREEK for 2360 see GREEK for 680

G2359.text: θρίξ qrivx thrix {threeks} genitive case trichos, etc.; of uncertain derivation; hair:--hair. Compare 2864. see GREEK for 2864

G2360.text: θροέω qroevw throeo {thro-eh'-o} from threomai to wail; to clamor, i.e. (by implication) to frighten:--trouble.

G2361.text: θρόμβος qrovmbos thrombos {throm'-bos} perhaps from 5142 (in the sense of thickening); a clot:--great drop. see GREEK for 5142

G2362.text: θρόνος qrovnos thronos {thron'-os} from thrao (to sit); a stately seat ("throne"); by implication, power or (concretely) a potentate:--seat, throne.

G2363.text: Θυάτιρα Quavtira Thuateira {thoo-at'-i-rah} of uncertain derivation; Thyatira, a place in Asia Minor:--Thyatira.

G2364.text: θυγάτηρ qugavthr thugater {thoo-gat'-air} apparently a primary word (compare "daughter"); a female child, or (by Hebraism) descendant (or inhabitant):--daughter.

G2365.text: θυγάτριον qugavtrion thugatrion {thoo-gat'-ree-on} from 2364; a daughterling:--little (young) daughter. see GREEK for 2364

G2366.text: θύελλα quvella thuella {thoo'-el-lah} from 2380 (in the sense of blowing) a storm:--tempest. see GREEK for 2380

G2367.text: θύϊνος quvi>nos thuinos {thoo'-ee-nos} from a derivative of 2380 (in the sense of blowing; denoting a certain fragrant tree); made of citron-wood:--thyine. see GREEK for 2380

G2368.text: θυμίαμα qumivama thumiama {thoo-mee'-am-ah} from 2370; an aroma, i.e. fragrant powder burnt in religious service; by implication, the burning itself:--incense, odour. see GREEK for 2370

G2369.text: θυμιατήριον qumiathvrion thumiasterion {thoo-mee-as-tay'-ree-on} from a derivative of 2370; a place of fumigation, i.e. the alter of incense (in the Temple):--censer. see GREEK for 2370

G2370.text: θυμιάω qumiavw thumiao {thoo-mee-ah'-o} from a derivative of 2380 (in the sense of smoking); to fumigate, i.e. offer aromatic fumes:--burn incense. see GREEK for 2380

G2371.text: θυμομαχέω qumomacevw thumomacheo {thoo-mom-akh-eh'-o} from a presumed compound of 2372 and 3164; to be in a furious fight, i.e. (figuratively) to be exasperated:--be highly displeased. see GREEK for 2372 see GREEK for 3164

G2372.text: θυμός qumovs thumos {thoo-mos'} from 2380; passion (as if breathing hard):--fierceness, indignation, wrath. Compare 5590. see GREEK for 2380 see GREEK for 5590

G2373.text: θυμόω qumovw thumoo {tho-mo'-o} from 2372; to put in a passion, i.e. enrage:--be wroth. see GREEK for 2372

G2374.text: θύρα quvra thura {thoo'-rah} apparently a primary word (compare "door"); a portal or entrance (the opening or the closure, literally or figuratively):--door, gate.

G2375.text: θυρεός qureovs thureos {thoo-reh-os'} from 2374; a large shield (as door-shaped):--shield. see GREEK for 2374

G2376.text: θυρίς qurivs thuris {thoo-rece'} from 2374; an aperture, i.e. window:--window. see GREEK for 2374

G2377.text: θυρωρός qurwrovs thuroros {thoo-ro-ros'} from 2374 and ouros (a watcher); a gate- warden:--that kept the door, porter. see GREEK for 2374

G2378.text: θυσία qusiva thusia {thoo-see'-ah} from 2380; sacrifice (the act or the victim, literally or figuratively):--sacrifice. see GREEK for 2380

G2379.text: θυσιαστήριον qusiasthvrion thusiasterion {thoo-see-as-tay'-ree-on} from a derivative of 2378; a place of sacrifice, i.e. an altar (special or genitive case, literal or figurative):--altar. see GREEK for 2378

G2380.text: θύω quvw thuo {thoo'-o} a primary verb; properly, to rush (breathe hard, blow, smoke), i.e. (by implication) to sacrifice (properly, by fire, but genitive case); by extension to immolate (slaughter for any purpose):--kill, (do) sacrifice, slay.

G2381.text: Θωμᾶς Qwma's Thomas {tho-mas'} of Chaldee origin (compare 8380); the twin; Thomas, a Christian:--Thomas. see HEBREW for 08380

G2382.text: θώραξ qwvrax thorax {tho'-rax} of uncertain affinity; the chest ("thorax"), i.e. (by implication) a corslet:--breast-plate.

G2383.text: Ἰάϊρος Ijavi>ros Iaeiros {ee-ah'-i-ros} of Hebrew origin (2971); Jairus (i.e. Jair), an Israelite:--Jairus. see HEBREW for 02971

G2384.text: Ἰακώβ Ijakwvb Iakob {ee-ak-obe'} of Hebrew origin (3290); Jacob (i.e. Ja`akob), the progenitor of the Israelites:--also an Israelite:--Jacob. see HEBREW for 03290

G2385.text: Ἰάκωβος Ijavkwbos Iakobos {ee-ak'-o-bos} the same as 2384 Graecized; Jacobus, the name of three Israelites:--James. see GREEK for 2384

G2386.text: ἴαμα i[ama iama {ee'-am-ah} from 2390; a cure (the effect):--healing. see GREEK for 2390

G2387.text: Ἰαμβρῆς Ijambrh's Iambres {ee-am-brace'} of Egyptian origin; Jambres, an Egyptian:--Jambres.

G2388.text: Ἰανναί Ijannaiv Ianna {ee-an-nah'} probably of Hebrew origin (compare 3238); Janna, an Israelite:--Janna. see HEBREW for 03238

G2389.text: Ἰάννης Ijavnnhs Iannes {ee-an-nace'} of Egyptian origin; Jannes, an Egyptian:--Jannes.

G2390.text: ἰάομαι ijavomai iaomai {ee-ah'-om-ahee} middle voice of apparently a primary verb; to cure (literally or figuratively):--heal, make whole.

G2391.text: Ἰάρετ Ijavret Iared {ee-ar'-ed} of Hebrew origin (3382); Jared (i.e. Jered), an antediluvian:--Jared. see HEBREW for 03382

G2392.text: ἴασις i[asis iasis {ee'-as-is} from 2390; curing (the act):--cure, heal(-ing). see GREEK for 2390

G2393.text: ἴασπις i[aspis iaspis {ee'-as-pis} probably of foreign origin (see 3471); "jasper", a gem:--jasper. see HEBREW for 03471

G2394.text: Ἰάσων Ijavswn Iason {ee-as'-oan} future active participle masculine of 2390; about to cure; Jason, a Christian:--Jason. see GREEK for 2390

G2395.text: ἰατρός ijatrovs iatros {ee-at-ros'} from 2390; a physician:--physician. see GREEK for 2390

G2396.text: ἴδε i[de ide {id'-eh} second person singular imperative active of 1492; used as an interjection to denote surprise; lo!:--behold, lo, see. see GREEK for 1492

G2397.text: εἰδέα eijdeva idea {id-eh'-ah} from 1492; a sight (comparative figuratively "idea"), i.e. aspect:--countenance. see GREEK for 1492

G2398.text: ἴδιος i[dios idios {id'-ee-os} of uncertain affinity; pertaining to self, i.e. one's own; by implication, private or separate:--X his acquaintance, when they were alone, apart, aside, due, his (own, proper, several), home, (her, our, thine, your) own (business), private(-ly), proper, severally, their (own).

G2399.text: ἰδιώτης ijdiwvths idiotes {id-ee-o'-tace} from 2398; a private person, i.e. (by implication) an ignoramus (compare "idiot"):--ignorant, rude, unlearned. see GREEK for 2398

G2400.text: ἰδού ijdouv idou {id-oo'} second person singular imperative middle voice of 1492; used as imperative lo!; --behold, lo, see. see GREEK for 1492

G2401.text: Ἰδουμαία Ijdoumaiva Idoumaia {id-oo-mah'-yah} of Hebrew origin (123); Idumaea (i.e. Edom), a region East (and South) of Palestine:--Idumaea. see HEBREW for 0123

G2402.text: ἱδρώς iJdrwvs hidros {hid-roce'} a strengthened form of a primary idos (sweat): perspiration:--sweat.

G2403.text: Ἰεζάβελ Ijezavbel Iezabel {ee-ed-zab-ale'} of Hebrew origin (348); Jezabel (i.e. Jezebel), a Tyrian woman (used as a synonym of a termagant or false teacher):--Jezabel. see HEBREW for 0348

G2404.text: Ἱεράπολις IJeravpolis Hierapolis {hee-er-ap'-ol-is} from 2413 and 4172; holy city; Hierapolis, a place in Asia Minor:--Hierapolis. see GREEK for 2413 see GREEK for 4172

G2405.text: ἱερατεία iJerateiva hierateia {hee-er-at-i'-ah} from 2407; priestliness, i.e. the sacerdotal function:--office of the priesthood, priest's office. see GREEK for 2407

G2406.text: ἱεράτευμα iJeravteuma hierateuma {hee-er-at'-yoo-mah} from 2407; the priestly fraternity, i.e. sacerdotal order (figuratively):--priesthood. see GREEK for 2407

G2407.text: ἱερατεύω iJerateuvw hierateuo {hee-er-at-yoo'-o} prolongation from 2409; to be a priest, i.e. perform his functions:--execute the priest's office. see GREEK for 2409

G2408.text: Ἰερεμίας Ijeremivas Ieremias {hee-er-em-ee'-as} of Hebrew origin (3414); Hieremias (i.e. Jermijah), an Israelite:--Jeremiah. see HEBREW for 03414

G2409.text: ἱερεύς iJereuvs hiereus {hee-er-yooce'} from 2413; a priest (literally or figuratively):--(high) priest. see GREEK for 2413

G2410.text: Ἰεριχώ Ijericwv Hiericho {hee-er-ee-kho'} of Hebrew origin (3405); Jericho, a place in Palestine:--Jericho. see HEBREW for 03405

G2411.text: ἱερόν iJerovn hieron {hee-er-on'} neuter of 2413; a sacred place, i.e. the entire precincts (whereas 3485 denotes the central sanctuary itself) of the Temple (at Jerusalem or elsewhere):--temple. see GREEK for 2413 see GREEK for 3485

G2412.text: ἱεροπρεπής iJeroprephvs hieroprepes {hee-er-op-rep-ace'} from 2413 and the same as 4241; reverent:--as becometh holiness. see GREEK for 2413 see GREEK for 4241

G2413.text: ἱερός iJerovs hieros {hee-er-os'} of uncertain affinity; sacred:--holy.

G2414.text: Ἱεροσόλυμα Ἰερουσαλήμ IJerosovluma Ijerousalhvm Hierosoluma {hee-er-os-ol'-oo-mah} of Hebrew origin (3389); Hierosolyma (i.e. Jerushalaim}, the capitol of Palestine:--Jerusalem. Compare 2419. see GREEK for 2419 see HEBREW for 03389

G2415.text: Ἱεροσολυμίτης IJerosolumivths Hierosolumites {hee-er-os-ol-oo-mee'-tace} from 2414; a Hierosolymite, i.e. inhabitant of Hierosolyma:--of Jerusalem. see GREEK for 2414

G2416.text: ἱεροσυλέω iJerosulevw hierosuleo {hee-er-os-ool-eh'-o} from 2417; to be a temple-robber (figuratively):--commit sacrilege. see GREEK for 2417

G2417.text: ἱερόσυλος iJerovsulos hierosulos {hee-er-os'-oo-los} from 2411 and 4813; a temple-despoiler:--robber of churches. see GREEK for 2411 see GREEK for 4813

G2418.text: ἱερουργέω iJerourgevw hierourgeo {hee-er-oorg-eh'-o} from a compound of 2411 and the base of 2041; to be a temple-worker, i.e. officiate as a priest (figuratively):--minister. see GREEK for 2411 see GREEK for 2041

G2419.text: Ἱεροσόλυμα IJerosovluma Hierousalem {hee-er-oo-sal-ame'} of Hebrew origin (3389); Hierusalem (i.e. Jerushalem), the capitol of Palestine:--Jerusalem. Compare 2414. see GREEK for 2414 see HEBREW for 03389

G2420.text: ἱερωσύνη iJerwsuvnh hierosune {hee-er-o-soo'-nay} from 2413; sacredness, i.e. (by implication) the priestly office:--priesthood. see GREEK for 2413

G2421.text: Ἰεσσαί Ijessaiv Iessai {es-es-sah'-ee} of Hebrew origin (3448); Jessae (i.e. Jishai), an Israelite:--Jesse. see HEBREW for 03448

G2422.text: Ἰεφθάε Ijefqave Iephthae {ee-ef-thah'-eh} of Hebrew origin (3316); Jephthae (i.e. Jiphtach), an Israelite:--Jephthah. see HEBREW for 03316

G2423.text: Ἰεχονίας Ijeconivas Iechonias {ee-ekh-on-ee'-as} of Hebrew origin (3204); Jechonias (i.e. Jekonjah), an Israelite:--Jechonias. see HEBREW for 03204

G2424.text: Ἰησοῦς Ijhsou's Iesous {ee-ay-sooce'} of Hebrew origin (3091); Jesus (i.e. Jehoshua), the name of our Lord and two (three) other Israelites:--Jesus. see HEBREW for 03091

G2425.text: ἱκανός iJkanovs hikanos {hik-an-os'} from hiko (hikano or hikneomai, akin to 2240) (to arrive); competent (as if coming in season), i.e. ample (in amount) or fit (in character):--able, + content, enough, good, great, large, long (while), many, meet, much, security, sore, sufficient, worthy. see GREEK for 2240

G2426.text: ἱκανότης iJkanovths hikanotes {hik-an-ot'-ace} from 2425; ability:--sufficiency. see GREEK for 2425

G2427.text: ἱκανόω iJkanovw hikanoo {hik-an-o'-o} from 2425; to enable, i.e. qualify:--make able (meet). see GREEK for 2425

G2428.text: ἱκετηρία iJkethriva hiketeria {hik-et-ay-ree'-ah} from a derivative of the base of 2425 (through the idea of approaching for a favor); intreaty:--supplication. see GREEK for 2425

G2429.text: ἰκμάς ijkmavs hikmas {hik-mas'} of uncertain affinity; dampness:--moisture.

G2430.text: Ἰκόνιον Ijkovnion Ikonion {ee-kon'-ee-on} perhaps from 1504; image-like; Iconium, a place in Asia Minor:--Iconium. see GREEK for 1504

G2431.text: ἱλαρός iJlarovs hilaros {hil-ar-os'} from the same as 2436; propitious or merry ("hilarious"), i.e. prompt or willing:--cheerful. see GREEK for 2436

G2432.text: ἱλαρότης iJlarovths hilarotes {hil-ar-ot'-ace} from 2431; alacrity:--cheerfulness. see GREEK for 2431

G2433.text: ἱλάσκομαι iJlavskomai hilaskomai {hil-as'-kom-ahee} middle voice from the same as 2436; to conciliate, i.e. (transitively) to atone for (sin), or (intransitively) be propitious:--be merciful, make reconciliation for. see GREEK for 2436

G2434.text: ἱλασμός iJlasmovs hilasmos {hil-as-mos'} atonement, i.e. (concretely) an expiator:--propitiation.

G2435.text: ἱλαστήριον iJlasthvrion hilasterion {hil-as-tay'-ree-on} neuter of a derivative of 2433; an expiatory (place or thing), i.e. (concretely) an atoning victim, or (specially) the lid of the Ark (in the Temple):--mercyseat, propitiation. see GREEK for 2433

G2436.text: ἵλεως i&lews hileos {hil'-eh-oce} perhaps from the alternate form of 138; cheerful (as attractive), i.e. propitious; adverbially (by Hebraism) God be gracious!, i.e. (in averting some calamity) far be it:--be it far, merciful. see GREEK for 138

G2437.text: Ἰλλυρικόν Ijllurikovn Illurikon {il-loo-ree-kon'} neuter of an adjective from a name of uncertain derivation: (the) Illyrican (shore), i.e. (as a name itself) Illyricum, a region of Europe:--Illyricum.

G2438.text: ἱμάς iJmavs himas {hee-mas'} perhaps from the same as 260; a strap, i.e. (specially) the tie (of a sandal) or the lash (of a scourge):--latchet, thong. see GREEK for 260

G2439.text: ἱματίζω iJmativzw himatizo {him-at-id'-zo} from 2440; to dress:--clothe. see GREEK for 2440

G2440.text: ἱμάτιον iJmavtion himation {him-at'-ee-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of ennumi (to put on); a dress (inner or outer):--apparel, cloke, clothes, garment, raiment, robe, vesture.

G2441.text: ἱματισμός iJmatismovs himatismos {him-at-is-mos'} from 2439; clothing:--apparel (X -led), array, raiment, vesture. see GREEK for 2439

G2442.text: ὁμείρομαι oJmeivromai himeiromai {him-i'-rom-ahee} 或 homeiromai {hom-i'rom-ahee} middle voice from himeros (a yearning; of uncertain affinity); to long for:--be affectionately desirous.

G2443.text: ἵνα i&na hina {hin'-ah} probably from the same as the former part of 1438 (through the demonstrative idea; compare 3588); in order that (denoting the purpose or the result):--albeit, because, to the intent (that), lest, so as, (so) that, (for) to. Compare 3363. see GREEK for 1438 see GREEK for 3588 see GREEK for 3363

G2444.text: ἱνατί iJnativ hinati {hin-at-ee'} from 2443 and 5101; for what reason ?, i.e. why?:--wherefore, why. see GREEK for 2443 see GREEK for 5101

G2445.text: Ἰόππη Ijovpph Ioppe {ee-op'-pay} of Hebrew origin (3305); Joppe (i.e. Japho), a place in Palestine:--Joppa. see HEBREW for 03305

G2446.text: Ἰορδάνης Ijordavnhs Iordanes {ee-or-dan'-ace} of Hebrew origin (3383); the Jordanes (i.e. Jarden), a river of Palestine:--Jordan. see HEBREW for 03383

G2447.text: ἰός ijovs ios {ee-os'} perhaps from eimi (to go) or hiemi (to send); rust (as if emitted by metals); also venom (as emitted by serpents):--poison, rust.

G2448.text: Ἰούδας Ijouvdas Iouda {ee-oo-dah'} of Hebrew origin (3063 or perhaps 3194); Judah (i.e. Jehudah or Juttah), a part of (or place in) Palestine:--Judah. see HEBREW for 03063 see HEBREW for 03194

G2449.text: Ἰουδαία Ijoudaiva Ioudaia {ee-oo-dah'-yah} feminine of 2453 (with 1093 implied); the Judaean land (i.e. Judaea), a region of Palestine:--Judaea. see GREEK for 2453 see GREEK for 1093

G2450.text: ἰουδαΐζω ijoudai?zw Ioudaizo {ee-oo-dah-id'-zo} from 2453; to become a Judaean, i.e. "Judaize":--live as the Jews. see GREEK for 2453

G2451.text: Ἰουδαϊκός Ijoudai>kovs Ioudaikos {ee-oo-dah-ee-kos'} from 2453; Judaic, i.e. resembling a Judaean:--Jewish. see GREEK for 2453

G2452.text: Ἰουδαϊκός Ijoudai>kovs Ioudaikos {ee-oo-dah-ee-koce'} adverb from 2451; Judaically or in a manner resembling a Judaean:--as do the Jews. see GREEK for 2451

G2453.text: Ἰουδαῖος Ijoudai'os Ioudaios {ee-oo-dah'-yos} from 2448 (in the sense of 2455 as a country); Judaean, i.e. belonging to Jehudah:--Jew(-ess), of Judaea. see GREEK for 2448 see GREEK for 2455

G2454.text: Ἰουδαϊσμός Ijoudai>smovs Ioudaismos {ee-oo-dah-is-mos'} from 2450; "Judaism", i.e. the Jewish faith and usages:--Jews' religion. see GREEK for 2450

G2455.text: Ἰούδας Ἰωδά Ijouvdas Ijwdav Ioudas {ee-oo-das'} of Hebrew origin (3063); Judas (i.e. Jehudah), the name of ten Israelites; also of the posterity of one of them and its region:--Juda(-h, -s); Jude. see HEBREW for 03063

G2456.text: Ἰουλία Ijouliva Ioulia {ee-oo-lee'-ah} feminine of the same as 2457; Julia, a Christian woman:--Julia. see GREEK for 2457

G2457.text: Ἰούλιος Ijouvlios Ioulios {ee-oo'-lee-os} of Latin origin; Julius, a centurion:--Julius.

G2458.text: Ἰουνιᾶς Ijounia's Iounias {ee-oo-nee'-as} of Latin origin; Junias, a Christian:--Junias.

G2459.text: Ἰοῦστος Ijou'stos Ioustos {ee-ooce'-tos} of Latin origin ("just"); Justus, the name of three Christian:--Justus.

G2460.text: ἱππεύς iJppeuvs hippeus {hip-yooce'} from 2462; an equestrian, i.e. member of a cavalry corps:--horseman. see GREEK for 2462

G2461.text: ἱππικόν iJppikovn hippikon {hip-pee-kon'} neuter of a derivative of 2462; the cavalry force:--horse(-men). see GREEK for 2462

G2462.text: ἵππος i&ppos hippos {hip'-pos} of uncertain affinity; a horse:--horse.

G2463.text: ἶρις i\\ris iris {ee'-ris} perhaps from 2046 (as a symbol of the female messenger of the pagan deities); a rainbow ("iris"):--rainbow. see GREEK for 2046

G2464.text: Ἰσαάκ Ijsaavk Isaak {ee-sah-ak'} of Hebrew origin (3327); Isaac (i.e. Jitschak), the son of Abraham:--Isaac. see HEBREW for 03327

G2465.text: ἰσάγγελος ijsavggelos isaggelos {ee-sang'-el-los} from 2470 and 32; like an angel, i.e. angelic:--equal unto the angels. see GREEK for 2470 see GREEK for 32

G2466.text: Ἰσσαχάρ Ijssacavr Isachar {ee-sakh-ar'} of Hebrew origin (3485); Isachar (i.e. Jissaskar), a son of Jacob (figuratively, his descendant):--Issachar. see HEBREW for 03485

G2467.text: οἶδα oi\\da isemi {is'-ay-mee} assumed by some as the base of certain irregular forms of 1942; to know:--know. see GREEK for 1942

G2468.text: οἶδα εἰμί oi\da eijmiv isthi {is'-thee} second person imperative present of 1510; be thou:--+ agree, be, X give thyself wholly to. see GREEK for 1510

G2469.text: Ἰσκαριώθ Ἰσκαριώτης Ijskariwvq Ijskariwvths Iskariotes {is-kar-ee-o'-tace} of Hebrew origin (probably 377 and 7149); inhabitant of Kerioth; Iscariotes (i.e. Keriothite), an epithet of Judas the traitor:--Iscariot. see HEBREW for 0377 see HEBREW for 07149

G2470.text: ἴσος i[sos isos {ee'-sos} probably from 1492 (through the idea of seeming); similar (in amount and kind):--+ agree, as much, equal, like. see GREEK for 1492

G2471.text: ἰσότης ijsovths isotes {ee-sot'-ace} likeness (in condition or proportion); by implication, equity:--equal(-ity).

G2472.text: ἰσότιμος ijsovtimos isotimos {ee-sot'-ee-mos} from 2470 and 5092; of equal value or honor:--like precious. see GREEK for 2470 see GREEK for 5092

G2473.text: ἰσόψυχος ijsovyucos isopsuchos {ee-sop'-soo-khos} from 2470 and 5590; of similar spirit:--likeminded. see GREEK for 2470 see GREEK for 5590

G2474.text: Ἰσραήλ Ijsrahvl Israel {is-rah-ale'} of Hebrew origin (3478); Israel (i.e. Jisrael), the adopted name of Jacob, including his descendants (literally or figuratively):--Israel. see HEBREW for 03478

G2475.text: Ἰσραηλίτης Ijsrahlivths Israelites {is-rah-ale-ee'-tace} from 2474; an "Israelite", i.e. descendant of Israel (literally or figuratively):--Israelite. see GREEK for 2474

G2476.text: ἵστημι i&sthmi histemi {his'-tay-mee} a prolonged form of a primary stao stah'-o (of the same meaning, and used for it in certain tenses); to stand (transitively or intransitively), used in various applications (literally or figuratively):--abide, appoint, bring, continue, covenant, establish, hold up, lay, present, set (up), stanch, stand (by, forth, still, up). Compare 5087. see GREEK for 5087

G2477.text: ἱστορέω iJstorevw historeo {his-tor-eh'-o} from a derivative of 1492; to be knowing (learned), i.e. (by implication) to visit for information (interview):--see. see GREEK for 1492

G2478.text: ἰσχυρός ijscurovs ischuros {is-khoo-ros'} from 2479; forcible (literally or figuratively):--boisterous, mighty(-ier), powerful, strong(-er, man), valiant. see GREEK for 2479

G2479.text: ἰσχύς ijscuvs ischus {is-khoos'} from a derivative of is (force; compare eschon, a form of 2192); forcefulness (literally or figuratively):--ability, might(-ily), power, strength. see GREEK for 2192

G2480.text: ἰσχύω ijscuvw ischuo {is-khoo'-o} from 2479; to have (or exercise) force (literally or figuratively):--be able, avail, can do(-not), could, be good, might, prevail, be of strength, be whole, + much work. see GREEK for 2479

G2481.text: ἴσως i[sws isos {ee'-soce} adverb from 2470; likely, i.e. perhaps:--it may be. see GREEK for 2470

G2482.text: Ἰταλία Ijtaliva Italia {ee-tal-ee'-ah} probably of foreign origin; Italia, a region of Europe:--Italy.

G2483.text: Ἰταλικός Ijtalikovs Italikos {ee-tal-ee-kos'} from 2482; Italic, i.e. belonging to Italia:--Italian. see GREEK for 2482

G2484.text: Ἰτουραῖος Ijtourai'os Itouraia {ee-too-rah'-yah} of Hebrew origin (3195); Ituraea (i.e. Jetur), a region of Palestine:--Ituraea. see HEBREW for 03195

G2485.text: ἰχθύδιον ijcquvdion ichthudion {ikh-thoo'-dee-on} diminutive from 2486; a petty fish:--little (small) fish. see GREEK for 2486

G2486.text: ἰχθύς ijcquvs ichthus {ikh-thoos'} of uncertain affinity; a fish:--fish.

G2487.text: ἴχνος i[cnos ichnos {ikh'-nos} from ikneomai (to arrive; compare 2240); a track (figuratively):--step. see GREEK for 2240

G2488.text: Ἰωαθάμ Ijwaqavm Ioatham {ee-o-ath'-am} of Hebrew origin (3147); Joatham (i.e. Jotham), an Israelite:--Joatham. see HEBREW for 03147

G2489.text: Ἰωάννα Ijwavnna Ioanna {ee-o-an'-nah} feminine of the same as 2491; Joanna, a Christian:--Joanna. see GREEK for 2491

G2490.text: Ἰωανάν Ijwanavn Ioannas {ee-o-an-nas'} a form of 2491; Joannas, an Israelite:--Joannas. see GREEK for 2491

G2491.text: Ἰωάννης Ijwavnnhs Ioannes {ee-o-an'-nace} of Hebrew origin (3110); Joannes (i.e. Jochanan), the name of four Israelites:--John. see HEBREW for 03110

G2492.text: Ἰώβ Ijwvb Iob {ee-obe'} of Hebrew origin (347); Job (i.e. Ijob), a patriarch:--Job. see HEBREW for 0347

G2493.text: Ἰωήλ Ijwhvl Ioel {ee-o-ale'} of Hebrew origin (3100); Joel, an Israelite:--Joel. see HEBREW for 03100

G2494.text: Ἰωνάμ Ijwnavm Ionan {ee-o-nan'} probably for 2491 or 2495; Jonan, an Israelite:--Jonan. see GREEK for 2491 see GREEK for 2495

G2495.text: Ἰωνᾶς Ijwna's Ionas {ee-o-nas'} of Hebrew origin (3124); Jonas (i.e. Jonah), the name of two Israelites:--Jonas. see HEBREW for 03124

G2496.text: Ἰωράμ Ijwravm Ioram {ee-o-ram'} of Hebrew origin (3141); Joram, an Israelite:--Joram. see HEBREW for 03141

G2497.text: Ἰωρίμ Ijwrivm Ioreim {ee-o-rime'} perhaps for 2496; Jorim, an Israelite:--Jorim. see GREEK for 2496

G2498.text: Ἰωσαφάτ Ijwsafavt Iosaphat {ee-o-saf-at'} of Hebrew origin (3092); Josaphat (i.e. Jehoshaphat), an Israelite:--Josaphat. see HEBREW for 03092

G2499.text: Ἰησοῦς Ijhsou's Iose {ee-o-say'} genitive case of 2500; Jose, an Israelite:--Jose. see GREEK for 2500

G2500.text: Ἰωσῆς Ijwsh's Ioses {ee-o-sace'} perhaps for 2501; Joses, the name of two Israelites:--Joses. Compare 2499. see GREEK for 2501 see GREEK for 2499

G2501.text: Ἰωσήφ Ijwshvf Ioseph {ee-o-safe'} of Hebrew origin (3130); Joseph, the name of seven Israelites:--Joseph. see HEBREW for 03130

G2502.text: Ἰωσίας Ijwsivas Iosias {ee-o-see'-as} of Hebrew origin (2977); Josias (i.e. Joshiah), an Israelite:--Josias. see HEBREW for 02977

G2503.text: ἰῶτα ijw'ta iota {ee-o'-tah} of Hebrew origin (the tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet); "iota", the name of the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, put (figuratively) for a very small part of anything:--jot.

G2504.text: κἀγώ kajgwv kago {kag-o'} from 2532 and 1473; so also the dative case kamoi kam-oy', and accusative case kame kam-eh' and (or also, even, etc.) I, (to) me:--(and, even, even so, so) I (also, in like wise), both me, me also. see GREEK for 2532 see GREEK for 1473

G2505.text: καθά kaqav katha {kath-ah'} from 2596 and the neuter plural of 3739; according to which things, i.e. just as:--as. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3739

G2506.text: καθαίρεσις kaqaivresis kathairesis {kath-ah'-ee-res-is} from 2507; demolition; figuratively, extinction:--destruction, pulling down. see GREEK for 2507

G2507.text: καθαιρέω kaqairevw kathaireo {kath-ahee-reh'-o} from 2596 and 138 (including its alternate); to lower (or with violence) demolish (literally or figuratively):--cast (pull, put, take) down, destroy. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 138

G2508.text: καθαίρω kaqaivrw kathairo {kath-ah'-ee-ro} from 2513; to cleanse, i.e. (specially) to prune; figuratively, to expiate:--purge. see GREEK for 2513

G2509.text: καθάπερ καθώσπερ kaqavper kaqwvsper kathaper {kath-ap'-er} from 2505 and 4007; exactly as:--(even, as well) as. see GREEK for 2505 see GREEK for 4007

G2510.text: καθάπτω kaqavptw kathapto {kath-ap'-to} from 2596 and 680; to seize upon:--fasten on. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 680

G2511.text: καθαρίζω kaqarivzw katharizo {kath-ar-id'-zo} from 2513; to cleanse (literally or figuratively):--(make) clean(-se), purge, purify. see GREEK for 2513

G2512.text: καθαρισμός kaqarismovs katharismos {kath-ar-is-mos'} from 2511; a washing off, i.e. (ceremonially) ablution, (morally) expiation:--cleansing, + purge, purification(-fying). see GREEK for 2511

G2513.text: καθαρός kaqarovs katharos {kath-ar-os'} of uncertain affinity; clean (literally or figuratively):--clean, clear, pure.

G2514.text: καθαρότης kaqarovths katharotes {kath-ar-ot'-ace} from 2513; cleanness (ceremonially):--purification. see GREEK for 2513

G2515.text: καθέδρα kaqevdra kathedra {kath-ed'-rah} from 2596 and the same as 1476; a bench (literally or figuratively):--seat. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 1476

G2516.text: καθέζομαι kaqevzomai kathezomai {kath-ed'-zom-ahee} from 2596 and the base of 1476; to sit down:--sit. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 1476

G2517.text: καθεξῆς kaqexh's kathexes {kath-ex-ace'} from 2596 and 1836; thereafter, i.e. consecutively; as a noun (by ellipsis of noun) a subsequent person or time:--after(-ward), by (in) order. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 1836

G2518.text: καθεύδω kaqeuvdw katheudo {kath-yoo'-do} from 2596 and heudo (to sleep); to lie down to rest, i.e. (by implication) to fall asleep (literally or figuratively):--(be a-)sleep. see GREEK for 2596

G2519.text: καθηγητής kaqhghthvs kathegetes {kath-ayg-ay-tace'} from a compound of 2596 and 2233; a guide, i.e. (figuratively) a teacher:--master. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2233

G2520.text: καθήκω kaqhvkw katheko {kath-ay'-ko} from 2596 and 2240; to reach to, i.e. (neuter of present active participle, figuratively as adjective) becoming:-- convenient, fit. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2240

G2521.text: κάθημαι kavqhmai kathemai {kath'-ay-mahee} from 2596; and hemai (to sit; akin to the base of 1476); to sit down; figuratively, to remain, reside:--dwell, sit (by, down). see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 1476

G2522.text: καθημερινός kaqhmerinovs kathemerinos {kath-ay-mer-ee-nos'} from 2596 and 2250; quotidian:--daily. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2250

G2523.text: καθίζω kaqivzw kathizo {kath-id'-zo} another (active) form for 2516; to seat down, i.e. set (figuratively, appoint); intransitively, to sit (down); figuratively, to settle (hover, dwell):--continue, set, sit (down), tarry. see GREEK for 2516

G2524.text: καθίημι kaqivhmi kathiemi {kath-ee'-ay-mee} from 2596; and hiemi (to send); to lower:--let down. see GREEK for 2596

G2525.text: καθίστημι kaqivsthmi kathistemi {kath-is'-tay-mee} from 2596 and 2476; to place down (permanently), i.e. (figuratively) to designate, constitute, convoy:--appoint, be, conduct, make, ordain, set. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2476

G2526.text: καθό kaqov katho {kath-o'} from 2596 and 3739; according to which thing, i.e. precisely as, in proportion as:--according to that, (inasmuch) as. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3739

G2527.text: καθόλου kaqovlou katholou {kath-ol'-oo} from 2596 and 3650; on the whole, i.e. entirely:--at all. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3650

G2528.text: καθοπλίζω kaqoplivzw kathoplizo {kath-op-lid'-zo} from 2596; and 3695; to equip fully with armor:--arm. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3695

G2529.text: καθοράω kaqoravw kathorao {kath-or-ah'-o} from 2596 and 3708; to behold fully, i.e. (figuratively) distinctly apprehend:--clearly see. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3708

G2530.text: καθότι kaqovti kathoti {kath-ot'-ee} from 2596; and 3739 and 5100; according to which certain thing, i.e. as far (or inasmuch) as:--(according, forasmuch) as, because (that). see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3739 see GREEK for 5100

G2531.text: καθώς kaqwvs kathos {kath-oce'} from 2596 and 5613; just (or inasmuch) as, that:--according to, (according, even) as, how, when. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 5613

G2532.text: καί kaiv kai {kahee} apparently, a primary particle, having a copulative and sometimes also a cumulative force; and, also, even, so then, too, etc.; often used in connection (or composition) with other particles or small words:--and, also, both, but, even, for, if, or, so, that, then, therefore, when, yet.

G2533.text: Καϊάφας Kai>avfas Kaiaphas {kah-ee-af'-as} of Chaldee origin; the dell; Caiaphas (i.e. Cajepha), an Israelite:--Caiaphas.

G2534.text: καίγε kaige kaige {kah'-ee-gheh} from 2532 and 1065; and at least (or even, indeed):--and, at least. see GREEK for 2532 see GREEK for 1065

G2535.text: Κάϊν Kavi>n Kain {kah'-in} of Hebrew origin (7014); Cain, (i.e. Cajin), the son of Adam:--Cain. see HEBREW for 07014

G2536.text: Καϊνάμ Kai>navm Kainan {kah-ee-nan'} of Hebrew origin (7018); Cainan (i.e. Kenan), the name of two patriarchs:--Cainan. see HEBREW for 07018

G2537.text: καινός kainovs kainos {kahee-nos'} of uncertain affinity; new (especially in freshness; while 3501 is properly so with respect to age:--new. see GREEK for 3501

G2538.text: καινότης kainovths kainotes {kahee-not'-ace} from 2537; renewal (figuratively):--newness. see GREEK for 2537

G2539.text: καίπερ kaivper kaiper {kah'-ee-per} from 2532 and 4007; and indeed, i.e. nevertheless or notwithstanding:--and yet, although. see GREEK for 2532 see GREEK for 4007

G2540.text: καιρός kairovs kairos {kahee-ros'} of uncertain affinity; an occasion, i.e. set or proper time:--X always, opportunity, (convenient, due) season, (due, short, while) time, a while. Compare 5550. see GREEK for 5550

G2541.text: Καῖσαρ Kai'sar Kaisar {kah'-ee-sar} of Latin origin; Caesar, a title of the Roman emperor:--Caesar.

G2542.text: Καισάρεια Καισαρία Kaisavreia Kaisariva Kaisereia {kahee-sar'-i-a} from 2541; Caesaria, the name of two places in Palestine:--Caesarea. see GREEK for 2541

G2543.text: καίτοι kaivtoi kaitoi {kah'-ee-toy} from 2532 and 5104; and yet, i.e. nevertheless:--although. see GREEK for 2532 see GREEK for 5104

G2544.text: καίτοιγε kaivtoige kaitoige {kah'-ee-toyg-eh} from 2543 and 1065; and yet indeed, i.e. although really:--nevertheless, though. see GREEK for 2543 see GREEK for 1065

G2545.text: καίω kaivw kaio {kah'-yo} apparently a primary verb; to set on fire, i.e. kindle or (by implication) consume:--burn, light.

G2546.text: κἀκεῖ kajkei' kakei {kak-i'} from 2532 and 1563; likewise in that place:--and there, there (thither) also. see GREEK for 2532 see GREEK for 1563

G2547.text: κἀκεῖθεν kajkei'qen kakeithen {kak-i'-then} from 2532 and 1564; likewise from that place (or time):--and afterward (from) (thence), thence also. see GREEK for 2532 see GREEK for 1564

G2548.text: κἀκεῖνος kajkei'nos kakeinos {kak-i'-nos} from 2532 and 1565; likewise that (or those):--and him (other, them), even he, him also, them (also), (and) they. see GREEK for 2532 see GREEK for 1565

G2549.text: κακία kakiva kakia {kak-ee'-ah} from 2556; badness, i.e. (subjectively) depravity, or (actively) malignity, or (passively) trouble:--evil, malice(-iousness), naughtiness, wickedness. see GREEK for 2556

G2550.text: κακοήθεια kakohvqeia kakoetheia {kak-o-ay'-thi-ah} from a compound of 2556 and 2239; bad character, i.e. (specially) mischievousness:--malignity. see GREEK for 2556 see GREEK for 2239

G2551.text: κακολογέω kakologevw kakologeo {kak-ol-og-eh'-o} from a compound of 2556 and 3056; to revile:--curse, speak evil of. see GREEK for 2556 see GREEK for 3056

G2552.text: κακοπάθεια kakopavqeia kakopatheia {kak-op-ath'-i-ah} from a compound of 2256 and 3806; hardship:--suffering affliction. see GREEK for 2256 see GREEK for 3806

G2553.text: κακοπαθέω kakopaqevw kakopatheo {kak-op-ath-eh'-o} from the same as 2552; to undergo hardship:--be afflicted, endure afflictions (hardness), suffer trouble. see GREEK for 2552

G2554.text: κακοποιέω kakopoievw kakopoieo {kak-op-oy-eh'-o} from 2555; to be a bad-doer, i.e. (objectively) to injure, or (genitive) to sin:--do(ing) evil. see GREEK for 2555

G2555.text: κακοποιός kakopoiovs kakopoios {kak-op-oy-os'} from 2556 and 4160; a bad-doer; (specially), a criminal:--evil-doer, malefactor. see GREEK for 2556 see GREEK for 4160

G2556.text: κακός kakovs kakos {kak-os'} apparently a primary word; worthless (intrinsically, such; whereas 4190 properly refers to effects), i.e. (subjectively) depraved, or (objectively) injurious:--bad, evil, harm, ill, noisome, wicked. see GREEK for 4190

G2557.text: κακοῦργος kakou'rgos kakourgos {kak-oor'-gos} from 2556 and the base of 2041; a wrong-doer, i.e. criminal:--evil-doer, malefactor. see GREEK for 2556 see GREEK for 2041

G2558.text: κακουχέομαι kakoucevomai kakoucheo {kak-oo-kheh'-o} from a presumed compound of 2556 and 2192; to maltreat:--which suffer adversity, torment. see GREEK for 2556 see GREEK for 2192

G2559.text: κακόω kakovw kakoo {kak-o'-o} from 2556; to injure; figuratively, to exasperate:--make evil affected, entreat evil, harm, hurt, vex. see GREEK for 2556

G2560.text: κακῶς kakw's kakos {kak-oce'} from 2556; badly (physically or morally):--amiss, diseased, evil, grievously, miserably, sick, sore. see GREEK for 2556

G2561.text: κάκωσις kavkwsis kakosis {kak'-o-sis} from 2559; maltreatment:--affliction. see GREEK for 2559

G2562.text: καλάμη kalavmh kalame {kal-am'-ay} feminine of 2563; a stalk of grain, i.e. (collectively) stubble:--stubble. see GREEK for 2563

G2563.text: κάλαμος kavlamos kalamos {kal'-am-os} or uncertain affinity; a reed (the plant or its stem, or that of a similar plant); by implication, a pen:--pen, reed.

G2564.text: καλέω kalevw kaleo {kal-eh'-o} akin to the base of 2753; to "call" (properly, aloud, but used in a variety of applications, directly or otherwise):--bid, call (forth), (whose, whose sur-)name (was (called)). see GREEK for 2753

G2565.text: καλλιέλαιος kallievlaios kallielaios {kal-le-el'-ah-yos} from the base of 2566 and 1636; a cultivated olive tree, i.e. a domesticated or improved one:--good olive tree. see GREEK for 2566 see GREEK for 1636

G2566.text: καλός kalovs kallion {kal-lee'-on} neuter of the (irregular) comparative of 2570; (adverbially) better than many:--very well. see GREEK for 2570

G2567.text: καλοδιδάσκαλος kalodidavskalos kalodidaskalos {kal-od-id-as'-kal-os} from 2570 and 1320; a teacher of the right:--teacher of good things. see GREEK for 2570 see GREEK for 1320

G2568.text: Καλοὶ Λιμένες Kaloi; Limevnes Kaloi Limenes {kal-oy' lee-men'-es} plural of 2570 and 3040; Good Harbors, i.e. Fairhaven, a bay of Crete:--fair havens. see GREEK for 2570 see GREEK for 3040

G2569.text: καλοποιέω kalopoievw kalopoieo {kal-op-oy-eh'-o} from 2570 and 4160; to do well, i.e. live virtuously:--well doing. see GREEK for 2570 see GREEK for 4160

G2570.text: καλός kalovs kalos {kal-os'} of uncertain affinity; properly, beautiful, but chiefly (figuratively) good (literally or morally), i.e. valuable or virtuous (for appearance or use, and thus distinguished from 18, which is properly intrinsic):--X better, fair, good(-ly), honest, meet, well, worthy. see GREEK for 18

G2571.text: κάλυμμα kavlumma kaluma {kal'-oo-mah} from 2572; a cover, i.e. veil:--vail. see GREEK for 2572

G2572.text: καλύπτω kaluvptw kalupto {kal-oop'-to} akin to 2813 and 2928; to cover up (literally or figuratively):--cover, hide. see GREEK for 2813 see GREEK for 2928

G2573.text: καλῶς kalw's kalos {kal-oce'} adverb from 2570; well (usually morally):--(in a) good (place), honestly, + recover, (full) well. see GREEK for 2570

G2574.text: κάμηλος kavmhlos kamelos {kam'-ay-los} of Hebrew origin (1581); a "camel":--camel. see HEBREW for 01581

G2575.text: κάμινος kavminos kaminos {kam'-ee-nos} probably from 2545; a furnace:--furnace. see GREEK for 2545

G2576.text: καμμύω kammuvw kammuo {kam-moo'-o} from a compound of 2596 and the base of 3466; to shut down, i.e. close the eyes:--close. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3466

G2577.text: κάμνω kavmnw kamno {kam'-no} apparently a primary verb; properly, to toil, i.e. (by implication) to tire (figuratively, faint, sicken):--faint, sick, be wearied.

G2578.text: κάμπτω kavmptw kampto {kamp'-to} apparently a primary verb; to bend:--bow.

G2579.text: κἄν ka[n kan {kan} from 2532 and 1437; and (or even) if:--and (also) if (so much as), if but, at the least, though, yet. see GREEK for 2532 see GREEK for 1437

G2580.text: Κανά Kanav Kana {kan-ah'} of Hebrew origin (compare 7071); Cana, a place in Palestine:--Cana. see HEBREW for 07071

G2581.text: Καναναῖος Kananai'os Kananites {kan-an-ee'-tace} of Chaldee origin (compare 7067); zealous; Cananites, an epithet:--Canaanite (by mistake for a derivative from 5477). see GREEK for 5477 see HEBREW for 07067

G2582.text: Κανδάκη Kandavkh Kandake {kan-dak'-ay} of foreign origin:--Candace, an Egyptian queen:--Candace.

G2583.text: κανών kanwvn kanon {kan-ohn'} from kane (a straight reed, i.e. rod); a rule ("canon"), i.e. (figuratively) a standard (of faith and practice); by implication, a boundary, i.e. (figuratively) a sphere (of activity):--line, rule.

G2584.text: Καφαρναούμ Kafarnaouvm Kapernaoum {cap-er-nah-oom'} of Hebrew origin (probably 3723 and 5151); Capernaum (i.e. Caphanachum), a place in Palestine:--Capernaum. see HEBREW for 03723 see HEBREW for 05151

G2585.text: καπηλεύω kaphleuvw kapeleuo {kap-ale-yoo'-o} from kapelos (a huckster); to retail, i.e. (by implication) to adulterate (figuratively):--corrupt.

G2586.text: καπνός kapnovs kapnos {kap-nos'} of uncertain affinity; smoke:--smoke.

G2587.text: Καππαδοκία Kappadokiva Kappadokia {kap-pad-ok-ee'-ah} of foreign origin; Cappadocia, a region of Asia Minor:--Cappadocia.

G2588.text: καρδία kardiva kardia {kar-dee'-ah} prolonged from a primary kar (Latin cor, "heart"); the heart, i.e. (figuratively) the thoughts or feelings (mind); also (by analogy) the middle:--(+ broken-)heart(-ed).

G2589.text: καρδιογνώστης kardiognwvsths kardiognostes {kar-dee-og-noce'-tace} from 2588 and 1097; a heart-knower:--which knowest the hearts. see GREEK for 2588 see GREEK for 1097

G2590.text: καρπός karpovs karpos {kar-pos'} probably from the base of 726; fruit (as plucked), literally or figuratively:--fruit. see GREEK for 726

G2591.text: Κάρπος Kavrpos Karpos {kar'-pos} perhaps for 2590; Carpus, probably a Christian:--Carpus. see GREEK for 2590

G2592.text: καρποφορέω karpoforevw karpophoreo {kar-pof-or-eh'-o} from 2593; to be fertile (literally or figuratively):--be (bear, bring forth) fruit(-ful). see GREEK for 2593

G2593.text: καρποφόρος karpofovros karpophoros {kar-pof-or'-os} from 2590 and 5342; fruitbearing (figuratively):--fruitful. see GREEK for 2590 see GREEK for 5342

G2594.text: καρτερέω karterevw kartereo {kar-ter-eh'-o} from a derivative of 2904 (transposed); to be strong, i.e. (figuratively) steadfast (patient):--endure. see GREEK for 2904

G2595.text: κάρφος kavrfos karphos {kar'-fos} from karpho (to wither); a dry twig or straw:--mote.

G2596.text: κατά katav kata {kat-ah'} a primary particle; (prepositionally) down (in place or time), in varied relations (according to the case (genitive, dative or accusative) with which it is joined):--about, according as (to), after, against, (when they were) X alone, among, and, X apart, (even, like) as (concerning, pertaining to touching), X aside, at, before, beyond, by, to the charge of, (charita-)bly, concerning, + covered, (dai-)ly, down, every, (+ far more) exceeding, X more excellent, for, from ... to, godly, in(-asmuch, divers, every, -to, respect of), ... by, after the manner of, + by any means, beyond (out of) measure, X mightily, more, X natural, of (up-)on (X part), out (of every), over against, (+ your) X own, + particularly, so, through(-oughout, -oughout every), thus, (un-)to(-gether, -ward), X uttermost, where(-by), with. In composition it retains many of these applications, and frequently denotes opposition, distribution, or intensity.

G2597.text: καταβαίνω katabaivnw katabaino {kat-ab-ah'-ee-no} from 2596 and the base of 939; to descend (literally or figuratively):--come (get, go, step) down, fall (down). see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 939

G2598.text: καταβάλλω katabavllw kataballo {kat-ab-al'-lo} from 2596 and 906; to throw down:--cast down, lay. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 906

G2599.text: καταβαρέω katabarevw katabareo {kat-ab-ar-eh'-o} from 2596 and 916; to impose upon:--burden. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 916

G2600.text: κατάβασις katavbasis katabasis {kat-ab'-as-is} from 2597; a declivity:--descent. see GREEK for 2597

G2601.text: καταβιβάζω katabibazo katabibazo {kat-ab-ib-ad'-zo} from 2596 and a derivative of the base of 939; to cause to go down, i.e. precipitate:--bring (thrust) down. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 939

G2602.text: καταβολή katabolhv katabole {kat-ab-ol-ay'} from 2598; a deposition, i.e. founding; figuratively, conception:--conceive, foundation. see GREEK for 2598

G2603.text: καταβραβεύω katabrabeuvw katabrabeuo {kat-ab-rab-yoo'-o} from 2596 and 1018 (in its original sense); to award the price against, i.e. (figuratively) to defraud (of salvation):--beguile of reward. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 1018

G2604.text: καταγγελεύς kataggeleuvs kataggeleus {kat-ang-gel-yooce'} from 2605; a proclaimer:--setter forth. see GREEK for 2605

G2605.text: καταγγέλλω kataggevllw kataggello {kat-ang-gel'-lo} from 2596 and the base of 32; to proclaim, promulgate:--declare, preach, shew, speak of, teach. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 32

G2606.text: καταγελάω katagelavw katagelao {kat-ag-el-ah'-o} to laugh down, i.e. deride:--laugh to scorn.

G2607.text: καταγινώσκω kataginwvskw kataginosko {kat-ag-in-o'-sko} from 2596 and 1097; to note against, i.e. find fault with:--blame, condemn. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 1097

G2608.text: κατάγνυμι katavgnumi katagnumi {kat-ag'-noo-mee} from 2596 and the base of 4486; to rend in pieces, i.e. crack apart:--break. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 4486

G2609.text: κατάγω katavgw katago {kat-ag'-o} from 2596 and 71; to lead down; specially, to moor a vessel:--bring (down, forth), (bring to) land, touch. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 71

G2610.text: καταγωνίζομαι katagwnivzomai katagonizomai {kat-ag-o-nid'-zom-ahee} from 2596 and 75; to struggle against, i.e. (by implication) to overcome:--subdue. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 75
