G2611.text: καταδέω katadevw katadeo {kat-ad-eh'-o} from 2596 and 1210; to tie down, i.e. bandage (a wound):--bind up. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 1210

G2612.text: κατάδηλος katavdhlos katadelos {kat-ad'-ay-los} from 2596 intensive and 1212; manifest:--far more evident. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 1212

G2613.text: καταδικάζω katadikavzw katadikazo {kat-ad-ik-ad'-zo} from 2596 and a derivative of 1349; to adjudge against, i.e. pronounce guilty:--condemn. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 1349

G2614.text: καταδιώκω katadiwvkw katadioko {kat-ad-ee-o'-ko} from 2596 and 1377; to hunt down, i.e. search for:--follow after. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 1377

G2615.text: καταδουλόω katadoulovw katadouloo {kat-ad-oo-lo'-o} from 2596 and 1402; to enslave utterly:--bring into bondage. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 1402

G2616.text: καταδυναστεύω katadunasteuvw katadunasteuo {kat-ad-oo-nas-tyoo'-o} from 2596 and a derivative of 1413; to exercise dominion against, i.e. oppress:--oppress. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 1413

G2617.text: καταισχύνω kataiscuvnw kataischuno {kat-ahee-skhoo'-no} from 2596 and 153; to shame down, i.e. disgrace or (by implication) put to the blush:--confound, dishonour, (be a-, make a-)shame(-d). see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 153

G2618.text: κατακαίω katakaivw katakaio {kat-ak-ah'-ee-o} from 2596 and 2545; to burn down (to the ground), i.e. consume wholly:--burn (up, utterly). see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2545

G2619.text: κατακαλύπτομαι katakaluvptomai katakalupto {kat-ak-al-oop'-to} from 2596 and 2572; to cover wholly, i.e. veil:--cover, hide. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2572

G2620.text: κατακαυχάομαι katakaucavomai katakauchaomai {kat-ak-ow-khah'-om-ahee} from 2596 and 2744; to exult against (i.e. over):--boast (against), glory, rejoice against. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2744

G2621.text: κατάκειμαι katavkeimai katakeimai {kat-ak'-i-mahee} from 2596 and 2749; to lie down, i.e. (by implication) be sick; specially, to recline at a meal:--keep, lie, sit at meat (down). see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2749

G2622.text: κατακλάω kataklavw kataklao {kat-ak-lah'-o} from 2596 and 2806; to break down, i.e. divide:--break. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2806

G2623.text: κατακλείω katakleivw katakleio {kat-ak-li'-o} from 2596 and 2808; to shut down (in a dungeon), i.e. incarcerate:--shut up. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2808

G2624.text: κατακληρονομέω kataklhronomevw kataklerodoteo {kat-ak-lay-rod-ot-eh'-o} from 2596 and a derivative of a compound of 2819 and 1325; to be a giver of lots to each, i.e. (by implication) to apportion an estate:--divide by lot. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2819 see GREEK for 1325

G2625.text: κατακλίνω kataklivnw kataklino {kat-ak-lee'-no} from 2596 and 2827; to recline down, i.e. (specially) to take a place at table:--(make) sit down (at meat). see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2827

G2626.text: κατακλύζω katakluvzw katakluzo {kat-ak-lood'-zo} from 2596 and the base of 2830; to dash (wash) down, i.e. (by implication) to deluge:--overflow. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2830

G2627.text: κατακλυσμός kataklusmovs kataklusmos {kat-ak-looce-mos'} from 2626; an inundation:--flood. see GREEK for 2626

G2628.text: κατακολουθέω katakolouqevw katakoloutheo {kat-ak-ol-oo-theh'-o} from 2596 and 190; to accompany closely:--follow (after). see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 190

G2629.text: κατακόπτω katakovptw katakopto {kat-ak-op'-to} from 2596 and 2875; to chop down, i.e. mangle:--cut. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2875

G2630.text: κατακρημνίζω katakrhmnivzw katakremnizo {kat-ak-rame-nid'-zo} from 2596 and a derivative of 2911; to precipitate down:--cast down headlong. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2911

G2631.text: κατάκριμα katavkrima katakrima {kat-ak'-ree-mah} from 2632; an adverse sentence (the verdict):--condemnation. see GREEK for 2632

G2632.text: κατακρίνω katakrivnw katakrino {kat-ak-ree'-no} from 2596 and 2919; to judge against, i.e. sentence:--condemn, damn. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2919

G2633.text: κατάκρισις katavkrisis katakrisis {kat-ak'-ree-sis} from 2632; sentencing adversely (the act):--condemn(-ation). see GREEK for 2632

G2634.text: κατακυριεύω katakurieuvw katakurieuo {kat-ak-oo-ree-yoo'-o} from 2596 and 2961; to lord against, i.e. control, subjugate:--exercise dominion over (lordship), be lord over, overcome. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2961

G2635.text: καταλαλέω katalalevw katalaleo {kat-al-al-eh'-o} from 2637; to be a traducer, i.e. to slander:--speak against (evil of). see GREEK for 2637

G2636.text: καταλαλιά katalaliav katalalia {kat-al-al-ee'-ah} from 2637; defamation:--backbiting, evil speaking. see GREEK for 2637

G2637.text: κατάλαλος katavlalos katalalos {kat-al'-al-os} from 2596 and the base of 2980; talkative against, i.e. a slanderer:--backbiter. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2980

G2638.text: καταλαμβάνω katalambavnw katalambano {kat-al-am-ban'-o} from 2596 and 2983; to take eagerly, i.e. seize, possess, etc. (literally or figuratively):--apprehend, attain, come upon, comprehend, find, obtain, perceive, (over-)take. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 2983

G2639.text: καταλέγω katalevgw katalego {kat-al-eg'-o} from 2596 and 3004 (in its original meaning); to lay down, i.e. (figuratively) to enrol:--take into the number. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3004

G2640.text: ὑπόλειμμα ὑπόλιμμα uJpovleimma uJpovlimma kataleimma {kat-al'-ime-mah} from 2641; a remainder, i.e. (by implication) a few:--remnant. see GREEK for 2641

G2641.text: καταλείπω kataleivpw kataleipo {kat-al-i'-po} from 2596 and 3007; to leave down, i.e. behind; by implication, to abandon, have remaining:--forsake, leave, reserve. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3007

G2642.text: καταλιθάζω kataliqavzw katalithazo {kat-al-ith-ad'-zo} from 2596 and 3034; to stone down, i.e. to death:--stone. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3034

G2643.text: καταλλαγή katallaghv katallage {kat-al-lag-ay'} from 2644; exchange (figuratively, adjustment), i.e. restoration to (the divine) favor:--atonement, reconciliation(-ing). see GREEK for 2644

G2644.text: καταλλάσσω katallavssw katallasso {kat-al-las'-so} from 2596 and 236; to change mutually, i.e. (figuratively) to compound a difference:--reconcile. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 236

G2645.text: κατάλοιπος katavloipos kataloipos {kat-al'-oy-pos} from 2596 and 3062; left down (behind), i.e remaining (plural the rest):--residue. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3062

G2646.text: κατάλυμα katavluma kataluma {kat-al'-oo-mah} from 2647; properly, a dissolution (breaking up of a journey), i.e. (by implication) a lodging-place:-- guestchamber, inn. see GREEK for 2647

G2647.text: καταλύω kataluvw kataluo {kat-al-oo'-o} from 2596 and 3089; to loosen down (disintegrate), i.e. (by implication) to demolish (literally or figuratively); specially (compare 2646) to halt for the night:--destroy, dissolve, be guest, lodge, come to nought, overthrow, throw down. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3089 see GREEK for 2646

G2648.text: καταμανθάνω katamanqavnw katamanthano {kat-am-an-than'-o} from 2596 and 3129; to learn thoroughly, i.e. (by implication) to note carefully:--consider. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3129

G2649.text: καταμαρτυρέω katamarturevw katamartureo {kat-am-ar-too-reh'-o} from 2596 and 3140; to testify against:--witness against. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3140

G2650.text: καταμένω katamevnw katameno {kat-am-en'-o} from 2596 and 3306; to stay fully, i.e. reside:--abide. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3306

G2651.text: καταμόνας katamonas katamonas {kat-am-on'-as} from 2596 and accusative case plural feminine of 3441 (with 5561 implied); according to sole places, i.e. (adverbially) separately:--alone. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 3441 see GREEK for 5561

G2652.text: κατάθεμα katavqema katanathema {kat-an-ath'-em-ah} from 2596 (intensive) and 331; an imprecation:--curse. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 331

G2653.text: καταθεματίζω kataqemativzw katanathematizo {kat-an-ath-em-at-id'-zo} from 2596 (intensive) and 332; to imprecate:--curse. see GREEK for 2596 see GREEK for 332

G2771.text: κέρδος kevrdos kerdos {ker'-dos} of uncertain affinity; gain (pecuniary or genitive case):--gain, lucre.

G2772.text: κέρμα kevrma kerma {ker'-mah} from 2751; a clipping (bit), i.e. (specially) a coin:--money. see GREEK for 2751

G2773.text: κερματιστής kermatisthvs kermatistes {ker-mat-is-tace'} from a derivative of 2772; a handler of coins, i.e. money-broker:--changer of money. see GREEK for 2772

G2774.text: κεφάλαιον kefavlaion kephalaion {kef-al'-ah-yon} neuter of a derivative of 2776; a principal thing, i.e. main point; specially, an amount (of money):--sum. see GREEK for 2776

G2775.text: κεφαλιόω kefaliovw kephalaioo {kef-al-ahee-o'-o} from the same as 2774; (specially) to strike on the head:--wound in the head. see GREEK for 2774

G2776.text: κεφαλή kefalhv kephale {kef-al-ay'} from the primary kapto (in the sense of seizing); the head (as the part most readily taken hold of), literally or figuratively:--head.

G2777.text: κεφαλίς kefalivs kephalis {kef-al-is'} from 2776; properly, a knob, i.e. (by implication) a roll (by extension from the end of a stick on which the manuscript was rolled):--volume. see GREEK for 2776

G2778.text: κῆνσος kh'nsos kensos {kane'-sos} of Latin origin; properly, an enrollment ("census"), i.e. (by implication) a tax:--tribute.

G2779.text: κῆπος kh'pos kepos {kay'-pos} of uncertain affinity; a garden:--garden.

G2780.text: κηπουρός khpourovs kepouros {kay-poo-ros'} from 2779 and ouros (a warden); a garden-keeper, i.e. gardener:--gardener. see GREEK for 2779

G2781.text: κηρίον ου τό kerion kerion {kay-ree'-on} diminutive from keos (wax); a cell for honey, i.e. (collectively) the comb:--(honey-)comb.

G2782.text: κήρυγμα khvrugma kerugma {kay'-roog-mah} from 2784; a proclamation (especially of the gospel; by implication, the gospel itself):--preaching. see GREEK for 2784

G2783.text: κῆρυξ kh'rux kerux {kay'-roox} from 2784; a herald, i.e. of divine truth (especially of the gospel):--preacher. see GREEK for 2784

G2784.text: κηρύσσω khruvssw kerusso {kay-roos'-so} of uncertain affinity; to herald (as a public crier), especially divine truth (the gospel):--preacher(-er), proclaim, publish.

G2785.text: κῆτος kh'tos ketos {kay'-tos} probably from the base of 5490; a huge fish (as gaping for prey):--whale. see GREEK for 5490

G2786.text: Κηφᾶς Khfa's Kephas {kay-fas'} of Chaldee origin (compare 3710); the Rock; Cephas (i.e. Kepha), a surname of Peter:--Cephas. see HEBREW for 03710

G2787.text: κιβωτός kibwtovs kibotos {kib-o-tos'} of uncertain derivation; a box, i.e. the sacred ark and that of Noah:--ark.

G2788.text: κιθάρα kiqavra kithara {kith-ar'-ah} of uncertain affinity; a lyre:--harp.

G2789.text: κιθαρίζω kiqarivzw kitharizo {kith-ar-id'-zo} from 2788; to play on a lyre:--harp. see GREEK for 2788

G2790.text: κιθαρῳδός kiqarw/dovs kitharodos {kith-ar-o'-dos} from 2788 and a derivative of the same as 5603; a lyre-singer(-player), i.e. harpist:--harper. see GREEK for 2788 see GREEK for 5603

G2791.text: Κιλικία Kilikiva Kilikia {kil-ik-ee'-ah} probably of foreign origin; Cilicia, a region of Asia Minor:--Cilicia.

G2792.text: κιννάμωμον kinnavmwmon kinamomon {kin-am'-o-mon} of foreign origin (compare 7076); cinnamon:--cinnamon. see HEBREW for 07076

G2793.text: κινδυνεύω kinduneuvw kinduneuo {kin-doon-yoo'-o} from 2794; to undergo peril:--be in danger, be (stand) in jeopardy. see GREEK for 2794

G2794.text: κίνδυνος kivndunos kindunos {kin'-doo-nos} of uncertain derivation; danger:--peril.

G2795.text: κινέω kinevw kineo {kin-eh'-o} from kio (poetic for eimi, to go); to stir (transitively), literally or figuratively:--(re-)move(-r), way.

G2796.text: κίνησις εως ἡ kinesis kinesis {kin'-ay-sis} from 2795; a stirring:--moving. see GREEK for 2795

G2797.text: Κείς Κίς Keivs Kivs Kis {kis} of Hebrew origin (7027); Cis (i.e. Kish), an Israelite:--Cis. see HEBREW for 07027

G2798.text: κλάδος klavdos klados {klad'-os} from 2806; a twig or bough (as if broken off):--branch. see GREEK for 2806

G2799.text: κλαίω klaivw klaio {klah'-yo} of uncertain affinity; to sob, i.e. wail aloud (whereas 1145 is rather to cry silently):--bewail, weep.

G2800.text: κλάσις klavsis klasis {klas'-is} from 2806; fracture (the act):--breaking. see GREEK for 2806

G2801.text: κλάσμα klavsma klasma {klas'-mah} from 2806; a piece (bit):--broken, fragment. see GREEK for 2806

G2802.text: Καῦδα Kau'da Klaude {klow'-day} of uncertain derivation; Claude, an island near Crete:--Clauda.

G2803.text: Κλαυδία Klaudiva Klaudia {klow-dee'-ah} feminine of 2804; Claudia, a Christian woman:--Claudia. see GREEK for 2804

G2804.text: Κλαύδιος Klauvdios Klaudios {klow'-dee-os} of Latin origin; Claudius, the name of two Romans:--Claudius.

G2805.text: κλαυθμός klauqmovs klauthmos {klowth-mos'} from 2799; lamentation:--wailing, weeping, X wept. see GREEK for 2799

G2806.text: κλάω klavw klao {klah'-o} a primary verb; to break (specially, of bread):--break.

G2807.text: κλείς kleivs kleis {klice} from 2808; a key (as shutting a lock), literally or figuratively:--key. see GREEK for 2808

G2808.text: κλείω kleivw kleio {kli'-o} a primary verb; to close (literally or figuratively):--shut (up).

G2809.text: κλέμμα klevmma klemma {klem'-mah} from 2813; stealing (properly, the thing stolen, but used of the act):--theft. see GREEK for 2813

G2810.text: Κλεοπᾶς Kleopa's Kleopas {kleh-op'-as} probably contracted from Kleopatros (compound of 2811 and 3962); Cleopas, a Christian:--Cleopas. see GREEK for 2811 see GREEK for 3962

G2811.text: κλέος klevos kleos {kleh'-os} from a shorter form of 2564; renown (as if being called):--glory. see GREEK for 2564

G2812.text: κλέπτης klevpths kleptes {klep'-tace} from 2813; a stealer (literally or figuratively):--thief. Compare 3027. see GREEK for 2813 see GREEK for 3027

G2813.text: κλέπτω klevptw klepto {klep'-to} a primary verb; to filch:--steal.

G2814.text: κλῆμα klh'ma klema {kaly'-mah} from 2806; a limb or shoot (as if broken off):--branch. see GREEK for 2806

G2815.text: κλῆμα klh'ma Klemes {klay'-mace} of Latin origin; merciful; Clemes (i.e. Clemens), a Christian:--Clement.

G2816.text: κληρονομέω klhronomevw kleronomeo {klay-ron-om-eh'-o} from 2818; to be an heir to (literally or figuratively):--be heir, (obtain by) inherit(-ance). see GREEK for 2818

G2817.text: κληρονομία klhronomiva kleronomia {klay-ron-om-ee'-ah} from 2818; heirship, i.e. (concretely) a patrimony or (genitive case) a possession:--inheritance. see GREEK for 2818

G2818.text: κληρονόμος klhronovmos kleronomos {klay-ron-om'-os} from 2819 and the base of 3551 (in its original sense of partitioning, i.e. (reflexively) getting by apportionment); a sharer by lot, i.e. inheritor (literally or figuratively); by implication, a possessor:--heir. see GREEK for 2819 see GREEK for 3551

G2819.text: κλῆρος klh'ros kleros {klay'-ros} probably from 2806 (through the idea of using bits of wood, etc., for the purpose; a die (for drawing chances); by implication, a portion (as if so secured); by extension, an acquisition (especially a patrimony, figuratively):--heritage, inheritance, lot, part. see GREEK for 2806

G2820.text: κληρόω klhrovw kleroo {klay-ro-o} from 2819; to allot, i.e. (figuratively) to assign (a privilege):--obtain an inheritance. see GREEK for 2819

G2821.text: κλῆσις klh'sis klesis {klay'-sis} from a shorter form of 2564; an invitation (figuratively):--calling. see GREEK for 2564

G2822.text: κλητός klhtovs kletos {klay-tos'} from the same as 2821; invited, i.e. appointed, or (specially), a saint:--called. see GREEK for 2821

G2823.text: κλίβανος klivbanos klibanos {klib'-an-os} of uncertain derivation; an earthen pot used for baking in:--oven.

G2824.text: κλίμα klivma klima {klee'-mah} from 2827; a slope, i.e. (specially) a "clime" or tract of country:--part, region. see GREEK for 2827

G2825.text: κλίνη klivnh kline {klee'-nay} from 2827; a couch (for sleep, sickness, sitting or eating):--bed, table. see GREEK for 2827

G2826.text: κλινίδιον klinivdion klinidion {klin-id'-ee-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of 2825; a pallet or little couch:--bed. see GREEK for 2825

G2827.text: κλίνω klivnw klino {klee'-no} a primary verb; to slant or slope, i.e. incline or recline (literally or figuratively):--bow (down), be far spent, lay, turn to flight, wear away.

G2828.text: κλισία klisiva klisia {klee-see'-ah} from a derivative of 2827; properly, reclination, i.e. (concretely and specially), a party at a meal:--company. see GREEK for 2827

G2829.text: κλοπή klophv klope {klop-ay'} from 2813; stealing:--theft. see GREEK for 2813

G2830.text: κλύδων kluvdwn kludon {kloo'-dohn} from kluzo (to billow or dash over); a surge of the sea (literally or figuratively):--raging, wave.

G2831.text: κλυδωνίζομαι kludwnivzomai kludonizomai {kloo-do-nid'-zom-ahee} middle voice from 2830; to surge, i.e. (figuratively) to fluctuate:--toss to and fro. see GREEK for 2830

G2832.text: Κλωπᾶς Klwpa's Klopas {klo-pas'} of Chaldee origin (corresponding to 256); Clopas, an Israelite:--Cleophas. see HEBREW for 0256

G2833.text: κνήθομαι knhvqomai knetho {knay'-tho} from a primary knao (to scrape); to scratch, i.e. (by implication) to tickle:--X itching.

G2834.text: Κνίδος Knivdos Knidos {knee'-dos} probably of foreign origin; Cnidus, a place in Asia Minor:--Cnidus.

G2835.text: κοδράντης kodravnths kodrantes {kod-ran'-tace} of Latin origin; a quadrans, i.e. the fourth part of an as:--farthing.

G2836.text: κοιλία koiliva koilia {koy-lee'-ah} from koilos ("hollow"); a cavity, i.e. (especially) the abdomen; by implication, the matrix; figuratively, the heart:--belly, womb.

G2837.text: κοιμάομαι koimavomai koimao {koy-mah'-o} from 2749; to put to sleep, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to slumber; figuratively, to decease:--(be a-, fall a-, fall on) sleep, be dead. see GREEK for 2749

G2838.text: κοίμησις koivmhsis koimesis {koy'-may-sis} from 2837; sleeping, i.e. (by implication) repose:--taking of rest. see GREEK for 2837

G2839.text: κοινός koinovs koinos {koy-nos'} probably from 4862; common, i.e. (literally) shared by all or several, or (ceremonially) profane:--common, defiled, unclean, unholy. see GREEK for 4862

G2840.text: κοινόω koinovw koinoo {koy-no'-o} from 2839; to make (or consider) profane (ceremonially):--call common, defile, pollute, unclean. see GREEK for 2839

G2841.text: κοινωνέω koinwnevw koinoneo {koy-no-neh'-o} from 2844; to share with others (objectively or subjectively):--communicate, distribute, be partaker. see GREEK for 2844

G2842.text: κοινωνία koinwniva koinonia {koy-nohn-ee'-ah} from 2844; partnership, i.e. (literally) participation, or (social) intercourse, or (pecuniary) benefaction:--(to) communicate(-ation), communion, (contri-)distribution, fellowship. see GREEK for 2844

G2843.text: κοινωνικός koinwnikovs koinonikos {koy-no-nee-kos'} from 2844; communicative, i.e. (pecuniarily) liberal:--willing to communicate. see GREEK for 2844

G2844.text: κοινωνός koinwnovs koinonos {koy-no-nos'} from 2839; a sharer, i.e. associate:--companion, X fellowship, partaker, partner. see GREEK for 2839

G2845.text: κοίτη koivth koite {koy'-tay} from 2749; a couch; by extension, cohabitation; by implication, the male sperm:--bed, chambering, X conceive. see GREEK for 2749

G2846.text: κοιτών koitwvn koiton {koy-tone'} from 2845; a bedroom:--+ chamberlain. see GREEK for 2845

G2847.text: κόκκινος kovkkinos kokkinos {kok'-kee-nos} from 2848 (from the kernel-shape of the insect); crimson-colored:--scarlet (colour, coloured). see GREEK for 2848

G2848.text: κόκκος kovkkos kokkos {kok'-kos} apparently a primary word; a kernel of seed:--corn, grain.

G2849.text: κολάζω kolavzw kolazo {kol-ad'-zo} from kolos (dwarf); properly, to curtail, i.e. (figuratively) to chastise (or reserve for infliction):--punish.

G2850.text: κολακεία kolakeiva kolakeia {kol-ak-i'-ah} from a derivative of kolax (a fawner); flattery:--X flattering.

G2851.text: κόλασις kovlasis kolasis {kol'-as-is} from 2849; penal infliction:--punishment, torment. see GREEK for 2849

G2852.text: κολαφίζω kolafivzw kolaphizo {kol-af-id'-zo} from a derivative of the base of 2849; to rap with the fist:--buffet. see GREEK for 2849

G2853.text: κολλάω kollavw kollao {kol-lah'-o} from kolla ("glue"); to glue, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to stick (figuratively):--cleave, join (self), keep company.

G2854.text: κολλούριον kollouvrion kollourion {kol-loo'-ree-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of kollura (a cake; prob akin to the base of 2853); properly, a poultice (as made of or in the form of crackers), i.e. (by analogy) a plaster:-- eyesalve. see GREEK for 2853

G2855.text: κολλυβιστής kollubisthvs kollubistes {kol-loo-bis-tace'} from a presumed derivative of kollubos (a small coin; probably akin to 2854); a coin-dealer:--(money-)changer. see GREEK for 2854

G2856.text: κολοβόω kolobovw koloboo {kol-ob-o'-o} from a derivative of the base of 2849; to dock, i.e. (figuratively) abridge:--shorten. see GREEK for 2849

G2857.text: Κολοσσαί Kolossaiv Kolossai {kol-os-sah'-ee} apparently feminine plural of kolossos ("colossal"); Colossae, a place in Asia Minor:--Colosse.

G2858.text: Κολοσσαεύς Kolossaeus Kolossaeus {kol-os-sayoos'} from 2857; a Colossaean, (i.e. inhabitant of Colossae:--Colossian. see GREEK for 2857

G2859.text: κόλπος kovlpos kolpos {kol'-pos} apparently a primary word; the bosom; by analogy, a bay:--bosom, creek.

G2860.text: κολυμβάω kolumbavw kolumbao {kol-oom-bah'-o} from kolumbos (a diver); to plunge into water:--swim.

G2861.text: κολυμβήθρα kolumbhvqra kolumbethra {kol-oom-bay'-thrah} a diving-place, i.e. pond for bathing (or swimming):--pool.

G2862.text: κολωνία kolwniva kolonia {kol-o-nee'-ah} of Latin origin; a Roman "colony" for veterans:--colony.

G2863.text: κομάω komavw komao {kom-ah'-o} from 2864; to wear tresses of hair:--have long hair. see GREEK for 2864

G2864.text: κόμη kovmh kome {kom'-ay} apparently from the same as 2865; the hair of the head (locks, as ornamental, and thus differing from 2359; which properly denotes merely the scalp):--hair. see GREEK for 2865 see GREEK for 2359

G2865.text: κομίζω komivzw komizo {kom-id'-zo} from a primary komeo (to tend, i.e. take care of); properly, to provide for, i.e. (by implication) to carry off (as if from harm; genitive case obtain):--bring, receive.

G2866.text: κομψότερον komyovteron kompsoteron {komp-sot'-er-on} neuter comparative of a derivative of the base of 2865 (meaning, properly, well dressed, i.e. nice); figuratively, convalescent:--+ began to amend.

G2867.text: κονιάω koniavw koniao {kon-ee-ah'-o} from konia (dust; by analogy, lime); to whitewash:--whiten.

G2868.text: κονιορτός koniortovs koniortos {kon-ee-or-tos'} from the base of 2867 and ornumi (to "rouse"); pulverulence (as blown about):--dust. see GREEK for 2867

G2869.text: κοπάζω kopavzw kopazo {kop-ad'-zo} from 2873; to tire, i.e. (figuratively) to relax:--cease. see GREEK for 2873

G2870.text: κοπετός kopetovs kopetos {kop-et-os'} from 2875; mourning (properly, by beating the breast):--lamentation. see GREEK for 2875

G2871.text: κοπή kophv kope {kop-ay'} from 2875; cutting, i.e. carnage:--slaughter. see GREEK for 2875

G2872.text: κοπιάω kopiavw kopiao {kop-ee-ah'-o} from a derivative of 2873; to feel fatigue; by implication, to work hard:--(bestow) labour, toil, be wearied. see GREEK for 2873

G2873.text: κόπος kovpos kopos {kop'-os} from 2875; a cut, i.e. (by analogy) toil (as reducing the strength), literally or figuratively; by implication, pains:--labour, + trouble, weariness. see GREEK for 2875

G2874.text: κόπρια kovpria kopria {kop-ree'-ah} from kopros (ordure; perhaps akin to 2875); manure:--dung(-hill). see GREEK for 2875

G2875.text: κόπτω kovptw kopto {kop'-to} a primary verb; to "chop"; specially, to beat the breast in grief:--cut down, lament, mourn, (be-)wail. Compare the base of 5114. see GREEK for 5114

G2876.text: κόραξ kovrax korax {kor'-ax} perhaps from 2880; a crow (from its voracity):--raven. see GREEK for 2880

G2877.text: κοράσιον koravsion korasion {kor-as'-ee-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of kore (a maiden); a (little) girl:--damsel, maid.

G2878.text: κορβᾶν κορβανᾶς korba'n korbana's korban {kor-ban'} and korbanas {kor-ban-as'} and korbanas kor-ban-as' of Hebrew and Chaldee origin respectively (7133); a votive offering and the offering; a consecrated present (to the Temple fund); by extension (the latter term) the Treasury itself, i.e. the room where the contribution boxes stood:--Corban, treasury. see HEBREW for 07133

G2879.text: Κόρε Kovre Kore {kor-eh'} of Hebrew origin (7141); Core (i.e. Korach), an Israelite:--Core. see HEBREW for 07141

G2880.text: κορέννυμι korevnnumi korennumi {kor-en'-noo-mee} a primary verb; to cram, i.e. glut or sate:--eat enough, full.

G2881.text: Κορίνθιος Korivnqios Korinthios {kor-in'-thee-os} from 2882; a Corinthian, i.e. inhabitant of Corinth:--Corinthian. see GREEK for 2882

G2882.text: Κόρινθος Kovrinqos Korinthos {kor'-in-thos} of uncertain derivation; Corinthus, a city of Greece:--Corinth.

G2883.text: Κορνήλιος Kornhvlios Kornelios {kor-nay'-lee-os} of Latin origin; Cornelius, a Roman:--Cornelius.

G2884.text: κόρος kovros koros {kor'-os} of Hebrew origin (3734); a cor, i.e. a specific measure:--measure. see HEBREW for 03734

G2885.text: κοσμέω kosmevw kosmeo {kos-meh'-o} from 2889; to put in proper order, i.e. decorate (literally or figuratively); specially, to snuff (a wick):--adorn, garnish, trim. see GREEK for 2889

G2886.text: κοσμικός kosmikovs kosmikos {kos-mee-kos'} from 2889 (in its secondary sense); terrene ("cosmic"), literally (mundane) or figuratively (corrupt):--worldly. see GREEK for 2889

G2887.text: κόσμιος kovsmios kosmios {kos'-mee-os} from 2889 (in its primary sense); orderly, i.e. decorous:--of good behaviour, modest. see GREEK for 2889

G2888.text: κοσμοκράτωρ kosmokravtwr kosmokrator {kos-mok-rat'-ore} from 2889 and 2902; a world-ruler, an epithet of Satan:--ruler. see GREEK for 2889 see GREEK for 2902

G2889.text: κόσμος kovsmos kosmos {kos'-mos} probably from the base of 2865; orderly arrangement, i.e. decoration; by implication, the world (in a wide or narrow sense, including its inhabitants, literally or figuratively (morally)):--adorning, world. see GREEK for 2865

G2890.text: Κούαρτος Kouvartos Kouartos {koo'-ar-tos} of Latin origin (fourth); Quartus, a Christian:--Quartus.

G2891.text: κουμ koum koumi {koo'-mee} of Chaldee origin (6966); cumi (i.e. rise!):--cumi. see HEBREW for 06966

G2892.text: κουστωδία koustwdiva koustodia {koos-to-dee'-ah} of Latin origin; "custody", i.e. a Roman sentry:--watch.

G2893.text: κουφίζω koufivzw kouphizo {koo-fid'-zo} from kouphos (light in weight); to unload:--lighten.

G2894.text: κόφινος kovfinos kophinos {kof'-ee-nos} of uncertain derivation; a (small) basket:--basket.

G2895.text: κράβαττος kravbattos krabbatos {krab'-bat-os} probably of foreign origin; a mattress:--bed.

G2896.text: κράζω kravzw krazo {krad'-zo} a primary verb; properly, to "croak" (as a raven) or scream, i.e. (genitive case) to call aloud (shriek, exclaim, intreat):--cry (out).

G2897.text: κρεπάλη κραιπάλη krepavlh kraipavlh kraipale {krahee-pal'-ay} probably from the same as 726; properly, a headache (as a seizure of pain) from drunkenness, i.e. (by implication) a debauch (by analogy, a glut):--surfeiting. see GREEK for 726

G2898.text: κρανίον kranivon kranion {kran-ee'-on} diminutive of a derivative of the base of 2768; a skull ("cranium"):--Calvary, skull. see GREEK for 2768

G2899.text: κράσπεδον kravspedon kraspedon {kras'-ped-on} of uncertain derivation; a margin, i.e. (specially), a fringe or tassel:--border, hem.

G2900.text: κραταιός krataiovs krataios {krat-ah-yos'} from 2904; powerful:--mighty. see GREEK for 2904

G2901.text: κραταιόω krataiovw krataioo {krat-ah-yo'-o} from 2900; to empower, i.e. (passively) increase in vigor:--be strengthened, be (wax) strong. see GREEK for 2900

G2902.text: κρατέω kratevw krateo {krat-eh'-o} from 2904; to use strength, i.e. seize or retain (literally or figuratively):--hold (by, fast), keep, lay hand (hold) on, obtain, retain, take (by). see GREEK for 2904

G2903.text: κράτιστος kravtistos kratistos {krat'-is-tos} superlative of a derivative of 2904; strongest, i.e. (in dignity) very honorable:--most excellent (noble). see GREEK for 2904

G2904.text: κράτος kravtos kratos {krat'-os} perhaps a primary word; vigor ("great") (literally or figuratively):--dominion, might(-ily), power, strength.

G2905.text: κραυγάζω kraugavzw kraugazo {krow-gad'-zo} from 2906; to clamor:--cry out. see GREEK for 2906

G2906.text: κραυγή kraughv krauge {krow-gay'} from 2896; an outcry (in notification, tumult or grief):--clamour, cry(-ing). see GREEK for 2896

G2907.text: κρέας krevas kreas {kreh'-as} perhaps a primary word; (butcher's) meat:--flesh.

G2908.text: ἀγαθός κρείττων κρείσσων ajgaqovs kreivttwn kreivsswn kreisson {krice'-son} neuter of an alternate form of 2909; (as noun) better, i.e. greater advantage:--better. see GREEK for 2909

G2909.text: κρείττων κρείσσων kreivttwn kreivsswn kreitton {krite'-tohn} comparative of a derivative of 2904; stronger, i.e. (figuratively) better, i.e. nobler:--best, better. see GREEK for 2904

G2910.text: κρεμάννυμι kremavnnumi kremannumi {krem-an'-noo-mee} a prolonged form of a primary verb; to hang:--hang.

G2911.text: κρημνός krhmnovs kremnos {krame-nos'} from 2910; overhanging, i.e. a precipice:--steep place. see GREEK for 2910

G2912.text: Κρής Krhvs Kres {krace} from 2914; a Cretan, i.e. inhabitant of Crete:--Crete, Cretian. see GREEK for 2914

G2913.text: Κρήσκης Krhvskhs Kreskes {krace'-kace} of Latin origin; growing; Cresces (i.e. Crescens), a Christian:--Crescens.

G2914.text: Κρήτη Krhvth Krete {kray'-tay} of uncertain derivation; Crete, an island in the Mediterranean:--Crete.

G2915.text: κριθή kriqhv krithe {kree-thay'} of uncertain derivation; barley:--barley.

G2916.text: κρίθινος krivqinos krithinos {kree'-thee-nos} from 2915; consisting of barley:--barley. see GREEK for 2915

G2917.text: κρίμα krivma krima {kree'-mah} from 2919; a decision (the function or the effect, for or against ("crime")):--avenge, condemned, condemnation, damnation, + go to law, judgment. see GREEK for 2919

G2918.text: κρίνον krivnon krinon {kree'-non} perhaps a prim word; a lily:--lily.

G2919.text: κρίνω krivnw krino {kree'-no} properly, to distinguish, i.e. decide (mentally or judicially); by implication, to try, condemn, punish:--avenge, conclude, condemn, damn, decree, determine, esteem, judge, go to (sue at the) law, ordain, call in question, sentence to, think.

G2920.text: κρίσις krivsis krisis {kree'-sis} decision (subjectively or objectively, for or against); by extension, a tribunal; by implication, justice (especially, divine law):--accusation, condemnation, damnation, judgment.

G2921.text: Κρίσπος Krivspos Krispos {kris'-pos} of Latin origin; "crisp"; Crispus, a Corinthian:--Crispus.

G2922.text: κριτήριον krithvrion kriterion {kree-tay'-ree-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of 2923; a rule of judging ("criterion"), i.e. (by implication) a tribunal:--to judge, judgment (seat). see GREEK for 2923

G2923.text: κριτής krithvs krites {kree-tace'} from 2919; a judge (genitive case or specially):--judge. see GREEK for 2919

G2924.text: κριτικός kritikovs kritikos {krit-ee-kos'} from 2923; decisive ("critical"), i.e. discriminative:--discerner. see GREEK for 2923

G2925.text: κρούω krouvw krouo {kroo'-o} apparently a primary verb; to rap:--knock.

G2926.text: κρυπτός kruptovs krupte {kroop-tay'} feminine of 2927; a hidden place, i.e. cellar ("crypt"):--secret. see GREEK for 2927

G2927.text: κρυπτός kruptovs kruptos {kroop-tos'} or kruphaios {kroof-ay'-os} from 2928; concealed, i.e. private:--hid(-den), inward(-ly), secret. see GREEK for 2928

G2928.text: κρύπτω κρύβω kruvptw kruvbw krupto {kroop'-to} a primary verb; to conceal (properly, by covering):--hide (self), keep secret, secret(-ly).

G2929.text: κρυσταλλίζω krustallivzw krustallizo {kroos-tal-lid'-zo} from 2930; to make (i.e. intransitively, resemble) ice ("crystallize"):--be clear as crystal. see GREEK for 2930

G2930.text: κρύσταλλος kruvstallos krustallos {kroos'-tal-los} from a derivative of kruos (frost); ice, i.e. (by analogy) rock "crystal":--crystal.

G2931.text: κρυφῇ krufh'/ kruphe {kroo-fay'} adverb from 2928; privately:--in secret. see GREEK for 2928

G2932.text: κτάομαι ktavomai ktaomai {ktah'-om-ahee} a primary verb; to get, i.e. acquire (by any means; own):--obtain, possess, provide, purchase.

G2933.text: κτῆμα kth'ma ktema {ktay'-mah} from 2932; an acquirement, i.e. estate:--possession. see GREEK for 2932

G2934.text: κτῆνος kth'nos ktenos {ktay'-nos} from 2932; property, i.e. (specially) a domestic animal:--beast. see GREEK for 2932

G2935.text: κτήτωρ kthvtwr ktetor {ktay'-tore} from 2932; an owner:--possessor. see GREEK for 2932

G2936.text: κτίζω ktivzw ktizo {ktid'-zo} probably akin to 2932 (through the idea of proprietorship of the manufacturer); to fabricate, i.e. found (form originally):--create, Creator, make. see GREEK for 2932

G2937.text: κτίσις ktivsis ktisis {ktis'-is} from 2936; original formation (properly, the act; by implication, the thing, literally or figuratively):--building, creation, creature, ordinance. see GREEK for 2936

G2938.text: κτίσμα ktivsma ktisma {ktis'-mah} from 2936; an original formation (concretely), i.e. product (created thing):--creature. see GREEK for 2936

G2939.text: κτίστης ktivsths ktistes {ktis-tace'} from 2936; a founder, i.e. God (as author of all things):--Creator. see GREEK for 2936

G2940.text: κυβεία kubeiva kubeia {koo-bi'-ah} from kubos (a "cube", i.e. die for playing); gambling, i.e. (figuratively) artifice or fraud:--sleight.

G2941.text: κυβέρνησις kubevrnhsis kubernesis {koo-ber'-nay-sis} from kubernao (of Latin origin, to steer); pilotage, i.e. (figuratively) directorship (in the church):--government.

G2942.text: κυβερνήτης kubernhvths kubernetes {koo-ber-nay'-tace} from the same as 2941; helmsman, i.e. (by implication) captain:--(ship) master. see GREEK for 2941

G2943.text: κυκλόθεν kuklovqen kuklothen {koo-kloth'-en} adverb from the same as 2945; from the circle, i.e. all around:--(round) about. see GREEK for 2945

G2944.text: κυκλόω κυκλεύω kuklovw kukleuvw kukloo {koo-klo'-o} from the same as 2945; to encircle, i.e. surround:--compass (about), come (stand) round about. see GREEK for 2945

G2945.text: κύκλῳ kuvklw/ kuklo {koo'-klo} as if dative case of kuklos (a ring, "cycle"; akin to 2947); i.e. in a circle (by implication, of 1722), i.e. (adverbially) all around:--round about. see GREEK for 2947 see GREEK for 1722

G2946.text: κυλισμός kulismovs kulisma {koo'-lis-mah} from 2947; a wallow (the effect of rolling), i.e. filth:--wallowing. see GREEK for 2947

G2947.text: κυλίομαι kulivomai kulioo {koo-lee-o'-o} from the base of 2949 (through the idea of circularity; compare 2945, 1507); to roll about:--wallow. see GREEK for 2949 see GREEK for 2945 see GREEK for 1507

G2948.text: κυλλός kullovs kullos {kool-los'} from the same as 2947; rocking about, i.e. crippled (maimed, in feet or hands):--maimed. see GREEK for 2947

G2949.text: κῦμα ku'ma kuma {koo'-mah} from kuo (to swell (with young), i.e. bend, curve); a billow (as bursting or toppling):--wave.

G2950.text: κύμβαλον kuvmbalon kumbalon {koom'-bal-on} from a derivative of the base of 2949; a "cymbal" (as hollow):--cymbal. see GREEK for 2949

G2951.text: κύμινον kuvminon kuminon {koo'-min-on} of foreign origin (compare 3646); dill or fennel ("cummin"):--cummin. see HEBREW for 03646

G2952.text: κυνάριον kunavrion kunarion {koo-nar'-ee-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of 2965; a puppy:--dog. see GREEK for 2965

G2953.text: Κύπριος Kuvprios Kuprios {koo'-pree-os} from 2954; a Cyprian (Cypriot), i.e. inhabitant of Cyprus:--of Cyprus. see GREEK for 2954

G2954.text: Κύπρος Kuvpros Kupros {koo'-pros} of uncertain origin; Cyprus, an island in the Mediterranean:--Cyprus.

G2955.text: κύπτω kuvptw kupto {koop'-to} probably from the base of 2949; to bend forward:--stoop (down). see GREEK for 2949

G2956.text: Κυρηναῖος Kurhnai'os Kurenaios {koo-ray-nah'-yos} from 2957; i.e. Cyrenaean, i.e. inhabitant of Cyrene:--of Cyrene, Cyrenian. see GREEK for 2957

G2957.text: Κυρήνη Kurhvnh Kurene {koo-ray'-nay} of uncertain derivation; Cyrene, a region of Africa:--Cyrene.

G2958.text: Κυρήνιος Kurhvnios Kurenios {koo-ray'-nee-os} of Latin origin; Cyrenius (i.e. Quirinus), a Roman:--Cyrenius.

G2959.text: κυρία kuriva Kuria {koo-ree'-ah} feminine of 2962; Cyria, a Christian woman:--lady. see GREEK for 2962

G2960.text: κυριακός kuriakovs kuriakos {koo-ree-ak-os'} from 2962; belonging to the Lord (Jehovah or Jesus):--Lord's. see GREEK for 2962

G2961.text: κυριεύω kurieuvw kurieuo {ko-ree-yoo'-o} from 2962; to rule:--have dominion over, lord, be lord of, exercise lordship over. see GREEK for 2962

G2962.text: κύριος kuvrios kurios {koo'-ree-os} from kuros (supremacy); supreme in authority, i.e. (as noun) controller; by implication, Master (as a respectful title):-- God, Lord, master, Sir.

G2963.text: κυριότης kuriovths kuriotes {koo-ree-ot'-ace} from 2962; mastery, i.e. (concretely and collectively) rulers:--dominion, government. see GREEK for 2962

G2964.text: κυρόω kurovw kuroo {koo-ro'-o} from the same as 2962; to make authoritative, i.e. ratify:--confirm. see GREEK for 2962

G2965.text: κύων kuvwn kuon {koo'-ohn} a primary word; a dog ("hound") (literally or figuratively):--dog.

G2966.text: κῶλον kw'lon kolon {ko'-lon} from the base of 2849; a limb of the body (as if lopped):--carcase. see GREEK for 2849

G2967.text: κωλύω kwluvw koluo {ko-loo'-o} from the base of 2849; to estop, i.e. prevent (by word or act):--forbid, hinder, keep from, let, not suffer, withstand. see GREEK for 2849

G2968.text: κώμη kwvmh kome {ko'-may} from 2749; a hamlet (as if laid down):--town, village. see GREEK for 2749

G2969.text: κωμόπολις kwmovpolis komopolis {ko-mop'-ol-is} from 2968 and 4172; an unwalled city:--town. see GREEK for 2968 see GREEK for 4172

G2970.text: κῶμος kw'mos komos {ko'-mos} from 2749; a carousal (as if letting loose):--revelling, rioting. see GREEK for 2749

G2971.text: κώνωψ kwvnwy konops {ko'-nopes} apparently a derivative of the base of 2759 and a derivative of 3700; a mosquito (from its stinging proboscis):--gnat. see GREEK for 2759 see GREEK for 3700

G2972.text: Κώς Kwvs Kos {koce} of uncertain origin; Cos, an island in the Mediterranean:--Cos.

G2973.text: Κωσάμ Kwsavm Kosam {ko-sam'} of Hebrew origin (compare 7081); Cosam (i.e. Kosam) an Israelite:--Cosam. see HEBREW for 07081

G2974.text: κωφός kwfovs kophos {ko-fos'} from 2875; blunted, i.e. (figuratively) of hearing (deaf) or speech (dumb):--deaf, dumb, speechless. see GREEK for 2875

G2975.text: λαγχάνω lagcavnw lagchano {lang-khan'-o} a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses; to lot, i.e. determine (by implication, receive) especially by lot:--his lot be, cast lots, obtain.

G2976.text: Λάζαρος Lavzaros Lazaros {lad'-zar-os} probably of Hebrew origin (499); Lazarus (i.e. Elazar), the name of two Israelites (one imaginary):--Lazarus. see HEBREW for 0499

G2977.text: λάθρᾳ lavqra/ lathra {lath'-rah} adverb from 2990; privately:--privily, secretly. see GREEK for 2990

G2978.text: λαῖλαψ lai'lay lailaps {lah'-ee-laps} of uncertain derivation; a whirlwind (squall):--storm, tempest.

G2979.text: λακτίζω laktivzw laktizo {lak-tid'-zo} from adverb lax (heelwise); to recalcitrate:--kick.

G2980.text: λαλέω lalevw laleo {lal-eh'-o} a prolonged form of an otherwise obsolete verb; to talk, i.e. utter words:--preach, say, speak (after), talk, tell, utter. Compare 3004. see GREEK for 3004

G2981.text: λαλιά laliav lalia {lal-ee-ah'} from 2980; talk:--saying, speech. see GREEK for 2980

G2982.text: λαμά lamav lama {lam-ah'} 或 lamma {lam-mah'} or lamma lam-mah'; of Hebrew origin (4100 with prepositional prefix); lama (i.e. why):--lama. see HEBREW for 04100

G2983.text: λαμβάνω lambavnw lambano {lam-ban'-o} a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is use only as an alternate in certain tenses; to take (in very many applications, literally and figuratively (properly objective or active, to get hold of; whereas 1209 is rather subjective or passive, to have offered to one; while 138 is more violent, to seize or remove)):--accept, + be amazed, assay, attain, bring, X when I call, catch, come on (X unto), + forget, have, hold, obtain, receive (X after), take (away, up). see GREEK for 1209 see GREEK for 138

G2984.text: Λάμεχ Lavmec Lamech {lam'-ekh} of Hebrew origin (3929); Lamech (i.e. Lemek), a patriarch:--Lamech. see HEBREW for 03929

G2985.text: λαμπάς lampavs lampas {lam-pas'} from 2989; a "lamp" or flambeau:--lamp, light, torch. see GREEK for 2989

G2986.text: λαμπρός lamprovs lampros {lam-pros'} from the same as 2985; radiant; by analogy, limpid; figuratively, magnificent or sumptuous (in appearance):--bright, clear, gay, goodly, gorgeous, white. see GREEK for 2985

G2987.text: λαμπρότης lamprovths lamprotes {lam-prot'-ace} from 2986; brilliancy:--brightness. see GREEK for 2986

G2988.text: λαμπρῶς lamprw's lampros {lam-proce'} adverb from 2986; brilliantly, i.e. figuratively, luxuriously:--sumptuously. see GREEK for 2986

G2989.text: λάμπω lavmpw lampo {lam'-po} a primary verb; to beam, i.e. radiate brilliancy (literally or figuratively):--give light, shine.

G2990.text: λανθάνω lanqavnw lanthano {lan-than'-o} a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses; to lie hid (literally or figuratively); often used adverbially, unwittingly:--be hid, be ignorant of, unawares.

G2991.text: λαξευτός laxeutovs laxeutos {lax-yoo-tos'} from a compound of las (a stone) and the base of 3584 (in its original sense of scraping); rock-quarried:--hewn in stone. see GREEK for 3584

G2992.text: λαός laovs laos {lah-os'} apparently a primary word; a people (in general; thus differing from 1218, which denotes one's own populace):--people. see GREEK for 1218

G2993.text: Λαοδίκεια Laodivkeia Laodikeia {lah-od-ik'-i-ah} from a compound of 2992 and 1349; Laodicia, a place in Asia Minor:--Laodicea. see GREEK for 2992 see GREEK for 1349

G2994.text: Λαοδικεύς Laodikeuvs Laodikeus {lah-od-ik-yooce'} from 2993; a Laodicean, i.e. inhabitant of Laodicia:--Laodicean. see GREEK for 2993

G2995.text: λάρυγξ lavrugx larugx {lar'-oongks} of uncertain derivation; the throat ("larynx"):--throat.

G2996.text: Λασέα Λασαία Laseva Lasaiva Lasaia {las-ah'-yah} of uncertain origin; Lasaea, a place in Crete:--Lasea.

G2997.text: λακάω lakavw lascho {las'-kho} a strengthened form of a primary verb, which only occurs in this and another prolonged form as alternate in certain tenses; to crack open (from a fall):--burst asunder.

G2998.text: λατομέω latomevw latomeo {lat-om-eh'-o} from the same as the first part of 2991 and the base of 5114; to quarry:--hew. see GREEK for 2991 see GREEK for 5114

G2999.text: λατρεία latreiva latreia {lat-ri'-ah} from 3000; ministration of God, i.e. worship:--(divine) service. see GREEK for 3000

G3000.text: λατρεύω latreuvw latreuo {lat-ryoo'-o} from latris (a hired menial); to minister (to God), i.e. render religious homage:--serve, do the service, worship(-per).

G3001.text: λάχανον lavcanon lachanon {lakh'-an-on} from lachaino (to dig); a vegetable:--herb.

G3002.text: Θαδδαῖος Qaddai'os Lebbaios {leb-bah'-yos} of uncertain origin; Lebbaeus, a Christian:--Lebbaeus.

G3003.text: λεγιών legiwvn legeon {leg-eh-ohn'} of Latin origin; a "legion", i.e. Roman regiment (figuratively):--legion.

G3004.text: λέγω levgw lego {leg'-o} a primary verb; properly, to "lay" forth, i.e. (figuratively) relate (in words (usually of systematic or set discourse; whereas 2036 and 5346 generally refer to an individual expression or speech respectively; while 4483 is properly to break silence merely, and 2980 means an extended or random harangue)); by implication, to mean:--ask, bid, boast, call, describe, give out, name, put forth, say(-ing, on), shew, speak, tell, utter. see GREEK for 2036 see GREEK for 5346 see GREEK for 4483 see GREEK for 2980

G3005.text: λεῖμμα lei'mma leimma {lime'-mah} from 3007; a remainder:--remnant. see GREEK for 3007

G3006.text: λεῖος lei'os leios {li'-os} apparently a primary word; smooth, i.e. "level":--smooth.

G3007.text: λείπω leivpw leipo {li'-po} a primary verb; to leave, i.e. (intransitively or passively) to fail or be absent:--be destitute (wanting), lack.

G3008.text: λειτουργέω leitourgevw leitourgeo {li-toorg-eh'-o} from 3011; to be a public servant, i.e. (by analogy) to perform religious or charitable functions (worship, obey, relieve):--minister. see GREEK for 3011

G3009.text: λειτουργία leitourgiva leitourgia {li-toorg-ee'-ah} from 3008; public function (as priest ("liturgy") or almsgiver):--ministration(-try), service. see GREEK for 3008

G3010.text: λειτουργικός leitourgikovs leitourgikos {li-toorg-ik-os'} from the same as 3008; functional publicly ("liturgic"); i.e. beneficient:--ministering. see GREEK for 3008

G3011.text: λειτουργός leitourgovs leitourgos {li-toorg-os'} from a derivative of 2992 and 2041; a public servant, i.e. a functionary in the Temple or Gospel, or (genitive case) a worshipper (of God) or benefactor (of man):--minister(-ed). see GREEK for 2992 see GREEK for 2041

G3012.text: λέντιον levntion lention {len'-tee-on} of Latin origin; a "linen" cloth, i.e. apron:--towel.

G3013.text: λεπίς lepivs lepis {lep-is'} from lepo (to peel); a flake:--scale.

G3014.text: λέπρα levpra lepra {lep'-rah} from the same as 3013; scaliness, i.e. "leprosy":--leprosy. see GREEK for 3013

G3015.text: λεπρός leprovs lepros {lep-ros'} from the same as 3014; scaly, i.e. leprous (a leper):--leper. see GREEK for 3014

G3016.text: λεπτόν leptovn lepton {lep-ton'} neuter of a derivative of the same as 3013; something scaled (light), i.e. a small coin:--mite. see GREEK for 3013

G3017.text: Λευί Λευίς Leuiv Leuivs Leui {lyoo'-ee} of Hebrew origin (3878); Levi, the name of three Israelites:--Levi. Compare 3018. see GREEK for 3018 see HEBREW for 03878

G3018.text: Λευί Leuiv Leuis {lyoo-is'} a form of 3017; Lewis (i.e. Levi), a Christian:--Levi. see GREEK for 3017

G3019.text: Λευίτης Leuivths Leuites {lyoo-ee'-tace} from 3017; a Levite, i.e. descendant of Levi:--Levite. see GREEK for 3017

G3020.text: Λευιτικός Leuitikovs Leuitikos {lyoo-it'-ee-kos} from 3019; Levitic, i.e. relating to the Levites:--Levitical. see GREEK for 3019

G3021.text: λευκαίνω leukaivnw leukaino {lyoo-kah'-ee-no} from 3022; to whiten:--make white, whiten. see GREEK for 3022

G3022.text: λευκός leukovs leukos {lyoo-kos'} from luke ("light"); white:--white.

G3023.text: λέων levwn leon {leh-ohn'} a primary word; a "lion":--lion.

G3024.text: λήθη lhvqh lethe {lay'-thay} from 2990; forgetfulness:--+ forget. see GREEK for 2990

G3025.text: ληνός lhnovs lenos {lay-nos'} apparently a primary word; a trough, i.e. wine-vat:--winepress.

G3026.text: λῆρος lh'ros leros {lay'-ros} apparently a primary word; twaddle, i.e. an incredible story:--idle tale.

G3027.text: λῃστής lh/sthvs lestes {lace-tace'} from leizomai (to plunder); a brigand:--robber, thief.

G3028.text: λῆμψις lh'myis lepsis {lape'-sis} from 2983; receipt (the act):--receiving. see GREEK for 2983

G3029.text: λίαν livan lian {lee'-an} of uncertain affinity; much (adverbially):--exceeding, great(-ly), sore, very (+ chiefest).

G3030.text: λίβανος livbanos libanos {lib'-an-os} of foreign origin (3828); the incense-tree, i.e. (by implication) incense itself:--frankincense. see HEBREW for 03828

G3031.text: λιβανωτός libanwtovs libanotos {lib-an-o-tos'} from 3030; frankincense, i.e. (by extension) a censer for burning it:--censer. see GREEK for 3030

G3032.text: Λιβερτῖνος Liberti'nos Libertinos {lib-er-tee'-nos} of Latin origin; a Roman freedman:--Libertine.

G3033.text: Λιβύη Libuvh Libue {lib-oo'-ay} probably from 3047; Libye, a region of Africa:--Libya. see GREEK for 3047

G3034.text: λιθάζω liqavzw lithazo {lith-ad'-zo} from 3037; to lapidate:--stone. see GREEK for 3037

G3035.text: λίθινος livqinos lithinos {lith-ee'-nos} from 3037; stony, i.e. made of stone:--of stone. see GREEK for 3037

G3036.text: λιθοβολέω liqobolevw lithoboleo {lith-ob-ol-eh'-o} from a compound of 3037 and 906; to throw stones, i.e. lapidate:--stone, cast stones. see GREEK for 3037 see GREEK for 906

G3037.text: λίθος livqos lithos {lee'-thos} apparently a primary word; a stone (literally or figuratively):--(mill-, stumbling-)stone.

G3038.text: λιθόστρωτος liqovstrwtos lithostrotos {lith-os'-tro-tos} from 3037 and a derivative of 4766; stone-strewed, i.e. a tessellated mosaic on which the Roman tribunal was placed:--Pavement. see GREEK for 3037 see GREEK for 4766

G3039.text: λικμάω likmavw likmao {lik-mah'-o} from likmos, the equivalent of liknon (a winnowing fan or basket); to winnow, i.e. (by analogy), to triturate:--grind to powder.

G3040.text: λιμήν limhvn limen {lee-mane'} apparently a primary word; a harbor:--haven. Compare 2568. see GREEK for 2568

G3041.text: λίμνη livmnh limne {lim'-nay} probably from 3040 (through the idea of nearness of shore); a pond (large or small):--lake. see GREEK for 3040

G3042.text: λιμός limovs limos {lee-mos'} probably from 3007 (through the idea of destitution); a scarcity of food:--dearth, famine, hunger. see GREEK for 3007

G3043.text: λίνον livnon linon {lee'-non} probably a primary word; flax, i.e. (by implication) "linen":--linen.

G3044.text: Λίνος Livnos Linos {lee'-nos} perhaps from 3043; Linus, a Christian:--Linus. see GREEK for 3043

G3045.text: λιπαρός liparovs liparos {lip-ar-os'} from lipos (grease); fat, i.e. (figuratively) sumptuous:--dainty.

G3046.text: λίτρα livtra litra {lee'-trah} of Latin origin (libra); a pound in weight:--pound.

G3047.text: λίψ livy lips {leeps} probably from leibo (to pour a "libation"); the south(- west) wind (as bringing rain, i.e. (by extension) the south quarter):--southwest.

G3048.text: λογία logiva logia {log-ee'-ah} from 3056 (in the commercial sense); a contribution:--collection, gathering. see GREEK for 3056

G3049.text: λογίζομαι logivzomai logizomai {log-id'-zom-ahee} middle voice from 3056; to take an inventory, i.e. estimate (literally or figuratively):--conclude, (ac-)count (of), + despise, esteem, impute, lay, number, reason, reckon, suppose, think (on). see GREEK for 3056

G3050.text: λογικός logikovs logikos {log-ik-os'} from 3056; rational ("logical"):--reasonable, of the word. see GREEK for 3056

G3051.text: λόγιον lovgion logion {log'-ee-on} neuter of 3052; an utterance (of God):--oracle. see GREEK for 3052

G3052.text: λόγιος lovgios logios {log'-ee-os} from 3056; fluent, i.e. an orator:--eloquent. see GREEK for 3056

G3053.text: λογισμός logismovs logismos {log-is-mos'} from 3049; computation, i.e. (figuratively) reasoning (conscience, conceit):--imagination, thought. see GREEK for 3049

G3054.text: λογομαχέω logomacevw logomacheo {log-om-akh-eh'-o} from a compound of 3056 and 3164; to be disputatious (on trifles):--strive about words. see GREEK for 3056 see GREEK for 3164

G3055.text: λογομαχία logomaciva logomachia {log-om-akh-ee'-ah} from the same as 3054; disputation about trifles ("logomachy"):--strife of words. see GREEK for 3054

G3056.text: λόγος lovgos logos {log'-os} from 3004; something said (including the thought); by implication, a topic (subject of discourse), also reasoning (the mental faculty) or motive; by extension, a computation; specially, (with the article in John) the Divine Expression (i.e. Christ):--account, cause, communication, X concerning, doctrine, fame, X have to do, intent, matter, mouth, preaching, question, reason, + reckon, remove, say(-ing), shew, X speaker, speech, talk, thing, + none of these things move me, tidings, treatise, utterance, word, work. see GREEK for 3004

G3057.text: λόγχη lovgch logche {long'-khay} perhaps a primary word; a "lance":--spear.

G3058.text: λοιδορέω loidorevw loidoreo {loy-dor-eh'-o} from 3060; to reproach, i.e. vilify:--revile. see GREEK for 3060

G3059.text: λοιδορία loidoriva loidoria {loy-dor-ee'-ah} from 3060; slander or vituperation:--railing, reproach(-fully). see GREEK for 3060

G3060.text: λοίδορος loivdoros loidoros {loy'-dor-os} from loidos (mischief); abusive, i.e. a blackguard:--railer, reviler.

G3061.text: λοιμός loimovs loimos {loy'-mos} of uncertain affinity; a plague (literally, the disease, or figuratively, a pest):--pestilence(-t).

G3062.text: λοιπός loipovs loipoy {loy-poy'} masculine plural of a derivative of 3007; remaining ones:--other, which remain, remnant, residue, rest. see GREEK for 3007

G3063.text: λοιπός loipovs loipon {loy-pon'} neuter singular of the same as 3062; something remaining (adverbially):--besides, finally, furthermore, (from) henceforth, moreover, now, + it remaineth, then. see GREEK for 3062

G3064.text: λοιπός loipovs loipou {loy-poo'} genitive case singular of the same as 3062; remaining time:--from henceforth. see GREEK for 3062

G3065.text: Λουκᾶς Louka's Loukas {loo-kas'} contracted from Latin Lucanus; Lucas, a Christian:--Lucas, Luke.

G3066.text: Λούκιος Louvkios Loukios {loo'-kee-os} of Latin origin; illuminative; Lucius, a Christian:--Lucius.

G3067.text: λουτρόν loutrovn loutron {loo-tron'} from 3068; a bath, i.e. (figuratively), baptism:--washing. see GREEK for 3068

G3068.text: λούω louvw louo {loo'-o} a primary verb; to bathe (the whole person; whereas 3538 means to wet a part only, and 4150 to wash, cleanse garments exclusively):--wash. see GREEK for 3538 see GREEK for 4150

G3069.text: Λύδδα Luvdda Ludda {lud'-dah} of Hebrew origin (3850); Lydda (i.e. Lod), a place in Palestine:--Lydda. see HEBREW for 03850

G3070.text: Λυδία Ludiva Ludia {loo-dee'-ah} properly, feminine of Ludios (of foreign origin) (a Lydian, in Asia Minor); Lydia, a Christian woman: -Lydia.

G3071.text: Λυκαονία Lukaoniva Lukaonia {loo-kah-on-ee'-ah} perhaps remotely from 3074; Lycaonia, a region of Asia Minor:--Lycaonia. see GREEK for 3074

G3072.text: Λυκαονιστί Lukaonistiv Lukaonisti {loo-kah-on-is-tee'} adverb from a derivative of 3071; Lycaonistically, i.e. in the language of the Lycaonians:--in the speech of Lycaonia. see GREEK for 3071

G3073.text: Λυκία Lukiva Lukia {loo-kee'-ah} probably remotely from 3074; Lycia, a province of Asia Minor:--Lycia. see GREEK for 3074

G3074.text: λύκος luvkos lukos {loo'-kos} perhaps akin to the base of 3022 (from the whitish hair); a wolf:--wolf. see GREEK for 3022

G3075.text: λυμαίνω lumaivnw lumainomai {loo-mah'-ee-nom-ahee} middle voice from a probably derivative of 3089 (meaning filth); properly, to soil, i.e. (figuratively) insult (maltreat):--make havock of. see GREEK for 3089

G3076.text: λυπέω lupevw lupeo {loo-peh'-o} from 3077; to distress; reflexively or passively, to be sad:--cause grief, grieve, be in heaviness, (be) sorrow(-ful), be (make) sorry. see GREEK for 3077

G3077.text: λύπη luvph lupe {loo'-pay} apparently a primary word; sadness:--grief, grievous, + grudgingly, heaviness, sorrow.

G3078.text: Λυσανίας Lusanivas Lusanias {loo-san-ee'-as} from 3080 and ania (trouble); grief-dispelling; Lysanias, a governor of Abilene:--Lysanias. see GREEK for 3080

G3079.text: Λυσίας Lusivas Lusias {loo-see'-as} of uncertain affinity; Lysias, a Roman:--Lysias.

G3080.text: λύσις luvsis lusis {loo'-sis} from 3089; a loosening, i.e. (specially), divorce:--to be loosed. see GREEK for 3089

G3081.text: λυσιτελέω lusitelevw lusitelei {loo-sit-el-i'} third person singular present indicative active of a derivative of a compound of 3080 and 5056; impersonally, it answers the purpose, i.e. is advantageous:--it is better. see GREEK for 3080 see GREEK for 5056

G3082.text: Λύστρα Luvstra Lustra {loos'-trah} of uncertain origin; Lystra, a place in Asia Minor:--Lystra.

G3083.text: λύτρον luvtron lutron {loo'-tron} from 3089; something to loosen with, i.e. a redemption price (figuratively, atonement):--ransom. see GREEK for 3089

G3084.text: λυτρόω lutrovw lutroo {loo-tro'-o} from 3083; to ransom (literally or figuratively):--redeem. see GREEK for 3083

G3085.text: λύτρωσις luvtrwsis lutrosis {loo'-tro-sis} from 3084; a ransoming (figuratively):--+ redeemed, redemption. see GREEK for 3084

G3086.text: λυτρωτής lutrwthvs lutrotes {loo-tro-tace'} from 3084; a redeemer (figuratively):--deliverer. see GREEK for 3084

G3087.text: λυχνία lucniva luchnia {lookh-nee'-ah} from 3088; a lamp-stand (literally or figuratively):--candlestick. see GREEK for 3088

G3088.text: λύχνος luvcnos luchnos {lookh'-nos} from the base of 3022; a portable lamp or other illuminator (literally or figuratively):--candle, light. see GREEK for 3022

G3089.text: λύω luvw luo {loo'-o} a primary verb; to "loosen" (literally or figuratively):--break (up), destroy, dissolve, (un-)loose, melt, put off. Compare 4486. see GREEK for 4486

G3090.text: Λωΐς Lwi?s Lois {lo-ece'} of uncertain origin; Lois, a Christian woman:--Lois.

G3091.text: Λώτ Lwvt Lot {lote} of Hebrew origin (3876); Lot, a patriarch:--Lot. see HEBREW for 03876

G3092.text: Μάαθ Mavaq Maath {mah-ath'} probably of Hebrew origin; Maath, an Israelite:--Maath.

G3093.text: Μαγαδάν Magadavn Magdala {mag-dal-ah'} of Chaldee origin (compare 4026); the tower; Magdala (i.e. Migdala), a place in Palestine:--Magdala. see HEBREW for 04026

G3094.text: Μαγδαληνή Magdalhnhv Magdalene {mag-dal-ay-nay'} feminine of a derivative of 3093; a female Magdalene, i.e. inhabitant of Magdala:--Magdalene. see GREEK for 3093

G3095.text: μαγεία mageiva mageia {mag-i'-ah} from 3096; "magic":--sorcery. see GREEK for 3096

G3096.text: μαγεύω mageuvw mageuo {mag-yoo'-o} from 3097; to practice magic:--use sorcery. see GREEK for 3097

G3097.text: μάγος mavgos magos {mag'-os} of foreign origin (7248); a Magian, i.e. Oriental scientist; by implication, a magician:--sorcerer, wise man. see HEBREW for 07248

G3098.text: Μαγώγ Magwvg Magog {mag-ogue'} of Hebrew origin (4031); Magog, a foreign nation, i.e. (figuratively) an Antichristian party:--Magog. see HEBREW for 04031

G3099.text: Μαδιάμ Madiavm Madian {mad-ee-on'} of Hebrew origin (4080); Madian (i.e. Midian), a region of Arabia:--Madian. see HEBREW for 04080

G3100.text: μαθητεύω maqhteuvw matheteuo {math-ayt-yoo'-o} from 3101; intransitively, to become a pupil; transitively, to disciple, i.e. enrol as scholar:--be disciple, instruct, teach. see GREEK for 3101

G3101.text: μαθητής maqhthvs mathetes {math-ay-tes'} from 3129; a learner, i.e. pupil:--disciple. see GREEK for 3129

G3102.text: μαθήτρια maqhvtria mathetria {math-ay'-tree-ah} feminine from 3101; a female pupil:--disciple. see GREEK for 3101

G3103.text: Μαθουσαλά Maqousalav Mathousala {math-oo-sal'-ah} of Hebrew origin (4968); Mathusala (i.e. Methushelach), an antediluvian:--Mathusala. see HEBREW for 04968

G3104.text: Μεννά Mennav Mainan {mahee-nan'} probably of Hebrew origin; Mainan, an Israelite:--Mainan.

G3105.text: μαίνομαι maivnomai mainomai {mah'-ee-nom-ahee} middle voice from a primary mao (to long for; through the idea of insensate craving); to rave as a "maniac":--be beside self (mad).

G3106.text: μακαρίζω makarivzw makarizo {mak-ar-id'-zo} from 3107; to beatify, i.e. pronounce (or esteem) fortunate:--call blessed, count happy. see GREEK for 3107

G3107.text: μακάριος makavrios makarios {mak-ar'-ee-os} a prolonged form of the poetical makar (meaning the same); supremely blest; by extension, fortunate, well off:-- blessed, happy(X -ier).

G3108.text: μακαρισμός makarismovs makarismos {mak-ar-is-mos'} from 3106; beatification, i.e. attribution of good fortune:--blessedness. see GREEK for 3106

G3109.text: Μακεδονία Makedoniva Makedonia {mak-ed-on-ee'-ah} from 3110; Macedonia, a region of Greece:--Macedonia. see GREEK for 3110

G3110.text: Μακεδών Makedwvn Makedon {mak-ed'-ohn} of uncertain derivation; a Macedon (Macedonian), i.e. inhabitant of Macedonia:--of Macedonia, Macedonian.

G3111.text: μάκελλον mavkellon makellon {mak'-el-lon} of Latin origin (macellum); a butcher's stall, meat market or provision-shop:--shambles.

G3112.text: μακρός makrovs makran {mak-ran'} feminine accusative case singular of 3117 (3598 being implied); at a distance (literally or figuratively):--(a-)far (off), good (great) way off. see GREEK for 3117 see GREEK for 3598

G3113.text: μακρόθεν makrovqen makrothen {mak-roth'-en} adverb from 3117; from a distance or afar:--afar off, from far. see GREEK for 3117

G3114.text: μακροθυμέω makroqumevw makrothumeo {mak-roth-oo-meh'-o} from the same as 3116; to be long-spirited, i.e. (objectively) forbearing or (subjectively) patient:--bear (suffer) long, be longsuffering, have (long) patience, be patient, patiently endure. see GREEK for 3116

G3115.text: μακροθυμία makroqumiva makrothumia {mak-roth-oo-mee'-ah} from the same as 3116; longanimity, i.e. (objectively) forbearance or (subjectively) fortitude:--longsuffering, patience. see GREEK for 3116

G3116.text: μακροθύμως makroquvmws makrothumos {mak-roth-oo-moce'} adverb of a compound of 3117 and 2372; with long (enduring) temper, i.e. leniently:--patiently. see GREEK for 3117 see GREEK for 2372

G3117.text: μακρός makrovs makros {mak-ros'} from 3372; long (in place (distant) or time (neuter plural)):--far, long. see GREEK for 3372

G3118.text: μακροχρόνιος makrocrovnios makrochronios {mak-rokh-ron'-ee-os} from 3117 and 5550; long-timed, i.e. long-lived:--live long. see GREEK for 3117 see GREEK for 5550

G3119.text: μαλακία malakiva malakia {mal-ak-ee'-ah} from 3120; softness, i.e. enervation (debility):--disease. see GREEK for 3120

G3120.text: μαλακός malakovs malakos {mal-ak-os'} of uncertain affinity; soft, i.e. fine (clothing); figuratively, a catamite:--effeminate, soft.

G3121.text: Μαλελεήλ Malelehvl Maleleel {mal-el-eh-ale'} of Hebrew origin (4111); Maleleel (i.e. Mahalalel), an antediluvian:--Maleleel. see HEBREW for 04111

G3122.text: μάλιστα mavlista malista {mal'-is-tah} neuter plural of the superlative of an apparently primary adverb mala (very); (adverbially) most (in the greatest degree) or particularly:--chiefly, most of all, (e-)specially.

G3123.text: μᾶλλον ma'llon mallon {mal'-lon} neuter of the comparative of the same as 3122; (adverbially) more (in a greater degree)) or rather:--+ better, X far, (the) more (and more), (so) much (the more), rather. see GREEK for 3122

G3124.text: Μάλχος Mavlcos Malchos {mal'-khos} of Hebrew origin (4429); Malchus, an Israelite:--Malchus. see HEBREW for 04429

G3125.text: μάμμη mavmmh mamme {mam'-may} of natural origin ("mammy"); a grandmother:--grandmother.

G3126.text: μαμωνᾶς mamwna's mammonas {mam-mo-nas'} of Chaldee origin (confidence, i.e. wealth, personified); mammonas, i.e. avarice (deified):--mammon.

G3127.text: Μαναήν Manahvn Manaen {man-ah-ane'} of uncertain origin; Manaen, a Christian:--Manaen.

G3128.text: Μανασσῆς Manassh's Manasses {man-as-sace'} of Hebrew origin (4519); Mannasses (i.e. Menashsheh), an Israelite:--Manasses. see HEBREW for 04519

G3129.text: μανθάνω manqavnw manthano {man-than'-o} prolongation from a primary verb, another form of which, matheo, is used as an alternate in certain tenses; to learn (in any way):--learn, understand.

G3130.text: μανία maniva mania {man-ee'-ah} from 3105; craziness:--(+ make) X mad. see GREEK for 3105

G3131.text: μάννα mavnna manna {man'-nah} of Hebrew origin (4478); manna (i.e. man), an edible gum:--manna. see HEBREW for 04478

G3132.text: μαντεύομαι manteuvomai manteuomai {mant-yoo'-om-ahee} from a derivative of 3105 (meaning a prophet, as supposed to rave through inspiration); to divine, i.e. utter spells (under pretense of foretelling:--by soothsaying. see GREEK for 3105

G3133.text: μαραίνομαι maraivnomai maraino {mar-ah'-ee-no} of uncertain affinity; to extinguish (as fire), i.e. (figuratively and passively) to pass away:--fade away.

G3134.text: μαρὰν ἀθά μαράνα θά mara;n ajqav maravna qav maran atha {mar'-an ath'-ah} of Chaldee origin (meaning our Lord has come); maranatha, i.e. an exclamation of the approaching divine judgment:--Maran-atha.

G3135.text: μαργαρίτης margarivths margarites {mar-gar-ee'-tace} from margaros (a pearl-oyster); a pearl:--pearl.

G3136.text: Μάρθα Mavrqa Martha {mar'-thah} probably of Chaldee origin (meaning mistress); Martha, a Christian woman:--Martha.

G3137.text: Μαρία Μαριάμ Mariva Mariavm Maria {mar-ee'-ah} 或 Mariam {mar-ee-am'} or Mariam mar-ee-am' of Hebrew origin (4813); Maria or Mariam (i.e. Mirjam), the name of six Christian females:-- Mary. see HEBREW for 04813

G3138.text: Μᾶρκος Ma'rkos Markos {mar'-kos} of Latin origin; Marcus, a Christian:--Marcus, Mark.

G3139.text: μάρμαρος mavrmaros marmaros {mar'-mar-os} from marmairo (to glisten); marble (as sparkling white):--marble.

G3140.text: μαρτυρέω marturevw martureo {mar-too-reh'-o} from 3144; to be a witness, i.e. testify (literally or figuratively):--charge, give (evidence), bear record, have (obtain, of) good (honest) report, be well reported of, testify, give (have) testimony, (be, bear, give, obtain) witness. see GREEK for 3144

G3141.text: μαρτυρία marturiva marturia {mar-too-ree'-ah} from 3144; evidence given (judicially or genitive case):--record, report, testimony, witness. see GREEK for 3144

G3142.text: μαρτύριον martuvrion marturion {mar-too'-ree-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of 3144; something evidential, i.e. (genitive case) evidence given or (specially), the Decalogue (in the sacred Tabernacle):--to be testified, testimony, witness. see GREEK for 3144

G3143.text: μαρτύρομαι martuvromai marturomai {mar-too'-rom-ahee} middle voice from 3144; to be adduced as a witness, i.e. (figuratively) to obtest (in affirmation or exhortation):--take to record, testify. see GREEK for 3144

G3144.text: μάρτυς mavrtus martus {mar'-toos} of uncertain affinity; a witness (literally (judicially) or figuratively (genitive case)); by analogy, a "martyr":-- martyr, record, witness.

G3145.text: μασάομαι masavomai massaomai {mas-sah'-om-ahee} from a primary masso (to handle or squeeze); to chew:--gnaw.

G3146.text: μαστιγόω mastigovw mastigoo {mas-tig-o'-o} from 3148; to flog (literally or figuratively):--scourge. see GREEK for 3148

G3147.text: μαστίζω mastivzw mastizo {mas-tid'-zo} from 3149; to whip (literally):--scourge. see GREEK for 3149

G3148.text: μάστιξ mavstix mastix {mas'-tix} probably from the base of 3145 (through the idea of contact); a whip (literally, the Roman flagellum for criminals; figuratively, a disease):--plague, scourging. see GREEK for 3145

G3149.text: μαστός mastovs mastos {mas-tos'} from the base of 3145; a (properly, female) breast (as if kneaded up):--pap. see GREEK for 3145

G3150.text: ματαιολογία mataiologiva mataiologia {mat-ah-yol-og-ee'-ah} from 3151; random talk, i.e. babble:--vain jangling. see GREEK for 3151

G3151.text: ματαιολόγος mataiolovgos mataiologos {mat-ah-yol-og'-os} from 3152 and 3004; an idle (i.e. senseless or mischievous) talker, i.e. a wrangler:--vain talker. see GREEK for 3152 see GREEK for 3004

G3152.text: μάταιος mavtaios mataios {mat'-ah-yos} from the base of 3155; empty, i.e. (literally) profitless, or (specially), an idol:--vain, vanity. see GREEK for 3155

G3153.text: ματαιότης mataiovths mataiotes {mat-ah-yot'-ace} from 3152; inutility; figuratively, transientness; morally, depravity:--vanity. see GREEK for 3152

G3154.text: ματαιόομαι mataiovomai mataioo {mat-ah-yo'-o} from 3152; to render (passively, become) foolish, i.e. (morally) wicked or (specially), idolatrous:--become vain. see GREEK for 3152

G3155.text: μάτην mavthn maten {mat'-ane} accusative case of a derivative of the base of 3145 (through the idea of tentative manipulation, i.e. unsuccessful search, or else of punishment); folly, i.e. (adverbially) to no purpose:--in vain. see GREEK for 3145

G3156.text: Μαθθαῖος Maqqai'os Matthaios {mat-thah'-yos} a shorter form of 3164; Matthaeus (i.e. Matthitjah), an Israelite and a Christian:--Matthew. see GREEK for 3164

G3157.text: Ματθάν Matqavn Matthan {mat-than'} of Hebrew origin (4977); Matthan (i.e. Mattan), an Israelite:--Matthan. see HEBREW for 04977

G3158.text: Ματθάτ Matqavt Matthat {mat-that'} probably a shortened form of 3161; Matthat (i.e. Mattithjah), the name of two Israelites:--Mathat. see GREEK for 3161

G3159.text: Μαθθίας Maqqivas Matthias {mat-thee'-as} apparently a shortened form of 3161; Matthias (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite:--Matthias. see GREEK for 3161

G3160.text: Ματταθά Mattaqav Mattatha {mat-tath-ah'} probably a shortened form of 3161 (compare 4992); Mattatha (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite:--Mattatha. see GREEK for 3161 see GREEK for 4992

G3161.text: Ματταθίας Mattaqivas Mattathias {mat-tath-ee'-as} of Hebrew origin (4993); Mattathias (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite and a Christian:--Mattathias. see HEBREW for 04993

G3162.text: μάχαιρα mavcaira machaira {makh'-ahee-rah} probably feminine of a presumed derivative of 3163; a knife, i.e. dirk; figuratively, war, judicial punishment:--sword. see GREEK for 3163

G3163.text: μάχη mavch mache {makh'-ay} from 3164; a battle, i.e. (figuratively) controversy:--fighting, strive, striving. see GREEK for 3164

G3164.text: μάχομαι mavcomai machomai {makh'-om-ahee} middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to war, i.e. (figuratively) to quarrel, dispute:--fight, strive.

G3165.text: ἐγώ ejgwv me {meh} a shorter (and probably originally) from of 1691; me:--I, me, my. see GREEK for 1691

G3166.text: αὐχέω aujcevw megalaucheo {meg-al-ow-kheh'-o} from a compound of 3173 and aucheo (to boast; akin to 837 and 2744); to talk big, i.e. be grandiloquent (arrogant, egotistic):--boast great things. see GREEK for 3173 see GREEK for 837 see GREEK for 2744

G3167.text: μεγαλεῖος megalei'os megaleios {meg-al-i'-os} from 3173; magnificent, i.e. (neuter, plural as noun) a conspicuous favor, or (subjectively) perfection:--great things, wonderful works. see GREEK for 3173

G3168.text: μεγαλειότης megaleiovths megaleiotes {meg-al-i-ot'-ace} from 3167; superbness, i.e. glory or splendor:--magnificence, majesty, mighty power. see GREEK for 3167

G3169.text: μεγαλοπρεπής megaloprephvs megaloprepes {meg-al-op-rep-ace'} from 3173 and 4241; befitting greatness or magnificence (majestic):--excellent. see GREEK for 3173 see GREEK for 4241

G3170.text: μεγαλύνω megaluvnw megaluno {meg-al-oo'-no} from 3173; to make (or declare) great, i.e. increase or (figuratively) extol:--enlarge, magnify, shew great. see GREEK for 3173

G3171.text: μεγάλως megavlws megalos {meg-al'-oce} adverb from 3173; much:--greatly. see GREEK for 3173

G3172.text: μεγαλωσύνη megalwsuvnh megalosune {meg-al-o-soo'-nay} from 3173; greatness, i.e. (figuratively) divinity (often God himself):--majesty. see GREEK for 3173

G3173.text: μέγας mevgas megas {meg'-as} (including the prolonged forms, feminine megale, plural megaloi, etc.; compare also 3176, 3187); big (literally or figuratively, in a very wide application):--(+ fear) exceedingly, great(-est), high, large, loud, mighty, + (be) sore (afraid), strong, X to years. see GREEK for 3176 see GREEK for 3187

G3174.text: μέγεθος mevgeqos megethos {meg'-eth-os} from 3173; magnitude (figuratively):--greatness. see GREEK for 3173

G3175.text: μεγιστάν megistavn megistanes {meg-is-tan'-es} plural from 3176; grandees:--great men, lords. see GREEK for 3176

G3176.text: μέγιστος mevgistos megistos {meg'-is-tos} superlative of 3173; greatest or very great:--exceeding great. see GREEK for 3173

G3177.text: μεθερμηνεύω meqermhneuvw methermeneuo {meth-er-mane-yoo'-o} from 3326 and 2059; to explain over, i.e. translate:--(by) interpret(-ation). see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 2059

G3178.text: μέθη mevqh methe {meth'-ay} apparently a primary word; an intoxicant, i.e. (by implication) intoxication:--drunkenness.

G3180.text: μεθοδεία meqodeiva methodeia {meth-od-i'-ah} from a compound of 3326 and 3593 (compare "method"); travelling over, i.e. travesty (trickery):--wile, lie in wait. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 3593

G3181.text: μεθόριον ου τό methorios methorios {meth-or'-ee-os} from 3326 and 3725; bounded alongside, i.e. contiguous (neuter plural as noun, frontier):--border. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 3725

G3182.text: μεθύσκω mequvskw methusko {meth-oos'-ko} a prolonged (transitive) form of 3184; to intoxicate:--be drunk(-en). see GREEK for 3184

G3183.text: μέθυσος mevqusos methusos {meth'-oo-sos} from 3184; tipsy, i.e. (as noun) a sot:--drunkard. see GREEK for 3184

G3184.text: μεθύω mequvw methuo {meth-oo'-o} from another form of 3178; to drink to intoxication, i.e. get drunk:--drink well, make (be) drunk(-en). see GREEK for 3178

G3185.text: μέγας mevgas meizon {mide'-zon} neuter of 3187; (adverbially) in greater degree:--the more. see GREEK for 3187

G3186.text: μέγας mevgas meizoteros {mide-zot'-er-os} continued comparative of 3187; still larger (figuratively):--greater. see GREEK for 3187

G3187.text: μέγας mevgas meizon {mide'-zone} irregular comparative of 3173; larger (literally or figuratively, specially, in age):--elder, greater(-est), more. see GREEK for 3173

G3188.text: μέλας mevlas melan {mel'-an} neuter of 3189 as noun; ink:--ink. see GREEK for 3189

G3189.text: μέλας mevlas melas {mel'-as} apparently a primary word; black:--black.

G3190.text: Μελεά Meleav Meleas {mel-eh-as'} of uncertain origin; Meleas, an Israelite:--Meleas.

G3191.text: μελετάω meletavw meletao {mel-et-ah'-o} from a presumed derivative of 3199; to take care of, i.e. (by implication) revolve in the mind:--imagine, (pre-)meditate. see GREEK for 3199

G3192.text: μέλι mevli meli {mel'-ee} apparently a primary word; honey:--honey.

G3193.text: μελίσσιος α ον melissios melissios {mel-is'-see-os} from 3192; relating to honey, i.e. bee (comb):--honeycomb. see GREEK for 3192

G3194.text: Μελιτήνη Μελίτη Melithvnh Melivth Melite {mel-ee'-tay} of uncertain origin; Melita, an island in the Mediterranean:--Melita.

G3195.text: μέλλω mevllw mello {mel'-lo} a strengthened form of 3199 (through the idea of expectation); to intend, i.e. be about to be, do, or suffer something (of persons or things, especially events; in the sense of purpose, duty, necessity, probability, possibility, or hesitation):--about, after that, be (almost), (that which is, things, + which was for) to come, intend, was to (be), mean, mind, be at the point, (be) ready, + return, shall (begin), (which, that) should (after, afterwards, hereafter) tarry, which was for, will, would, be yet. see GREEK for 3199

G3196.text: μέλος mevlos melos {mel'-os} of uncertain affinity; a limb or part of the body:--member.

G3197.text: Μελχί Melciv Melchi {mel-khee'} of Hebrew origin (4428 with pronominal suffix, my king); Melchi (i.e. Malki), the name of two Israelites:--Melchi. see HEBREW for 04428

G3198.text: Μελχισέδεκ Melcisevdek Melchisedek {mel-khis-ed-ek'} of Hebrew origin (4442); Melchisedek (i.e. Malkitsedek), a patriarch:--Melchisedec. see HEBREW for 04442

G3199.text: μέλω mevlw melo {mel'-o} a primary verb; to be of interest to, i.e. to concern (only third person singular present indicative used impersonally, it matters):--(take) care.

G3200.text: μεμβράνα membravna membrana {mem-bran'-ah} of Latin origin ("membrane"); a (written) sheep-skin:--parchment.

G3201.text: μέμφομαι mevmfomai memphomai {mem'-fom-ahee} middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to blame:--find fault.

G3202.text: μεμψίμοιρος memyivmoiros mempsimoiros {mem-psim'-oy-ros} from a presumed derivative of 3201 and moira (fate; akin to the base of 3313); blaming fate, i.e. querulous (discontented):--complainer. see GREEK for 3201 see GREEK for 3313

G3303.text: μέν mevn men {men} a primary particle; properly, indicative of affirmation or concession (in fact); usually followed by a contrasted clause with 1161 (this one, the former, etc.):--even, indeed, so, some, truly, verily. Often compounded with other particles in an intensive or asseverative sense. see GREEK for 1161

G3304.text: μενοῦν μενοῦνγε menou'n menou'nge menounge {men-oon'-geh} from 3203 and 3767 and 1065; so then at least:--nay but, yea doubtless (rather, verily). see GREEK for 3203 see GREEK for 3767 see GREEK for 1065

G3305.text: μέντοι mevntoi mentoi {men'-toy} from 3203 and 5104; indeed though, i.e. however:--also, but, howbeit, nevertheless, yet. see GREEK for 3203 see GREEK for 5104

G3306.text: μένω mevnw meno {men'-o} a primary verb; to stay (in a given place, state, relation or expectancy):--abide, continue, dwell, endure, be present, remain, stand, tarry (for), X thine own.

G3307.text: μερίζω merivzw merizo {mer-id'-zo} from 3313; to part, i.e. (literally) to apportion, bestow, share, or (figuratively) to disunite, differ:--deal, be difference between, distribute, divide, give participle see GREEK for 3313

G3308.text: μέριμνα mevrimna merimna {mer'-im-nah} from 3307 (through the idea of distraction); solicitude:--care. see GREEK for 3307

G3309.text: μεριμνάω merimnavw merimnao {mer-im-nah'-o} from 3308; to be anxious about:--(be, have) care(-ful), take thought. see GREEK for 3308

G3310.text: μερίς merivs meris {mer-ece'} feminine of 3313; a portion, i.e. province, share or (abstractly) participation:--part (X -akers). see GREEK for 3313

G3311.text: μερισμός merismovs merismos {mer-is-mos'} from 3307; a separation or distribution:--dividing asunder, gift. see GREEK for 3307

G3312.text: μεριστής meristhvs meristes {mer-is-tace'} from 3307; an apportioner (administrator):--divider. see GREEK for 3307

G3313.text: μέρος mevros meros {mer'-os} from an obsolete but more primary form of meiromai (to get as a section or allotment); a division or share (literally or figuratively, in a wide application):--behalf, course, coast, craft, particular (+ -ly), part (+ -ly), piece, portion, respect, side, some sort(-what).

G3314.text: μεσημβρία meshmbriva mesembria {mes-ame-bree'-ah} from 3319 and 2250; midday; by implication, the south:--noon, south. see GREEK for 3319 see GREEK for 2250

G3315.text: μεσιτεύω mesiteuvw mesiteuo {mes-it-yoo'-o} from 3316; to interpose (as arbiter), i.e (by implication) to ratify (as surety):--confirm. see GREEK for 3316

G3316.text: μεσίτης mesivths mesites {mes-ee'-tace} from 3319; a go-between, i.e. (simply) an internunciator, or (by implication) a reconciler (intercessor):--mediator. see GREEK for 3319

G3317.text: μεσονύκτιον mesonuvktion mesonuktion {mes-on-ook'-tee-on} neuter of compound of 3319 and 3571; midnight (especially as a watch):--midnight. see GREEK for 3319 see GREEK for 3571

G3318.text: Μεσοποταμία Mesopotamiva Mesopotamia {mes-op-ot-am-ee'-ah} from 3319 and 4215; Mesopotamia (as lying between the Euphrates and the Tigris; compare 0763), a region of Asia:--Mesopotamia. see GREEK for 3319 see GREEK for 4215 see HEBREW for 0763

G3319.text: μέσος mevsos mesos {mes'-os} from 3326; middle (as an adjective or (neuter) noun):--among, X before them, between, + forth, mid(-day, -night), midst, way. see GREEK for 3326

G3320.text: μεσότοιχον mesovtoicon mesotoichon {mes-ot'-oy-khon} from 3319 and 5109; a partition (figuratively):--middle wall. see GREEK for 3319 see GREEK for 5109

G3321.text: μεσουράνημα mesouravnhma mesouranema {mes-oo-ran'-ay-mah} from a presumed compound of 3319 and 3772; mid-sky:--midst of heaven. see GREEK for 3319 see GREEK for 3772

G3322.text: μεσόω mesovw mesoo {mes-o'-o} from 3319; to form the middle, i.e. (in point of time), to be half-way over:--be about the midst. see GREEK for 3319
