G3323.text: Μεσσίας Messivas Messias {mes-see'-as} of Hebrew origin (4899); the Messias (i.e. Mashiach), or Christ:--Messias. see HEBREW for 04899

G3324.text: μεστός mestovs mestos {mes-tos'} of uncertain derivation:--replete (literally or figuratively):--full.

G3325.text: μεστόω mestovw mestoo {mes-to'-o} from 3324; to replenish, i.e. (by implication) to intoxicate:--fill. see GREEK for 3324

G3326.text: μετά metav meta {met-ah'} a primary preposition (often used adverbially); properly, denoting accompaniment; "amid" (local or causal); modified variously according to the case (genitive association, or accusative succession) with which it is joined; occupying an intermediate position between 575 or 1537 and 1519 or 4314; less intimate than 1722 and less close than 4862):--after(-ward), X that he again, against, among, X and, + follow, hence, hereafter, in, of, (up-)on, + our, X and setting, since, (un-)to, + together, when, with (+ -out). Often used in composition, in substantially the same relations of participation or proximity, and transfer or sequence. see GREEK for 4314 see GREEK for 575 see GREEK for 1537 see GREEK for 1519 see GREEK for 1722 see GREEK for 4862

G3327.text: μεταβαίνω metabaivnw metabaino {met-ab-ah'-ee-no} from 3326 and the base of 939; to change place:--depart, go, pass, remove. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 939

G3328.text: μεταβάλλω metabavllw metaballo {met-ab-al'-lo} from 3326 and 906; to throw over, i.e. (middle voice figuratively) to turn about in opinion:--change mind. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 906

G3329.text: μετάγω metavgw metago {met-ag'-o} from 3326 and 718; to lead over, i.e. transfer (direct):--turn about. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 718

G3330.text: μεταδίδωμι metadivdwmi metadidomi {met-ad-id'-o-mee} from 3326 and 1325; to give over, i.e. share:--give, impart. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 1325

G3331.text: μετάθεσις metavqesis metathesis {met-ath'-es-is} from 3346; transposition, i.e. transferral (to heaven), disestablishment (of a law):--change, removing, translation. see GREEK for 3346

G3332.text: μεταίρω metaivrw metairo {met-ah'-ee-ro} from 3326 and 142; to betake oneself, i.e. remove (locally):--depart. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 142

G3333.text: μετακαλέω metakalevw metakaleo {met-ak-al-eh'-o} from 3326 and 2564; to call elsewhere, i.e. summon:--call (for, hither). see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 2564

G3334.text: μετακινέω metakinevw metakineo {met-ak-ee-neh'-o} from 3326 and 2795; to stir to a place elsewhere, i.e. remove (figuratively):--move away. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 2795

G3335.text: μεταλαμβάνω metalambavnw metalambano {met-al-am-ban'-o} from 3326 and 2983; to participate; genitive case, to accept (and use):--eat, have, be partaker, receive, take. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 2983

G3336.text: μετάλημψις metavlhmyis metalepsis {met-al'-ape-sis} from 3335; participation:--taking. see GREEK for 3335

G3337.text: μεταλλάσσω metallavssw metallasso {met-al-las'-so} from 3326 and 236; to exchange:--change. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 236

G3338.text: μεταμέλομαι metamevlomai metamellomai {met-am-el'-lom-ahee} from 3326 and the middle voice of 3199; to care afterwards, i.e. regret:--repent (self). see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 3199

G3339.text: μεταμορφόω metamorfovw metamorphoo {met-am-or-fo'-o} from 3326 and 3445; to transform (literally or figuratively, "metamorphose"):--change, transfigure, transform. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 3445

G3340.text: μετανοέω metanoevw metanoeo {met-an-o-eh'-o} from 3326 and 3539; to think differently or afterwards, i.e. reconsider (morally, feel compunction):--repent. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 3539

G3341.text: μετάνοια metavnoia metanoia {met-an'-oy-ah} from 3340; (subjectively) compunction (for guilt, including reformation); by implication, reversal (of (another's) decision):--repentance. see GREEK for 3340

G3342.text: μεταξύ metaxuv metaxu {met-ax-oo'} from 3326 and a form of 4862; betwixt (of place or person); (of time) as adjective, intervening, or (by implication) adjoining:--between, mean while, next. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 4862

G3343.text: μεταπέμπω metapevmpw metapempo {met-ap-emp'-o} from 3326 and 3992; to send from elsewhere, i.e. (middle voice) to summon or invite:--call (send) foreign see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 3992

G3344.text: μεταστρέφω μετατρέπω metastrevfw metatrevpw metastrepho {met-as-tref'-o} from 3326 and 4762; to turn across, i.e. transmute or (figuratively) corrupt:--pervert, turn. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 4762

G3345.text: μετασχηματίζω metaschmativzw metaschematizo {met-askh-ay-mat-id'-zo} from 3326 and a derivative of 4976; to transfigure or disguise; figuratively, to apply (by accommodation):--transfer, transform (self). see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 4976

G3346.text: μετατίθημι metativqhmi metatithemi {met-at-ith'-ay-mee} from 3326 and 5087; to transfer, i.e. (literally) transport, (by implication) exchange, (reflexively) change sides, or (figuratively) pervert:--carry over, change, remove, translate, turn. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 5087

G3347.text: μετέπειτα metevpeita metepeita {met-ep'-i-tah} from 3326 and 1899; thereafter:--afterward. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 1899

G3348.text: μετέχω metevcw metecho {met-ekh'-o} from 3326 and 2192; to share or participate; by implication, belong to, eat (or drink):--be partaker, pertain, take part, use. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 2192

G3349.text: μετεωρίζομαι metewrivzomai meteorizo {met-eh-o-rid'-zo} from a compound of 3326 and a collateral form of 142 or perhaps rather 109 (compare "meteor"); to raise in mid-air, i.e. (figuratively) suspend (passively, fluctuate or be anxious):--be of doubtful mind. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 142 see GREEK for 109

G3350.text: μετοικεσία metoikesiva metoikesia {met-oy-kes-ee'-ah} from a derivative of a compound of 3326 and 3624; a change of abode, i.e. (specially), expatriation:--X brought, carried(-ying) away (in-)to. see GREEK for 3326 see GREEK for 3624

G3351.text: μετοικίζω metoikivzw metoikizo {met-oy-kid'-zo} from the same as 3350; to transfer as a settler or captive, i.e colonize or exile:--carry away, remove into. see GREEK for 3350

G3352.text: μετοχή metochv metoche {met-okh-ay'} from 3348; participation, i.e. intercourse:--fellowship. see GREEK for 3348

G3353.text: μέτοχος mevtocos metochos {met'-okh-os} from 3348; participant, i.e. (as noun) a sharer; by implication, an associate:--fellow, partaker, partner. see GREEK for 3348

G3354.text: μετρέω metrevw metreo {met-reh'-o} from 3358; to measure (i.e. ascertain in size by a fixed standard); by implication, to admeasure (i.e. allot by rule):--figuratively, to estimate:--measure, mete. see GREEK for 3358

G3355.text: μετρητής metrhthvs metretes {met-ray-tace'} from 3354; a measurer, i.e. (specially), a certain standard measure of capacity for liquids:--firkin. see GREEK for 3354

G3356.text: μετριοπαθέω metriopaqevw metriopatheo {met-ree-op-ath-eh'-o} from a compound of the base of 3357 and 3806; to be moderate in passion, i.e. gentle (to treat indulgently):--have compassion. see GREEK for 3357 see GREEK for 3806

G3357.text: μετρίως metrivws metrios {met-ree'-oce} adverb from a derivative of 3358; moderately, i.e. slightly:--a little. see GREEK for 3358

G3358.text: μέτρον mevtron metron {met'-ron} an apparently primary word; a measure ("metre"), literally or figuratively; by implication, a limited portion (degree):-- measure.

G3359.text: μέτωπον mevtwpon metopon {met'-o-pon } from 3326 and ops (the face); the forehead (as opposite the countenance):--forehead. see GREEK for 3326

G3360.text: μέχρι μεχρίς μέχρι μεχρίς mevcri mecrivs mevcri mecrivs mechri {mekh'-ree} 或 mechris {mekh-ris'} or mechris mekh-ris' from 3372; as far as, i.e. up to a certain point (as a preposition, of extent (denoting the terminus, whereas 891 refers especially to the space of time or place intervening) or conjunction):--till, (un-)to, until. see GREEK for 3372 see GREEK for 891

G3361.text: μή mhv me {may} a primary particle of qualified negation (whereas 3756 expresses an absolute denial); (adverb) not, (conjunction) lest; also (as an interrogative implying a negative answer (whereas 3756 expects an affirmative one)) whether:--any but (that), X forbear, + God forbid, + lack, lest, neither, never, no (X wise in), none, nor, (can-)not, nothing, that not, un(-taken), without. Often used in compounds in substantially the same relations. See also 3362, 3363, 3364, 3372, 3373, 3375, 3378. see GREEK for 3756 see GREEK for 3362 see GREEK for 3363 see GREEK for 3364 see GREEK for 3372 see GREEK for 3373 see GREEK for 3375 see GREEK for 3378

G3362.text: ἐὰν ean me ean me {eh-an' may} i.e. 1437 and 3361; if not, i.e. unless:--X before, but, except, if, no, (if, + whosoever) not. see GREEK for 3361 see GREEK for 1437

G3363.text: μή mhv hina me {hin'-ah may} i.e. 2443 and 3361; in order (or so) that not:--albeit not, lest, that, no(-t, (-thing)). see GREEK for 3361 see GREEK for 2443

G3364.text: οὐ ou me ou me {oo may} i.e. 3756 and 3361; a double negative strengthening the denial; not at all:--any more, at all, by any (no) means, neither, never, no (at all), in no case (wise), nor ever, not (at all, in any wise). Compare 3378. see GREEK for 3361 see GREEK for 3378 see GREEK for 3756

G3365.text: μηδαμῶς mhdamw's medamos {may-dam-oce'} adverb from a compound of 3361 and amos (somebody); by no means:--not so. see GREEK for 3361

G3366.text: μηδέ mhdev mede {may-deh'} from 3361 and 1161; but not, not even; in a continued negation, nor:--neither, nor (yet), (no) not (once, so much as). see GREEK for 3361 see GREEK for 1161

G3368.text: μηδέποτε mhdevpote medepote {may-dep'-ot-eh} from 3366 and 4218; not even ever:--never. see GREEK for 3366 see GREEK for 4218

G3369.text: μηδέπω mhdevpw medepo {may-dep'-o} from 3366 and 4452; not even yet:--not yet. see GREEK for 3366 see GREEK for 4452

G3370.text: Μῆδος Mh'dos Medos {may'-dos} of foreign origin (compare 4074); a Median, or inhabitant of Media:--Mede. see HEBREW for 04074

G3371.text: μηκέτι mhkevti meketi {may-ket'-ee} from 3361 and 2089; no further:--any longer, (not) henceforth, hereafter, no henceforward (longer, more, soon), not any more. see GREEK for 3361 see GREEK for 2089

G3372.text: μῆκος mh'kos mekos {may'-kos} probably akin to 3173; length (literally or figuratively) length. see GREEK for 3173

G3373.text: μηκύνω mhkuvnw mekuno {may-koo'-no} from 3372; to lengthen, i.e. (middle voice) to enlarge:--grow up. see GREEK for 3372

G3374.text: μηλωτή mhlwthv melote {may-lo-tay'} from melon (a sheep); a sheep-skin:--sheepskin.

G3375.text: μήν mhvn men {mane} a stronger form of 3303; a particle of affirmation (only with 2229); assuredly:--+ surely. see GREEK for 3303 see GREEK for 2229

G3376.text: μήν mhvn men {mane} a primary word; a month:--month.

G3377.text: μηνύω mhnuvw menuo {may-noo'-o} probably from the same base as 3145 and 3415 (i.e. mao, to strive); to disclose (through the idea of mental effort and thus calling to mind), i.e. report, declare, intimate:--shew, tell. see GREEK for 3145 see GREEK for 3415

G3378.text: οὗτος ou|tos me ouk {may ook} i.e. 3361 and 3756; as interrogative and negative, is it not that?:--neither (followed by no), + never, not. Compare 3364. see GREEK for 3756 see GREEK for 3364 see GREEK for 3361

G3379.text: μήποτε mhvpote mepote {may'-pot-eh} 或 me pote {may pot'-eh} me pote may pot'-eh from 3361 and 4218; not ever; also if (or lest) ever (or perhaps):--if peradventure, lest (at any time, haply), not at all, whether or not. see GREEK for 3361 see GREEK for 4218

G3380.text: μήπω mhvpw mepo {may'-po} from 3361 and 4452; not yet:--not yet. see GREEK for 3361 see GREEK for 4452

G3381.text: μήπως mepos mepos {may'-pos} 或 me pos {may poce} me pos may poce from 3361 and 4458; lest somehow:--lest (by any means, by some means, haply, perhaps). see GREEK for 3361 see GREEK for 4458

G3382.text: μηρός mhrovs meros {may-ros'} perhaps a primary word; a thigh:--thigh.

G3383.text: μήτε mhvte mete {may'-teh} from 3361 and 5037; not too, i.e. (in continued negation) neither or nor; also, not even:--neither, (n-)or, so as much. see GREEK for 3361 see GREEK for 5037

G3384.text: μήτηρ mhvthr meter {may'-tare} apparently a primary word; a "mother" (literally or figuratively, immediate or remote):--mother.

G3385.text: μήτι mhvti meti {may'-tee} from 3361 and the neuter of 5100; whether at all:--not (the particle usually not expressed, except by the form of the question). see GREEK for 3361 see GREEK for 5100

G3386.text: μήτιγε mhvtige metige {may'-tig-eh} from 3385 and 1065; not at all then, i.e. not to say (the rather still):--how much more. see GREEK for 3385 see GREEK for 1065

G3387.text: μήτις metis metis {may'-tis} 或是 me tis {may tis} me tis may tis from 3361 and 5100; whether any:--any (sometimes unexpressed except by the simple interrogative form of the sentence). see GREEK for 3361 see GREEK for 5100

G3388.text: μήτρα mhvtra metra {may'-trah} from 3384; the matrix:--womb. see GREEK for 3384

G3389.text: μητρολῴας mhtrolwv/as metraloas {may-tral-o'-as} from 3384 and the base of 257; a mother-thresher, i.e. matricide:--murderer of mothers. see GREEK for 3384 see GREEK for 257

G3390.text: μητρόπολις metropolis metropolis {may-trop'-ol-is} from 3384 and 4172; a mother city, i.e. "metropolis":--chiefest city. see GREEK for 3384 see GREEK for 4172

G3391.text: εἷς ei|s mia {mee'-ah} irregular feminine of 1520; one or first:--a (certain), + agree, first, one, X other. see GREEK for 1520

G3392.text: μιαίνω miaivnw miaino {me-ah'-ee-no} perhaps a primary verb; to sully or taint, i.e. contaminate (ceremonially or morally):--defile.

G3393.text: μίασμα mivasma miasma {mee'-as-mah} from 3392 ("miasma"); (morally) foulness (properly, the effect):--pollution. see GREEK for 3392

G3394.text: μιασμός miasmovs miasmos {mee-as-mos'} from 3392; (morally) contamination (properly, the act):--uncleanness. see GREEK for 3392

G3395.text: μίγμα mivgma migma {mig'-mah} from 3396; a compound:--mixture. see GREEK for 3396

G3396.text: μίγνυμι mivgnumi mignumi {mig'-noo-mee} a primary verb; to mix:--mingle.

G3397.text: μικρός mikrovs mikron {mik-ron'} masculine or neuter singular of 3398 (as noun); a small space of time or degree:--a (little) (while). see GREEK for 3398

G3398.text: μικρός mikrovs mikros {mik-ros'} 包括其比较级 mikroteros {mik-rot'-er-os} mikroteros mik-rot'-er-os apparently a primary word; small (in size, quantity, number or (figuratively) dignity):--least, less, little, small.

G3399.text: Μίλητος Mivlhtos Miletos {mil'-ay-tos} of uncertain origin; Miletus, a city of Asia Minor:--Miletus.

G3400.text: μίλιον mivlion milion {mil'-ee-on} of Latin origin; a thousand paces, i.e. a "mile":--mile.

G3401.text: μιμέομαι mimevomai mimeomai {mim-eh'-om-ahee} middle voice from mimos (a "mimic"); to imitate:--follow.

G3402.text: μιμητής mimhthvs mimetes {mim-ay-tace'} from 3401; an imitator:--follower. see GREEK for 3401

G3403.text: μιμνῄσκω mimnhv/skw mimnesko {mim-nace'-ko} a prolonged form of 3415 (from which some of the tenses are borrowed); to remind, i.e. (middle voice) to recall to mind:--be mindful, remember. see GREEK for 3415

G3404.text: μισέω misevw miseo {mis-eh'-o} from a primary misos (hatred); to detest (especially to persecute); by extension, to love less:--hate(-ful).

G3405.text: μισθαποδοσία misqapodosiva misthapodosia {mis-thap-od-os-ee'-ah} from 3406; requital (good or bad):--recompence of reward. see GREEK for 3406

G3406.text: μισθαποδότης misqapodovths misthapodotes {mis-thap-od-ot'-ace} from 3409 and 591; a renumerator:--rewarder. see GREEK for 3409 see GREEK for 591

G3407.text: μίσθιος mivsqios misthios {mis'-thee-os} from 3408; a wage-earner:--hired servant. see GREEK for 3408

G3408.text: μισθός misqovs misthos {mis-thos'} apparently a primary word; pay for service (literally or figuratively), good or bad:--hire, reward, wages.

G3409.text: μισθόω misqovw misthoo {mis-tho'-o} from 3408; to let out for wages, i.e. (middle voice) to hire:--hire. see GREEK for 3408

G3410.text: μίσθωμα mivsqwma misthoma {mis'-tho-mah} from 3409; a rented building:--hired house. see GREEK for 3409

G3411.text: μισθωτός misqwtovs misthotos {mis-tho-tos'} from 3409; a wage-worker (good or bad):--hired servant, hireling. see GREEK for 3409

G3412.text: Μιτυλήνη Mitulhvnh Mitulene {mit-oo-lay'-nay} for mutilene (abounding in shellfish); Mitylene (or Mytilene), a town on the island of Lesbos:--Mitylene.

G3413.text: Μιχαήλ Micahvl Michael {mikh-ah-ale'} of Hebrew origin (4317); Michael, an archangel:--Michael. see HEBREW for 04317

G3414.text: μνᾶ mna' mna {mnah} of Latin origin; a mna (i.e. mina), a certain weight:-- pound.

G3415.text: μιμνῄσκομαι μιμνῄσκω mimnhv/skomai mimnhv/skw mnaomai {mnah'-om-ahee} middle voice of a derivative of 3306 or perhaps of the base of 3145 (through the idea of fixture in the mind or of mental grasp); to bear in mind, i.e. recollect; by implication, to reward or punish:--be mindful, remember, come (have) in remembrance. Compare 3403. see GREEK for 3403 see GREEK for 3306 see GREEK for 3145

G3416.text: Μνάσων Mnavswn Mnason {mnah'-sohn} of uncertain origin; Mnason, a Christian:--Mnason.

G3417.text: μνεία mneiva mneia {mni'-ah} from 3415 or 3403; recollection; by implication, recital:--mention, remembrance. see GREEK for 3415 see GREEK for 3403

G3418.text: μνῆμα mnh'ma mnema {mnay'-mah} from 3415; a memorial, i.e. sepulchral monument (burial-place):--grave, sepulchre, tomb. see GREEK for 3415

G3419.text: μνημεῖον mnhmei'on mnemeion {mnay-mi'-on} from 3420; a remembrance, i.e. cenotaph (place of interment):--grave, sepulchre, tomb. see GREEK for 3420

G3420.text: μνήμη mnhvmh mneme {mnay'-may} from 3403; memory:--remembrance. see GREEK for 3403

G3421.text: μνημονεύω mnhmoneuvw mnemoneuo {mnay-mon-yoo'-o} from a derivative of 3420; to exercise memory, i.e. recollect; by implication, to punish; also to rehearse:--make mention; be mindful, remember. see GREEK for 3420

G3422.text: μνημόσυνον mnhmovsunon mnemosunon {mnay-mos'-oo-non} from 3421; a reminder (memorandum), i.e. record:--memorial. see GREEK for 3421

G3423.text: μνηστεύω mnhsteuvw mnesteuo {mnace-tyoo'-o} from a derivative of 3415; to give a souvenir (engagement present), i.e. betroth:--espouse. see GREEK for 3415

G3424.text: μογιλάλος mogilavlos mogilalos {mog-il-al'-os} from 3425 and 2980; hardly talking, i.e. dumb (tongue-tied):--having an impediment in his speech. see GREEK for 3425 see GREEK for 2980

G3425.text: μόγις movgis mogis {mog'-is} adverb from a primary mogos (toil); with difficulty:--hardly.

G3426.text: μόδιος movdios modios {mod'-ee-os} of Latin origin; a modius, i.e. certain measure for things dry (the quantity or the utensil):--bushel.

G3427.text: ἐγώ ejgwv moi {moy} the simpler form of 1698; to me:--I, me, mine, my. see GREEK for 1698

G3428.text: μοιχαλίς moicalivs moichalis {moy-khal-is'} a prolonged form of the feminine of 3432; an adulteress (literally or figuratively):--adulteress(-ous, -y). see GREEK for 3432

G3429.text: μοιχάω moicavw moichao {moy-khah'-o} from 3432; (middle voice) to commit adultery:--commit adultery. see GREEK for 3432

G3430.text: μοιχεία moiceiva moicheia {moy-khi'-ah} from 3431; adultery:--adultery. see GREEK for 3431

G3431.text: μοιχεύω moiceuvw moicheuo {moy-khyoo'-o} from 3432; to commit adultery:--commit adultery. see GREEK for 3432

G3432.text: μοιχός moicovs moichos {moy-khos'} perhaps a primary word; a (male) paramour; figuratively, apostate:--adulterer.

G3433.text: μόλις movlis molis {mol'-is} probably by variation for 3425; with difficulty:--hardly, scarce(-ly), + with much work. see GREEK for 3425

G3434.text: Μολόχ Molovc Moloch {mol-okh'} of Hebrew origin (4432); Moloch (i.e. Molek), an idol:--Moloch. see HEBREW for 04432

G3435.text: μολύνω moluvnw moluno {mol-oo'-no} probably from 3189; to soil (figuratively):--defile. see GREEK for 3189

G3436.text: μολυσμός molusmovs molusmos {mol-oos-mos'} from 3435; a stain; i.e. (figuratively) immorality:--filthiness. see GREEK for 3435

G3437.text: μομφή momfhv momphe {mom-fay'} from 3201; blame, i.e. (by implication), a fault:--quarrel. see GREEK for 3201

G3438.text: μονή monhv mone {mon-ay'} from 3306; a staying, i.e. residence (the act or the place):--abode, mansion. see GREEK for 3306

G3439.text: μονογενής monogenhvs monogenes {mon-og-en-ace'} from 3441 and 1096; only-born, i.e. sole:--only (begotten, child). see GREEK for 3441 see GREEK for 1096

G3440.text: μόνοσι μόνος movnosi movnos monon {mon'-on} neuter of 3441 as adverb; merely:--alone, but, only. see GREEK for 3441

G3441.text: μόνος movnos monos {mon'-os} probably from 3306; remaining, i.e. sole or single; by implication, mere:--alone, only, by themselves. see GREEK for 3306

G3442.text: μονόφθαλμος monovfqalmos monophthalmos {mon-of'-thal-mos} from 3441 and 3788; one-eyed:--with one eye. see GREEK for 3441 see GREEK for 3788

G3443.text: μονόομαι monovomai monoo {mon-o'-o} from 3441; to isolate, i.e. bereave:--be desolate. see GREEK for 3441

G3444.text: μορφή morfhv morphe {mor-fay'} perhaps from the base of 3313 (through the idea of adjustment of parts); shape; figuratively, nature:--form. see GREEK for 3313

G3445.text: μορφόω morfovw morphoo {mor-fo'-o} from the same as 3444; to fashion (figuratively):--form. see GREEK for 3444

G3446.text: μόρφωσις movrfwsis morphosis {mor'-fo-sis} from 3445; formation, i.e. (by implication), appearance (semblance or (concretely) formula):--form. see GREEK for 3445

G3447.text: μοσχοποιέω moscopoievw moschopoieo {mos-khop-oy-eh'-o} from 3448 and 4160; to fabricate the image of a bullock:--make a calf. see GREEK for 3448 see GREEK for 4160

G3448.text: μόσχος movscos moschos {mos'-khos} probably strengthened for oschos (a shoot); a young bullock:--calf.

G3449.text: μόχθος movcqos mochthos {mokh'-thos} from the base of 3425; toil, i.e. (by implication) sadness:--painfulness, travail. see GREEK for 3425

G3450.text: ἐγώ ejgwv mou {moo} the simpler form of 1700; of me:--I, me, mine (own), my. see GREEK for 1700

G3451.text: μουσικός mousikovs mousikos {moo-sik-os'} from Mousa (a Muse); "musical", i.e. (as noun) a minstrel:--musician.

G3452.text: μυελός muelovs muelos {moo-el-os'} perhaps a primary word; the marrow:--marrow.

G3453.text: μυέω muevw mueo {moo-eh'-o} from the base of 3466; to initiate, i.e. (by implication) to teach:--instruct. see GREEK for 3466

G3454.text: μῦθος mu'qos muthos {moo'-thos} perhaps from the same as 3453 (through the idea of tuition); a tale, i.e. fiction ("myth"):--fable. see GREEK for 3453

G3455.text: μυκάομαι mukavomai mukaomai {moo-kah'-om-ahee} from a presumed derivative of muzo ( to "moo"); to bellow (roar):--roar.

G3456.text: μυκτηρίζω mukthrivzw mukterizo {mook-tay-rid'-zo} from a derivative of the base of 3455 (meaning snout, as that whence lowing proceeds); to make mouths at, i.e. ridicule:--mock. see GREEK for 3455

G3457.text: μυλικός mulikovs mulikos {moo-lee-kos'} from 3458; belonging to a mill:--mill(-stone). see GREEK for 3458

G3458.text: μύλος muvlos mulos {moo'-los} probably ultimately from the base of 3433 (through the idea of hardship); a "mill", i.e. (by implication), a grinder (millstone):--millstone. see GREEK for 3433

G3459.text: μυλών ῶνος ὁ mulon mulon {moo'-lone} from 3458; a mill-house:--mill. see GREEK for 3458

G3460.text: Μύρρα Μύρα Muvrra Muvra Mura {moo'-rah} of uncertain derivation; Myra, a place in Asia Minor:--Myra.

G3461.text: μυριάς muriavs murias {moo-ree'-as} from 3463; a ten-thousand; by extension, a "myriad" or indefinite number:--ten thousand. see GREEK for 3463

G3462.text: μυρίζω murivzw murizo {moo-rid'-zo} from 3464; to apply (perfumed) unguent to:--anoint. see GREEK for 3464

G3463.text: μύριοι muvrioi murioi {moo'-ree-oi} plural of an apparently primary word (properly, meaning very many); ten thousand; by extension, innumerably many:--ten thousand.

G3464.text: μύρον muvron muron {moo'-ron} probably of foreign origin (compare 4753, 4666); "myrrh", i.e. (by implication) perfumed oil:--ointment. see HEBREW for 04753 see GREEK for 04666

G3465.text: Μυσία Musiva Musia {moo-see'-ah} of uncertain origin; Mysia, a region of Asia Minor:--Mysia.

G3466.text: μυστήριον musthvrion musterion {moos-tay'-ree-on} from a derivative of muo (to shut the mouth); a secret or "mystery" (through the idea of silence imposed by initiation into religious rites):--mystery.

G3467.text: μυωπάζω muwpavzw muopazo {moo-ope-ad'-zo} from a compound of the base of 3466 and ops (the face; from 3700); to shut the eyes, i.e. blink (see indistinctly):-- cannot see far off. see GREEK for 3466 see GREEK for 3700

G3468.text: μώλωψ mwvlwy molops {mo'-lopes} from molos ("moil"; probably akin to the base of 3433) and probably ops (the face; from 3700); a mole ("black eye") or blow-mark:--stripe. see GREEK for 3433 see GREEK for 3700

G3469.text: μωμάομαι mwmavomai momaomai {mo-mah'-om-ahee} from 3470; to carp at, i.e. censure (discredit):--blame. see GREEK for 3470

G3470.text: μῶμος mw'mos momos {mo'-mos} perhaps from 3201; a flaw or blot, i.e. (figuratively) disgraceful person:--blemish. see GREEK for 3201

G3471.text: μωραίνω mwraivnw moraino {mo-rah'-ee-no} from 3474; to become insipid; figuratively, to make (passively, act) as a simpleton:--become fool, make foolish, lose savour. see GREEK for 3474

G3472.text: μωρία mwriva moria {mo-ree'-ah} from 3474; silliness, i.e. absurdity:--foolishness. see GREEK for 3474

G3473.text: μωρολογία mwrologiva morologia {mo-rol-og-ee'-ah} from a compound of 3474 and 3004; silly talk, i.e. buffoonery:--foolish talking. see GREEK for 3474 see GREEK for 3004

G3474.text: μωρός mwrovs moros {mo-ros'} probably from the base of 3466; dull or stupid (as if shut up), i.e. heedless, (morally) blockhead, (apparently) absurd:--fool(-ish, X -ishness). see GREEK for 3466

G3475.text: Μωϋσῆς Mwu>sh's Moseus {moce-yoos'} 或 Moses {mo-sace'} 或 Mouses {mo-oo-sace'} or Moses mo-sace', or Mouses mo-oo-sace' of Hebrew origin; (4872); Moseus, Moses, or Mouses (i.e. Mosheh), the Hebrew lawgiver:--Moses. see HEBREW for 04872

G3476.text: Ναασσών Naasswvn Naasson {nah-as-sone'} of Hebrew origin (5177); Naasson (i.e. Nachshon), an Israelite:--Naasson. see HEBREW for 05177

G3477.text: Ναγγαί Naggaiv Naggai {nang-gah'-ee} probably of Hebrew origin (compare 5052); Nangae (i.e. perhaps Nogach), an Israelite:--Nagge. see HEBREW for 05052

G3478.text: Ναζαρά Ναζαρέτ Ναζαρέθ Nazarav Nazarevt Nazarevq Nazareth {nad-zar-eth'} 或 Nazaret {nad-zar-et'} or Nazaret nad-zar-et'; of uncertain derivation; Nazareth or Nazaret, a place in Palestine:--Nazareth.

G3479.text: Ναζαρηνός Nazarhnovs Nazarenos {nad-zar-ay-nos'} from 3478; a Nazarene, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth:--of Nazareth. see GREEK for 3478

G3480.text: Ναζωραῖος Nazwrai'os Nazoraios {nad-zo-rah'-yos} from 3478; a Nazoraean, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth; by extension, a Christian:--Nazarene, of Nazareth. see GREEK for 3478

G3481.text: Ναθάμ Naqavm Nathan {nath-an'} of Hebrew origin (5416); Nathan, an Israelite:--Nathan. see HEBREW for 05416

G3482.text: Ναθαναήλ Naqanahvl Nathanael {nath-an-ah-ale'} of Hebrew origin (5417); Nathanael (i.e. Nathanel), an Israelite and Christian:--Nathanael. see HEBREW for 05417

G3483.text: ναί naiv nai {nahee} a primary particle of strong affirmation; yes:--even so, surely, truth, verily, yea, yes.

G3484.text: Ναΐν Nai?n Nain {nah-in'} probably of Hebrew origin (compare 4999); Nain, a place in Palestine:--Nain. see HEBREW for 04999

G3485.text: ναός naovs naos {nah-os'} from a primary naio (to dwell); a fane, shrine, temple :--shrine, temple. Compare 2411. see GREEK for 2411

G3486.text: Ναούμ Naouvm Naoum {nah-oom'} of Hebrew origin (5151); Naum (i.e. Nachum), an Israelite:--Naum. see HEBREW for 05151

G3487.text: νάρδος navrdos nardos {nar'dos} of foreign origin (compare 5373); "nard":--(spike-)nard. see HEBREW for 05373

G3488.text: Νάρκισσος Navrkissos Narkissos {nar'-kis-sos} a flower of the same name, from narke (stupefaction, as a "narcotic"); Narcissus, a Roman:--Narcissus.

G3489.text: ναυαγέω nauagevw nauageo {now-ag-eh'-o} from a compound of 3491 and 71; to be shipwrecked (stranded, "navigate"), literally or figuratively:--make (suffer) shipwreck. see GREEK for 3491 see GREEK for 71

G3490.text: ναύκληρος nauvklhros naukleros {now'-klay-ros} from 3491 and 2819 ("clerk"); a captain:--owner of a ship. see GREEK for 3491 see GREEK for 2819

G3491.text: ναῦς nau's naus {nowce} from nao or neo (to float); a boat (of any size):--ship.

G3492.text: ναύτης nauvths nautes {now'-tace} from 3491; a boatman, i.e. seaman:--sailor, shipman. see GREEK for 3491

G3493.text: Ναχώρ Nacwvr Nachor {nakh-ore'} of Hebrew origin (5152); Nachor, the grandfather of Abraham:--Nachor. see HEBREW for 05152

G3494.text: νεανίας neanivas neanias {neh-an-ee'-as} from a derivative of 3501; a youth (up to about forty years):--young man. see GREEK for 3501

G3495.text: νεανίσκος neanivskos neaniskos {neh-an-is'-kos} from the same as 3494; a youth (under forty):--young man. see GREEK for 3494

G3496.text: Νεάπολις εως ἡ Neapolis Neapolis {neh-ap'-ol-is} from 3501 and 4172; new town; Neapolis, a place in Macedonia:--Neapolis. see GREEK for 3501 see GREEK for 4172

G3497.text: Ναιμάν Naimavn Neeman {neh-eh-man'} of Hebrew origin (5283); Neeman (i.e. Naaman), a Syrian:--Naaman. see HEBREW for 05283

G3498.text: νεκρός nekrovs nekros {nek-ros'} from an apparently primary nekus (a corpse); dead (literally or figuratively; also as noun):--dead.

G3499.text: νεκρόω nekrovw nekroo {nek-ro'-o} from 3498; to deaden, i.e. (figuratively) to subdue:--be dead, mortify. see GREEK for 3498

G3500.text: νέκρωσις nevkrwsis nekrosis {nek'-ro-sis} from 3499; decease; figuratively, impotency:--deadness, dying. see GREEK for 3499

G3501.text: νέος nevos neos {neh'-os} 和其比较级 neoteros {neh-o'-ter-os} including the comparative neoteros neh-o'-ter-os; a primary word; "new", i.e. (of persons) youthful, or (of things) fresh; figuratively, regenerate:--new, young.

G3502.text: νοσσός nossovs neossos {neh-os-sos'} from 3501; a youngling (nestling):--young. see GREEK for 3501

G3503.text: νεότης neovths neotes {neh-ot'-ace} from 3501; newness, i.e. youthfulness:--youth. see GREEK for 3501

G3504.text: νεόφυτος neovfutos neophutos {neh-of'-oo-tos} from 3501 and a derivative of 5453; newly planted, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert ("neophyte"):--novice. see GREEK for 3501 see GREEK for 5453

G3505.text: Νέρων Neron Neron {ner'-ohn} of Latin origin; Neron (i.e. Nero), a Roman emperor:--Nero.

G3506.text: νεύω neuvw neuo {nyoo'-o} apparently a primary verb; to "nod", i.e. (by analogy), signal:--beckon.

G3507.text: νεφέλη nefevlh nephele {nef-el'-ay} from 3509; properly, cloudiness, i.e. (concretely) a cloud:--cloud. see GREEK for 3509

G3508.text: Νεφθαλίμ Nefqalivm Nephthaleim {nef-thal-ime'} of Hebrew origin (5321); Nephthaleim (i.e. Naphthali), a tribe in Palestine:--Nephthalim. see HEBREW for 05321

G3509.text: νέφος nevfos nephos {nef'-os} apparently a primary word; a cloud:--cloud.

G3510.text: νεφρός nefrovs nephros {nef-ros'} of uncertain affinity; a kidney (plural), i.e. (figuratively) the inmost mind:--reins.

G3511.text: νεωκόρος newkovros neokoros {neh-o-kor'-os} from a form of 3485 and koreo (to sweep); a temple-servant, i.e. (by implication) a votary:--worshipper. see GREEK for 3485

G3512.text: νεωτερικός newterikovs neoterikos {neh-o-ter'-ik-os} from the comparative of 3501; appertaining to younger persons, i.e. juvenile:--youthful. see GREEK for 3501

G3513.text: νή nhv ne {nay} probably an intensive form of 3483; a particle of attestation (accompanied by the object invoked or appealed to in confirmation); as sure as:--I protest by. see GREEK for 3483

G3514.text: νήθω nhvqw netho {nay'-tho} from neo (of like meaning); to spin:--spin.

G3515.text: νηπιάζω nhpiavzw nepiazo {nay-pee-ad'-zo} from 3516; to act as a babe, i.e. (figuratively) innocently:--be a child. see GREEK for 3516

G3516.text: νήπιος nhvpios nepios {nay'-pee-os} from an obsolete particle ne- (implying negation) and 2031; not speaking, i.e. an infant (minor); figuratively, a simple-minded person, an immature Christian:--babe, child (+ -ish). see GREEK for 2031

G3517.text: Νηρεύς Nhreuvs Nereus {nare-yoos'} apparently from a derivative of the base of 3491 (meaning wet); Nereus, a Christian:--Nereus. see GREEK for 3491

G3518.text: Νηρί Nhriv Neri {nay-ree'} of Hebrew origin (5374); Neri (i.e. Nerijah), an Israelite:--Neri. see HEBREW for 05374

G3519.text: νησίον nhsivon nesion {nay-see'-on} diminutive of 3520; an islet:--island. see GREEK for 3520

G3520.text: νῆσος nh'sos nesos {nay'-sos} probably from the base of 3491; an island:--island, isle. see GREEK for 3491

G3521.text: νηστεία nhsteiva nesteia {nace-ti'-ah} from 3522; abstinence (from lack of food, or voluntary and religious); specially, the fast of the Day of Atonement:-- fast(-ing). see GREEK for 3522

G3522.text: νηστεύω nhsteuvw nesteuo {nace-tyoo'-o} from 3523; to abstain from food (religiously):--fast. see GREEK for 3523

G3523.text: νῆστις nh'stis nestis {nace'-tis} from the inseparable negative particle ne- (not) and 2068; not eating, i.e. abstinent from food (religiously):--fasting. see GREEK for 2068

G3524.text: νηφάλιος nhfavlios nephaleos {nay-fal'-eh-os} or nephalios {nay-fal'-ee-os} nephalios nay-fal'-ee-os from 3525; sober, i.e. (figuratively) circumspect:--sober. see GREEK for 3525

G3525.text: νήφω nhvfw nepho {nay'-fo} of uncertain affinity: to abstain from wine (keep sober), i.e. (figuratively) be discreet:--be sober, watch.

G3526.text: Νίγερ Nivger Niger {neeg'-er} of Latin origin; black; Niger, a Christian:--Niger.

G3527.text: Νικάνωρ Nikavnwr Nikanor {nik-an'-ore} probably from 3528; victorious; Nicanor, a Christian:--Nicanor. see GREEK for 3528

G3528.text: νικάω nikavw nikao {nik-ah'-o} from 3529; to subdue (literally or figuratively):--conquer, overcome, prevail, get the victory. see GREEK for 3529

G3529.text: νίκη nivkh nike {nee'-kay} apparently a primary word; conquest (abstractly), i.e. (figuratively) the means of success:--victory.

G3530.text: Νικόδημος Nikovdhmos Nikodemos {nik-od'-ay-mos} from 3534 and 1218; victorious among his people; Nicodemus, an Israelite:--Nicodemus. see GREEK for 3534 see GREEK for 1218

G3531.text: Νικολαΐτης Nikolai?ths Nikolaites {nik-ol-ah-ee'-tace} from 3532; a Nicolaite, i.e. adherent of Nicolaus:--Nicolaitane. see GREEK for 3532

G3532.text: Νικόλαος Nikovlaos Nikolaos {nik-ol'-ah-os} from 3534 and 2994; victorious over the people; Nicolaus, a heretic:--Nicolaus. see GREEK for 3534 see GREEK for 2994

G3533.text: Νικόπολις Nikovpolis Nikopolis {nik-op'-ol-is} from 3534 and 4172; victorious city; Nicopolis, a place in Macedonia:--Nicopolis. see GREEK for 3534 see GREEK for 4172

G3534.text: νῖκος ni'kos nikos {nee'-kos} from 3529; a conquest (concretely), i.e. (by implication) triumph:--victory. see GREEK for 3529

G3535.text: Νινευΐ ἡ Nineui Nineui {nin-yoo-ee'} of Hebrew origin (5210); Ninevi (i.e. Nineveh), the capital of Assyria:--Nineve. see HEBREW for 05210

G3536.text: Νινευίτης Nineuivths Nineuites {nin-yoo-ee'-tace} from 3535; a Ninevite, i.e. inhabitant of Nineveh:--of Nineve, Ninevite. see GREEK for 3535

G3537.text: νιπτήρ nipthvr nipter {nip-tare'} from 3538; a ewer:--bason. see GREEK for 3538

G3538.text: νίπτω nivptw nipto {nip'-to} to cleanse (especially the hands or the feet or the face); ceremonially, to perform ablution:--wash. Compare 3068. see GREEK for 3068

G3539.text: νοέω noevw noeo {no-eh'-o} from 3563; to exercise the mind (observe), i.e. (figuratively) to comprehend, heed:--consider, perceive, think, understand. see GREEK for 3563

G3540.text: νόημα novhma noema {no'-ay-mah} from 3539; a perception, i.e. purpose, or (by implication) the intellect, disposition, itself:--device, mind, thought. see GREEK for 3539

G3541.text: νόθος novqos nothos {noth'-os} of uncertain affinity; a spurious or illegitimate son:--bastard.

G3542.text: νομή nomhv nome {nom-ay'} feminine from the same as 3551; pasture, i.e. (the act) feeding (figuratively, spreading of a gangrene), or (the food) pasturage:--X eat, pasture. see GREEK for 3551

G3543.text: νομίζω nomivzw nomizo {nom-id'-zo} from 3551; properly, to do by law (usage), i.e. to accustom (passively, be usual); by extension, to deem or regard:-- suppose, thing, be wont. see GREEK for 3551

G3544.text: νομικός nomikovs nomikos {nom-ik-os'} from 3551; according (or pertaining) to law, i.e. legal (ceremonially); as noun, an expert in the (Mosaic) law:--about the law, lawyer. see GREEK for 3551

G3545.text: νομίμως nomivmws nomimos {nom-im'-oce} adverb from a derivative of 3551; legitimately (specially, agreeably to the rules of the lists):--lawfully. see GREEK for 3551

G3546.text: νόμισμα novmisma nomisma {nom'-is-mah} from 3543; what is reckoned as of value (after the Latin numisma), i.e. current coin:--money. see GREEK for 3543

G3547.text: νομοδιδάσκαλος nomodidavskalos nomodidaskalos {nom-od-id-as'-kal-os} from 3551 and 1320; an expounder of the (Jewish) law, i.e. a Rabbi:--doctor (teacher) of the law. see GREEK for 3551 see GREEK for 1320

G3548.text: νομοθεσία nomoqesiva nomothesia {nom-oth-es-ee'-ah} from 3550; legislation (specially, the institution of the Mosaic code):--giving of the law. see GREEK for 3550

G3549.text: νομοθετέομαι nomoqetevomai nomotheteo {nom-oth-et-eh'-o} from 3550; to legislate, i.e. (passively) to have (the Mosaic) enactments injoined, be sanctioned (by them):--establish, receive the law. see GREEK for 3550

G3550.text: νομοθέτης nomoqevths nomothetes {nom-oth-et'-ace} from 3551 and a derivative of 5087; a legislator:--lawgiver. see GREEK for 3551 see GREEK for 5087

G3551.text: νόμος novmos nomos {nom'-os} from a primary nemo (to parcel out, especially food or grazing to animals); law (through the idea of prescriptive usage), genitive case (regulation), specially, (of Moses (including the volume); also of the Gospel), or figuratively (a principle):--law.

G3552.text: νόσεω novsew noseo {nos-eh'-o} from 3554; to be sick, i.e. (by implication, of a diseased appetite) to hanker after (figuratively, to harp upon):--dote. see GREEK for 3554

G3553.text: νόσημα ατος τό nosema nosema {nos'-ay-ma} from 3552; an ailment:--disease. see GREEK for 3552

G3554.text: νόσος novsos nosos {nos'-os} of uncertain affinity; a malady (rarely figuratively, of moral disability):--disease, infirmity, sickness.

G3555.text: νοσσιά nossiav nossia {nos-see-ah'} from 3502; a brood (of chickens):--brood. see GREEK for 3502

G3556.text: νοσσίον nossivon nossion {nos-see'-on} diminutive of 3502; a birdling:--chicken. see GREEK for 3502

G3557.text: νοσφίζω nosfivzw nosphizomai {nos-fid'-zom-ahee} middle voice from nosphi (apart or clandestinely); to sequestrate for oneself, i.e. embezzle:--keep back, purloin.

G3558.text: νότος novtos notos {not'-os} of uncertain affinity; the south(-west) wind; by extension, the southern quarter itself:--south (wind).

G3559.text: νουθεσία nouqesiva nouthesia {noo-thes-ee'-ah} from 3563 and a derivative of 5087; calling attention to, i.e. (by implication) mild rebuke or warning:--admonition. see GREEK for 3563 see GREEK for 5087

G3560.text: νουθετέω nouqetevw noutheteo {noo-thet-eh'-o} from the same as 3559; to put in mind, i.e. (by implication) to caution or reprove gently:--admonish, warn. see GREEK for 3559

G3561.text: νεομηνία neomhniva noumenia {noo-may-nee'-ah} or neomenia {ne-o-may-nee'-a} feminine of a compound of 3501 and 3376 (as noun by implication, of 2250); the festival of new moon:--new moon. see GREEK for 3501 see GREEK for 3376 see GREEK for 2250

G3562.text: νουνεχῶς nounecw's nounechos {noon-ekh-oce'} adverb from a comparative of the accusative case of 3563 and 2192; in a mind-having way, i.e. prudently:--discreetly. see GREEK for 3563 see GREEK for 2192

G3563.text: νοῦς nou's nous {nooce} probably from the base of 1097; the intellect, i.e. mind (divine or human; in thought, feeling, or will); by implication, meaning:--mind, understanding. Compare 5590. see GREEK for 1097 see GREEK for 5590

G3564.text: Νύμφα Nuvmfa Numphas {noom-fas'} probably contracted for a compound of 3565 and 1435; nymph-given (i.e. -born); Nymphas, a Christian:--Nymphas. see GREEK for 3565 see GREEK for 1435

G3565.text: νύμφη nuvmfh numphe {noom-fay'} from a primary but obsolete verb nupto (to veil as a bride; compare Latin "nupto," to marry); a young married woman (as veiled), including a betrothed girl; by implication, a son's wife:--bride, daughter in law.

G3566.text: νυμφίος numfivos numphios {noom-fee'-os} from 3565; a bride-groom (literally or figuratively):--bridegroom. see GREEK for 3565

G3567.text: νυμφών numfwvn numphon {noom-fohn'} from 3565; the bridal room:--bridechamber. see GREEK for 3565

G3568.text: νῦν nu'n nun {noon} a primary particle of present time; "now" (as adverb of date, a transition or emphasis); also as noun or adjective present or immediate:--henceforth, + hereafter, of late, soon, present, this (time). See also 3569, 3570. see GREEK for 3569 see GREEK for 3570

G3569.text: τανῦν tanun tanun {tan-oon'} 或是 ta nun {tah noon} ta nun tah noon from neuter plural of 3588 and 3568; the things now, i.e. (adverbially) at present:--(but) now. see GREEK for 3588 see GREEK for 3568

G3570.text: νυνί nuniv nuni {noo-nee'} a prolonged form of 3568 for emphasis; just now:--now. see GREEK for 3568

G3571.text: νύξ nuvx nux {noox} a primary word; "night" (literally or figuratively):-- (mid-)night.

G3572.text: νύσσω nuvssw nusso {noos'-so} apparently a primary word; to prick ("nudge"):--pierce.

G3573.text: νυστάζω nustavzw nustazo {noos-tad'-zo} from a presumed derivative of 3506; to nod, i.e. (by implication) to fall asleep; figuratively, to delay:--slumber. see GREEK for 3506

G3574.text: νυχθήμερον nucqhvmeron nuchthemeron {nookh-thay'-mer-on} from 3571 and 2250; a day-and-night, i.e. full day of twenty-four hours:--night and day. see GREEK for 3571 see GREEK for 2250

G3575.text: Νῶε Nw'e Noe {no'-eh} of Hebrew origin (5146); Noe, (i.e. Noach), a patriarch:--Noe. see HEBREW for 05146

G3576.text: νωθρός nwqrovs nothros {no-thros'} from a derivative of 3541; sluggish, i.e. (literally) lazy, or (figuratively) stupid:--dull, slothful. see GREEK for 3541

G3577.text: νῶτος nw'tos notos {no'-tos} of uncertain affinity; the back:--back.

G3578.text: ξενία xeniva xenia {xen-ee'-ah} from 3581; hospitality, i.e. (by implication) a place of entertainment:--lodging. see GREEK for 3581

G3579.text: ξενίζω xenivzw xenizo {xen-id'-zo} from 3581; to be a host (passively, a guest); by implication, be (make, appear) strange:--entertain, lodge, (think it) strange. see GREEK for 3581

G3580.text: ξενοδοχέω xenodocevw xenodocheo {xen-od-okh-eh'-o} from a compound of 3581 and 1209; to be hospitable:--lodge strangers. see GREEK for 3581 see GREEK for 1209

G3581.text: ξένος xevnos xenos {xen'-os} apparently a primary word; foreign (literally, alien, or figuratively, novel); by implication, a guest or (vice-versa) entertainer:--host, strange(-r).

G3582.text: ξέστης xevsths xestes {xes'-tace} as if from xeo (properly, to smooth; by implication, (of friction) to boil or heat); a vessel (as fashioned or for cooking) (or perhaps by corruption from the Latin sextarius, the sixth of a modius, i.e. about a pint), i.e. (specially), a measure for liquids or solids, (by analogy, a pitcher):--pot.

G3583.text: ξηραίνω xhraivnw xeraino {xay-rah'-ee-no} from 3584; to desiccate; by implication, to shrivel, to mature:--dry up, pine away, be ripe, wither (away). see GREEK for 3584

G3584.text: ξηρός xhrovs xeros {xay-ros'} from the base of 3582 (through the idea of scorching); arid; by implication, shrunken, earth (as opposed to water):--dry land, withered. see GREEK for 3582

G3585.text: ξύλινος xuvlinos xulinos {xoo'-lin-os} from 3586; wooden:--of wood. see GREEK for 3586

G3586.text: ξύλον xuvlon xulon {xoo'-lon} from another form of the base of 3582; timber (as fuel or material); by implication, a stick, club or tree or other wooden article or substance:--staff, stocks, tree, wood. see GREEK for 3582

G3587.text: ξυράω xuravw xurao {xoo-rah'-o} from a derivative of the same as 3586 (meaning a razor); to shave or "shear" the hair:--shave. see GREEK for 3586

G3588.text: ὁ ἡ τό oJ hJ tov ho {ho} 包括阴性的 he {hay}, 和中性的 to {to} he hay, and the neuter to to in all their inflections; the definite article; the (sometimes to be supplied, at others omitted, in English idiom):--the, this, that, one, he, she, it, etc.

G3589.text: ὀγδοήκοντα ojgdohvkonta ogdoekonta {og-do-ay'-kon-tah} from 3590; ten times eight:--fourscore. see GREEK for 3590

G3590.text: ὄγδοος o[gdoos ogdoos {og'-do-os} from 3638; the eighth:--eighth. see GREEK for 3638

G3591.text: ὄγκος o[gkos ogkos {ong'-kos} probably from the same as 43; a mass (as bending or bulging by its load), i.e. burden (hindrance):--weight. see GREEK for 43

G3592.text: ὅδε o&de hode {hod'-eh} 包括阴性 hede {hay'-deh} hede hay'-deh, and the neuter tode tod'-e from 3588 and 1161; the same, i.e. this or that one (plural these or those); often used as a personal pronoun:--he, she, such, these, thus. see GREEK for 3588 see GREEK for 1161

G3593.text: ὁδεύω oJdeuvw hodeuo {hod-yoo'-o} from 3598; to travel:--journey. see GREEK for 3598

G3594.text: ὁδηγέω oJdhgevw hodegeo {hod-ayg-eh'-o} from 3595; to show the way (literally or figuratively (teach)):--guide, lead. see GREEK for 3595

G3595.text: ὁδηγός oJdhgovs hodegos {hod-ayg-os'} from 3598 and 2233; a conductor (literally or figuratively (teacher)):--guide, leader. see GREEK for 3598 see GREEK for 2233

G3596.text: ὁδοιπορέω oJdoiporevw hodoiporeo {hod-oy-por-eh'-o} from a compound of 3598 and 4198; to be a wayfarer, i.e. travel:--go on a journey. see GREEK for 3598 see GREEK for 4198

G3597.text: ὁδοιπορία oJdoiporiva hodoiporia {hod-oy-por-ee'-ah} from the same as 3596; travel:--journey(-ing). see GREEK for 3596

G3598.text: ὁδός oJdovs hodos {hod-os'} apparently a primary word; a road; by implication, a progress (the route, act or distance); figuratively, a mode or means:--journey, (high-)way.

G3599.text: ὀδούς ojdouvs odous {od-ooce} perhaps from the base of 2068; a "tooth":--tooth. see GREEK for 2068

G3600.text: ὀδυνάω ojdunavw odunao {od-oo-nah'-o} from 3601; to grieve:--sorrow, torment. see GREEK for 3601

G3601.text: ὀδύνη ojduvnh odune {od-oo'-nay} from 1416; grief (as dejecting):--sorrow. see GREEK for 1416

G3602.text: ὀδυρμός ojdurmovs odurmos {od-oor-mos'} from a derivative of the base of 1416; moaning, i.e. lamentation:--mourning. see GREEK for 1416

G3603.text: ὅ ho esti ho esti {ho es-tee'} from the neuter of 3739 and the third person singular present indicative of 1510; which is:--called, which is (make), that is (to say). see GREEK for 3739 see GREEK for 1510

G3604.text: Ὀζίας Ojzivas Ozias {od-zee'-as} of Hebrew origin (5818); Ozias (i.e. Uzzijah), an Israelite:--Ozias. see HEBREW for 05818

G3605.text: ὄζω o[zw ozo {od'-zo} a primary verb (in a strengthened form); to scent (usually an ill "odor"): stink.

G3606.text: ὅθεν o&qen hothen {hoth'-en} from 3739 with the directive enclitic of source; from which place or source or cause (adverb or conjunction):--from thence, (from) whence, where(-by, -fore, -upon). see GREEK for 3739

G3607.text: ὀθόνη ojqovnh othone {oth-on'-ay} of uncertain affinity; a linen cloth, i.e. (especially) a sail:--sheet.

G3608.text: ὀθόνιον ojqovnion othonion {oth-on'-ee-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of 3607; a linen bandage:--linen clothes. see GREEK for 3607

G3609.text: οἰκεῖος oijkei'os oikeios {oy-ki'-os} from 3624; domestic, i.e. (as noun), a relative, adherent:--(those) of the (his own) house(-hold). see GREEK for 3624

G3610.text: οἰκέτης oijkevths oiketes {oy-ket'-ace} from 3611; a fellow resident, i.e. menial domestic:--(household) servant. see GREEK for 3611

G3611.text: οἰκέω oijkevw oikeo {oy-keh'-o} from 3624; to occupy a house, i.e. reside (figuratively, inhabit, remain, inhere); by implication, to cohabit:--dwell. See also 3625. see GREEK for 3624 see GREEK for 3625

G3612.text: οἴκημα oi[khma oikema {oy'-kay-mah} from 3611; a tenement, i.e. (specially), a jail:--prison. see GREEK for 3611

G3613.text: οἰκητήριον oijkhthvrion oiketerion {oy-kay-tay'-ree-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of 3611 (equivalent to 3612); a residence (literally or figuratively):--habitation, house. see GREEK for 3611 see GREEK for 3612

G3614.text: οἰκία oijkiva oikia {oy-kee'-ah} from 3624; properly, residence (abstractly), but usually (concretely) an abode (literally or figuratively); by implication, a family (especially domestics):--home, house(-hold). see GREEK for 3624

G3615.text: οἰκιακός oijkiakovs oikiakos {oy-kee-ak-os'} from 3614; familiar, i.e. (as noun) relatives:--they (them) of (his own) household. see GREEK for 3614

G3616.text: οἰκοδεσποτέω oijkodespotevw oikodespoteo {oy-kod-es-pot-eh'-o} from 3617; to be the head of (i.e. rule) a family:--guide the house. see GREEK for 3617

G3617.text: οἰκοδεσπότης oijkodespovths oikodespotes {oy-kod-es-pot'-ace} from 3624 and 1203; the head of a family:--goodman (of the house), householder, master of the house. see GREEK for 3624 see GREEK for 1203

G3619.text: οἰκοδομή oijkodomhv oikodome {oy-kod-om-ay'} feminine (abstract) of a compound of 3624 and the base of 1430; architecture, i.e. (concretely) a structure; figuratively, confirmation:--building, edify(-ication, -ing). see GREEK for 3624 see GREEK for 1430

G3620.text: οἰκοδομία oikodomia oikodomia {oy-kod-om-ee'-ah} from the same as 3619; confirmation:--edifying. see GREEK for 3619

G3621.text: οἰκονομέω oijkonomevw oikonomeo {oy-kon-om-eh'-o} from 3623; to manage (a house, i.e. an estate):--be steward. see GREEK for 3623

G3622.text: οἰκονομία oijkonomiva oikonomia {oy-kon-om-ee'-ah} from 3623; administration (of a household or estate); specially, a (religious) "economy":--dispensation, stewardship. see GREEK for 3623

G3623.text: οἰκονόμος oijkonovmos oikonomos {oy-kon-om'-os} from 3624 and the base of 3551; a house-distributor (i.e. manager), or overseer, i.e. an employee in that capacity; by extension, a fiscal agent (treasurer); figuratively, a preacher (of the Gospel):--chamberlain, governor, steward. see GREEK for 3624 see GREEK for 3551

G3624.text: οἶκος oi\\kos oikos {oy'-kos} of uncertain affinity; a dwelling (more or less extensive, literal or figurative); by implication, a family (more or less related, literally or figuratively):--home, house(-hold), temple.

G3625.text: οἰκουμένη oijkoumevnh oikoumene {oy-kou-men'-ay} feminine participle present passive of 3611 (as noun, by implication, of 1093); land, i.e. the (terrene part of the) globe; specially, the Roman empire:--earth, world. see GREEK for 3611 see GREEK for 1093

G3626.text: οἰκουργός oijkourgovs oikouros {oy-koo-ros'} from 3624 and ouros (a guard; be "ware"); a stayer at home, i.e. domestically inclined (a "good housekeeper"):--keeper at home. see GREEK for 3624

G3627.text: οἰκτίρω oijktivrw oikteiro {oyk-ti'-ro} 在某些时态亦作 oiktereo {oyk-ter-eh'-o} oiktereo oyk-ter-eh'-o from oiktos (pity); to exercise pity:--have compassion on.

G3628.text: οἰκτιρμός oijktirmovs oiktirmos {oyk-tir-mos'} from 3627; pity:--mercy. see GREEK for 3627

G3629.text: οἰκτίρμων oijktivrmwn oiktirmon {oyk-tir'-mone} from 3627; compassionate:--merciful, of tender mercy. see GREEK for 3627

G3630.text: οἰνοπότης oijnopovths oinopotes {oy-nop-ot'-ace} from 3631 and a derivative of the alternate of 4095; a tippler:--winebibber. see GREEK for 3631 see GREEK for 4095

G3631.text: οἶνος oi\\nos oinos {oy'-nos} a primary word (or perhaps of Hebrew origin (3196)); "wine" (literally or figuratively):--wine. see HEBREW for 03196

G3632.text: οἰνοφλυγία oijnoflugiva oinophlugia {oy-nof-loog-ee'-ah} from 3631 and a form of the base of 5397; an overflow (or surplus) of wine, i.e. vinolency (drunkenness):--excess of wine. see GREEK for 3631 see GREEK for 5397

G3633.text: οἴομαι οἶμαι oi[omai oi\\mai oiomai {oy'-om-ahee} 或 (缩简型) oimai {oy'-mahee} oimai oy'-mahee middle voice apparently from 3634; to make like (oneself), i.e. imagine (be of the opinion):--suppose, think. see GREEK for 3634

G3634.text: οἷος oi|os hoios {hoy'-os} probably akin to 3588, 3739, and 3745; such or what sort of (as a correlation or exclamation); especially the neuter (adverbially) with negative, not so:--so (as), such as, what (manner of), which. see GREEK for 3745 see GREEK for 3588 see GREEK for 3739

G3635.text: ὀκνέω ojknevw okneo {ok-neh'-o} from oknos (hesitation); to be slow (figuratively, loath):--delay.

G3636.text: ὀκνηρός ojknhrovs okneros {ok-nay-ros'} from 3635; tardy, i.e. indolent; (figuratively) irksome:--grievous, slothful. see GREEK for 3635

G3637.text: ὀκταήμερος ojktahvmeros oktaemeros {ok-tah-ay'-mer-os} from 3638 and 2250; an eight-day old person or act:--the eighth day. see GREEK for 3638 see GREEK for 2250

G3638.text: ὀκτώ ojktwv okto {ok-to'} a primary numeral; "eight":--eight.

G3639.text: ὄλεθρος o[leqros olethros {ol'-eth-ros} from a primary ollumi (to destroy; a prolonged form); ruin, i.e. death, punishment:--destruction.

G3640.text: ὀλιγόπιστος ojligovpistos oligopistos {ol-ig-op'-is-tos} from 3641 and 4102; incredulous, i.e. lacking confidence (in Christ):--of little faith. see GREEK for 3641 see GREEK for 4102

G3641.text: ὀλίγος ojlivgos oligos {ol-ee'-gos} of uncertain affinity; puny (in extent, degree, number, duration or value); especially neuter (adverbially) somewhat:--+ almost, brief(-ly), few, (a) little, + long, a season, short, small, a while.

G3642.text: ὀλιγόψυχος ojligovyucos oligopsuchos {ol-ig-op'-soo-khos} from 3641 and 6590; little-spirited, i.e. faint-hearted:--feebleminded. see GREEK for 6590 see GREEK for 3641

G3643.text: ὀλιγωρέω ojligwrevw oligoreo {ol-ig-o-reh'-o} from a compound of 3641 and ora ("care"); to have little regard for, i.e. to disesteem:--despise. see GREEK for 3641

G3644.text: ὀλοθρευτής ojloqreuthvs olothreutes {ol-oth-ryoo-tace'} from 3645; a ruiner, i.e. (specially), a venomous serpent:--destroyer. see GREEK for 3645

G3645.text: ὀλοθρεύω ojloqreuvw olothreuo {ol-oth-ryoo'-o} from 3639; to spoil, i.e. slay:--destroy. see GREEK for 3639

G3646.text: ὁλοκαύτωμα oJlokauvtwma holokautoma {hol-ok-ow'-to-mah} from a derivative of a compound of 3650 and a derivative of 2545; a wholly-consumed sacrifice ("holocaust"):--(whole) burnt offering. see GREEK for 3650 see GREEK for 2545

G3647.text: ὁλοκληρία oJloklhriva holokleria {hol-ok-lay-ree'-ah} from 3648; integrity, i.e. physical wholeness:--perfect soundness. see GREEK for 3648

G3648.text: ὁλόκληρος oJlovklhros holokleros {hol'-ok'-lay-ros} from 3650 and 2819; complete in every part, i.e. perfectly sound (in body):--entire, whole. see GREEK for 3650 see GREEK for 2819

G3649.text: ὀλολύζω ojloluvzw ololuzo {ol-ol-odd'-zo} a reduplicated primary verb; to "howl" or "halloo", i.e. shriek:--howl.

G3650.text: ὅλος o&los holos {hol'-os} a primary word; "whole" or "all", i.e. complete (in extent, amount, time or degree), especially (neuter) as noun or adverb:--all, altogether, every whit, + throughout, whole.

G3651.text: ὁλοτελής oJlotelhvs holoteles {hol-ot-el-ace'} from 3650 and 5056; complete to the end, i.e. absolutely perfect:--wholly. see GREEK for 3650 see GREEK for 5056

G3652.text: Ὀλυμπᾶς Ojlumpa's Olumpas {ol-oom-pas'} probably a contraction from Olumpiodoros (Olympian-bestowed, i.e. heaven-descended); Olympas, a Christian:--Olympas.

G3653.text: ὄλυνθος o[lunqos olunthos {ol'-oon-thos} of uncertain derivation; an unripe (because out of season) fig:--untimely fig.

G3654.text: ὅλως o&lws holos {hol'-oce} adverb from 3650; completely, i.e. altogether; (by analogy), everywhere; (negatively) not by any means:--at all, commonly, utterly. see GREEK for 3650

G3655.text: ὄμβρος o[mbros ombros {om'-bros} of uncertain affinity; a thunder storm:--shower.

G3656.text: ὁμιλέω oJmilevw homileo {hom-il-eh'-o} from 3658; to be in company with, i.e. (by implication) to converse:--commune, talk. see GREEK for 3658

G3657.text: ὁμιλία oJmiliva homilia {hom-il-ee'-ah} from 3658; companionship ("homily"), i.e. (by implication) intercourse:--communication. see GREEK for 3658

G3658.text: ὅμιλος homilos homilos {hom'-il-os} from the base of 3674 and a derivative of the alternate of 138 (meaning a crowd); association together, i.e. a multitude:--company. see GREEK for 3674 see GREEK for 138

G3659.text: ὄμμα o[mma omma {om'-mah} from 3700; a sight, i.e. (by implication) the eye:--eye. see GREEK for 3700

G3660.text: ὀμνύω ojmnuvw omnuo {om-noo'-o} but obsolete omo, for which another prolonged form omoo om-o'-o is used in certain tenses; to swear, i.e. take (or declare on) oath:--swear.

G3661.text: ὁμοθυμαδόν oJmoqumadovn homothumadon {hom-oth-oo-mad-on'} adverb from a compound of the base of 3674 and 2372; unanimously:--with one accord (mind). see GREEK for 3674 see GREEK for 2372

G3662.text: ὁμοιάζω homoiazo homoiazo {hom-oy-ad'-zo} from 3664; to resemble:--agree. see GREEK for 3664

G3663.text: ὁμοιοπαθής oJmoiopaqhvs homoiopathes {hom-oy-op-ath-ace'} from 3664 and the alternate of 3958; similarly affected:--of (subject to) like passions. see GREEK for 3664 see GREEK for 3958

G3664.text: ὅμοιος o&moios homoios {hom'-oy-os} from the base of 3674; similar (in appearance or character):--like, + manner. see GREEK for 3674

G3665.text: ὁμοιότης oJmoiovths homoiotes {hom-oy-ot'-ace} from 3664; resemblance:--like as, similitude. see GREEK for 3664

G3666.text: ὁμοιόω oJmoiovw homoioo {hom-oy-o'-o} from 3664; to assimilate, i.e. compare; passively, to become similar:--be (make) like, (in the) liken(-ess), resemble. see GREEK for 3664

G3667.text: ὁμοίωμα oJmoivwma homoioma {hom-oy'-o-mah} from 3666; a form; abstractly, resemblance:--made like to, likeness, shape, similitude. see GREEK for 3666

G3668.text: ὁμοίως oJmoivws homoios {hom-oy'-oce} adverb from 3664; similarly:--likewise, so. see GREEK for 3664

G3669.text: ὁμοίωσις oJmoivwsis homoiosis {hom-oy'-o-sis} from 3666; assimilation, i.e. resemblance:--similitude. see GREEK for 3666

G3670.text: ὁμολογέω oJmologevw homologeo {hom-ol-og-eh'-o} from a compound of the base of 3674 and 3056; to assent, i.e. covenant, acknowledge:--con- (pro-)fess, confession is made, give thanks, promise. see GREEK for 3674 see GREEK for 3056

G3671.text: ὁμολογία oJmologiva homologia {hom-ol-og-ee'-ah} from the same as 3670; acknowledgment:--con- (pro-)fession, professed. see GREEK for 3670

G3672.text: ὁμολογουμένως oJmologoumevnws homologoumenos {hom-ol-og-ow-men'-oce} adverb of present passive participle of 3670; confessedly:--without controversy. see GREEK for 3670

G3673.text: ὁμότεχνος oJmovtecnos homotechnos {hom-ot'-ekh-nos} from the base of 3674 and 5078; a fellow-artificer:--of the same craft. see GREEK for 3674 see GREEK for 5078

G3674.text: ὁμοῦ oJmou' homou {hom-oo'} genitive case of homos (the same; akin to 260) as adverb; at the same place or time:--together. see GREEK for 260

G3675.text: ὁμόφρων oJmovfrwn homophron {hom-of'-rone} from the base of 3674 and 5424; like-minded, i.e. harmonious:--of one mind. see GREEK for 5424 see GREEK for 3674

G3676.text: ὅμως o&mws homos {hom'-oce} adverb from the base of 3674; at the same time, i.e. (conjunctionally) notwithstanding, yet still:--and even, nevertheless, though but. see GREEK for 3674

G3677.text: ὄναρ o[nar onar {on'-ar} of uncertain derivation; a dream:--dream.

G3678.text: ὀνάριον ojnavrion onarion {on-ar'-ee-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of 3688; a little ass:--young ass. see GREEK for 3688

G3679.text: ὀνειδίζω ojneidivzw oneidizo {on-i-did'-zo} from 3681; to defame, i.e. rail at, chide, taunt:--cast in teeth, (suffer) reproach, revile, upbraid. see GREEK for 3681

G3680.text: ὀνειδισμός ojneidismovs oneidismos {on-i-dis-mos'} from 3679; contumely:--reproach. see GREEK for 3679

G3681.text: ὄνειδος o[neidos oneidos {on'-i-dos} probably akin to the base of 3686; notoriety, i.e. a taunt (disgrace):--reproach. see GREEK for 3686

G3682.text: Ὀνήσιμος Ojnhvsimos Onesimos {on-ay'-sim-os} from 3685; profitable; Onesimus, a Christian:--Onesimus. see GREEK for 3685

G3683.text: Ὀνησίφορος Ojnhsivforos Onesiphoros {on-ay-sif'-or-os} from a derivative of 3685 and 5411; profit-bearer; Onesiphorus, a Christian:--Onespiphorus. see GREEK for 3685 see GREEK for 5411

G3684.text: ὀνικός ojnikovs onikos {on-ik-os'} from 3688; belonging to a ass, i.e. large (so as to be turned by a ass):--millstone. see GREEK for 3688

G3685.text: ὀνίναμαι ojnivnamai oninemi {on-in'-ay-mee} a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb (onomai, to slur); for which another prolonged form (onao) is used as an alternate in some tenses (unless indeed it be identical with the base of 3686 through the idea of notoriety); to gratify, i.e. (middle voice) to derive pleasure or advantage from:--have joy. see GREEK for 3686

G3686.text: ὄνομα o[noma onoma {on'-om-ah} from a presumed derivative of the base of 1097 (compare 3685); a "name" (literally or figuratively) (authority, character):--called, (+ sur-)name(-d). see GREEK for 1097 see GREEK for 3685

G3687.text: ὀνομάζω ojnomavzw onomazo {on-om-ad'-zo} from 3686; to name, i.e. assign an appellation; by extension, to utter, mention, profess:--call, name. see GREEK for 3686

G3688.text: ὄνος o[nos onos {on'-os} apparently a primary word; a donkey:--an ass.

G3689.text: ὄντως o[ntws ontos {on'-toce} adverb of the oblique cases of 5607; really:--certainly, clean, indeed, of a truth, verily. see GREEK for 5607

G3690.text: ὄξος o[xos oxos {oz-os} from 3691; vinegar, i.e. sour wine:--vinegar. see GREEK for 3691

G3691.text: ὀξύς ojxuvs oxus {oz-oos'} probably akin to the base of 188 ("acid"); keen; by analogy, rapid:--sharp, swift. see GREEK for 188

G3692.text: ὀπή ojphv ope {op-ay'} probably from 3700; a hole (as if for light), i.e. cavern; by analogy, a spring (of water):--cave, place. see GREEK for 3700

G3693.text: ὄπισθεν o[pisqen opisthen {op'-is-then} from opis (regard; from 3700) with enclitic of source; from the rear (as a secure aspect), i.e. at the back (adverb and preposition of place or time):--after, backside, behind. see GREEK for 3700

G3694.text: ὀπίσω ojpivsw opiso {op-is'-o} from the same as 3693 with enclitic of direction; to the back, i.e. aback (as adverb or preposition of time or place; or as noun):--after, back(-ward), (+ get) behind, + follow. see GREEK for 3693

G3695.text: ὁπλίζω oJplivzw hoplizo {hop-lid'-zo} from 3696; to equip (with weapons (middle voice and figuratively)):--arm self. see GREEK for 3696

G3696.text: ὅπλον o&plon hoplon {hop'-lon} probably from a primary hepo (to be busy about); an implement or utensil or tool (literally or figuratively, especially, offensive for war):--armour, instrument, weapon.

G3697.text: ὁποῖος oJpoi'os hopoios {hop-oy'-os} from 3739 and 4169; of what kind that, i.e. how (as) great (excellent) (specially, as an indefinite correlative to the definite antecedent 5108 of quality):--what manner (sort) of, such as whatsoever. see GREEK for 3739 see GREEK for 4169 see GREEK for 5108

G3698.text: ὁπότε hopote hopote {hop-ot'-eh} from 3739 and 4218; what(-ever) then, i.e. (of time) as soon as:--when. see GREEK for 3739 see GREEK for 4218

G3699.text: ὅπου o&pou hopou {hop'-oo} from 3739 and 4225; what(-ever) where, i.e. at whichever spot:--in what place, where(-as, -soever), whither (+ soever). see GREEK for 3739 see GREEK for 4225

G3700.text: ὀπτάνομαι ojptavnomai optanomai {op-tan'-om-ahee} 或 optomai {op-tom-ahee} of the primary (middle voice) optomai op'-tom-ahee; which is used for it in certain tenses; and both as alternate of 3708 to gaze (i.e. with wide-open eyes, as at something remarkable; and thus differing from 991, which denotes simply voluntary observation; and from 1492, which expresses merely mechanical, passive or casual vision; while 2300, and still more emphatically its intensive 2334, signifies an earnest but more continued inspection; and 4648 a watching from a distance):--appear, look, see, shew self. see GREEK for 3708 see GREEK for 991 see GREEK for 1492 see GREEK for 2300 see GREEK for 2334 see GREEK for 4648

G3701.text: ὀπτασία ojptasiva optasia {op-tas-ee'-ah} from a presumed derivative of 3700; visuality, i.e. (concretely) an apparition:--vision. see GREEK for 3700

G3702.text: ὀπτός ojptovs optos {op-tos'} from an obsolete verb akin to hepso (to "steep"); cooked, i.e. roasted:--broiled.

G3703.text: ὀπώρα ojpwvra opora {op-o'-rah} apparently from the base of 3796 and 5610; properly, even-tide of the (summer) season (dog-days), i.e. (by implication) ripe fruit:--fruit. see GREEK for 3796 see GREEK for 5610

G3704.text: ὅπως o&pws hopos {hop'-oce} from 3739 and 4459; what(-ever) how, i.e. in the manner that (as adverb or conjunction of coincidence, intentional or actual):--because, how, (so) that, to, when. see GREEK for 3739 see GREEK for 4459

G3705.text: ὅραμα o&rama horama {hor'-am-ah} from 3708; something gazed at, i.e. a spectacle (especially supernatural):--sight, vision. see GREEK for 3708

G3706.text: ὅρασις o&rasis horasis {hor'-as-is} from 3708; the act of gazing, i.e. (externally) an aspect or (internally) an inspired appearance:--sight, vision. see GREEK for 3708

G3707.text: ὁρατός oJratovs horatos {hor-at-os'} from 3708; gazed at, i.e. (by implication) capable of being seen:--visible. see GREEK for 3708

G3708.text: ὁράω oJravw horao {hor-ah'-o} properly, to stare at (compare 3700), i.e. (by implication) to discern clearly (physically or mentally); by extension, to attend to; by Hebraism, to experience; passively, to appear:--behold, perceive, see, take heed. see GREEK for 3700

G3709.text: ὀργή ojrghv orge {or-gay'} from 3713; properly, desire (as a reaching forth or excitement of the mind), i.e. (by analogy), violent passion (ire, or (justifiable) abhorrence); by implication punishment:--anger, indignation, vengeance, wrath. see GREEK for 3713

G3710.text: ὀργίζω ojrgivzw orgizo {or-gid'-zo} from 3709; to provoke or enrage, i.e. (passively) become exasperated:--be angry (wroth). see GREEK for 3709

G3711.text: ὀργίλος ojrgivlos orgilos {org-ee'-los} from 3709; irascible:--soon angry. see GREEK for 3709

G3712.text: ὀργυιά ojrguiav orguia {org-wee-ah'} from 3713; a stretch of the arms, i.e. a fathom:--fathom. see GREEK for 3713

G3713.text: ὀρέγομαι ojrevgomai oregomai {or-eg'-om-ahee} middle voice of apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (compare 3735); to stretch oneself, i.e. reach out after (long for):--covet after, desire. see GREEK for 3735

G3714.text: ὀρεινός ojreinovs oreinos {or-i-nos} from 3735; mountainous, i.e. (feminine by implication, of 5561) the Highlands (of Judaea):--hill country. see GREEK for 3735 see GREEK for 5561

G3715.text: ὄρεξις o[rexis orexis {or'-ex-is} from 3713; excitement of the mind, i.e. longing after:--lust. see GREEK for 3713

G3716.text: ὀρθοποδέω ojrqopodevw orthopodeo {or-thop-od-eh'-o} from a compound of 3717 and 4228; to be straight-footed, i.e. (figuratively) to go directly forward:--walk uprightly. see GREEK for 3717 see GREEK for 4228

G3717.text: ὀρθός ojrqovs orthos {or-thos'} probably from the base of 3735; right (as rising), i.e. (perpendicularly) erect (figuratively, honest), or (horizontally) level or direct:--straight, upright. see GREEK for 3735

G3718.text: ὀρθοτομέω ojrqotomevw orthotomeo {or-thot-om-eh'-o} from a compound of 3717 and the base of 5114, to make a straight cut, i.e. (figuratively) to dissect (expound) correctly (the divine message):--rightly divide. see GREEK for 3717 see GREEK for 5114

G3719.text: ὀρθρίζω ojrqrivzw orthrizo {or-thrid'-zo} from 3722; to use the dawn, i.e. (by implication) to repair betimes:--come early in the morning. see GREEK for 3722

G3720.text: ὀρθρινός ojrqrinovs orthrinos {or-thrin-os'} from 3722; relating to the dawn, i.e. matutinal (as an epithet of Venus, especially brilliant in the early day):--morning. see GREEK for 3722

G3721.text: ὄρθριος ία ιον orthrios orthrios {or'-three-os} from 3722; in the dawn, i.e. up at day-break:--early. see GREEK for 3722

G3722.text: ὄρθρος o[rqros orthros {or'-thros} from the same as 3735; dawn (as sun-rise, rising of light); by extension, morn:--early in the morning. see GREEK for 3735

G3723.text: ὀρθῶς ojrqw's orthos {or-thoce'} adverb from 3717; in a straight manner, i.e. (figuratively) correctly (also morally):--plain, right(-ly). see GREEK for 3717

G3724.text: ὁρίζω oJrivzw horizo {hor-id'-zo} from 3725; to mark out or bound ("horizon"), i.e. (figuratively) to appoint, decree, specify:--declare, determine, limit, ordain. see GREEK for 3725

G3725.text: ὅριον o&rion horion {hor'-ee-on} neuter of a derivative of an apparently primary horos (a bound or limit); a boundary-line, i.e. (by implication) a frontier (region):--border, coast.

G3726.text: ὁρκίζω oJrkivzw horkizo {hor-kid'-zo} from 3727; to put on oath, i.e. make swear; by analogy, to solemnly enjoin:--adjure, charge. see GREEK for 3727

G3727.text: ὅρκος o&rkos horkos {hor'-kos} from herkos (a fence; perhaps akin to 3725); a limit, i.e. (sacred) restraint (specially, an oath):--oath. see GREEK for 3725

G3728.text: ὁρκωμοσία oJrkwmosiva horkomosia {hor-ko-mos-ee'ah} from a compound of 3727 and a derivative of 3660; asseveration on oath:--oath. see GREEK for 3727 see GREEK for 3660

G3729.text: ὁρμάω oJrmavw hormao {hor-mah'-o} from 3730; to start, spur or urge on, i.e. (reflexively) to dash or plunge:--run (violently), rush. see GREEK for 3730

G3730.text: ὁρμή oJrmhv horme {hor-may'} of uncertain affinity; a violent impulse, i.e. onset:--assault.

G3731.text: ὅρμημα o&rmhma hormema {hor'-may-mah} from 3730; an attack, i.e. (abstractly) precipitancy:--violence. see GREEK for 3730

G3732.text: ὄρνεον o[rneon orneon {or'-neh-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of 3733; a birdling:--bird, fowl. see GREEK for 3733

G3733.text: ὄρνις o[rnis ornis {or'-nis} probably from a prolonged form of the base of 3735; a bird (as rising in the air), i.e. (specially), a hen (or female domestic fowl):--hen. see GREEK for 3735

G3734.text: ὁροθεσία oJroqesiva horothesia {hor-oth-es-ee'-ah} from a compound of the base of 3725 and a derivative of 5087; a limit-placing, i.e. (concretely) boundary-line:--bound. see GREEK for 3725 see GREEK for 5087

G3735.text: ὄρος o[ros oros {or'-os} probably from an obsolete oro (to rise or "rear"; perhaps akin to 142; compare 3733); a mountain (as lifting itself above the plain): -hill, mount(-ain). see GREEK for 142 see GREEK for 3733

G3736.text: ὀρύσσω ojruvssw orusso {or-oos'-so} apparently a primary verb; to "burrow" in the ground, i.e. dig:--dig.

G3737.text: ὀρφανός ojrfanovs orphanos {or-fan-os'} of uncertain affinity; bereaved ("orphan"), i.e. parentless:--comfortless, fatherless.

G3738.text: ὀρχέομαι ojrcevomai orcheomai {or-kheh'-om-ahee} middle voice from orchos (a row or ring); to dance (from the ranklike or regular motion):--dance.

G3739.text: ὅς ἥ ὅ o&s h& o& hos {hos} 包括阴性的 he {hay}, 和中性的 ho {ho} he hay, and neuter ho ho probably a primary word (or perhaps a form of the article 3588); the relatively (sometimes demonstrative) pronoun, who, which, what, that:--one, (an-, the) other, some, that, what, which, who(-m, -se), etc. See also 3757. see GREEK for 3588 see GREEK for 3757

G3740.text: ὁσάκις oJsavkis hosakis {hos-ak'-is} multiple adverb from 3739; how (i.e. with 302, so) many times as:--as oft(-en) as. see GREEK for 3739 see GREEK for 302

G3741.text: ὅσιος o&sios hosios {hos'-ee-os} of uncertain affinity; properly, right (by intrinsic or divine character; thus distinguished from 1342, which refers rather to human statutes and relations; from 2413, which denotes formal consecration; and from 40, which relates to purity from defilement), i.e. hallowed (pious, sacred, sure):--holy, mercy, shalt be. 342 see GREEK for 2413 see GREEK for 40

G3742.text: ὁσιότης oJsiovths hosiotes {hos-ee-ot'-ace} from 3741; piety:--holiness. see GREEK for 3741

G3743.text: ὁσίως oJsivws hosios {hos-ee-oce'} adverb from 3741; piously:--holily. see GREEK for 3741

G3744.text: ὀσμή ojsmhv osme {os-may'} from 3605; fragrance (literally or figuratively):--odour, savour. see GREEK for 3605

G3745.text: ὅσος o&sos hosos {hos'-os} by reduplication from 3739; as (much, great, long, etc.) as:--all (that), as (long, many, much) (as), how great (many, much), (in-)asmuch as, so many as, that (ever), the more, those things, what (great, -soever), wheresoever, wherewithsoever, which, X while, who(-soever). see GREEK for 3739

G3746.text: ὅσπερ ἥπερ ὅπερ hosper hosper {hos'-per} from 3739 and 4007; who especially:--whomsoever. see GREEK for 3739 see GREEK for 4007

G3747.text: ὀστέον ὀστοῦν ojstevon ojstou'n osteon {os-teh'-on} 或缩写型 ostoun {os-toon'} ostoun os-toon' of uncertain affinity; a bone:--bone.

G3748.text: ὅστις o&stis hostis {hos'-tis} 包括阴性的 hetis {hay'-tis} hetis hay'-tis, and the neuter ho,ti hot'-ee from 3739 and 5100; which some, i.e. any that; also (definite) which same:--X and (they), (such) as, (they) that, in that they, what(-soever), whereas ye, (they) which, who(-soever). Compare 3754. see GREEK for 3739 see GREEK for 5100 see GREEK for 3754

G3749.text: ὀστράκινος ojstravkinos ostrakinos {os-tra'-kin-os} from ostrakon ("oyster") (a tile, i.e. terra cotta); earthen-ware, i.e. clayey; by implication, frail:--of earth, earthen.

G3750.text: ὄσφρησις o[sfrhsis osphresis {os'-fray-sis} from a derivative of 3605; smell (the sense):--smelling. see GREEK for 3605

G3751.text: ὀσφῦς ojsfu's osphus {os-foos'} of uncertain affinity; the loin (externally), i.e. the hip; internally (by extension) procreative power:--loin.

G3752.text: ὅταν o&tan hotan {hot'-an} from 3753 and 302; whenever (implying hypothesis or more or less uncertainty); also causatively (conjunctionally) inasmuch as:--as long (soon) as, that, + till, when(-soever), while. see GREEK for 3753 see GREEK for 302

G3753.text: ὅτε o&te hote {hot'-eh} from 3739 and 5037; at which (thing) too, i.e. when:--after (that), as soon as, that, when, while. see GREEK for 3739 see GREEK for 5037

G3754.text: ὅτι o&ti hoti {hot'-ee} neuter of 3748 as conjunction; demonstrative, that (sometimes redundant); causative, because:--as concerning that, as though, because (that), for (that), how (that), (in) that, though, why. see GREEK for 3748

G3755.text: ὅστις o&stis hotou {hot'-oo} for the genitive case of 3748 (as adverb); during which same time, i.e. whilst:--whiles. see GREEK for 3748

G3756.text: οὐ ouj ou {oo} ， 在母音前用 ouk {ook} ; 在有气号之前用ouch {ookh} ouk ook, and (before an aspirate) ouch ookh a primary word; the absolute negative (compare 3361) adverb; no or not:--+ long, nay, neither, never, no (X man), none, (can-)not, + nothing, + special, un(-worthy), when, + without, + yet but. See also 3364, 3372. see GREEK for 3361 see GREEK for 3364 see GREEK for 3372

G3757.text: οὗ ou| hou {hoo} genitive case of 3739 as adverb; at which place, i.e. where:--where(-in), whither(-soever). see GREEK for 3739

G3758.text: οὐά oujav oua {oo-ah'} a primary exclamation of surprise; "ah":--ah.

G3759.text: οὐαί oujaiv ouai {oo-ah'-ee} a primary exclamation of grief; "woe":--alas, woe.

G3760.text: οὐδαμῶς oujdamw's oudamos {oo-dam-oce'} adverb from (the feminine) of 3762; by no means:--not. see GREEK for 3762

G3761.text: οὐδέ oujdev oude {oo-deh'} from 3756 and 1161; not however, i.e. neither, nor, not even:--neither (indeed), never, no (more, nor, not), nor (yet), (also, even, then) not (even, so much as), + nothing, so much as. see GREEK for 3756 see GREEK for 1161

G3762.text: οὐδείς οὐθείς oujdeivs oujqeivs oudeis {oo-dice'} 包括阴性的 oudemia {oo-dem-ee'-ah} oudemia oo-dem-ee'-ah, and neuter ouden oo-den' from 3761 and 1520; not even one (man, woman or thing), i.e. none, nobody, nothing:--any (man), aught, man, neither any (thing), never (man), no (man), none (+ of these things), not (any, at all, -thing), nought. see GREEK for 3761 see GREEK for 1520

G3763.text: οὐδέποτε oujdevpote oudepote {oo-dep'-ot-eh} from 3761 and 4218; not even at any time, i.e. never at all:--neither at any time, never, nothing at any time. see GREEK for 3761 see GREEK for 4218

G3764.text: οὐδέπω oujdevpw oudepo {oo-dep'-o} from 3761 and 4452; not even yet:--as yet not, never before (yet), (not) yet. see GREEK for 3761 see GREEK for 4452

G3766.text: οὐκοῦν oujkou'n oukoun {ook-oon'} from 3756 and 3767; is it not therefore that, i.e. (affirmatively) hence or so:--then. see GREEK for 3756 see GREEK for 3767

G3767.text: οὖν ou\\n oun {oon} apparently a primary word; (adverbially) certainly, or (conjunctionally) accordingly:--and (so, truly), but, now (then), so (likewise then), then, therefore, verily, wherefore.

G3768.text: οὔπω ou[pw oupo {oo'-po} from 3756 and 4452; not yet:--hitherto not, (no...) as yet, not yet. see GREEK for 3756 see GREEK for 4452

G3769.text: οὐρά oujrav oura {oo-rah'} apparently a primary word; a tail:--tail.

G3770.text: οὐράνιος oujravnios ouranios {oo-ran'-ee-os} from 3772; celestial, i.e. belonging to or coming from the sky:--heavenly. see GREEK for 3772

G3771.text: οὐρανόθεν oujranovqen ouranothen {oo-ran-oth'-en} from 3772 and the enclitic of source; from the sky:--from heaven. see GREEK for 3772

G3772.text: οὐρανός oujranovs ouranos {oo-ran-os'} perhaps from the same as 3735 (through the idea of elevation); the sky; by extension, heaven (as the abode of God); by implication, happiness, power, eternity; specially, the Gospel (Christianity):--air, heaven(-ly), sky. see GREEK for 3735

G3773.text: Οὐρβανός Oujrbanovs Ourbanos {oor-ban-os'} of Latin origin; Urbanus (of the city, "urbane"), a Christian:--Urbanus.

G3774.text: Οὐρίας Oujrivas Ourias {oo-ree'-as} of Hebrew origin (223); Urias (i.e. Urijah), a Hittite:--Urias. see HEBREW for 0223

G3775.text: οὖς ou\\s ous {ooce} apparently a primary word; the ear (physically or mentally):--ear.

G3776.text: οὐσία oujsiva ousia {oo-see'-ah} from the feminine of 5607; substance, i.e. property (possessions):--goods, substance. see GREEK for 5607

G3777.text: οὔτε ou[te oute {oo'-teh} from 3756 and 5037; not too, i.e. neither or nor; by analogy, not even:--neither, none, nor (yet), (no, yet) not, nothing. see GREEK for 3756 see GREEK for 5037

G3779.text: οὕτω οὕτως ou&tw ou&tws houto {hoo'-to} 或 (用于母音前 vowel} houtos {hoo'-toce} houtos hoo'-toce adverb from 3778; in this way (referring to what precedes or follows):--after that, after (in) this manner, as, even (so), for all that, like(-wise), no more, on this fashion(-wise), so (in like manner), thus, what. see GREEK for 3778

G3780.text: οὐχί oujciv ouchi {oo-khee'} intensive of 3756; not indeed:--nay, not. see GREEK for 3756

G3781.text: ὀφειλέτης ojfeilevths opheiletes {of-i-let'-ace} from 3784; an ower, i.e. person indebted; figuratively, a delinquent; morally, a transgressor (against God):--debtor, which owed, sinner. see GREEK for 3784

G3782.text: ὀφειλή ojfeilhv opheile {of-i-lay'} from 3784; indebtedness, i.e. (concretely) a sum owed; figuratively, obligation, i.e. (conjugal) duty:--debt, due. see GREEK for 3784

G3783.text: ὀφείλημα ojfeivlhma opheilema {of-i'-lay-mah} from (the alternate of) 3784; something owed, i.e. (figuratively) a due; morally, a fault:--debt. see GREEK for 3784

G3785.text: ὄφελον o[felon ophelon {of'-el-on} first person singular of a past tense of 3784; I ought (wish), i.e. (interjection) oh that!:--would (to God). see GREEK for 3784
