G3786.text: ὄφελος o[felos ophelos {of'-el-os} from ophello (to heap up, i.e. accumulate or benefit); gain:--advantageth, profit.

G3787.text: ὀφθαλμοδουλία ojfqalmodouliva ophthalmodouleia {of-thal-mod-oo-li'-ah} from 3788 and 1397; sight-labor, i.e. that needs watching (remissness):--eye-service. see GREEK for 3788 see GREEK for 1397

G3788.text: ὀφθαλμός ojfqalmovs ophthalmos {of-thal-mos'} from 3700; the eye (literally or figuratively); by implication, vision; figuratively, envy (from the jealous side-glance):--eye, sight. see GREEK for 3700

G3789.text: ὄφις o[fis ophis {of'-is} probably from 3700 (through the idea of sharpness of vision); a snake, figuratively, (as a type of sly cunning) an artful malicious person, especially Satan:--serpent. see GREEK for 3700

G3790.text: ὀφρῦς ojfru's ophrus {of-roos'} perhaps from 3700 (through the idea of the shading or proximity to the organ of vision); the eye-"brow" or forehead, i.e. (figuratively) the brink of a precipice:--brow. see GREEK for 3700

G3791.text: ὀχλέω ojclevw ochleo {okh-leh'-o} from 3793; to mob, i.e. (by implication) to harass:--vex. see GREEK for 3793

G3792.text: ὀχλοποιέω ojclopoievw ochlopoieo {okh-lop-oy-eh'-o} from 3793 and 4160; to make a crowd, i.e. raise a public disturbance:--gather a company. see GREEK for 3793 see GREEK for 4160

G3793.text: ὄχλος o[clos ochlos {okh'los} from a derivative of 2192 (meaning a vehicle); a throng (as borne along); by implication, the rabble; by extension, a class of people; figuratively, a riot:--company, multitude, number (of people), people, press. see GREEK for 2192

G3794.text: ὀχύρωμα ojcuvrwma ochuroma {okh-oo'-ro-mah} from a remote derivative of 2192 (meaning to fortify, through the idea of holding safely); a castle (figuratively, argument):--stronghold. see GREEK for 2192

G3795.text: ὀψάριον ojyavrion opsarion {op-sar'-ee-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of 3702; a relish to other food (as if cooked sauce), i.e. (specially), fish (presumably salted and dried as a condiment):--fish. see GREEK for 3702

G3796.text: ὀψέ ojyev opse {op-seh'} from the same as 3694 (through the idea of backwardness); (adverbially) late in the day; by extension, after the close of the day:--(at) even, in the end. see GREEK for 3694

G3797.text: ὄψιμος o[yimos opsimos {op'-sim-os} from 3796; later, i.e. vernal (showering):--latter. see GREEK for 3796

G3798.text: ὄψιος o[yios opsios {op'-see-os} from 3796; late; feminine (as noun) afternoon (early eve) or nightfall (later eve):--even(-ing, (-tide)). see GREEK for 3796

G3799.text: ὄψις o[yis opsis {op'-sis} from 3700; properly, sight (the act), i.e. (by implication) the visage, an external show:--appearance, countenance, face. see GREEK for 3700

G3800.text: ὀψώνιον ojywvnion opsonion {op-so'-nee-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of the same as 3795; rations for a soldier, i.e. (by extension) his stipend or pay:-- wages. see GREEK for 3795

G3801.lemma: ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος
G3801.text: ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ho on kai ho en kai ho erchomenos ho on kai ho en kai ho erchomenos {ho own kahee ho ane kahee ho er-khom'-en-os} ho own kahee ho ane kahee ho er-khom'-en-os a phrase combining 3588 with the present participle and imperfect of 1510 and the present participle of 2064 by means of 2532; the one being and the one that was and the one coming, i.e. the Eternal, as a divine epithet of Christ:--which art (is, was), and (which) wast (is, was), and art (is) to come (shalt be). see GREEK for 1510 see GREEK for 2532 see GREEK for 3588 see GREEK for 2064

G3802.text: παγιδεύω pagideuvw pagideuo {pag-id-yoo'-o} from 3803; to ensnare (figuratively):--entangle. see GREEK for 3803

G3803.text: παγίς pagivs pagis {pag-ece'} from 4078; a trap (as fastened by a noose or notch); figuratively, a trick or statagem (temptation):--snare. see GREEK for 4078

G3804.text: πάθημα pavqhma pathema {path'-ay-mah} from a presumed derivative of 3806; something undergone, i.e. hardship or pain; subjectively, an emotion or influence:-- affection, affliction, motion, suffering. see GREEK for 3806

G3805.text: παθητός paqhtovs pathetos {path-ay-tos'} from the same as 3804; liable (i.e. doomed) to experience pain:--suffer. see GREEK for 3804

G3806.text: πάθος pavqos pathos {path'-os} from the alternate of 3958; properly, suffering ("pathos"), i.e. (subjectively) a passion (especially concupiscence):-- (inordinate) affection, lust. see GREEK for 3958

G3807.text: παιδαγωγός paidagwgovs paidagogos {pahee-dag-o-gos'} from 3816 and a reduplicated form of 71; a boy-leader, i.e. a servant whose office it was to take the children to school; (by implication, (figuratively) a tutor ("paedagogue")):-- instructor, schoolmaster. see GREEK for 3816 see GREEK for 71

G3808.text: παιδάριον paidavrion paidarion {pahee-dar'-ee-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of 3816; a little boy:--child, lad. see GREEK for 3816

G3809.text: παιδεία paideiva paideia {pahee-di'-ah} from 3811; tutorage, i.e. education or training; by implication, disciplinary correction:--chastening, chastisement, instruction, nurture. see GREEK for 3811

G3810.text: παιδευτής paideuthvs paideutes {pahee-dyoo-tace'} from 3811; a trainer, i.e. teacher or (by implication) discipliner:--which corrected, instructor. see GREEK for 3811

G3811.text: παιδεύω paideuvw paideuo {pahee-dyoo'-o} from 3816; to train up a child, i.e. educate, or (by implication), discipline (by punishment):--chasten(-ise), instruct, learn, teach. see GREEK for 3816

G3812.text: παιδιόθεν paidiovqen paidiothen {pahee-dee-oth'-en} adverb (of source) from 3813; from infancy:--of a child. see GREEK for 3813

G3813.text: παιδίον paidivon paidion {pahee-dee'-on} neuter diminutive of 3816; a childling (of either sex), i.e. (properly), an infant, or (by extension) a half-grown boy or girl; figuratively, an immature Christian:--(little, young) child, damsel. see GREEK for 3816

G3814.text: παιδίσκη paidivskh paidiske {pahee-dis'-kay} feminine diminutive of 3816; a girl, i.e. (specially), a female slave or servant:--bondmaid(-woman), damsel, maid(-en). see GREEK for 3816

G3815.text: παίζω paivzw paizo {paheed'-zo} from 3816; to sport (as a boy):--play. see GREEK for 3816

G3816.text: παῖς pai's pais {paheece} perhaps from 3817; a boy (as often beaten with impunity), or (by analogy), a girl, and (genitive case) a child; specially, a slave or servant (especially a minister to a king; and by eminence to God):--child, maid(-en), (man) servant, son, young man. see GREEK for 3817

G3817.text: παίω paivw paio {pah'-yo} a primary verb; to hit (as if by a single blow and less violently than 5180); specially, to sting (as a scorpion):--smite, strike. see GREEK for 5180

G3818.text: ακατιανή Pakatiane Pakatiane {pak-at-ee-an-ay'} feminine of an adjective of uncertain derivation; Pacatianian, a section of Phrygia:--Pacatiana.

G3819.text: πάλαι pavlai palai {pal'-ahee} probably another form for 3825 (through the idea of retrocession); (adverbially) formerly, or (by relatively) sometime since; (elliptically as adjective) ancient:--any while, a great while ago, (of) old, in time past. see GREEK for 3825

G3820.text: παλαιός palaiovs palaios {pal-ah-yos'} from 3819; antique, i.e. not recent, worn out:--old. see GREEK for 3819

G3821.text: παλαιότης palaiovths palaiotes {pal-ah-yot'-ace} from 3820; antiquatedness:--oldness. see GREEK for 3820

G3822.text: παλαιόω palaiovw palaioo {pal-ah-yo'-o} from 3820; to make (passively, become) worn out, or declare obsolete:--decay, make (wax) old. see GREEK for 3820

G3823.text: πάλη pavlh pale {pal'-ay} from pallo (to vibrate; another form for 906); wrestling:--+ wrestle. see GREEK for 906

G3824.text: παλιγγενεσία paliggenesiva paliggenesia {pal-ing-ghen-es-ee'-ah} from 3825 and 1078; (spiritual) rebirth (the state or the act), i.e. (figuratively) spiritual renovation; specially, Messianic restoration:--regeneration. see GREEK for 3825 see GREEK for 1078

G3825.text: πάλιν pavlin palin {pal'-in} probably from the same as 3823 (through the idea of oscillatory repetition); (adverbially) anew, i.e. (of place) back, (of time) once more, or (conjunctionally) furthermore or on the other hand:--again. see GREEK for 3823

G3826.text: παμπληθεί pamplhqeiv pamplethei {pam-play-thi'} dative case (adverb) of a compound of 3956 and 4128; in full multitude, i.e. concertedly or simultaneously:--all at once. see GREEK for 3956 see GREEK for 4128

G3827.text: πάμπολυς παμπόλλη πάμπολυ pampolus pampolus {pam-pol-ooce} from 3956 and 4183; full many, i.e. immense:--very great. see GREEK for 3956 see GREEK for 4183

G3828.text: ∏αμφυλία Pamfuliva Pamphulia {pam-fool-ee'-ah} from a compound of 3956 and 4443; every-tribal, i.e. heterogeneous (5561 being implied); Pamphylia, a region of Asia Minor:--Pamphylia. see GREEK for 3956 see GREEK for 4443 see GREEK for 5561

G3829.text: πανδοχεῖον pandocei'on pandocheion {pan-dokk-i'-on} neuter of a presumed compound of 3956 and a derivative of 1209; all-receptive, i.e. a public lodging-place (caravanserai or khan):--inn. see GREEK for 3956 see GREEK for 1209

G3830.text: πανδοχεύς pandoceuvs pandocheus {pan-dokh-yoos'} from the same as 3829; an innkeeper (warden of a caravanserai):--host. see GREEK for 3829

G3831.text: πανηγύρις panhguvris paneguris {pan-ay'-goo-ris} from 3956 and a derivative of 58; a mass-meeting, i.e. (figuratively) universal companionship:--general assembly. see GREEK for 3956 see GREEK for 58

G3832.text: πανοικεί panoikeiv panoiki {pan-oy-kee'} adverb from 3956 and 3624; with the whole family:--with all his house. see GREEK for 3956 see GREEK for 3624

G3833.text: πανοπλία panopliva panoplia {pan-op-lee'-ah} from a compound of 3956 and 3696; full armor ("panoply"):--all (whole) armour. see GREEK for 3956 see GREEK for 3696

G3834.text: πανουργία panourgiva panourgia {pan-oorg-ee'-ah} from 3835; adroitness, i.e. (in a bad sense) trickery or sophistry:--(cunning) craftiness, subtilty. see GREEK for 3835

G3835.text: πανοῦργος panou'rgos panourgos {pan-oor'-gos} from 3956 and 2041; all-working, i.e. adroit (shrewd):--crafty. see GREEK for 3956 see GREEK for 2041

G3836.text: πανταχόθεν pantachothen pantachothen {pan-takh-oth'-en} adverb (of source) from 3837; from all directions:--from every quarter. see GREEK for 3837

G3837.text: πανταχοῦ πανταχῇ pantacou' pantach'/ pantachou {pan-takh-oo'} genitive case (as adverb of place) of a presumed derivative of 3956; universally:--in all places, everywhere. see GREEK for 3956

G3838.text: παντελής pantelhvs panteles {pan-tel-ace'} from 3956 and 5056; full-ended, i.e. entire (neuter as noun, completion):--+ in (no) wise, uttermost. see GREEK for 3956 see GREEK for 5056

G3839.text: πάντῃ pavnth/ pante {pan'-tay} adverb (of manner) from 3956; wholly:--always. see GREEK for 3956

G3840.text: πάντοθεν pavntoqen pantothen {pan-toth'-en} adverb (of source) from 3956; from (i.e. on) all sides:--on every side, round about. see GREEK for 3956

G3841.text: παντοκράτωρ pantokravtwr pantokrator {pan-tok-rat'-ore} from 3956 and 2904; the all-ruling, i.e. God (as absolute and universal sovereign):--Almighty, Omnipotent. see GREEK for 3956 see GREEK for 2904

G3842.text: πάντοτε pavntote pantote {pan'-tot-eh} from 3956 and 3753; every when, i.e. at all times:--alway(-s), ever(-more). see GREEK for 3956 see GREEK for 3753

G3843.text: πάντως pavntws pantos {pan'-toce} adverb from 3956; entirely; specially, at all events, (with negative, following) in no event:--by all means, altogether, at all, needs, no doubt, in (no) wise, surely. see GREEK for 3956

G3844.text: παρά parav para {par-ah'} a primary preposition; properly, near; i.e. (with genitive case) from beside (literally or figuratively), (with dative case) at (or in) the vicinity of (objectively or subjectively), (with accusative case) to the proximity with (local (especially beyond or opposed to) or causal (on account of):--above, against, among, at, before, by, contrary to, X friend, from, + give (such things as they), + that (she) had, X his, in, more than, nigh unto, (out) of, past, save, side...by, in the sight of, than, (there-)fore, with. In compounds it retains the same variety of application.

G3845.text: παραβαίνω parabaivnw parabaino {par-ab-ah'-ee-no} from 3844 and the base of 939; to go contrary to, i.e. violate a command:--(by) transgress(-ion). see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 939

G3846.text: παραβάλλω parabavllw paraballo {par-ab-al'-lo} from 3844 and 906; to throw alongside, i.e. (reflexively) to reach a place, or (figuratively) to liken:--arrive, compare. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 906

G3847.text: παράβασις paravbasis parabasis {par-ab'-as-is} from 3845; violation:--breaking, transgression. see GREEK for 3845

G3848.text: παραβάτης parabavths parabates {par-ab-at'-ace} from 3845; a violator:--breaker, transgress(-or). see GREEK for 3845

G3849.text: παραβιάζομαι parabiavzomai parabiazomai {par-ab-ee-ad'-zom-ahee} from 3844 and the middle voice of 971; to force contrary to (nature), i.e. compel (by entreaty):--constrain. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 971

G3850.text: παραβολή parabolhv parabole {par-ab-ol-ay'} from 3846; a similitude ("parable"), i.e. (symbolic) fictitious narrative (of common life conveying a moral), apothegm or adage:--comparison, figure, parable, proverb. see GREEK for 3846

G3851.text: παραβολεύομαι paraboleuvomai parabouleuomai {par-ab-ool-yoo'-om-ahee} from 3844 and the middle voice of 1011; to misconsult, i.e. disregard:--not (to) regard(-ing). see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1011

G3852.text: παραγγελία paraggeliva paraggelia {par-ang-gel-ee'-ah} from 3853; a mandate:--charge, command. see GREEK for 3853

G3853.text: παραγγέλλω paraggevllw paraggello {par-ang-gel'-lo} from 3844 and the base of 32; to transmit a message, i.e. (by implication) to enjoin:--(give in) charge, (give) command(-ment), declare. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 32

G3854.text: παραγίνομαι paragivnomai paraginomai {par-ag-in'-om-ahee} from 3844 and 1096; to become near, i.e. approach (have arrived); by implication, to appear publicly:--come, go, be present. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1096

G3855.text: παράγω paravgw parago {par-ag'-o} from 3844 and 71; to lead near, i.e. (reflexively or intransitively) to go along or away:--depart, pass (away, by, forth). see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 71

G3856.text: παραδειγματίζω paradeigmativzw paradeigmatizo {par-ad-igue-mat-id'-zo} from 3844 and 1165; to show alongside (the public), i.e. expose to infamy:--make a public example, put to an open shame. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1165

G3857.text: παράδεισος paravdeisos paradeisos {par-ad'-i-sos} of Oriental origin (compare 6508); a park, i.e. (specially), an Eden (place of future happiness, "paradise"):--paradise. see HEBREW for 06508

G3858.text: παραδέχομαι paradevcomai paradechomai {par-ad-ekh'-om-ahee} from 3844 and 1209; to accept near, i.e. admit or (by implication) delight in:--receive. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1209

G3859.text: διαπαρατριβή diaparatribhv paradiatribe {par-ad-ee-at-ree-bay'} from a compound of 3844 and 1304; misemployment, i.e. meddlesomeness:--perverse disputing. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1304

G3860.text: παραδίδωμι paradivdwmi paradidomi {par-ad-id'-o-mee} from 3844 and 1325; to surrender, i.e yield up, intrust, transmit:--betray, bring forth, cast, commit, deliver (up), give (over, up), hazard, put in prison, recommend. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1325

G3861.text: παράδοξος paravdoxos paradoxos {par-ad'-ox-os} from 3844 and 1391 (in the sense of seeming); contrary to expectation, i.e. extraordinary ("paradox"):--strange. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1391

G3862.text: παράδοσις paravdosis paradosis {par-ad'-os-is} from 3860; transmission, i.e. (concretely) a precept; specially, the Jewish traditionary law:--ordinance, tradition. see GREEK for 3860

G3863.text: παραζηλόω parazhlovw parazeloo {par-ad-zay-lo'-o} from 3844 and 2206; to stimulate alongside, i.e. excite to rivalry:--provoke to emulation (jealousy). see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 2206

G3864.text: παραθαλάσσιος paraqalavssios parathalassios {par-ath-al-as'-see-os} from 3844 and 2281; along the sea, i.e. maritime (lacustrine):--upon the sea coast. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 2281

G3865.text: παραθεωρέω paraqewrevw paratheoreo {par-ath-eh-o-reh'-o} from 3844 and 2334; to overlook or disregard:--neglect. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 2334

G3866.text: παραθήκη paraqhvkh paratheke {par-ath-ay'-kay} from 3908; a deposit, i.e. (figuratively) trust:--committed unto. see GREEK for 3908

G3867.text: παραινέω parainevw paraineo {par-ahee-neh'-o} from 3844 and 134; to mispraise, i.e. recommend or advise (a different course):--admonish, exhort. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 134

G3868.text: παραιτέομαι paraitevomai paraiteomai {par-ahee-teh'-om-ahee} from 3844 and the middle voice of 154; to beg off, i.e. deprecate, decline, shun:--avoid, (make) excuse, intreat, refuse, reject. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 154

G3869.text: παρακαθέζομαι parakaqevzomai parakathizo {par-ak-ath-id'-zo} from 3844 and 2523; to sit down near:--sit. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 2523

G3870.text: παρακαλέω parakalevw parakaleo {par-ak-al-eh'-o} from 3844 and 2564; to call near, i.e. invite, invoke (by imploration, hortation or consolation):--beseech, call for, (be of good) comfort, desire, (give) exhort(-ation), intreat, pray. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 2564

G3871.text: παρακαλύπτω parakaluvptw parakalupto {par-ak-al-oop'-to} from 3844 and 2572; to cover alongside, i.e. veil (figuratively):--hide. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 2572

G3872.text: παρακαταθήκη parakatatheke parakatatheke {par-ak-at-ath-ay'-kay} from a compound of 3844 and 2698; something put down alongside, i.e. a deposit (sacred trust):--that (thing) which is committed (un-)to (trust). see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 2698

G3873.text: παράκειμαι paravkeimai parakeimai {par-ak'-i-mahee} from 3844 and 2749; to lie near, i.e. be at hand (figuratively, be prompt or easy):--be present. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 2749

G3874.text: παράκλησις paravklhsis paraklesis {par-ak'-lay-sis} from 3870; imploration, hortation, solace:--comfort, consolation, exhortation, intreaty. see GREEK for 3870

G3875.text: παράκλητος paravklhtos parakletos {par-ak'-lay-tos} an intercessor, consoler:--advocate, comforter.

G3876.text: παρακοή parakohv parakoe {par-ak-o-ay'} from 3878; inattention, i.e. (by implication) disobedience:--disobedience. see GREEK for 3878

G3877.text: παρακολουθέω parakolouqevw parakoloutheo {par-ak-ol-oo-theh'-o} from 3844 and 190; to follow near, i.e. (figuratively) attend (as a result), trace out, conform to:--attain, follow, fully know, have understanding. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 190

G3878.text: παρακούω parakouvw parakouo {par-ak-oo'-o} from 3844 and 191; to mishear, i.e. (by implication) to disobey:--neglect to hear. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 191

G3879.text: παρακύπτω parakuvptw parakupto {par-ak-oop'-to} from 3844 and 2955; to bend beside, i.e. lean over (so as to peer within):--look (into), stoop down. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 2955

G3880.text: παραλαμβάνω paralambavnw paralambano {par-al-am-ban'-o} from 3844 and 2983; to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself (in any familiar or intimate act or relation); by analogy, to assume an office; figuratively, to learn:--receive, take (unto, with). see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 2983

G3882.text: παράλιος paravlios paralios {par-al'-ee-os} from 3844 and 251; beside the salt (sea), i.e. maritime:--sea coast. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 251

G3883.text: παραλλαγή parallaghv parallage {par-al-lag-ay'} from a compound of 3844 and 236; transmutation (of phase or orbit), i.e. (figuratively) fickleness: variableness. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 236

G3884.text: παραλογίζομαι paralogivzomai paralogizomai {par-al-og-id'-zom-ahee} from 3844 and 3049; to misreckon, i.e. delude:--beguile, deceive. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3049

G3885.text: παραλυτικός paralutikovs paralutikos {par-al-oo-tee-kos'} from a derivative of 3886; as if dissolved, i.e. "paralytic":--that had (sick of) the palsy. see GREEK for 3886

G3886.text: παραλύω paraluvw paraluo {par-al-oo'-o} from 3844 and 3089; to loosen beside, i.e. relax (perfect passive participle, paralyzed or enfeebled):--feeble, sick of the (taken with) palsy. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3089

G3887.text: παραμένω paramevnw parameno {par-am-en'-o} from 3844 and 3306; to stay near, i.e. remain (literally, tarry; or figuratively, be permanent, persevere):--abide, continue. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3306 see GREEK for 3306 see GREEK for 3844

G3888.text: παραμυθέομαι paramuqevomai paramutheomai {par-am-oo-theh'-om-ahee} from 3844 and the middle voice of a derivative of 3454; to relate near, i.e. (by implication) encourage, console:--comfort. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3454

G3889.text: παραμυθία paramuqiva paramuthia {par-am-oo-thee'-ah} from 3888; consolation (properly, abstract):--comfort. see GREEK for 3888

G3890.text: παραμύθιον paramuvqion paramuthion {par-am-oo'-thee-on} neuter of 3889; consolation (properly, concretely):--comfort. see GREEK for 3889

G3891.text: παρανομέω paranomevw paranomeo {par-an-om-eh'-o} from a compound of 3844 and 3551; to be opposed to law, i.e. to transgress:--contrary to law. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3551

G3892.text: παρανομία paranomiva paranomia {par-an-om-ee'-ah} from the same as 3891; transgression: iniquity. see GREEK for 3891

G3893.text: παραπικραίνω parapikraivnw parapikraino {par-ap-ik-rah'-ee-no} from 3844 and 4087; to embitter alongside, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate:--provoke. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 4087

G3894.text: παραπικρασμός parapikrasmovs parapikrasmos {par-ap-ik-ras-mos'} from 3893; irritation:--provocation. see GREEK for 3893

G3895.text: παραπίπτω parapivptw parapipto {par-ap-ip'-to} from 3844 and 4098; to fall aside, i.e. (figuratively) to apostatize:--fall away. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 4098

G3896.text: παραπλέω paraplevw parapleo {par-ap-leh'-o} from 3844 and 4126; to sail near:--sail by. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 4126

G3897.text: παραπλήσιον paraplhvsion paraplesion {par-ap-lay'-see-on} neuter of a compound of 3844 and the base of 4139 (as adverb); close by, i.e. (figuratively) almost:--nigh unto. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 4139

G3898.text: παραπλησίως paraplhsivws paraplesios {par-ap-lay-see'-oce} adverb from the same as 3897; in a manner near by, i.e. (figuratively) similarly:--likewise. see GREEK for 3897

G3899.text: παραπορεύομαι paraporeuvomai paraporeuomai {par-ap-or-yoo'-om-ahee} from 3844 and 4198; to travel near:--go, pass (by). see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 4198

G3900.text: παράπτωμα paravptwma paraptoma {par-ap'-to-mah} from 3895; a side-slip (lapse or deviation), i.e. (unintentional) error or (wilful) transgression:--fall, fault, offence, sin, trespass. see GREEK for 3895

G3901.text: παραρρέω pararrevw pararrhueo {par-ar-hroo-eh'-o} from 3844 and the alternate of 4482; to flow by, i.e. (figuratively) carelessly pass (miss):--let slip. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 4482

G3902.text: παράσημος paravshmos parasemos {par-as'-ay-mos} from 3844 and the base of 4591; side-marked, i.e. labelled (with a badge (figure-head) of a ship):--sign. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 4591

G3903.text: παρασκευάζω paraskeuavzw paraskeuazo {par-ask-yoo-ad'-zo} from 3844 and a derivative of 4632; to furnish aside, i.e. get ready:--prepare self, be (make) ready. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 4632

G3904.text: παρασκευή paraskeuhv paraskeue {par-ask-yoo-ay'} as if from 3903; readiness:--preparation. see GREEK for 3903

G3905.text: παρατείνω parateivnw parateino {par-at-i'-no} from 3844 and teino (to stretch); to extend along, i.e. prolong (in point of time):--continue. see GREEK for 3844

G3906.text: παρατηρέω parathrevw paratereo {par-at-ay-reh'-o} from 3844 and 5083; to inspect alongside, i.e. note insidiously or scrupulously:--observe, watch. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 5083

G3907.text: παρατήρησις parathvrhsis parateresis {par-at-ay'-ray-sis} from 3906; inspection, i.e. ocular evidence:--obervation. see GREEK for 3906

G3908.text: παρατίθημι parativqhmi paratithemi {par-at-ith'-ay-mee} from 3844 and 5087; to place alongside, i.e. present (food, truth); by implication, to deposit (as a trust or for protection):--allege, commend, commit (the keeping of), put forth, set before. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 5087

G3909.text: παρατυγχάνω paratugcavnw paratugchano {par-at-oong-khan'-o} from 3844 and 5177; to chance near, i.e. fall in with:--meet with. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 5177

G3910.text: παραυτίκα parautivka parautika {par-ow-tee'-kah} from 3844 and a derivative of 846; at the very instant, i.e. momentary:--but for a moment. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 846

G3911.text: παραφέρω parafevrw paraphero {par-af-er'-o} from 3844 and 5342 (including its alternate forms); to bear along or aside, i.e. carry off (literally or figuratively); by implication, to avert:--remove, take away. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 5342

G3912.text: παραφρονέω parafronevw paraphroneo {par-af-ron-eh'-o} from 3844 and 5426; to misthink, i.e. be insane (silly):--as a fool. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 5426

G3913.text: παραφρονία parafroniva paraphronia {par-af-ron-ee'-ah} from 3912; insanity, i.e. foolhardiness:--madness. see GREEK for 3912

G3914.text: παραχειμάζω paraceimavzw paracheimazo {par-akh-i-mad'-zo} from 3844 and 5492; to winter near, i.e. stay with over the rainy season:--winter. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 5492

G3915.text: παραχειμασία paraceimasiva paracheimasia {par-akh-i-mas-ee'-ah} from 3914; a wintering over:--winter in. see GREEK for 3914

G3916.text: παραχρῆμα paracrh'ma parachrema {par-akh-ray'-mah} from 3844 and 5536 (in its original sense); at the thing itself, i.e. instantly:--forthwith, immediately, presently, straightway, soon. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 5536

G3917.text: πάρδαλις pavrdalis pardalis {par'-dal-is} feminine of pardos (a panther); a leopard:--leopard.

G3918.text: πάρειμι pavreimi pareimi {par'-i-mee} from 3844 and 1510 (including its various forms); to be near, i.e. at hand; neuter present participle (singular) time being, or (plural) property:--come, X have, be here, + lack, (be here) present. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1510

G3919.text: παρεισάγω pareisavgw pareisago {par-ice-ag'-o} from 3844 and 1521; to lead in aside, i.e. introduce surreptitiously:--privily bring in. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1521

G3920.text: παρείσακτος pareivsaktos pareisaktos {par-ice'-ak-tos} from 3919; smuggled in: unawares brought in. see GREEK for 3919

G3921.text: παρεισδύω pareisduvw pareisduno {par-ice-doo'-no} from 3844 and a compound of 1519 and 1416; to settle in alongside, i.e. lodge stealthily:--creep in unawares. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1519 see GREEK for 1416

G3922.text: παρεισέρχομαι pareisevrcomai pareiserchomai {par-ice-er'-khom-ahee} from 3844 and 1525; to come in alongside, i.e. supervene additionally or steathily:--come in privily, enter. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1525

G3923.text: παρεισφέρω pareisfevrw pareisphero {par-ice-fer'-o} from 3844 and 1533; to bear in alongside, i.e. introduce simultaneously:--give. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1533

G3924.text: παρεκτός parektovs parektos {par-ek-tos'} from 3844 and 1622; near outside, i.e. besides:--except, saving, without. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1622

G3925.text: παρεμβολή parembolhv parembole {par-em-bol-ay'} from a compound of 3844 and 1685; a throwing in beside (juxtaposition), i.e. (specially), battle-array, encampment or barracks (tower Antonia):--army, camp, castle. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1685

G3926.text: παρενοχλέω parenoclevw parenochleo {par-en-okh-leh'-o} from 3844 and 1776; to harass further, i.e. annoy:--trouble. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1776

G3927.text: παρεπίδημος parepivdhmos parepidemos {par-ep-id'-ay-mos} from 3844 and the base of 1927; an alien alongside, i.e. a resident foreigner:--pilgrim, stranger. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 1927

G3928.text: παρέρχομαι parevrcomai parerchomai {par-er'-khom-ahee} from 3844 and 2064; to come near or aside, i.e. to approach (arrive), go by (or away), (figuratively) perish or neglect, (causative) avert:--come (forth), go, pass (away, by, over), past, transgress. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 2064

G3929.text: πάρεσις pavresis paresis {par'-es-is} from 2935; praetermission, i.e. toleration:--remission. see GREEK for 2935

G3930.text: παρέχω parevcw parecho {par-ekh'-o} from 3844 and 2192; to hold near, i.e. present, afford, exhibit, furnish occasion:--bring, do, give, keep, minister, offer, shew, + trouble. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 2192

G3931.text: παρηγορία parhgoriva paregoria {par-ay-gor-ee'-ah} from a compound of 3844 and a derivative of 58 (meaning to harangue an assembly); an address alongside, i.e. (specially), consolation:--comfort. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 58

G3932.text: παρθενία parqeniva parthenia {par-then-ee'-ah} from 3933; maidenhood:--virginity. see GREEK for 3933

G3933.text: παρθένος parqevnos parthenos {par-then'-os} of unknown origin; a maiden; by implication, an unmarried daughter:--virgin.

G3934.text: ∏άρθος Pavrqos Parthos {par'-thos} probably of foreign origin; a Parthian, i.e. inhabitant of Parthia:--Parthian.

G3935.text: παρίημι parivhmi pariemi {par-ee'-ay-mi} from 3844 and hiemi (to send); to let by, i.e. relax:--hang down. see GREEK for 3844

G3936.text: παρίστημι parivsthmi paristemi {par-is'-tay-mee} 或是扩充型的 paristano {par-is-tan'-o} paristano par-is-tan'-o from 3844 and 2476; to stand beside, i.e. (transitively) to exhibit, proffer, (specially), recommend, (figuratively) substantiate; or (intransitively) to be at hand (or ready), aid:--assist, bring before, command, commend, give presently, present, prove, provide, shew, stand (before, by, here, up, with), yield. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 2476

G3937.text: ∏αρμενᾶς Parmena's Parmenas {par-men-as'} probably by contraction for Parmenides (a derivative of a compound of 3844 and 3306); constant; Parmenas, a Christian:--Parmenas. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3306

G3938.text: πάροδος pavrodos parodos {par'-od-os} from 3844 and 3598; a by-road, i.e. (actively) a route:--way. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3598

G3939.text: παροικέω paroikevw paroikeo {par-oy-keh'-o} from 3844 and 3611; to dwell near, i.e. reside as a foreigner:--sojourn in, be a stranger. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3611

G3940.text: παροικία paroikiva paroikia {par-oy-kee'-ah} from 3941; foreign residence:--sojourning, X as strangers. see GREEK for 3941

G3941.text: πάροικος pavroikos paroikos {par'-oy-kos} from 3844 and 3624; having a home near, i.e. (as noun) a by-dweller (alien resident):--foreigner, sojourn, stranger. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3624

G3942.text: παροιμία paroimiva paroimia {par-oy-mee'-ah} from a compound of 3844 and perhaps a derivative of 3633; apparently a state alongside of supposition, i.e. (concretely) an adage; specially, an enigmatical or fictitious illustration:--parable, proverb. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3633

G3943.text: πάροινος pavroinos paroinos {par'-oy-nos} from 3844 and 3631; staying near wine, i.e. tippling (a toper):--given to wine. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3631

G3944.text: παροίχομαι paroivcomai paroichomai {par-oy'-khom-ahee} from 3844 and oichomai (to depart); to escape along, i.e. be gone:--past. see GREEK for 3844

G3945.text: παρομοιάζω paromoiavzw paromoiazo {par-om-oy-ad'-zo} from 3946; to resemble:--be like unto. see GREEK for 3946

G3946.text: παρόμοιος parovmoios paromoios {par-om'-oy-os} from 3844 and 3664; alike nearly, i.e. similar:--like. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3664

G3947.text: παροξύνω paroxuvnw paroxuno {par-ox-oo'-no} from 3844 and a derivative of 3691; to sharpen alongside, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate:--easily provoke, stir. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3691

G3948.text: παροξυσμός paroxusmovs paroxusmos {par-ox-oos-mos'} from 3947 ("paroxysm"); incitement (to good), or dispute (in anger):--contention, provoke unto. see GREEK for 3947

G3949.text: παροργίζω parorgivzw parorgizo {par-org-id'-zo} from 3844 and 3710; to anger alongside, i.e. enrage:--anger, provoke to wrath. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3710

G3950.text: παροργισμός parorgismovs parorgismos {par-org-is-mos'} from 3949; rage:--wrath. see GREEK for 3949

G3951.text: παροτρύνω parotruvnw parotruno {par-ot-roo'-no} from 3844 and otruno (to spur); to urge along, i.e. stimulate (to hostility):--stir up. see GREEK for 3844

G3952.text: παρουσία parousiva parousia {par-oo-see'-ah} from the present participle of 3918; a being near, i.e. advent (often, return; specially, of Christ to punish Jerusalem, or finally the wicked); (by implication) physically, aspect:--coming, presence. see GREEK for 3918

G3953.text: παροψίς paroyivs paropsis {par-op-sis'} from 3844 and the base of 3795; a side-dish (the receptacle):--platter. see GREEK for 3844 see GREEK for 3795

G3954.text: παρρησία parrhsiva parrhesia {par-rhay-see'-ah} from 3956 and a derivative of 4483; all out-spokenness, i.e. frankness, bluntness, publicity; by implication, assurance:--bold (X -ly, -ness, -ness of speech), confidence, X freely, X openly, X plainly(-ness). see GREEK for 3956 see GREEK for 4483

G3955.text: παρρησιάζομαι parrhsiavzomai parrhesiazomai {par-hray-see-ad'-zom-ahee} middle voice from 3954; to be frank in utterance, or confident in spirit and demeanor:--be (wax) bold, (preach, speak) boldly. see GREEK for 3954

G3956.text: πᾶς pa's pas {pas} including all the forms of declension; apparently a primary word; all, any, every, the whole:--all (manner of, means), alway(-s), any (one), X daily, + ever, every (one, way), as many as, + no(-thing), X thoroughly, whatsoever, whole, whosoever.

G3957.text: πάσχα pavsca pascha {pas'-khah} of Chaldee origin (compare 6453); the Passover (the meal, the day, the festival or the special sacrifices connected with it):--Easter, Passover. see HEBREW for 06453

G3958.text: πάσχω,pavscw "3958 pascho {pas'-kho} 包括 (patho {path'-o} 和 pentho {pen'-tho}) patho path'-o, and pentho pen'-tho, used only in certain tenses for it apparently a primary verb; to experience a sensation or impression (usually painful):--feel, passion, suffer, vex.

G3959.text: ∏άταρα Pavtara Patara {pat'-ar-ah} probably of foreign origin; Patara, a place in Asia Minor:--Patara.

G3960.text: πατάσσω patavssw patasso {pat-as'-so} probably prolongation from 3817; to knock (gently or with a weapon or fatally):--smite, strike. Compare 5180. see GREEK for 3817 see GREEK for 5180

G3961.text: πατέω patevw pateo {pat-eh'-o} from a derivative probably of 3817 (meaning a "path"); to trample (literally or figuratively):--tread (down, under foot). see GREEK for 3817

G3962.text: πατήρ pathvr pater {pat-ayr'} apparently a primary word; a "father" (literally or figuratively, near or more remote):--father, parent.

G3963.text: ∏άτμος Pavtmos Patmos {pat'-mos} of uncertain derivation; Patmus, an islet in the Mediterranean:--Patmos.

G3964.text: πατρολῴας patrolwv/as patraloas {pat-ral-o'-as} from 3962 and the same as the latter part of 3389; a parricide:--murderer of fathers. see GREEK for 3962 see GREEK for 3389

G3965.text: πατριά patriav patria {pat-ree-ah'} as if feminine of a derivative of 3962; paternal descent, i.e. (concretely) a group of families or a whole race (nation):--family, kindred, lineage. see GREEK for 3962

G3966.text: πατριάρχης patriavrchs patriarches {pat-ree-arkh'-ace} from 3965 and 757; a progenitor ("patriarch"):--patriarch. see GREEK for 3965 see GREEK for 757

G3967.text: πατρικός patrikovs patrikos {pat-ree-kos'} from 3962; paternal, i.e. ancestral:--of fathers. see GREEK for 3962

G3968.text: πατρίς patrivs patris {pat-rece'} from 3902; a father-land, i.e. native town; (figuratively) heavenly home:--(own) country. see GREEK for 3902

G3969.text: ∏ατροβᾶς Patroba's Patrobas {pat-rob'-as} perhaps a contraction for Patrobios (a compound of 3962 and 979); father's life; Patrobas, a Christian:--Patrobas. see GREEK for 3962 see GREEK for 979

G3970.text: πατροπαράδοτος patroparavdotos patroparadotos {pat-rop-ar-ad'-ot-os} from 3962 and a derivative of 3860 (in the sense of handing over or down); traditionary:--received by tradition from fathers. see GREEK for 3962 see GREEK for 3860

G3971.text: πατρῷος patrw'/os patroos {pat-ro'-os} from 3962; paternal, i.e. hereditary:--of fathers. see GREEK for 3962

G3972.text: ∏αῦλος Pau'los Paulos {pow'-los} of Latin origin; (little; but remotely from a derivative of 3973, meaning the same); Paulus, the name of a Roman and of an apostle:--Paul, Paulus. see GREEK for 3973

G3973.text: παύω pauvw pauo {pow'-o} a primary verb ("pause"); to stop (transitively or intransitively), i.e. restrain, quit, desist, come to an end:--cease, leave, refrain.

G3974.text: ∏άφος Pavfos Paphos {paf'-os} of uncertain derivation; Paphus, a place in Cyprus:--Paphos.

G3975.text: παχύνω pacuvnw pachuno {pakh-oo'-no} from a derivative of 4078 (meaning thick); to thicken, i.e. (by implication) to fatten (figuratively, stupefy or render callous):--wax gross. see GREEK for 4078

G3976.text: πέδη pevdh pede {ped'-ay} ultimately from 4228; a shackle for the feet:--fetter. see GREEK for 4228

G3977.text: πεδινός pedinovs pedinos {ped-ee-nos'} from a derivative of 4228 (meaning the ground); level (as easy for the feet):--plain. see GREEK for 4228

G3978.text: πεζεύω pezeuvw pezeuo {ped-zyoo'-o} from the same as 3979; to foot a journey, i.e. travel by land:--go afoot. see GREEK for 3979

G3979.text: πεζῇ pezh'/ peze {ped-zay'} dative case feminine of a derivative of 4228 (as adverb); foot-wise, i.e. by walking:--a- (on) foot. see GREEK for 4228

G3980.text: πειθαρχέω peiqarcevw peitharcheo {pi-tharkh-eh'-o} from a compound of 3982 and 757; to be persuaded by a ruler, i.e. (genitive case) to submit to authority; by analogy, to conform to advice:--hearken, obey (magistrates). see GREEK for 3982 see GREEK for 757

G3981.text: πειθός peiqovs peithos {pi-thos'} or peitho {pi-tho'} from 3982; persuasive:--enticing. see GREEK for 3982

G3982.text: πείθω peivqw peitho {pi'-tho} a primary verb; to convince (by argument, true or false); by analogy, to pacify or conciliate (by other fair means); reflexively or passively, to assent (to evidence or authority), to rely (by inward certainty):--agree, assure, believe, have confidence, be (wax) conflent, make friend, obey, persuade, trust, yield.

G3983.text: πεινάω peinavw peinao {pi-nah'-o} from the same as 3993 (through the idea of pinching toil; "pine"); to famish (absolutely or comparatively); figuratively, to crave:--be an hungered. see GREEK for 3993

G3984.text: πεῖρα pei'ra peira {pi'-rah} from the base of 4008 (through the idea of piercing); a test, i.e. attempt, experience:--assaying, trial. see GREEK for 4008

G3985.text: πειράζω peiravzw peirazo {pi-rad'-zo} from 3984; to test (objectively), i.e. endeavor, scrutinize, entice, discipline:--assay, examine, go about, prove, tempt(-er), try. see GREEK for 3984

G3986.text: πειρασμός peirasmovs peirasmos {pi-ras-mos'} from 3985; a putting to proof (by experiment (of good), experience (of evil), solicitation, discipline or provocation); by implication, adversity:--temptation, X try. see GREEK for 3985

G3987.text: πειράω peiravw peirao {pi-rah'-o} from 3984; to test (subjectively), i.e. (reflexively) to attempt:--assay. see GREEK for 3984

G3988.text: πεισμονή peismonhv peismone {pice-mon-ay'} from a presumed derivative of 3982; persuadableness, i.e. credulity:--persuasion. see GREEK for 3982

G3989.text: πέλαγος pevlagos pelagos {pel'-ag-os} of uncertain affinity; deep or open sea, i.e. the main:--depth, sea.

G3990.text: πελεκίζω pelekivzw pelekizo {pel-ek-id'-zo} from a derivative of 4141 (meaning an axe); to chop off (the head), i.e. truncate:--behead. see GREEK for 4141

G3991.text: πέμπτος pevmptos pemptos {pemp'-tos} from 4002; fifth:--fifth. see GREEK for 4002

G3992.text: πέμπω pevmpw pempo {pem'-po} apparently a primary verb; to dispatch (from the subjective view or point of departure, whereas hiemi (as a stronger form of eimi) refers rather to the objective point or terminus ad quem, and 4724 denotes properly, the orderly motion involved), especially on a temporary errand; also to transmit, bestow, or wield:--send, thrust in. see GREEK for 4724

G3993.text: πένης pevnhs penes {pen'-ace} from a primary peno (to toil for daily subsistence); starving, i.e. indigent:--poor. Compare 4434. see GREEK for 4434

G3994.text: πενθερά penqerav penthera {pen-ther-ah'} feminine of 3995; a wife's mother:--mother in law, wife's mother. see GREEK for 3995

G3995.text: πενθερός penqerovs pentheros {pen-ther-os'} of uncertain affinity; a wife's father:--father in law.

G3996.text: πενθέω penqevw pentheo {pen-theh'-o} from 3997; to grieve (the feeling or the act):--mourn, (be-)wail. see GREEK for 3997

G3997.text: πένθος pevnqos penthos {pen'-thos} strengthened from the alternate of 3958; grief:--mourning, sorrow. see GREEK for 3958

G3998.text: πενιχρός penicrovs penichros {pen-ikh-ros'} prolongation from the base of 3993; necessitous:--poor. see GREEK for 3993

G3999.text: πεντάκις pentavkis pentakis {pen-tak-ece'} multiplicative adverb from 4002; five times:--five times. see GREEK for 4002

G4000.text: πεντακισχίλιοι pentakiscivlioi pentakischilioi {pen-tak-is-khil'-ee-oy} from 3999 and 5507; five times a thousand:--five thousand. see GREEK for 3999 see GREEK for 5507

G4001.text: πεντακόσιοι pentakovsioi pentakosioi {pen-tak-os'-ee-oy} from 4002 and 1540; five hundred:--five hundred. see GREEK for 4002 see GREEK for 1540

G4002.text: πέντε pevnte pente {pen'-teh} a primary number; "five":--five.

G4003.text: πεντεκαιδέκατος pentekaidevkatos pentekaidekatos {pen-tek-ahee-ded'-at-os} from 4002 and 2532 and 1182; five and tenth:--fifteenth. see GREEK for 4002 see GREEK for 2532 see GREEK for 1182

G4004.text: πεντήκοντα penthvkonta pentekonta {pen-tay'-kon-tah} multiplicative of 4002; fifty:--fifty. see GREEK for 4002

G4005.text: πεντηκοστή penthkosthv pentekoste {pen-tay-kos-tay'} feminine of the ordinal of 4004; fiftieth (2250 being implied) from Passover, i.e. the festival of "Pentecost":--Pentecost. see GREEK for 4004 see GREEK for 2250

G4006.text: πεποίθησις pepoivqhsis pepoithesis {pep-oy'-thay-sis} from the perfect of the alternate of 3958; reliance:--confidence, trust. see GREEK for 3958

G4007.text: περαιτέρω peraitevrw per {per} from the base of 4008; an enclitic particle significant of abundance (thoroughness), i.e. emphasis; much, very or ever:--(whom-)soever. see GREEK for 4008

G4008.text: πέραν pevran peran {per'-an} apparently accusative case of an obsolete derivative of peiro (to "pierce"); through (as adverb or preposition), i.e. across:--beyond, farther (other) side, over.

G4009.text: πέρας pevras peras {per'-as} from the same as 4008; an extremity:--end, ut-(ter-)most participle see GREEK for 4008

G4010.text: ∏έργαμος Pevrgamos Pergamos {per'-gam-os} from 4444; fortified; Pergamus, a place in Asia Minor:--Pergamos. see GREEK for 4444

G4011.text: ∏έργη Pevrgh Perge {perg'-ay} probably from the same as 4010; a tower; Perga, a place in Asia Minor:--Perga. see GREEK for 4010

G4012.text: περί periv peri {per-ee'} from the base of 4008; properly, through (all over), i.e. around; figuratively with respect to; used in various applications, of place, cause or time (with the genitive case denoting the subject or occasion or superlative point; with the accusative case the locality, circuit, matter, circumstance or general period):--(there-)about, above, against, at, on behalf of, X and his company, which concern, (as) concerning, for, X how it will go with, ((there-, where-)) of, on, over, pertaining (to), for sake, X (e-)state, (as) touching, (where-)by (in), with. In comparative, it retains substantially the same meaning of circuit (around), excess (beyond), or completeness (through). see GREEK for 4008

G4013.text: περιάγω periavgw periago {per-ee-ag'-o} from 4012 and 71; to take around (as a companion); reflexively, to walk around:--compass, go (round) about, lead about. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 71

G4014.text: περιαιρέω periairevw periaireo {per-ee-ahee-reh'-o} from 4012 and 138 (including its alternate); to remove all around, i.e. unveil, cast off (anchor); figuratively, to expiate:--take away (up). see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 138

G4015.text: περιαστράπτω periastravptw periastrapto {per-ee-as-trap'-to} from 4012 and 797; to flash all around, i.e. envelop in light:--shine round (about). see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 797

G4016.text: περιβάλλω peribavllw periballo {per-ee-bal'-lo} from 4012 and 906; to throw all around, i.e. invest (with a palisade or with clothing):--array, cast about, clothe(-d me), put on. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 906

G4017.text: περιβλέπω periblevpw periblepo {per-ee-blep'-o} from 4012 and 991; to look all around:--look (round) about (on). see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 991

G4018.text: περιβόλαιον peribovlaion peribolaion {per-ib-ol'-ah-yon} neuter of a presumed derivative of 4016; something thrown around one, i.e. a mantle, veil:--covering, vesture. see GREEK for 4016

G4019.text: περιδέω peridevw perideo {per-ee-deh'-o} 4012 and 1210; to bind around one, i.e. enwrap:--bind about. see GREEK for 1210 see GREEK for 4012

G4020.text: περιεργάζομαι periergavzomai periergazomai {per-ee-er-gad'-zom-ahee} from 4012 and 2038; to work all around, i.e. bustle about (meddle):--be a busybody. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2038

G4021.text: περίεργος perivergos periergos {per-ee'-er-gos} from 4012 and 2041; working all around, i.e. officious (meddlesome, neuter plural magic):--busybody, curious arts. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2041

G4022.text: περιέρχομαι perievrcomai perierchomai {per-ee-er'-khom-ahee} from 4012 and 2064 (including its alternate); to come all around, i.e. stroll, vacillate, veer:--fetch a compass, vagabond, wandering about. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2064

G4023.text: περιέχω perievcw periecho {per-ee-ekh'-o} from 4012 and 2192; to hold all around, i.e. include, clasp (figuratively):--+ astonished, contain, after (this manner). see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2192

G4024.text: περιζώννυμι perizwvnnumi perizonnumi {per-id-zone'-noo-mee} from 4012 and 2224; to gird all around, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to fasten on one's belt (literally or figuratively):--gird (about, self). see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2224

G4025.text: περίθεσις perivqesis perithesis {per-ith'-es-is} from 4060; a putting all around, i.e. decorating oneself with:--wearing. see GREEK for 4060

G4026.text: περιΐστημι perii?sthmi periistemi {per-ee-is'-tay-mee} from 4012 and 2476; to stand all around, i.e. (near) to be a bystander, or (aloof) to keep away from:--avoid, shun, stand by (round about). see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2476

G4027.text: περικάθαρμα perikavqarma perikatharma {per-ee-kath'-ar-mah} from a compound of 4012 and 2508; something cleaned off all around, i.e. refuse (figuratively):--filth. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2508

G4028.text: περικαλύπτω perikaluvptw perikalupto {per-ee-kal-oop'-to} from 4012 and 2572; to cover all around, i.e. entirely (the face, a surface):--blindfold, cover, overlay. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2572

G4029.text: περίκειμαι perivkeimai perikeimai {per-ik'-i-mahee} from 4012 and 2749; to lie all around, i.e. inclose, encircle, hamper (literally or figuratively):--be bound (compassed) with, hang about. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2749

G4030.text: περικεφαλαία perikefalaiva perikephalaia {per-ee-kef-al-ah'-yah} feminine of a compound of 4012 and 2776; encirclement of the head, i.e. a helmet:--helmet. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2776

G4031.text: περικρατής perikrathvs perikrates {per-ee-krat-ace'} from 4012 and 2904; strong all around, i.e. a master (manager):--+ come by. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2904

G4032.text: περικρύβω perikruvbw perikrupto {per-ee-kroop'-to} from 4012 and 2928; to conceal all around, i.e. entirely:--hide. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2928

G4033.text: περικυκλόω perikuklovw perikukloo {per-ee-koo-klo'-o} from 4012 and 2944; to encircle all around, i.e. blockade completely:--compass round. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2944

G4034.text: περιλάμπω perilavmpw perilampo {per-ee-lam'-po} from 4012 and 2989; to illuminate all around, i.e. invest with a halo:--shine round about. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 2989

G4035.text: περιλείπομαι perileivpomai perileipo {per-ee-li'-po} from 4012 and 3007; to leave all around, i.e. (passively) survive:--remain. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 3007

G4036.text: περίλυπος perivlupos perilupos {per-il'-oo-pos} from 4012 and 3077; grieved all around, i.e. intensely sad:--exceeding (very) sorry(-owful). see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 3077

G4037.text: περιμένω perimevnw perimeno {per-ee-men'-o} from 4012 and 3306; to stay around, i.e. await:--wait for. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 3306

G4038.text: πέριξ pevrix perix {per'-ix} adverb from 4012; all around, i.e. (as an adjective) circumjacent:--round about. see GREEK for 4012

G4039.text: περιοικέω perioikevw perioikeo {per-ee-oy-keh'-o} from 4012 and 3611; to reside around, i.e. be a neighbor:--dwell round about. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 3611

G4040.text: περίοικος perivoikos perioikos {per-ee'-oy-kos} from 4012 and 3624; housed around, i.e. neighboring (used elliptically as a noun):--neighbour. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 3624

G4041.text: περιούσιος periouvsios periousios {per-ee-oo'-see-os} from the present participle feminine of a compound of 4012 and 1510; being beyond usual, i.e. special (one's own):--peculiar. see GREEK for 1510

G4042.text: περιοχή periochv perioche {per-ee-okh-ay'} from 4023; a being held around, i.e. (concretely) a passage (of Scripture, as circumscribed):--place. see GREEK for 4023

G4043.text: περιπατέω peripatevw peripateo {per-ee-pat-eh'-o} from 4012 and 3961; to tread all around, i.e. walk at large (especially as proof of ability); figuratively, to live, deport oneself, follow (as a companion or votary):--go, be occupied with, walk (about). see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 3961

G4044.text: περιπείρω peripeivrw peripeiro {per-ee-pi'-ro} from 4012 and the base of 4008; to penetrate entirely, i.e. transfix (figuratively):--pierce through. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 4008

G4045.text: περιπίπτω peripivptw peripipto {per-ee-pip'-to} from 4012 and 4098; to fall into something that is all around, i.e. light among or upon, be surrounded with:--fall among (into). see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 4098

G4046.text: περιποιέω peripoievw peripoieomai {per-ee-poy-eh'-om-ahee} middle voice from 4012 and 4160; to make around oneself, i.e. acquire (buy):--purchase. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 4160

G4047.text: περιποίησις peripoivhsis peripoiesis {per-ee-poy'-ay-sis} from 4046; acquisition (the act or the thing); by extension, preservation:--obtain(-ing), peculiar, purchased, possession, saving. see GREEK for 4046

G4048.text: περιρήγνυμι perirhvgnumi perirrhegnumi {per-ir-hrayg'-noo-mee} from 4012 and 4486; to tear all around, i.e. completely away:--rend off. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 4486

G4049.text: περισπάω perispavw perispao {per-ee-spah'-o} from 4012 and 4685; to drag all around, i.e. (figuratively) to distract (with care):--cumber. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 4685

G4050.text: περισσεία perisseiva perisseia {per-is-si'-ah} from 4052; surplusage, i.e. superabundance:--abundance(-ant, (-ly)), superfluity. see GREEK for 4052

G4051.text: περίσσευμα perivsseuma perisseuma {per-is'-syoo-mah} from 4052; a surplus, or superabundance:--abundance, that was left, over and above. see GREEK for 4052

G4052.text: περισσεύω perisseuvw perisseuo {per-is-syoo'-o} from 4053; to superabound (in quantity or quality), be in excess, be superfluous; also (transitively) to cause to superabound or excel:--(make, more) abound, (have, have more) abundance (be more) abundant, be the better, enough and to spare, exceed, excel, increase, be left, redound, remain (over and above). see GREEK for 4053

G4053.text: περισσός perissovs perissos {per-is-sos'} from 4012 (in the sense of beyond); superabundant (in quantity) or superior (in quality); by implication, excessive; adverbially (with 1537) violently; neuter (as noun) preeminence:--exceeding abundantly above, more abundantly, advantage, exceedingly, very highly, beyond measure, more, superfluous, vehement(-ly). see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 1537

G4054.text: περισσότερος perissovteros perissoteron {per-is-sot'-er-on} neuter of 4055 (as adverb); in a more superabundant way:--more abundantly, a great deal, far more. see GREEK for 4055

G4055.text: περισσότερος perissovteros perissoteros {per-is-sot'-er-os} comparative of 4053; more superabundant (in number, degree or character):--more abundant, greater (much) more, overmuch. see GREEK for 4053

G4056.text: περισσοτέρως perissotevrws perissoteros {per-is-sot-er'-oce} adverb from 4055; more superabundantly:--more abundant(-ly), X the more earnest, (more) exceedingly, more frequent, much more, the rather. see GREEK for 4055

G4057.text: περισσῶς perissw's perissos {per-is-soce'} adverb from 4053; superabundantly:--exceedingly, out of measure, the more. see GREEK for 4053

G4058.text: περιστερά peristerav peristera {per-is-ter-ah'} of uncertain derivation; a pigeon:--dove, pigeon.

G4059.text: περιτέμνω peritevmnw peritemno {per-ee-tem'-no} from 4012 and the base of 5114; to cut around, i.e. (specially) to circumcise:--circumcise. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 5114

G4060.text: περιτίθημι peritivqhmi peritithemi {per-ee-tith'-ay-mee} from 4012 and 5087; to place around; by implication, to present:--bestow upon, hedge round about, put about (on, upon), set about. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 5087

G4061.text: περιτομή peritomhv peritome {per-it-om-ay'} from 4059; circumcision (the rite, the condition or the people, literally or figuratively):--X circumcised, circumcision. see GREEK for 4059

G4062.text: περιτρέπω peritrevpw peritrepo {per-ee-trep'-o} from 4012 and the base of 5157; to turn around, i.e. (mentally) to craze:--+ make mad. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 5157

G4063.text: περιτρέχω peritrevcw peritrecho {per-ee-trekh'-o} from 4012 and 5143 (including its alternate); to run around, i.e. traverse:--run through. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 5143

G4064.text: περιφέρω perifevrw periphero {per-ee-fer'-o} from 4012 and 5342; to convey around, i.e. transport hither and thither:--bear (carry) about. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 5342

G4065.text: περιφρονέω perifronevw periphroneo {per-ee-fron-eh'-o} from 4012 and 5426; to think beyond, i.e. depreciate (contemn):--despise. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 5426

G4066.text: περίχωρος perivcwros perichoros {per-ikh'-o-ros} from 4012 and 5561; around the region, i.e. circumjacent (as noun, with 1093 implied vicinity):--country (round) about, region (that lieth) round about. see GREEK for 4012 see GREEK for 5561 see GREEK for 1093

G4067.text: περίψημα perivyhma peripsema {per-ip'-say-mah} from a comparative of 4012 and psao (to rub); something brushed all around, i.e. off-scrapings (figuratively, scum):--offscouring. see GREEK for 4012

G4068.text: περπερεύομαι perpereuvomai perpereuomai {per-per-yoo'-om-ahee} middle voice from perperos (braggart; perhaps by reduplication of the base of 4008); to boast:--vaunt itself. see GREEK for 4008

G4069.text: ∏ερσίς Persivs Persis {per-sece'} a Persian woman; Persis, a Christian female:--Persis.

G4070.text: πέρυσι pevrusi perusi {per'-oo-si} adverb from 4009; the by-gone, i.e. (as noun) last year:--+ a year ago. see GREEK for 4009

G4071.text: πετεινόν peteinovn peteinon {pet-i-non'} neuter of a derivative of 4072; a flying animal, i.e. bird:--bird, fowl. see GREEK for 4072

G4072.text: πέτομαι pevtomai petomai {pet'-om-ahee} or 扩展型 petaomai {pet-ah'-om-ahee} petaomai pet-ah'-om-ahee, or contracted ptaomai ptah'-om-ahee middle voice of a primary verb; to fly:--fly(-ing).

G4073.text: πέτρα pevtra petra {pet'-ra} feminine of the same as 4074; a (mass of) rock (literally or figuratively):--rock. see GREEK for 4074

G4074.text: ∏έτρος Pevtros Petros {pet'-ros} apparently a primary word; a (piece of) rock (larger than 3037); as a name, Petrus, an apostle:--Peter, rock. Compare 2786. see GREEK for 3037 see GREEK for 2786

G4075.text: πετρῶδες petrw'des petrodes {pet-ro'-dace} from 4073 and 1491; rock-like, i.e. rocky:--stony. see GREEK for 4073 see GREEK for 1491

G4076.text: πήγανον phvganon peganon {pay'-gan-on} from 4078; rue (from its thick or fleshy leaves):--rue. see GREEK for 4078

G4077.text: πηγή phghv pege {pay-gay'} probably from 4078 (through the idea of gushing plumply); a fount (literally or figuratively), i.e. source or supply (of water, blood, enjoyment) (not necessarily the original spring):--fountain, well. see GREEK for 4078

G4078.text: πήγνυμι phvgnumi pegnumi {payg'-noo-mee} a prolonged form of a primary verb (which in its simpler form occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to fix ("peg"), i.e. (specially) to set up (a tent):--pitch.

G4079.text: πηδάλιον phdavlion pedalion {pay-dal'-ee-on} neuter of a (presumed) derivative of pedon (the blade of an oar; from the same as 3976); a "pedal", i.e. helm:--rudder. see GREEK for 3976

G4080.text: πηλίκος phlivkos pelikos {pay-lee'-kos} a quantitative form (the feminine) of the base of 4225; how much (as an indefinite), i.e. in size or (figuratively) dignity:--how great (large). see GREEK for 4225

G4081.text: πηλός phlovs pelos {pay-los'} perhaps a primary word; clay:--clay.

G4082.text: πήρα phvra pera {pay'-rah} of uncertain affinity; a wallet or leather pouch for food:--scrip.

G4083.text: πῆχυς ph'cus pechus {pay'-khoos} of uncertain affinity; the fore-arm, i.e. (as a measure) a cubit:--cubit.

G4084.text: πιάζω piavzw piazo {pee-ad'-zo} probably another form of 971; to squeeze, i.e. seize (gently by the hand (press), or officially (arrest), or in hunting (capture)):--apprehend, catch, lay hand on, take. Compare 4085. see GREEK for 971 see GREEK for 4085

G4085.text: πιέζω pievzw piezo {pee-ed'-zo} another form for 4084; to pack:--press down. see GREEK for 4084

G4086.text: πιθανολογία piqanologiva pithanologia {pith-an-ol-og-ee'-ah} from a compound of a derivative of 3982 and 3056; persuasive language:--enticing words. see GREEK for 3982 see GREEK for 3056

G4087.text: πικραίνω pikraivnw pikraino {pik-rah'-ee-no} from 4089; to embitter (literally or figuratively):--be (make) bitter. see GREEK for 4089

G4088.text: πικρία pikriva pikria {pik-ree'-ah} from 4089; acridity (especially poison), literally or figuratively:--bitterness. see GREEK for 4089

G4089.text: πικρός pikrovs pikros {pik-ros'} perhaps from 4078 (through the idea of piercing); sharp (pungent), i.e. acrid (literally or figuratively):--bitter. see GREEK for 4078

G4090.text: πικρῶς pikrw's pikros {pik-roce'} adverb from 4089; bitterly, i.e. (figuratively) violently:--bitterly. see GREEK for 4089

G4091.text: ∏ιλᾶτος Pila'tos Pilatos {pil-at'-os} of Latin origin; close-pressed, i.e. firm; Pilatus, a Roman:--Pilate.

G4092.text: πίμπρημι pivmprhmi pimpremi {pim'-pray-mee} primary preo preh'-o which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to fire, i.e. burn (figuratively and passively, become inflamed with fever):--be (X should have) swollen.

G4093.text: πινακίδιον pinakivdion pinakidion {pin-ak-id'-ee-on} diminutive of 4094; a tablet (for writing on):--writing table. see GREEK for 4094

G4094.text: πίναξ pivnax pinax {pin'-ax} apparently a form of 4109; a plate:--charger, platter. see GREEK for 4109

G4095.text: πίνω pivnw pino {pee'-no} pio pee'-o, which (together with another form) poo po'-o occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses; to imbibe (literally or figuratively):--drink.

G4096.text: πιότης piovths piotes {pee-ot'-ace} from pion (fat; perhaps akin to the alternate of 4095 through the idea of repletion); plumpness, i.e. (by implication) richness (oiliness):--fatness. see GREEK for 4095

G4097.text: πιπράσκω pipravskw piprasko {pip-ras'-ko} prao prah'-o; (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses) contracted from perao (to traverse; from the base of 4008); to traffic (by travelling), i.e. dispose of as merchandise or into slavery (literally or figuratively):--sell. see GREEK for 4008

G4098.text: πίπτω pivptw pipto {pip'-to} peto pet'-o; (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); probably akin to 4072 through the idea of alighting; to fall (literally or figuratively):--fail, fall (down), light on. see GREEK for 4072

G4099.text: ∏ισιδίος ∏ισιδία Pisidivos Pisidiva Pisidia {pis-id-ee'-ah} probably of foreign origin; Pisidia, a region of Asia Minor:--Pisidia.

G4100.text: πιστεύω pisteuvw pisteuo {pist-yoo'-o} from 4102; to have faith (in, upon, or with respect to, a person or thing), i.e. credit; by implication, to entrust (especially one's spiritual well-being to Christ):--believe(-r), commit (to trust), put in trust with. see GREEK for 4102

G4101.text: πιστικός pistikovs pistikos {pis-tik-os'} from 4102; trustworthy, i.e. genuine (unadulterated):--spike-(nard). see GREEK for 4102

G4102.text: πίστις pivstis pistis {pis'-tis} from 3982; persuasion, i.e. credence; moral conviction (of religious truth, or the truthfulness of God or a religious teacher), especially reliance upon Christ for salvation; abstractly, constancy in such profession; by extension, the system of religious (Gospel) truth itself:--assurance, belief, believe, faith, fidelity. see GREEK for 3982

G4103.text: πιστός pistovs pistos {pis-tos'} from 3982; objectively, trustworthy; subjectively, trustful:--believe(-ing, -r), faithful(-ly), sure, true. see GREEK for 3982

G4104.text: πιστόομαι pistovomai pistoo {pis-to'-o} from 4103; to assure:--assure of. see GREEK for 4103

G4105.text: πλανάω planavw planao {plan-ah'-o} from 4106; to (properly, cause to) roam (from safety, truth, or virtue):--go astray, deceive, err, seduce, wander, be out of the way. see GREEK for 4106

G4106.text: πλάνη plavnh plane {plan'-ay} feminine of 4108 (as abstractly); objectively, fraudulence; subjectively, a straying from orthodoxy or piety:--deceit, to deceive, delusion, error. see GREEK for 4108

G4107.text: πλανήτης planhvths planetes {plan-ay'-tace} 或 planes {plan'-ace} from 4108; a rover ("planet"), i.e. (figuratively) an erratic teacher:--wandering. see GREEK for 4108

G4108.text: πλάνος plavnos planos {plan'-os} of uncertain affinity; roving (as a tramp), i.e. (by implication) an impostor or misleader; --deceiver, seducing.

G4109.text: πλάξ plavx plax {plax} from 4111; a moulding-board, i.e. flat surface ("plate", or tablet, literally or figuratively):--table. see GREEK for 4111

G4110.text: πλάσμα plavsma plasma {plas'-mah} from 4111; something moulded:--thing formed. see GREEK for 4111

G4111.text: πλάσσω plavssw plasso {plas'-so} a primary verb; to mould, i.e. shape or fabricate:--form.

G4112.text: πλαστός plastovs plastos {plas-tos'} from 4111; moulded, i.e. (by implication) artificial or (figuratively) fictitious (false):--feigned. see GREEK for 4111

G4113.text: πλατεία plateiva plateia {plat-i'-ah} feminine of 4116; a wide "plat" or "place", i.e. open square:--street. see GREEK for 4116

G4114.text: πλάτος plavtos platos {plat'-os} from 4116; width:--breadth. see GREEK for 4116

G4115.text: πλατύνω platuvnw platuno {plat-oo'-no} from 4116; to widen (literally or figuratively):--make broad, enlarge. see GREEK for 4116

G4116.text: πλατύς platuvs platus {plat-oos'} from 4111; spread out "flat" ("plot"), i.e. broad:--wide. see GREEK for 4111

G4117.text: πλέγμα plevgma plegma {pleg'-mah} from 4120; a plait (of hair):--broidered hair. see GREEK for 4120

G4119.text: πολύς poluvs pleion {pli-own} 中性 pleion {pli'-on} 或 pleon {pleh'-on} pleion pli'-on, or pleon pleh'-on comparative of 4183; more in quantity, number, or quality; also (in plural) the major portion:--X above, + exceed, more excellent, further, (very) great(-er), long(-er), (very) many, greater (more) part, + yet but. see GREEK for 4183

G4120.text: πλέκω plevkw pleko {plek'-o} a primary word; to twine or braid:--plait.

G4121.text: πλεονάζω pleonavzw pleonazo {pleh-on-ad'-zo} from 4119; to do, make or be more, i.e. increase (transitively or intransitively); by extension, to superabound:--abound, abundant, make to increase, have over. see GREEK for 4119

G4122.text: πλεονεκτέω pleonektevw pleonekteo {pleh-on-cek-teh'-o} from 4123; to be covetous, i.e. (by implication) to over-reach:--get an advantage, defraud, make a gain. see GREEK for 4123

G4123.text: πλεονέκτης pleonevkths pleonektes {pleh-on-ek'-tace} from 4119 and 2192; holding (desiring) more, i.e. eager for gain (avaricious, hence a defrauder):--covetous. see GREEK for 4119 see GREEK for 2192

G4124.text: πλεονεξία pleonexiva pleonexia {pleh-on-ex-ee'-ah} from 4123; avarice, i.e. (by implication) fraudulency, extortion:--covetous(-ness) practices, greediness. see GREEK for 4123

G4125.text: πλευρά pleurav pleura {plyoo-rah'} of uncertain affinity; a rib, i.e. (by extension) side:--side.

G4126.text: πλέω plevw pleo {pleh'-o} pleuo plyoo'-o; which is used as an alternate in certain tenses; probably a form of 4150 (through the idea of plunging through the water); to pass in a vessel:--sail. See also 4130. see GREEK for 4150 see GREEK for 4130

G4127.text: πληγή plhghv plege {play-gay'} from 4141; a stroke; by implication, a wound; figuratively, a calamity:--plague, stripe, wound(-ed). see GREEK for 4141

G4128.text: πλῆθος plh'qos plethos {play'-thos} from 4130; a fulness, i.e. a large number, throng, populace:--bundle, company, multitude. see GREEK for 4130

G4129.text: πληθύνω plhquvnw plethuno {play-thoo'-no} from another form of 4128; to increase (transitively or intransitively):--abound, multiply. see GREEK for 4128

G4130.text: πίμπλημι pivmplhmi pletho {play'-tho} pleo pleh'-o (which appears only as an alternate in certain tenses and in the reduplicated form pimplemi) to "fill" (literally or figuratively (imbue, influence, supply)); specially, to fulfil (time):--accomplish, full (...come), furnish.

G4131.text: πλήκτης plhvkths plektes {plake'-tace} from 4141; a smiter, i.e. pugnacious (quarrelsome):--striker. see GREEK for 4141

G4132.text: πλήμμυρα plhvmmura plemmura {plame-moo'-rah} prolonged from 4130; flood-tide, i.e. (by analogy) a freshet:--flood. see GREEK for 4130

G4133.text: πλήν plhvn plen {plane} from 4119; moreover (besides), i.e. albeit, save that, rather, yet:--but (rather), except, nevertheless, notwithstanding, save, than. see GREEK for 4119

G4134.text: πλήρης plhvrhs pleres {play'-race} from 4130; replete, or covered over; by analogy, complete:--full. see GREEK for 4130

G4135.text: πληροφορέω plhroforevw plerophoreo {play-rof-or-eh'-o} from 4134 and 5409; to carry out fully (in evidence), i.e. completely assure (or convince), entirely accomplish:--most surely believe, fully know (persuade), make full proof of. see GREEK for 4134 see GREEK for 5409

G4136.text: πληροφορία plhroforiva plerophoria {play-rof-or-ee'-ah} from 4135; entire confidence:--(full) assurance. see GREEK for 4135

G4137.text: πληρόω plhrovw pleroo {play-ro'-o} from 4134; to make replete, i.e. (literally) to cram (a net), level up (a hollow), or (figuratively) to furnish (or imbue, diffuse, influence), satisfy, execute (an office), finish (a period or task), verify (or coincide with a prediction), etc.:--accomplish, X after, (be) complete, end, expire, fill (up), fulfil, (be, make) full (come), fully preach, perfect, supply. see GREEK for 4134

G4138.text: πλήρωμα plhvrwma pleroma {play'-ro-mah} from 4137; repletion or completion, i.e. (subjectively) what fills (as contents, supplement, copiousness, multitude), or (objectively) what is filled (as container, performance, period):--which is put in to fill up, piece that filled up, fulfilling, full, fulness. see GREEK for 4137

G4139.text: πλησίον plhsivon plesion {play-see'-on} neuter of a derivative of pelas (near); (adverbially) close by; as noun, a neighbor, i.e. fellow (as man, countryman, Christian or friend):--near, neighbour.

G4140.text: πλησμονή plhsmonhv plesmone {place-mon-ay'} from a presumed derivative of 4130; a filling up, i.e. (figuratively) gratification:--satisfying. see GREEK for 4130

G4141.text: πλήσσω plhvssw plesso {place'-so} apparently another form of 4111 (through the idea of flattening out); to pound, i.e. (figuratively) to inflict with (calamity):--smite. Compare 5180. see GREEK for 5180 see GREEK for 4111

G4142.text: πλοιάριον ploiavrion ploiarion {ploy-ar'-ee-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of 4143; a boat:--boat, little (small) ship. see GREEK for 4143

G4143.text: πλοῖον ploi'on ploion {ploy'-on} from 4126; a sailer, i.e. vessel:--ship(-ing). see GREEK for 4126

G4144.text: πλοῦς plou's ploos {plo'-os} from 4126; a sail, i.e. navigation:--course, sailing, voyage. see GREEK for 4126

G4145.text: πλούσιος plouvsios plousios {ploo'-see-os} from 4149; wealthy; figuratively, abounding with:--rich. see GREEK for 4149

G4146.text: πλουσίως plousivws plousios {ploo-see'-oce} adverb from 4145; copiously:--abundantly, richly. see GREEK for 4145

G4147.text: πλουτέω ploutevw plouteo {ploo-teh'-o} from 4148; to be (or become) wealthy (literally or figuratively):--be increased with goods, (be made, wax) rich. see GREEK for 4148

G4148.text: πλουτίζω ploutivzw ploutizo {ploo-tid'-zo} from 4149; to make wealthy (figuratively):--en- (make) rich. see GREEK for 4149

G4149.text: πλοῦτος plou'tos ploutos {ploo'-tos} from the base of 4130; wealth (as fulness), i.e. (literally) money, possessions, or (figuratively) abundance, richness, (specially), valuable bestowment:--riches. see GREEK for 4130

G4150.text: πλύνω pluvnw pluno {ploo'-no} a prolonged form of an obsolete pluo (to "flow"); to "plunge", i.e. launder clothing:--wash. Compare 3068, 3538. see GREEK for 3068 see GREEK for 3538

G4151.text: πνεῦμα pneu'ma pneuma {pnyoo'-mah} from 4154; a current of air, i.e. breath (blast) or a breeze; by analogy or figuratively, a spirit, i.e. (human) the rational soul, (by implication) vital principle, mental disposition, etc., or (superhuman) an angel, demon, or (divine) God, Christ's spirit, the Holy Spirit:--ghost, life, spirit(-ual, -ually), mind. Compare 5590. see GREEK for 4154 see GREEK for 5590

G4152.text: πνευματικός pneumatikovs pneumatikos {pnyoo-mat-ik-os'} from 4151; non-carnal, i.e. (humanly) ethereal (as opposed to gross), or (daemoniacally) a spirit (concretely), or (divinely) supernatural, regenerate, religious:--spiritual. Compare 5591. see GREEK for 4151 see GREEK for 5591

G4153.text: πνευματικῶς pneumatikw's pneumatikos {pnyoo-mat-ik-oce'} adverb from 4152; non-physically, i.e. divinely, figuratively:--spiritually. see GREEK for 4152

G4154.text: πνέω pnevw pneo {pneh'-o} a primary word; to breathe hard, i.e. breeze:--blow. Compare 5594. see GREEK for 5594

G4155.text: πνίγω pnivgw pnigo {pnee'-go} strengthened from 4154; to wheeze, i.e. (causative, by implication) to throttle or strangle (drown):--choke, take by the throat. see GREEK for 4154

G4156.text: πνικτός pniktovs pniktos {pnik-tos'} from 4155; throttled, i.e. (neuter concretely) an animal choked to death (not bled):--strangled. see GREEK for 4155

G4157.text: πνοή pnohv pnoe {pno-ay'} from 4154; respiration, a breeze:--breath, wind. see GREEK for 4154

G4158.text: ποδήρης podhvrhs poderes {pod-ay'-race} from 4228 and another element of uncertain affinity; a dress (2066 implied) reaching the ankles:--garment down to the foot. see GREEK for 4228 see GREEK for 2066

G4159.text: πόθεν povqen pothen {poth'-en} from the base of 4213 with enclitic adverb of origin; from which (as interrogative) or what (as relative) place, state, source or cause:--whence. see GREEK for 4213

G4160.text: ποιέω poievw poieo {poy-eh'-o} apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary; to make or do (in a very wide application, more or less direct):--abide, + agree, appoint, X avenge, + band together, be, bear, + bewray, bring (forth), cast out, cause, commit, + content, continue, deal, + without any delay, (would) do(-ing), execute, exercise, fulfil, gain, give, have, hold, X journeying, keep, + lay wait, + lighten the ship, make, X mean, + none of these things move me, observe, ordain, perform, provide, + have purged, purpose, put, + raising up, X secure, shew, X shoot out, spend, take, tarry, + transgress the law, work, yield. Compare 4238. see GREEK for 4238

G4161.text: ποίημα poivhma poiema {poy'-ay-mah} from 4160; a product, i.e. fabric (literally or figuratively):--thing that is made, workmanship. see GREEK for 4160

G4162.text: ποίησις poivhsis poiesis {poy'-ay-sis} from 4160; action, i.e. performance (of the law):--deed. see GREEK for 4160

G4163.text: ποιητής poihthvs poietes {poy-ay-tace'} from 4160; a performer; specially, a "poet"; --doer, poet. see GREEK for 4160

G4164.text: ποικίλος poikivlos poikilos {poy-kee'-los} of uncertain derivation; motley, i.e. various in character:--divers, manifold.

G4165.text: ποιμαίνω poimaivnw poimaino {poy-mah'-ee-no} from 4166; to tend as a shepherd of (figuratively, superviser):--feed (cattle), rule. see GREEK for 4166

G4166.text: ποιμήν poimhvn poimen {poy-mane'} of uncertain affinity; a shepherd (literally or figuratively):--shepherd, pastor.

G4167.text: ποίμνη poivmnh poimne {poym'-nay} contraction from 4165; a flock (literally or figuratively):--flock, fold. see GREEK for 4165

G4168.text: ποίμνιον poivmnion poimnion {poym'-nee-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of 4167; a flock, i.e. (figuratively) group (of believers):--flock. see GREEK for 4167

G4169.text: ποῖος poi'os poios {poy'-os} from the base of 4226 and 3634; individualizing interrogative (of character) what sort of, or (of number) which one:--what (manner of), which. see GREEK for 4226 see GREEK for 3634

G4170.text: πολεμέω polemevw polemeo {pol-em-eh'-o} from 4171; to be (engaged) in warfare, i.e. to battle (literally or figuratively): -fight, (make) war. see GREEK for 4171

G4171.text: πόλεμος povlemos polemos {pol'-em-os} from pelomai (to bustle); warfare (literally or figuratively; a single encounter or a series):--battle, fight, war.

G4172.text: πόλις povlis polis {pol'-is} probably from the same as 4171, or perhaps from 4183; a town (properly, with walls, of greater or less size):--city. see GREEK for 4183 see GREEK for 4171

G4173.text: πολιτάρχης politavrchs politarches {pol-it-ar'-khace} from 4172 and 757; a town-officer, i.e. magistrate:--ruler of the city. see GREEK for 4172 see GREEK for 757

G4174.text: πολιτεία politeiva politeia {pol-ee-ti'-ah} from 4177 ("polity"); citizenship; concretely, a community:--commonwealth, freedom. see GREEK for 4177

G4175.text: πολίτευμα polivteuma politeuma {pol-it'-yoo-mah} from 4176; a community, i.e. (abstractly) citizenship (figuratively):--conversation. see GREEK for 4176

G4176.text: πολιτεύομαι politeuvomai politeuomai {pol-it-yoo'-om-ahee} middle voice of a derivative of 4177; to behave as a citizen (figuratively):--let conversation be, live. see GREEK for 4177

G4177.text: πολίτης polivths polites {pol-ee'-tace} from 4172; a townsman:--citizen. see GREEK for 4172

G4178.text: πολλάκις pollavkis pollakis {pol-lak'-is} multiplicative adverb from 4183; many times, i.e. frequently:--oft(-en, -entimes, -times). see GREEK for 4183

G4179.text: πολλαπλασίων pollaplasivwn pollaplasion {pol-lap-las-ee'-ohn} from 4183 and probably a derivative of 4120; manifold, i.e. (neuter as noun) very much more:--manifold more. see GREEK for 4183 see GREEK for 4120

G4181.text: πολυμερῶς polumerw's polumeros {pol-oo-mer'-oce} adverb from a compound of 4183 and 3313; in many portions, i.e. variously as to time and agency (piecemeal):--at sundry times. see GREEK for 4183 see GREEK for 3313

G4182.text: πολυποίκιλος polupoivkilos polupoikilos {pol-oo-poy'-kil-os} from 4183 and 4164; much variegated, i.e. multifarious:--manifold. see GREEK for 4183 see GREEK for 4164

G4184.text: πολύσπλαγχνος poluvsplagcnos polusplagchnos {pol-oo'-splankh-nos} from 4183 and 4698 (figuratively); extremely compassionate:--very pitiful. see GREEK for 4183 see GREEK for 4698

G4185.text: πολυτελής polutelhvs poluteles {pol-oo-tel-ace'} from 4183 and 5056; extremely expensive:--costly, very precious, of great price. see GREEK for 4183 see GREEK for 5056

G4186.text: πολύτιμος poluvtimos polutimos {pol-oot'-ee-mos} from 4183 and 5092; extremely valuable:--very costly, of great price. see GREEK for 4183 see GREEK for 5092

G4187.text: πολυτρόπως polutrovpws polutropos {pol-oot-rop'-oce} adverb from a compound of 4183 and 5158; in many ways, i.e. variously as to method or form:--in divers manners. see GREEK for 4183 see GREEK for 5158

G4188.text: πόμα povma poma {pom'-ah} from the alternate of 4095; a beverage:--drink. see GREEK for 4095

G4189.text: πονηρία ponhriva poneria {pon-ay-ree'-ah} from 4190; depravity, i.e. (specially), malice; plural (concretely) plots, sins:--iniquity, wickedness. see GREEK for 4190

G4190.text: πονηρός ponhrovs poneros {pon-ay-ros'} from a derivative of 4192; hurtful, i.e. evil (properly, in effect or influence, and thus differing from 2556, which refers rather to essential character, as well as from 4550, which indicates degeneracy from original virtue); figuratively, calamitous; also (passively) ill, i.e. diseased; but especially (morally) culpable, i.e. derelict, vicious, facinorous; neuter (singular) mischief, malice, or (plural) guilt; masculine (singular) the devil, or (plural) sinners:--bad, evil, grievous, harm, lewd, malicious, wicked(-ness). See also 4191. see GREEK for 4192 see GREEK for 2556 see GREEK for 4550 see GREEK for 4191

G4191.text: πονηρός ponhrovs comparative of 4190; more evil:--more wicked. see GREEK for 4190

G4193.text: ∏οντικός Pontikovs Pontikos {pon-tik-os'} from 4195; a Pontican, i.e. native of Pontus:--born in Pontus. see GREEK for 4195

G4194.text: ∏όντιος Povntios Pontios {pon'-tee-os} of Latin origin; apparently bridged; Pontius, a Roman:--Pontius.

G4195.text: ∏όντος Povntos Pontos {pon'-tos} a sea; Pontus, a region of Asia Minor:--Pontus.

G4196.text: ∏όπλιος Povplios Poplios {pop'-lee-os} of Latin origin; apparently "popular"; Poplius (i.e. Publius), a Roman:--Publius.

G4197.text: πορεία poreiva poreia {por-i'-ah} from 4198; travel (by land); figuratively (plural) proceedings, i.e. career:--journey(-ing), ways. see GREEK for 4198

G4198.text: πορεύομαι poreuvomai poreuomai {por-yoo'-om-ahee} middle voice from a derivative of the same as 3984; to traverse, i.e. travel (literally or figuratively; especially to remove (figuratively, die), live, etc.); --depart, go (away, forth, one's way, up), (make a, take a) journey, walk. see GREEK for 3984

G4199.text: πορθέω porqevw portheo {por-theh'-o} prolongation from pertho (to sack); to ravage (figuratively):--destroy, waste.

G4200.text: πορισμός porismovs porismos {por-is-mos'} from a derivative of poros (a way, i.e. means); furnishing (procuring), i.e. (by implication) money-getting (acquisition):--gain.

G4201.text: ∏όρκιος Povrkios Porkios {por'-kee-os} of Latin origin; apparently swinish; Porcius, a Roman:--Porcius.
