G5275.text: ὑπολείπω uJpoleivpw hupoleipo {hoop-ol-i'-po} from 5295 and 3007; to leave under (behind), i.e. (passively) to remain (survive):--be left. see GREEK for 5295 see GREEK for 3007

G5276.text: ὑπολήνιον uJpolhvnion hupolenion {hoop-ol-ay'-nee-on} neuter of a presumed compound of 5259 and 3025; vessel or receptacle under the press, i.e. lower wine-vat:--winefat. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 3025

G5277.text: ὑπολιμπάνω uJpolimpavnw hupolimpano {hoop-ol-im-pan'-o} a prolonged form for 5275; to leave behind, i.e. bequeath:--leave. see GREEK for 5275

G5278.text: ὑπομένω uJpomevnw hupomeno {hoop-om-en'-o} from 5259 and 3306; to stay under (behind), i.e. remain; figuratively, to undergo, i.e. bear (trials), have fortitude, persevere:--abide, endure, (take) patient(-ly), suffer, tarry behind. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 3306

G5279.text: ὑπομιμνῄσκω uJpomimnhv/skw hupomimnesko {hoop-om-im-nace'-ko} from 5259 and 3403; to remind quietly, i.e. suggest to the (middle voice, one's own) memory:--put in mind, remember, bring to (put in) remembrance. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 3403

G5280.text: ὑπόμνησις uJpovmnhsis hupomnesis {hoop-om'-nay-sis} from 5279; a reminding or (reflexively) recollection:--remembrance. see GREEK for 5279

G5281.text: ὑπομονή uJpomonhv hupomone {hoop-om-on-ay'} from 5278; cheerful (or hopeful) endurance, constancy:--enduring, patience, patient continuance (waiting). see GREEK for 5278

G5282.text: ὑπονοέω uJponoevw huponoeo {hoop-on-o-eh'-o} from 5259 and 3539; to think under (privately), i.e. to surmise or conjecture:--think, suppose, deem. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 3539

G5283.text: ὑπόνοια uJpovnoia huponoia {hoop-on'-oy-ah} from 5282; suspicion:--surmising. see GREEK for 5282

G5284.text: ὑποπλέω uJpoplevw hupopleo {hoop-op-leh'-o} from 5259 and 4126; to sail under the lee of:--sail under. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 4126

G5285.text: ὑποπνέω uJpopnevw hupopneo {hoop-op-neh'-o} from 5259 and 4154; to breathe gently, i.e. breeze:--blow softly. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 4154

G5286.text: ὑποπόδιον uJpopovdion hupopodion {hoop-op-od'-ee-on} neuter of a compound of 5259 and 4228; something under the feet, i.e. a foot-rest (figuratively):--footstool. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 4228

G5287.text: ὑπόστασις uJpovstasis hupostasis {hoop-os'-tas-is} from a compound of 5259 and 2476; a setting under (support), i.e. (figuratively) concretely, essence, or abstractly, assurance (objectively or subjectively):--confidence, confident, person, substance. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 2476

G5288.text: ὑποστέλλω uJpostevllw hupostello {hoop-os-tel'-lo} from 5259 and 4724; to withhold under (out of sight), i.e. (reflexively) to cower or shrink, (figuratively) to conceal (reserve):--draw (keep) back, shun, withdraw. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 4724

G5289.text: ὑποστολή uJpostolhv hupostole {hoop-os-tol-ay'} from 5288; shrinkage (timidity), i.e. (by implication) apostasy:--draw back. see GREEK for 5288

G5290.text: ὑποστρέφω uJpostrevfw hupostrepho {hoop-os-tref'-o} from 5259 and 4762; to turn under (behind), i.e. to return (literally or figuratively):--come again, return (again, back again), turn back (again). see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 4762

G5291.text: ὑποστρωννύω uJpostrwnnuvw hupostronnumi {hoop-os-trone'-noo-mee} from 5259 and 4766; to strew underneath (the feet as a carpet):--spread. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 4766

G5292.text: ὑποταγή uJpotaghv hupotage {hoop-ot-ag-ay'} from 5293; subordination:--subjection. see GREEK for 5293

G5293.text: ὑποτάσσω uJpotavssw hupotasso {hoop-ot-as'-so} from 5259 and 5021; to subordinate; reflexively, to obey:--be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 5021

G5294.text: ὑποτίθημι uJpotivqhmi hupotithemi {hoop-ot-ith'-ay-mee} from 5259 and 5087; to place underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to hazard, (reflexively) to suggest:--lay down, put in remembrance. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 5087

G5295.text: ὑποτρέχω uJpotrevcw hupotrecho {hoop-ot-rekh'-o} from 5259 and 5143 (including its alternate); to run under, i.e. (specially), to sail past:--run under. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 5143

G5296.text: ὑποτύπωσις uJpotuvpwsis hupotuposis {hoop-ot-oop'-o-sis} from a compound of 5259 and a derivative of 5179; typification under (after), i.e. (concretely) a sketch (figuratively) for imitation:--form, pattern. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 5179

G5297.text: ὑποφέρω uJpofevrw hupophero {hoop-of-er'-o} from 5259 and 5342; to bear from underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to undergo hardship:--bear, endure. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 5342

G5298.text: ὑποχωρέω uJpocwrevw hupochoreo {hoop-okh-o-reh'-o} from 5259 and 5562; to vacate down, i.e. retire quietly:--go aside, withdraw self. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 5562

G5299.text: ὑπωπιάζω uJpwpiavzw hupopiazo {hoop-o-pee-ad'-zo} from a compound of 5259 and a derivative of 3700; to hit under the eye (buffet or disable an antagonist as a pugilist), i.e. (figuratively) to tease or annoy (into compliance), subdue (one's passions):--keep under, weary. see GREEK for 5259 see GREEK for 3700

G5300.text: ὗς u|s hus {hoos} apparently a primary word; a hog ("swine"):--sow.

G5301.text: ὕσσωπος u&sswpos hussopos {hoos'-so-pos} of foreign origin (231); "hyssop":--hyssop. see HEBREW for 0231

G5302.text: ὑστερέω uJsterevw hustereo {hoos-ter-eh'-o} from 5306; to be later, i.e. (by implication) to be inferior; generally, to fall short (be deficient):--come behind (short), be destitute, fail, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse. see GREEK for 5306

G5303.text: ὑστέρημα uJstevrhma husterema {hoos-ter'-ay-mah} from 5302; a deficit; specially, poverty:--that which is behind, (that which was) lack(-ing), penury, want. see GREEK for 5302

G5304.text: ὑστέρησις uJstevrhsis husteresis {hoos-ter'-ay-sis} a falling short, i.e. (specially), penury:--want.

G5305.text: ὕστερος u&steros husteron {hoos'-ter-on} neuter of 5306 as adverb; more lately, i.e. eventually:--afterward, (at the) last (of all). see GREEK for 5306

G5306.text: ὕστερος u&steros husteros {hoos'-ter-os} comparative from 5259 (in the sense of behind); later:--latter. see GREEK for 5259

G5307.text: ὑφαντός uJfantovs huphantos {hoo-fan-tos'} from huphaino to weave; woven, i.e. (perhaps) knitted:--woven.

G5308.text: ὑψηλός uJyhlovs hupselos {hoop-say-los'} from 5311; lofty (in place or character):--high(-er, -ly) (esteemed). see GREEK for 5311

G5309.text: ὑψηλοφρονέω uJyhlofronevw hupselophroneo {hoop-say-lo-fron-eh'-o} from a compound of 5308 and 5424; to be lofty in mind, i.e. arrogant:--be highminded. see GREEK for 5308 see GREEK for 5424

G5310.text: ὕψιστος u&yistos hupsistos {hoop'-sis-tos} superlative from the base of 5311; highest, i.e. (masculine singular) the Supreme (God), or (neuter plural) the heavens:--most high, highest. see GREEK for 5311

G5311.text: ὕψος u&yos hupsos {hoop'-sos} from a derivative of 5228; elevation, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, (specially), the sky, or (figuratively) dignity:--be exalted, height, (on) high. see GREEK for 5228

G5312.text: ὑψόω uJyovw hupsoo {hoop-so'-o} from 5311; to elevate (literally or figuratively):--exalt, lift up. see GREEK for 5311

G5313.text: ὕψωμα u&ywma hupsoma {hoop'-so-mah} from 5312; an elevated place or thing, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, or (by implication) a barrier (figuratively):-- height, high thing. see GREEK for 5312

G5314.text: φάγος favgos phagos {fag'-os} from 5315; a glutton:--gluttonous. see GREEK for 5315

G5315.text: ἐσθίω ejsqivw phago {fag'-o} a primary verb (used as an alternate of 2068 in certain tenses); to eat (literally or figuratively):--eat, meat. see GREEK for 2068

G5316.text: φαίνω faivnw phaino {fah'-ee-no} prolongation for the base of 5457; to lighten (shine), i.e. show (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative):-- appear, seem, be seen, shine, X think. see GREEK for 5457

G5317.text: Φάλεκ Favlek Phalek {fal'-ek} of Hebrew origin (6389); Phalek (i.e. Peleg), a patriarch:--Phalec. see HEBREW for 06389

G5318.text: φανερός fanerovs phaneros {fan-er-os'} from 5316; shining, i.e. apparent (literally or figuratively); neuter (as adverb) publicly, externally:--abroad, + appear, known, manifest, open (+ -ly), outward (+ -ly). see GREEK for 5316

G5319.text: φανερόω fanerovw phaneroo {fan-er-o'-o} from 5318; to render apparent (literally or figuratively):--appear, manifestly declare, (make) manifest (forth), shew (self). see GREEK for 5318

G5320.text: φανερῶς fanerw's phaneros {fan-er-oce'} adverb from 5318; plainly, i.e. clearly or publicly:--evidently, openly. see GREEK for 5318

G5321.text: φανέρωσις fanevrwsis phanerosis {fan-er'-o-sis} from 5319; exhibition, i.e. (figuratively) expression, (by extension) a bestowment:--manifestation. see GREEK for 5319

G5322.text: φανός fanovs phanos {fan-os'} from 5316; a lightener, i.e. light; lantern:--lantern. see GREEK for 5316

G5323.text: Φανουήλ Fanouhvl Phanouel {fan-oo-ale'} of Hebrew origin (6439); Phanuel (i.e. Penuel), an Israelite:--Phanuel. see HEBREW for 06439

G5324.text: φαντάζω fantavzw phantazo {fan-tad'-zo} from a derivative of 5316; to make apparent, i.e. (passively) to appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle):--sight. see GREEK for 5316

G5325.text: φαντασία fantasiva phantasia {fan-tas-ee'-ah} from a derivative of 5324; (properly abstract) a (vain) show ("fantasy"):--pomp. see GREEK for 5324

G5326.text: φάντασμα favntasma phantasma {fan'-tas-mah} from 5324; (properly concrete) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), i.e. spectre:--spirit. see GREEK for 5324

G5327.text: φάραγξ favragx pharagx {far'-anx} properly, strengthened from the base of 4008 or rather of 4486; a gap or chasm, i.e. ravine (winter-torrent):--valley. see GREEK for 4486 see GREEK for 4008

G5328.text: Φαραώ Farawv Pharao {far-ah-o'} of foreign origin (6547); Pharao (i.e. Pharoh), an Egyptian king:--Pharaoh. see HEBREW for 06547

G5329.text: Φάρες Favres Phares {far-es'} of Hebrew origin (6557); Phares (i.e. Perets), an Israelite:--Phares. see HEBREW for 06557

G5330.text: Φαρισαῖος Farisai'os Pharisaios {far-is-ah'-yos} of Hebrew origin (compare 6567); a separatist, i.e. exclusively religious; a Pharisean, i.e. Jewish sectary:--Pharisee. see HEBREW for 06567

G5331.text: φαρμακεία farmakeiva pharmakeia {far-mak-i'-ah} from 5332; medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic (literally or figuratively):--sorcery, witchcraft. see GREEK for 5332

G5332.text: φαρμακεύς pharmakeus pharmakeus {far-mak-yoos'} from pharmakon (a drug, i.e. spell-giving potion); a druggist ("pharmacist") or poisoner, i.e. (by extension) a magician:--sorcerer.

G5333.text: φάρμακος favrmakos pharmakos {far-mak-os'} the same as 5332:--sorcerer.

G5334.text: φάσις favsis phasis {fas'-is} from 5346 (not the same as "phase", which is from 5316); a saying, i.e. report:--tidings. see GREEK for 5346 see GREEK for 5316

G5335.text: φάσκω favskw phasko {fas'-ko} prolongation from the same as 5346; to assert:--affirm, profess, say. see GREEK for 5346

G5336.text: φάτνη favtnh phatne {fat'-nay} from pateomai (to eat); a crib (for fodder):--manager, stall.

G5337.text: φαῦλος fau'los phaulos {fow'-los} apparently a primary word; "foul" or "flawy", i.e. (figuratively) wicked:--evil.

G5338.text: φέγγος fevggos pheggos {feng'-gos} probably akin to the base of 5457 (compare 5350); brilliancy:--light. see GREEK for 5457 see GREEK for 5350

G5339.text: φείδομαι feivdomai pheidomai {fi'-dom-ahee} of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently:--forbear, spare.

G5340.text: φειδομένως feidomevnws pheidomenos {fi-dom-en'-oce} adverb from participle of 5339; abstemiously, i.e. stingily:--sparingly. see GREEK for 5339

G5341.text: φαιλόνης failovnhs phelones {fel-on'-ace} by transposition for a derivative probably of 5316 (as showing outside the other garments); a mantle (surtout):-- cloke. see GREEK for 5316

G5342.text: φέρω fevrw phero {fer'-o} a primary verb -- for which other, and apparently not cognate ones are used in certain tenses only; namely, oio oy'-o; and enegko en-eng'-ko to "bear" or carry (in a very wide application, literally and figuratively, as follows):--be, bear, bring (forth), carry, come, + let her drive, be driven, endure, go on, lay, lead, move, reach, rushing, uphold.

G5343.text: φεύγω feuvgw pheugo {fyoo'-go} apparently a primary verb; to run away (literally or figuratively); by implication, to shun; by analogy, to vanish:--escape, flee (away).

G5344.text: Φῆλιξ Fh'lix Phelix {fay'-lix} of Latin origin; happy; Phelix (i.e. Felix), a Roman:--Felix.

G5345.text: φήμη fhvmh pheme {fay'-may} from 5346; a saying, i.e. rumor ("fame"):--fame. see GREEK for 5346

G5346.text: φημί fhmiv phemi {fay-mee'} properly, the same as the base of 5457 and 5316; to show or make known one's thoughts, i.e. speak or say:--affirm, say. Compare 3004. see GREEK for 5457 see GREEK for 5316 see GREEK for 3004

G5347.text: Φῆστος Fh'stos Phestos {face'-tos} of Latin derivation; festal; Phestus (i.e. Festus), a Roman:--Festus.

G5348.text: φθάνω fqavnw phthano {fthan'-o} apparently a primary verb; to be beforehand, i.e. anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at:--(already) attain, come, prevent.

G5349.text: φθαρτός fqartovs phthartos {fthar-tos'} from 5351; decayed, i.e. (by implication) perishable:--corruptible. see GREEK for 5351

G5350.text: φθέγγομαι fqevggomai phtheggomai {ftheng'-gom-ahee} probably akin to 5338 and thus to 5346; to utter a clear sound, i.e. (generally) to proclaim:--speak. see GREEK for 5346 see GREEK for 5338

G5351.text: φθείρω fqeivrw phtheiro {fthi'-ro} probably strengthened from phthio (to pine or waste); properly, to shrivel or wither, i.e. to spoil (by any process) or (generally) to ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to deprave):--corrupt (self), defile, destroy.

G5352.text: φθινοπωρινός fqinopwrinovs phthinoporinos {fthin-op-o-ree-nos'} from derivative of phthino (to wane; akin to the base of 5351) and 3703 (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves):--whose fruit withereth. see GREEK for 5351 see GREEK for 3703

G5353.text: φθόγγος fqovggos phthoggos {ftong'-gos} from 5350; utterance, i.e. a musical note (vocal or instrumental):--sound. see GREEK for 5350

G5354.text: φθονέω fqonevw phthoneo {fthon-eh'-o} from 5355; to be jealous of:--envy. see GREEK for 5355

G5355.text: φθόνος fqovnos phthonos {fthon'-os} probably akin to the base of 5351; ill-will (as detraction), i.e. jealousy (spite):--envy. see GREEK for 5351

G5356.text: φθορά fqorav phthora {fthor-ah'} from 5351; decay, i.e. ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively):--corruption, destroy, perish. see GREEK for 5351

G5357.text: φιάλη fiavlh phiale {fee-al'-ay} of uncertain affinity; a broad shallow cup ("phial"):--vial.

G5358.text: φιλάγαθος filavgaqos philagathos {fil-ag'-ath-os} from 5384 and 18; fond to good, i.e. a promoter of virtue:--love of good men. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 18

G5359.text: Φιλαδέλφεια Filadevlfeia Philadelpheia {fil-ad-el'-fee-ah} from Philadelphos (the same as 5361), a king of Pergamos; Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor:--Philadelphia. see GREEK for 5361

G5360.text: φιλαδελφία filadelfiva philadelphia {fil-ad-el-fee'-ah} from 5361; fraternal affection:--brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren. see GREEK for 5361

G5361.text: φιλάδελφος filavdelfos philadelphos {fil-ad'-el-fos} from 5384 and 80; fond of brethren, i.e. fraternal:--love as brethren. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 80

G5362.text: φίλανδρος fivlandros philandros {fil'-an-dros} from 5384 and 435; fond of man, i.e. affectionate as a wife:--love their husbands. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 435

G5363.text: φιλανθρωπία filanqrwpiva philanthropia {fil-an-thro-pee'-ah} from the same as 5364; fondness of mankind, i.e. benevolence ("philanthropy"):--kindness, love towards man. see GREEK for 5364

G5364.text: φιλανθρώπως filanqrwvpws philanthropos {fil-an-thro'-poce} adverb from a compound of 5384 and 444; fondly to man ("philanthropically"), i.e. humanely:--courteously. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 444

G5365.text: φιλαργυρία filarguriva philarguria {fil-ar-goo-ree'-ah} from 5366; avarice:--love of money. see GREEK for 5366

G5366.text: φιλάργυρος filavrguros philarguros {fil-ar'-goo-ros} from 5384 and 696; fond of silver (money), i.e. avaricious:--covetous. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 696

G5367.text: φίλαυτος fivlautos philautos {fil'-ow-tos} from 5384 and 846; fond of self, i.e. selfish:--lover of own self. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 846

G5368.text: φιλέω filevw phileo {fil-eh'-o} from 5384; to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)), i.e. have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while 25 is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as 2309 and 1014, or as 2372 and 3563 respectively; the former being chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specially, to kiss (as a mark of tenderness):--kiss, love. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 2372 see GREEK for 25 see GREEK for 2309 see GREEK for 1014 see GREEK for 3563

G5369.text: φιλήδονος filhvdonos philedonos {fil-ay'-don-os} from 5384 and 2237; fond of pleasure, i.e. voluptuous:--lover of pleasure. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 2237

G5370.text: φίλημα fivlhma philema {fil'-ay-mah} from 5368; a kiss:--kiss. see GREEK for 5368

G5371.text: Φιλήμων Filhvmwn Philemon {fil-ay'-mone} from 5368; friendly; Philemon, a Christian:--Philemon. see GREEK for 5368

G5372.text: Φίλητος Fivlhtos Philetos {fil-ay-tos'} from 5368; amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity:--Philetus. see GREEK for 5368

G5373.text: φιλία filiva philia {fil-ee'-ah} from 5384; fondness:--friendship. see GREEK for 5384

G5374.text: Φιλιππήσιος Filipphvsios Philippesios {fil-ip-pay'-see-os} from 5375; a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. native of Philippi:--Philippian. see GREEK for 5375

G5375.text: Φίλιπποι Fivlippoi Philippoi {fil'-ip-poy} plural of 5376; Philippi, a place in Macedonia:--Philippi. see GREEK for 5376

G5376.text: Φίλιππος Fivlippos Philippos {fil'-ip-pos} from 5384 and 2462; fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites:--Philip. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 2462

G5377.text: φιλόθεος filovqeos philotheos {fil-oth'-eh-os} from 5384 and 2316; fond of God, i.e. pious:--lover of God. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 2316

G5378.text: Φιλόλογος Filovlogos Philologos {fil-ol'-og-os} from 5384 and 3056; fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian:--Philologus. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 3056

G5379.text: φιλονεικία filoneikiva philoneikia {fil-on-i-kee'-ah} from 5380; quarrelsomeness, i.e. a dispute:--strife. see GREEK for 5380

G5380.text: φιλόνεικος filovneikos philoneikos {fil-on'-i-kos} from 5384 and neikos (a quarrel; probably akin to 3534); fond of strife, i.e. disputatious:--contentious. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 3534

G5381.text: φιλοξενία filoxeniva philoxenia {fil-ox-en-ee'-ah} from 5382; hospitableness:--entertain stranger, hospitality. see GREEK for 5382

G5382.text: φιλόξενος filovxenos philoxenos {fil-ox'-en-os} from 5384 and 3581; fond of guests, i.e. hospitable:--given to (lover of, use) hospitality. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 3581

G5383.text: φιλοπρωτεύω filoprwteuvw philoproteuo {fil-op-rote-yoo'-o} from a compound of 5384 and 4413; to be fond of being first, i.e. ambitious of distinction:--love to have the preeminence. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 4413

G5384.text: φίλος fivlos philos {fee'-los} properly, dear, i.e. a friend; actively, fond, i.e. friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.):--friend.

G5385.text: φιλοσοφία filosofiva philosophia {fil-os-of-ee'-ah} from 5386; "philosophy", i.e. (specially), Jewish sophistry:--philosophy. see GREEK for 5386

G5386.text: φιλόσοφος filovsofos philosophos {fil-os'-of-os} from 5384 and 4680; fond of wise things, i.e. a "philosopher":--philosopher. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 4680

G5387.text: φιλόστοργος filovstorgos philostorgos {fil-os'-tor-gos} from 5384 and storge (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children); fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow Christian:--kindly affectioned. see GREEK for 5384

G5388.text: φιλότεκνος filovteknos philoteknos {fil-ot'-ek-nos} from 5384 and 5043; fond of one's children, i.e. maternal:--love their children. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 5043

G5389.text: φιλοτιμέομαι filotimevomai philotimeomai {fil-ot-im-eh'-om-ahee} middle voice from a compound of 5384 and 5092; to be fond of honor, i.e. emulous (eager or earnest to do something):--labour, strive, study. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 5092

G5390.text: φιλοφρόνως filofrovnws philophronos {fil-of-ron'-oce} adverb from 5391; with friendliness of mind, i.e. kindly:--courteously. see GREEK for 5391

G5391.text: φιλόφρων ον philophron philophron {fil-of'-rone} from 5384 and 5424; friendly of mind, i.e. kind:--courteous. see GREEK for 5384 see GREEK for 5424

G5392.text: φιμόω fimovw phimoo {fee-mo'-o} from phimos (a muzzle); to muzzle:--muzzle.

G5393.text: Φλέγων Flevgwn Phlegon {fleg'-one} active participle of the base of 5395; blazing; Phlegon, a Christian:--Phlegon. see GREEK for 5395

G5394.text: φλογίζω flogivzw phlogizo {flog-id'-zo} from 5395; to cause a blaze, i.e. ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion):--set on fire. see GREEK for 5395

G5395.text: φλόξ flovx phlox {flox} from a primary phlego (to "flash" or "flame"); a blaze:--flame(-ing).

G5396.text: φλυαρέω fluarevw phluareo {floo-ar-eh'-o} from 5397; to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously:--prate against. see GREEK for 5397

G5397.text: φλύαρος fluvaros phluaros {floo'-ar-os} from phluo (to bubble); a garrulous person, i.e. prater:--tattler.

G5398.text: φοβερός foberovs phoberos {fob-er-os'} from 5401; frightful, i.e. (objectively) formidable:--fearful, terrible. see GREEK for 5401

G5399.text: φοβέω fobevw phobeo {fob-eh'-o} from 5401; to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. revere:--be (+ sore) afraid, fear (exceedingly), reverence. see GREEK for 5401

G5400.text: φόβητρον φόβηθρον fovbhtron fovbhqron phobetron {fob'-ay-tron} neuter of a derivative of 5399; a frightening thing, i.e. terrific portent:--fearful sight. see GREEK for 5399

G5401.text: φόβος fovbos phobos {fob'-os} from a primary phebomai (to be put in fear); alarm or fright:--be afraid, + exceedingly, fear, terror.

G5402.text: Φοίβη Foivbh Phoibe {foy'-bay} feminine of phoibos (bright; probably akin to the base of 5457); Phoebe, a Christian woman:--Phebe. see GREEK for 5457

G5403.text: Φοινίκη Foinivkh Phoinike {foy-nee'-kay} from 5404; palm-country; Phoenice (or Phoenicia), a region of Palestine:--Phenice, Phenicia. see GREEK for 5404

G5404.text: φοῖνιξ foi'nix phoinix {foy'-nix} of uncertain derivation; a palm-tree:--palm (tree).

G5405.text: φοῖνιξ foi'nix Phoinix {foy'-nix} probably the same as 5404; Phoenix, a place in Crete:--Phenice. see GREEK for 5404

G5406.text: φονεύς foneuvs phoneus {fon-yooce'} from 5408; a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which 443 does not necessarily imply; while 4607 is a special term for a public bandit):--murderer. see GREEK for 5408 see GREEK for 443 see GREEK for 4607

G5407.text: φονεύω foneuvw phoneuo {fon-yoo'-o} from 5406; to be a murderer (of):--kill, do murder, slay. see GREEK for 5406

G5408.text: φόνος fovnos phonos {fon'-os} from an obsolete primary pheno (to slay); murder:--murder, + be slain with, slaughter.

G5409.text: φορέω forevw phoreo {for-eh'-o} from 5411; to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment:--bear, wear. see GREEK for 5411

G5410.text: φόρον fovron Phoron {for'-on} of Latin origin; a forum or market-place; only in comparative with 675; a station on the Appian road:--forum. see GREEK for 675

G5411.text: φόρος fovros phoros {for'-os} from 5342; a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas 5056 is usually a general toll on goods or travel):--tribute. see GREEK for 5342 see GREEK for 5056

G5412.text: φορτίζω fortivzw phortizo {for-tid'-zo} from 5414; to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety):--lade, by heavy laden. see GREEK for 5414

G5413.text: φορτίον fortivon phortion {for-tee'-on} diminutive of 5414; an invoice (as part of freight), i.e. (figuratively) a task or service:--burden. see GREEK for 5414

G5414.text: φορτίον fortivon phortos {for'-tos} from 5342; something carried, i.e. the cargo of a ship:--lading. see GREEK for 5342

G5415.text: Φορτουνᾶτος Fortouna'tos Phortounatos {for-too-nat'-os} of Latin origin; "fortunate"; Fortunatus, a Christian:--Fortunatus.

G5416.text: φραγέλλιον fragevllion phragellion {frag-el'-le-on} neuter of a derivative from the base of 5417; a whip, i.e. Roman lash as a public punishment:--scourge. see GREEK for 5417

G5417.text: φραγελλόω fragellovw phragelloo {frag-el-lo'-o} from a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; to whip, i.e. lash as a public punishment:--scourge.

G5418.text: φραγμός fragmovs phragmos {frag-mos'} from 5420; a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively):--hedge (+ round about), partition. see GREEK for 5420

G5419.text: φράζω fravzw phrazo {frad'-zo} probably akin to 5420 through the idea of defining; to indicate (by word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound:-- declare. see GREEK for 5420

G5420.text: φράσσω fravssw phrasso {fras'-so} apparently a strengthening form of the base of 5424; to fence or inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to silence):--stop. see GREEK for 5424

G5421.text: φρέαρ frevar phrear {freh'-ar} of uncertain derivation; a hole in the ground (dug for obtaining or holding water or other purposes), i.e. a cistern or well; figuratively, an abyss (as a prison):--well, pit.

G5422.text: φρεναπατάω frenapatavw phrenapatao {fren-ap-at-ah'-o} from 5423; to be a mind-misleader, i.e. delude:--deceive. see GREEK for 5423

G5423.text: φρεναπάτης frenapavths phrenapates {fren-ap-at'-ace} from 5424 and 539; a mind-misleader, i.e. seducer:--deceiver. see GREEK for 5424 see GREEK for 539

G5424.text: φρήν frhvn phren {frane} probably from an obsolete phrao (to rein in or curb; compare 5420); the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive faculties):--understanding. see GREEK for 5420

G5425.text: φρίσσω frivssw phrisso {fris'-so} apparently a primary verb; to "bristle" or chill, i.e. shudder (fear):--tremble.

G5426.text: φρονέω fronevw phroneo {fron-eh'-o} from 5424; to exercise the mind, i.e. entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience):--set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think. see GREEK for 5424

G5427.text: φρόνημα frovnhma phronema {fron'-ay-mah} from 5426; (mental) inclination or purpose:--(be, + be carnally, + be spiritually) mind(-ed). see GREEK for 5426

G5428.text: φρόνησις frovnhsis phronesis {fron'-ay-sis} from 5426; mental action or activity, i.e. intellectual or moral insight:--prudence, wisdom. see GREEK for 5426

G5429.text: φρόνιμος frovnimos phronimos {fron'-ee-mos} from 5424; thoughtful, i.e. sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while 4680 denotes practical skill or acumen; and 4908 indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative):--wise(-r). see GREEK for 5424 see GREEK for 4680 see GREEK for 4908

G5430.text: φρονίμως fronivmws phronimos {fron-im'-oce} adverb from 5429; prudently:--wisely. see GREEK for 5429

G5431.text: φροντίζω frontivzw phrontizo {fron-tid'-zo} from a derivative of 5424; to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious:--be careful. see GREEK for 5424

G5432.text: φρουρέω frourevw phroureo {froo-reh'-o} from a compound of 4253 and 3708; to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect:--keep (with a garrison). Compare 5083. see GREEK for 4253 see GREEK for 3708 see GREEK for 5083

G5433.text: φρυάσσω fruavssw phruasso {froo-as'-so} akin to 1032, 1031; to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult:--rage. see GREEK for 1031 see GREEK for 1032

G5434.text: φρύγανον fruvganon phruganon {froo'-gan-on} neuter of a presumed derivative of phrugo (to roast or parch; akin to the base of 5395); something desiccated, i.e. a dry twig:--stick. see GREEK for 5395

G5435.text: Φρυγία Frugiva Phrugia {froog-ee'-ah} probably of foreign origin; Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor:--Phrygia.

G5436.text: Φύγελος Fuvgelos Phugellos {foog'-el-los} probably from 5343; fugitive; Phygellus, an apostate Christian:--Phygellus. see GREEK for 5343

G5437.text: φυγή fughv phuge {foog-ay'} from 5343; a fleeing, i.e. escape:--flight. see GREEK for 5343

G5438.text: φυλακή fulakhv phulake {foo-lak-ay'} from 5442; a guarding or (concretely, guard), the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or (specially), the time (as a division of day or night), literally or figuratively:--cage, hold, (im-)prison(-ment), ward, watch. see GREEK for 5442

G5439.text: φυλακίζω fulakivzw phulakizo {foo-lak-id'-zo} from 5441; to incarcerate:--imprison. see GREEK for 5441

G5440.text: φυλακτήριον fulakthvrion phulakterion {foo-lak-tay'-ree-on} neuter of a derivative of 5442; a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts:-- phylactery. see GREEK for 5442

G5441.text: φύλαξ fuvlax phulax {foo'-lax} from 5442; a watcher or sentry:--keeper. see GREEK for 5442

G5442.text: φυλάσσω fulavssw phulasso {foo-las'-so} probably from 5443 through the idea of isolation; to watch, i.e. be on guard (literally of figuratively); by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid:--beward, keep (self), observe, save. Compare 5083. see GREEK for 5443 see GREEK for 5083

G5443.text: φυλή fulhv phule {foo-lay'} from 5453 (compare 5444); an offshoot, i.e. race or clan:--kindred, tribe. see GREEK for 5453 see GREEK for 5444

G5444.text: φύλλον fuvllon phullon {fool'-lon} from the same as 5443; a sprout, i.e. leaf:--leaf. see GREEK for 5443

G5445.text: φύραμα fuvrama phurama {foo'-ram-ah} from a prolonged form of phuro (to mix a liquid with a solid; perhaps akin to 5453 through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough:--lump. see GREEK for 5453

G5446.text: φυσικός fusikovs phusikos {foo-see-kos'} from 5449; "physical", i.e. (by implication) instinctive:--natural. Compare 5591. see GREEK for 5449 see GREEK for 5591

G5447.text: φυσικῶς fusikw's phusikos {foo-see-koce'} adverb from 5446; "physically", i.e. (by implication) instinctively:--naturally. see GREEK for 5446

G5448.text: φυσιόω fusiovw phusioo {foo-see-o'-o} from 5449 in the primary sense of blowing; to inflate, i.e. (figuratively) make proud (haughty):--puff up. see GREEK for 5449

G5449.text: φύσις fuvsis phusis {foo'-sis} from 5453; growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage:--(man-)kind, nature(-al). see GREEK for 5453

G5450.text: φυσίωσις fusivwsis phusiosis {foo-see'-o-sis} from 5448; inflation, i.e. (figuratively) haughtiness:--swelling. see GREEK for 5448

G5451.text: φυτεία futeiva phuteia {foo-ti'-ah} from 5452; trans-planting, i.e. (concretely) a shrub or vegetable:--plant. see GREEK for 5452

G5452.text: φυτεύω futeuvw phuteuo {foot-yoo'-o} from a derivative of 5453; to set out in the earth, i.e. implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine:--plant. see GREEK for 5453

G5453.text: φύω fuvw phuo {foo'-o} a primary verb; probably originally, to "puff" or blow, i.e. to swell up; but only used in the implied sense, to germinate or grow (sprout, produce), literally or figuratively:--spring (up).

G5454.text: φωλεός fwleovs pholeos {fo-leh-os'} of uncertain derivative; a burrow or lurking-place:--hole.

G5455.text: φωνέω fwnevw phoneo {fo-neh'-o} from 5456; to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation:--call (for), crow, cry. see GREEK for 5456

G5456.text: φωνή fwnhv phone {fo-nay'} probably akin to 5316 through the idea of disclosure; a tone (articulate, bestial or artificial); by implication, an address (for any purpose), saying or language:--noise, sound, voice. see GREEK for 5316

G5457.text: φῶς fw's phos {foce} from an obsolete phao (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays; compare 5316, 5346); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative):--fire, light. see GREEK for 5316 see GREEK for 5346

G5458.text: φωστήρ fwsthvr phoster {foce-tare'} from 5457; an illuminator, i.e. (concretely) a luminary, or (abstractly) brilliancy:--light. see GREEK for 5457

G5459.text: φωσφόρος fwsfovros phosphoros {foce-for'-os} from 5457 and 5342; light-bearing ("phosphorus"), i.e. (specially), the morning-star (figuratively):--day star. see GREEK for 5457 see GREEK for 5342

G5460.text: φωτεινός fwteinovs photeinos {fo-ti-nos'} from 5457; lustrous, i.e. transparent or well-illuminated (figuratively):--bright, full of light. see GREEK for 5457

G5461.text: φωτίζω fwtivzw photizo {fo-tid'-zo} from 5457; to shed rays, i.e. to shine or (transitively) to brighten up (literally or figuratively):--enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see. see GREEK for 5457

G5462.text: φωτισμός fwtismovs photismos {fo-tis-mos'} from 5461; illumination (figuratively):--light. see GREEK for 5461

G5463.text: χαίρω caivrw chairo {khah'-ee-ro} a primary verb; to be "cheer"ful, i.e. calmly happy or well-off; impersonally, especially as salutation (on meeting or parting), be well:--farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hall, joy(- fully), rejoice.

G5464.text: χάλαζα cavlaza chalaza {khal'-ad-zah} probably from 5465; hail:--hail. see GREEK for 5465

G5465.text: χαλάω calavw chalao {khal-ah'-o} from the base of 5490; to lower (as into a void):--let down, strike. see GREEK for 5490

G5466.text: Χαλδαῖος Caldai'os Chaldaios {khal-dah'-yos} probably of Hebrew or (3778); a Chaldoean (i.e. Kasdi), or native or the region of the lower Euphrates:--Chaldaean. see HEBREW for 03778

G5467.text: χαλεπός calepovs chalepos {khal-ep-os'} perhaps from 5465 through the idea of reducing the strength; difficult, i.e. dangerous, or (by implication) furious:--fierce, perilous. see GREEK for 5465

G5468.text: χαλιναγωγέω calinagwgevw chalinagogeo {khal-in-ag-ogue-eh'-o} from a compound of 5469 and the reduplicated form of 71; to be a bit-leader, i.e. to curb (figuratively):--bridle. see GREEK for 5469 see GREEK for 71

G5469.text: χαλινός calinovs chalinos {khal-ee-nos'} from 5465; a curb or head-stall (as curbing the spirit):--bit, bridle. see GREEK for 5465

G5470.text: χαλκοῦς calkou's chalkeos {khal'-keh-os} from 5475; coppery:--brass. see GREEK for 5475

G5471.text: χαλκεύς calkeuvs chalkeus {khalk-yooce'} from 5475; a copper-worker or brazier:--coppersmith. see GREEK for 5475

G5472.text: χαλκηδών calkhdwvn chalkedon {khal-kay-dohn'} from 5475 and perhaps 1491; copper-like, i.e. "chalcedony":--chalcedony. see GREEK for 5475 see GREEK for 1491

G5473.text: χαλκίον calkivon chalkion {khal-kee'-on} diminutive from 5475; a copper dish:--brazen vessel. see GREEK for 5475

G5474.text: χαλκολίβανον calkolivbanon chalkolibanon {khal-kol-ib'-an-on} neuter of a compound of 5475 and 3030 (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy); burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre:--fine brass. see GREEK for 5475 see GREEK for 3030

G5475.text: χαλκός calkovs chalkos {khal-kos'} perhaps from 5465 through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose); copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it):--brass, money. see GREEK for 5465

G5476.text: χαμαί camaiv chamai {kham-ah'-ee} adverb perhaps from the base of 5490 through the idea of a fissure in the soil; earthward, i.e. prostrate:--on (to) the ground. see GREEK for 5490

G5477.text: Χανάαν Canavan Chanaan {khan-ah-an'} of Hebrew origin (3667); Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of Palestine:--Chanaan. see HEBREW for 03667

G5478.text: Χαναναῖος Cananai'os Chanaanaios {khan-ah-an-ah'-yos} from 5477; a Chanaanoean (i.e. Kenaanite), or native of gentile Palestine:--of Canaan. see GREEK for 5477

G5479.text: χαρά carav chara {khar-ah'} from 5463; cheerfulness, i.e. calm delight:--gladness, X greatly, (X be exceeding) joy(-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous). see GREEK for 5463

G5480.text: χάραγμα cavragma charagma {khar'-ag-mah} from the same as 5482; a scratch or etching, i.e. stamp (as a badge of servitude), or scupltured figure (statue):--graven, mark. see GREEK for 5482

G5481.text: χαρακτήρ carakthvr charakter {khar-ak-tare'} from the same as 5482; a graver (the tool or the person), i.e. (by implication) engraving (("character"), the figure stamped, i.e. an exact copy or (figuratively) representation):--express image. see GREEK for 5482

G5482.text: χάραξ cavrax charax {khar'-ax} from charasso (to sharpen to a point; akin to 1125 through the idea of scratching); a stake, i.e. (by implication) a palisade or rampart (military mound for circumvallation in a siege):--trench. see GREEK for 1125

G5483.text: χαρίζομαι carivzomai charizomai {khar-id'-zom-ahee} middle voice from 5485; to grant as a favor, i.e. gratuitously, in kindness, pardon or rescue:--deliver, (frankly) forgive, (freely) give, grant. see GREEK for 5485

G5484.text: χάριν cavrin charin {khar'-in} accusative case of 5485 as preposition; through favor of, i.e. on account of:--be-(for) cause of, for sake of, +...fore, X reproachfully. see GREEK for 5485

G5485.text: χάρις cavris charis {khar'-ece} from 5463; graciousness (as gratifying), of manner or act (abstract or concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine influence upon the heart, and its reflection in the life; including gratitude):--acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace(- ious), joy, liberality, pleasure, thank(-s, -worthy). see GREEK for 5463

G5486.text: χάρισμα cavrisma charisma {khar'-is-mah} from 5483; a (divine) gratuity, i.e. deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty:--(free) gift. see GREEK for 5483

G5487.text: χαριτόω caritovw charitoo {khar-ee-to'-o} from 5485; to grace, i.e. indue with special honor:--make accepted, be highly favoured. see GREEK for 5485

G5488.text: Χαρράν Carravn Charrhan {khar-hran'} of Hebrew origin (2771); Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in Mesopotamia:--Charran. see HEBREW for 02771

G5489.text: χάρτης cavrths chartes {khar'-tace} from the same as 5482; a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be scribbled over):--paper. see GREEK for 5482

G5490.text: χάσμα cavsma chasma {khas'-mah} from a form of an obsolete primary chao (to "gape" or "yawn"); a "chasm" or vacancy (impassable interval):--gulf.

G5491.text: χεῖλος cei'los cheilos {khi'-los} from a form of the same as 5490; a lip (as a pouring place); figuratively, a margin (of water):--lip, shore. see GREEK for 5490

G5492.text: χειμάζω ceimavzw cheimazo {khi-mad'-zo} from the same as 5494; to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a gale:--be tossed with tempest. see GREEK for 5494

G5493.text: χείμαρρος ceivmarros cheimarrhos {khi'-mar-hros} from the base of 5494 and 4482; a storm-runlet, i.e. winter-torrent:--brook. see GREEK for 5494 see GREEK for 4482

G5494.text: χειμών ceimwvn cheimon {khi-mone'} from a derivative of cheo (to pour; akin to the base of 5490 through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication, the rainy season, i.e. winter:--tempest, foul weather, winter.

G5495.text: χείρ ceivr cheir {khire} perhaps from the base of 5494 in the sense of its congener the base of 5490 (through the idea of hollowness for grasping); the hand (literally or figuratively (power); especially (by Hebraism) a means or instrument):--hand. see GREEK for 5494 see GREEK for 5490

G5496.text: χειραγωγέω ceiragwgevw cheiragogeo {khi-rag-ogue-eh'-o} from 5497; to be a hand-leader, i.e. to guide (a blind person):--lead by the hand. see GREEK for 5497

G5497.text: χειραγωγός ceiragwgovs cheiragogos {khi-rag-o-gos'} from 5495 and a reduplicated form of 71; a hand-leader, i.e. personal conductor (of a blind person):--some to lead by the hand. see GREEK for 5495 see GREEK for 71

G5498.text: χειρόγραφον ceirovgrafon cheirographon {khi-rog'-raf-on} neuter of a compound of 5495 and 1125; something hand-written ("chirograph"), i.e. a manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond (figuratively)):--handwriting. see GREEK for 5495 see GREEK for 1125

G5499.text: χειροποίητος ceiropoivhtos cheiropoietos {khi-rop-oy'-ay-tos} from 5495 and a derivative of 4160; manufactured, i.e. of human construction:--made by (make with) hands. see GREEK for 5495 see GREEK for 4160

G5500.text: χειροτονέω ceirotonevw cheirotoneo {khi-rot-on-eh'-o} from a comparative of 5495 and teino (to stretch); to be a hand-reacher or voter (by raising the hand), i.e. (generally) to select or appoint:--choose, ordain. see GREEK for 5495

G5501.text: χείρων ceivrwn cheiron {khi'-rone} irregular comparative of 2556; from an obsolete equivalent cheres (of uncertain derivation); more evil or aggravated (physically, mentally or morally):--sorer, worse. see GREEK for 2556

G5502.text: Χερούβ Cerouvb cheroubim {kher-oo-beem'} plural of Hebrew origin (3742); "cherubim" (i.e. cherubs or kerubim):--cherubims. see HEBREW for 03742

G5503.text: χῇρος ch'/ros chera {khay'-rah} feminine of a presumed derivative apparently from the base of 5490 through the idea of deficiency; a widow (as lacking a husband), literally or figuratively:--widow. see GREEK for 5490

G5504.text: ἐχθές ejcqevs chthes {khthes} of uncertain derivation; "yesterday"; by extension, in time past or hitherto:--yesterday.

G5505.text: χιλιάς ciliavs chilias {khil-ee-as'} from 5507; one thousand ("chiliad"):--thousand. see GREEK for 5507

G5506.text: χιλίαρχος cilivarcos chiliarchos {khil-ee'-ar-khos} from 5507 and 757; the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch"; i.e. colonel:--(chief, high) captain. see GREEK for 5507 see GREEK for 757

G5507.text: χίλιοι civlioi chilioi {khil'-ee-oy} plural of uncertain affinity; a thousand:--thousand.

G5508.text: Χίος Civos Chios {khee'-os} of uncertain derivation; Chios, an island in the Mediterranean:--Chios.

G5509.text: χιτών citwvn chiton {khee-tone'} of foreign origin (3801); a tunic or shirt:--clothes, coat, garment. see HEBREW for 03801

G5510.text: χιών ciwvn chion {khee-one'} perhaps akin to the base of 5490 (5465) or 5494 (as descending or empty); snow:--snow. see GREEK for 5490 see GREEK for 5465 see GREEK for 5494

G5511.text: χλαμύς clamuvs chlamus {khlam-ooce'} of uncertain derivation; a military cloak:--robe.

G5512.text: χλευάζω διαχλευάζω cleuavzw diacleuavzw chleuazo {khlyoo-ad'-zo} from a derivative probably of 5491; to throw out the lip, i.e. jeer at:--mock. see GREEK for 5491

G5513.text: χλιαρός cliarovs chliaros {khlee-ar-os'} from chlio (to warm); tepid:--lukewarm.

G5514.text: Χλόη Clovh Chloe {khlo'-ay} feminine of apparently a primary word; "green"; Chloe, a Christian female:--Chloe.

G5515.text: χλωρός clwrovs chloros {khlo-ros'} from the same as 5514; greenish, i.e. verdant, dun-colored:--green, pale. see GREEK for 5514

G5516.text: χξϛ chi chi xi stigma {khee xee stig'-ma} the 22nd, 14th and an obsolete letter (4742 as a cross) of the Greek alphabet (intermediate between the 5th and 6th), used as numbers; denoting respectively 600, 60 and 6; 666 as a numeral:--six hundred threescore and six. see GREEK for 4742

G5517.text: χοϊκός coi>kovs choikos {kho-ik-os'} from 5522; dusty or dirty (soil-like), i.e. (by implication) terrene:--earthy. see GREEK for 5522

G5518.text: χοῖνιξ coi'nix choinix {khoy'-nix} of uncertain derivation; a choenix or certain dry measure:--measure.

G5519.text: χοῖρος coi'ros choiros {khoy'-ros} of uncertain derivation; a hog:--swine.

G5520.text: χολάω colavw cholao {khol-ah'-o} from 5521; to be bilious, i.e. (by implication) irritable (enraged, "choleric"):--be angry. see GREEK for 5521

G5521.text: χολή colhv chole {khol-ay'} feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as 5514 (from the greenish hue); "gall" or bile, i.e. (by analogy) poison or an anodyne (wormwood, poppy, etc.):--gall.

G5522.text: χοῦς cou's choos {kho'-os} from the base of 5494; a heap (as poured out), i.e. rubbish; loose dirt:--dust. see GREEK for 5494

G5523.text: Χοραζίν Corazivn Chorazin {khor-ad-zin'} of uncertain derivation; Chorazin, a place in Palestine:--Chorazin.

G5524.text: χορηγέω corhgevw choregeo {khor-ayg-eh'-o} from a compound of 5525 and 71; to be a dance-leader, i.e. (generally) to furnish:--give, minister. see GREEK for 5525 see GREEK for 71

G5525.text: χορός corovs choros {khor-os'} of uncertain derivation; a ring, i.e. round dance ("choir":--dancing.

G5526.text: χορτάζω cortavzw chortazo {khor-tad'-zo} from 5528; to fodder, i.e. (generally) to gorge (supply food in abundance):--feed, fill, satisfy. see GREEK for 5528

G5527.text: χόρτασμα covrtasma chortasma {khor'-tas-mah} from 5526; forage, i.e. food:--sustenance. see GREEK for 5526

G5528.text: χόρτος covrtos chortos {khor'-tos} apparently a primary word; a "court" or "garden", i.e. (by implication, of pasture) herbage or vegetation:--blade, grass, hay.

G5529.text: Χουζᾶς Couza's Chouzas {khood-zas'} of uncertain origin; Chuzas, an officer of Herod:--Chuza.

G5530.text: χράομαι cravomai chraomai {khrah'-om-ahee} middle voice of a primary verb (perhaps rather from 5495, to handle); to furnish what is needed; (give an oracle, "graze" (touch slightly), light upon, etc.), i.e. (by implication) to employ or (by extension) to act towards one in a given manner:--entreat, use. Compare 5531; 5534. see GREEK for 5531 see GREEK for 5495 see GREEK for 5534

G5531.text: κίχρημι kivcrhmi chrao {khrah'-o} probably the same as the base of 5530; to loan:--lend. see GREEK for 5530

G5532.text: χρεία creiva chreia {khri'-ah} from the base of 5530 or 5534; employment, i.e. an affair; also (by implication) occasion, demand, requirement or destitution:--business, lack, necessary(-ity), need(-ful), use, want. see GREEK for 5534 see GREEK for 5530

G5533.text: χρεοφειλέτης creofeilevths chreopheiletes {khreh-o-fi-let'-ace} from a derivative of 5531 and 3781; a loan-ower, i.e. indebted person:--debtor. see GREEK for 5531 see GREEK for 3781

G5534.text: χρή crhv chre {khray} third person singular of the same as 5530 or 5531 used impersonally; it needs (must or should) be:--ought. see GREEK for 5530 see GREEK for 5531

G5535.text: χρῄζω crhv/zw chrezo {khrade'-zo} from 5532; to make (i.e. have) necessity, i.e. be in want of:--(have) need. see GREEK for 5532

G5536.text: χρῆμα crh'ma chrema {khray'-mah} something useful or needed, i.e. wealth, price:--money, riches.

G5537.text: χρηματίζω crhmativzw chrematizo {khray-mat-id'-zo} from 5536; to utter an oracle (compare the original sense of 5530), i.e. divinely intimate; by implication, (compare the secular sense of 5532) to constitute a firm for business, i.e. (generally) bear as a title:--be called, be admonished (warned) of God, reveal, speak. see GREEK for 5536 see GREEK for 5530 see GREEK for 5532

G5538.text: χρηματισμός crhmatismovs chrematismos {khray-mat-is-mos'} from 5537; a divine response or revelation:--answer of God. see GREEK for 5537

G5539.text: χρήσιμον crhvsimon chresimos {khray'-see-mos} from 5540; serviceable:--profit. see GREEK for 5540

G5540.text: χρῆσις crh'sis chresis {khray'-sis} from 5530; employment, i.e. (specially), sexual intercourse (as an occupation of the body):--use. see GREEK for 5530

G5541.text: χρηστεύομαι crhsteuvomai chresteuomai {khraste-yoo'-om-ahee} middle voice from 5543; to show oneself useful, i.e. act benevolently:--be kind. see GREEK for 5543

G5542.text: χρηστολογία crhstologiva chrestologia {khrase-tol-og-ee'-ah} from a compound of 5543 and 3004; fair speech, i.e. plausibility:--good words. see GREEK for 5543 see GREEK for 3004

G5543.text: χρηστός crhstovs chrestos {khrase-tos'} from 5530; employed, i.e. (by implication) useful (in manner or morals):--better, easy, good(-ness), gracious, kind. see GREEK for 5530

G5544.text: χρηστότης crhstovths chrestotes {khray-stot'-ace} from 5543; usefulness, i.e. morally, excellence (in character or demeanor):--gentleness, good(-ness), kindness. see GREEK for 5543

G5545.text: χρῖσμα cri'sma chrisma {khris'-mah} from 5548; an unguent or smearing, i.e. (figuratively) the special endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit:--anointing, unction. see GREEK for 5548

G5546.text: Χριστιανός Cristianovs Christianos {khris-tee-an-os'} from 5547; a Christian, i.e. follower of Christ:--Christian. see GREEK for 5547

G5547.text: Χριστός Cristovs Christos {khris-tos'} from 5548; anointed, i.e. the Messiah, an epithet of Jesus:--Christ. see GREEK for 5548

G5548.text: χρίω crivw chrio {khree'-o} probably akin to 5530 through the idea of contact; to smear or rub with oil, i.e. (by implication) to consecrate to an office or religious service:--anoint. see GREEK for 5530

G5549.text: χρονίζω cronivzw chronizo {khron-id'-zo} from 5550; to take time, i.e. linger:--delay, tarry. see GREEK for 5550

G5550.text: χρόνος crovnos chronos {khron'-os} of uncertain derivation; a space of time (in general, and thus properly distinguished from 2540, which designates a fixed or special occasion; and from 165, which denotes a particular period) or interval; by extension, an individual opportunity; by implication, delay:--+ years old, season, space, (X often-)time(-s), (a) while. see GREEK for 2540 see GREEK for 165

G5551.text: χρονοτριβέω cronotribevw chronotribeo {khron-ot-rib-eh'-o} from a presumed compound of 5550 and the base of 5147; to be a time-wearer, i.e. to procrastinate (linger):--spend time. see GREEK for 5550 see GREEK for 5147

G5552.text: χρυσοῦς crusou's chruseos {khroo'-seh-os} from 5557; made of gold:--of gold, golden. see GREEK for 5557

G5553.text: χρυσίον crusivon chrusion {khroo-see'-on} diminutive of 5557; a golden article, i.e. gold plating, ornament, or coin:--gold. see GREEK for 5557

G5554.text: χρυσοδακτύλιος crusodaktuvlios chrusodaktulios {khroo-sod-ak-too'-lee-os} from 5557 and 1146; gold-ringed, i.e. wearing a golden finger-ring or similar jewelry:--with a gold ring. see GREEK for 5557 see GREEK for 1146

G5555.text: χρυσόλιθος crusovliqos chrusolithos {khroo-sol'-ee-thos} from 5557 and 3037; gold-stone, i.e. a yellow gem ("chrysolite"):--chrysolite. see GREEK for 5557 see GREEK for 3037

G5556.text: χρυσόπρασος crusovprasos chrusoprasos {khroo-sop'-ras-os} from 5557 and prason (a leek); a greenish-yellow gem ("chrysoprase"):--chrysoprase. see GREEK for 5557

G5557.text: χρυσός crusovs chrusos {khroo-sos'} perhaps from the base of 5530 (through the idea of the utility of the metal); gold; by extension, a golden article, as an ornament or coin:--gold. see GREEK for 5530

G5558.text: χρυσόω crusovw chrusoo {khroo-so'-o} from 5557; to gild, i.e. bespangle with golden ornaments:--deck. see GREEK for 5557

G5559.text: χρώς crwvs chros {khroce} probably akin to the base of 5530 through the idea of handling; the body (properly, its surface or skin):--body. see GREEK for 5530

G5560.text: χωλός cwlovs cholos {kho-los'} apparently a primary word; "halt", i.e. limping:--cripple, halt, lame.

G5561.text: χώρα cwvra chora {kho'-rah} feminine of a derivative of the base of 5490 through the idea of empty expanse; room, i.e. a space of territory (more or less extensive; often including its inhabitants):--coast, county, fields, ground, land, region. Compare 5117. see GREEK for 5117 see GREEK for 5490

G5562.text: χωρέω cwrevw choreo {kho-reh'-o} from 5561; to be in (give) space, i.e. (intransitively) to pass, enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or figuratively):--come, contain, go, have place, (can, be room to) receive. see GREEK for 5561

G5563.text: χωρίζω cwrivzw chorizo {kho-rid'-zo} from 5561; to place room between, i.e. part; reflexively, to go away:--depart, put asunder, separate. see GREEK for 5561

G5564.text: χωρίον cwrivon chorion {kho-ree'-on} diminutive of 5561; a spot or plot of ground:--field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession. see GREEK for 5561

G5565.text: χωρίς cwrivs choris {kho-rece'} adverb from 5561; at a space, i.e. separately or apart from (often as preposition):--beside, by itself, without. see GREEK for 5561

G5566.text: χῶρος cw'ros choros {kho'-ros} of Latin origin; the north-west wind:--north west.

G5567.text: ψάλλω yavllw psallo {psal'-lo} probably strengthened from psao (to rub or touch the surface; compare 5597); to twitch or twang, i.e. to play on a stringed instrument (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes):--make melody, sing (psalms). see GREEK for 5597

G5568.text: ψαλμός yalmovs psalmos {psal-mos'} from 5567; a set piece of music, i.e. a sacred ode (accompanied with the voice, harp or other instrument; a "psalm"); collectively, the book of the Psalms:--psalm. Compare 5603. see GREEK for 5567 see GREEK for 5603

G5569.text: ψευδάδελφος yeudavdelfos pseudadelphos {psyoo-dad'-el-fos} from 5571 and 80; a spurious brother, i.e. pretended associate:--false brethren. see GREEK for 5571 see GREEK for 80

G5570.text: ψευδαπόστολος yeudapovstolos pseudapostolos {psyoo-dap-os'-tol-os} from 5571 and 652; a spurious apostle, i.e. pretended pracher:--false teacher. see GREEK for 5571 see GREEK for 652

G5571.text: ψευδής yeudhvs pseudes {psyoo-dace'} from 5574; untrue, i.e. erroneous, deceitful, wicked:--false, liar. see GREEK for 5574

G5572.text: ψευδοδιδάσκαλος yeudodidavskalos pseudodidaskalos {psyoo-dod-id-as'-kal-os} from 5571 and 1320; a spurious teacher, i.e. propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine:--false teacher. see GREEK for 5571 see GREEK for 1320

G5573.text: ψευδολόγος yeudolovgos pseudologos {psyoo-dol-og'-os} from 5571 and 3004; mendacious, i.e. promulgating erroneous Christian doctrine:--speaking lies. see GREEK for 5571 see GREEK for 3004

G5574.text: ψεύδομαι yeuvdomai pseudomai {psyoo'-dom-ahee} middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to utter an untruth or attempt to deceive by falsehood:--falsely, lie.

G5575.text: ψευδόμαρτυς yeudovmartus pseudomartur {psyoo-dom-ar'-toor} from 5571 and a kindred form of 3144; a spurious witness, i.e. bearer of untrue testimony:--false witness. see GREEK for 5571 see GREEK for 3144

G5576.text: ψευδομαρτυρέω yeudomarturevw pseudomartureo {psyoo-dom-ar-too-reh'-o} from 5575; to be an untrue testifier, i.e. offer falsehood in evidence:--be a false witness. see GREEK for 5575

G5577.text: ψευδομαρτυρία yeudomarturiva pseudomarturia {psyoo-dom-ar-too-ree'-ah} from 5575; untrue testimony:--false witness. see GREEK for 5575

G5578.text: ψευδοπροφήτης yeudoprofhvths pseudoprophetes {psyoo-dop-rof-ay'-tace} from 5571 and 4396; a spurious prophet, i.e. pretended foreteller or religious impostor:--false prophet. see GREEK for 5571 see GREEK for 4396

G5579.text: ψεῦδος yeu'dos pseudos {psyoo'-dos} from 5574; a falsehood:--lie, lying. see GREEK for 5574

G5580.text: ψευδόχριστος yeudovcristos pseudochristos {psyoo-dokh'-ris-tos} from 5571 and 5547; a spurious Messiah:--false Christ. see GREEK for 5571 see GREEK for 5547

G5581.text: ψευδώνυμος yeudwvnumos pseudonumos {psyoo-do'-noo-mos} from 5571 and 3686; untruly named:--falsely so called. see GREEK for 5571 see GREEK for 3686

G5582.text: ψεῦσμα yeu'sma pseusma {psyoos'-mah} from 5574; a fabrication, i.e. falsehood:--lie. see GREEK for 5574

G5583.text: ψεύστης yeuvsths pseustes {psyoos-tace'} from 5574; a falsifier:--liar. see GREEK for 5574

G5584.text: ψηλαφάω yhlafavw pselaphao {psay-laf-ah'-o} from the base of 5567 (compare 5586); to manipulate, i.e. verify by contact; figuratively, to search for:--feel after, handle, touch. see GREEK for 5567 see GREEK for 5586

G5585.text: ψηφίζω yhfivzw psephizo {psay-fid'-zo} from 5586; to use pebbles in enumeration, i.e. (generally) to compute:--count. see GREEK for 5586

G5586.text: ψῆφος yh'fos psephos {psay'-fos} from the same as 5584; a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote:--stone, voice. see GREEK for 5584

G5587.text: ψιθυρισμός yiqurismovs psithurismos {psith-oo-ris-mos'} from a derivative of psithos (a whisper; by implication, a slander; probably akin to 5574); whispering, i.e. secret detraction:--whispering. see GREEK for 5574

G5588.text: ψιθυριστής yiquristhvs psithuristes {psith-oo-ris-tace'} from the same as 5587; a secret calumniator:--whisperer. see GREEK for 5587

G5589.text: ψιχίον yicivon psichion {psikh-ee'-on} diminutive from a derivative of the base of 5567 (meaning a crumb); a little bit or morsel:--crumb. see GREEK for 5567

G5590.text: ψυχή yuchv psuche {psoo-khay'} from 5594; breath, i.e. (by implication) spirit, abstractly or concretely (the animal sentient principle only; thus distinguished on the one hand from 4151, which is the rational and immortal soul; and on the other from 2222, which is mere vitality, even of plants: these terms thus exactly correspond respectively to the Hebrew 5315, 7307 and 2416):--heart (+ -ily), life, mind, soul, + us, + you. see GREEK for 5594 see GREEK for 4151 see GREEK for 2222 see HEBREW for 05315 see HEBREW for 07307 see HEBREW for 02416

G5591.text: ψυχικός yucikovs psuchikos {psoo-khee-kos'} from 5590; sensitive, i.e. animate (in distinction on the one hand from 4152, which is the higher or renovated nature; and on the other from 5446, which is the lower or bestial nature):--natural, sensual. see GREEK for 5590 see GREEK for 4152 see GREEK for 5446

G5592.text: ψῦχος yu'cos psuchos {psoo'-khos} from 5594; coolness:--cold. see GREEK for 5594

G5593.text: ψυχρός yucrovs psuchros {psoo-chros'} from 5592; chilly (literally or figuratively):--cold. see GREEK for 5592

G5594.text: ψύχω yuvcw psucho {psoo'-kho} a primary verb; to breathe (voluntarily but gently, thus differing on the one hand from 4154, which denotes properly a forcible respiration; and on the other from the base of 109, which refers properly to an inanimate breeze), i.e. (by implication, of reduction of temperature by evaporation) to chill (figuratively):--wax cold. see GREEK for 4154 see GREEK for 109

G5595.text: ψωμίζω ywmivzw psomizo {pso-mid'-zo} from the base of 5596; to supply with bits, i.e. (generally) to nourish:--(bestow to) feed. see GREEK for 5596

G5596.text: ψωμίον ywmivon psomion {pso-mee'-on} diminutive from a derivative of the base of 5597; a crumb or morsel (as if rubbed off), i.e. a mouthful:--sop. see GREEK for 5597

G5597.text: ψώχω ywvcw psocho {pso'-kho} prolongation from the same base as 5567; to triturate, i.e. (by analogy) to rub out (kernels from husks with the fingers or hand):--rub. see GREEK for 5567

G5598.text: ὦ w\\ omega {o'-meg-ah} the last letter of the Greek alphabet, i.e. (figuratively) the finality:--Omega.

G5599.text: ὦ w\\ o {o} a primary interjection; as a sign of the vocative case, O; as a note of exclamation, oh:--O.

G5601.text: Ἰωβήλ Ἰωβήδ Ijwbhvl Ijwbhvd Obed {o-bade'} of Hebrew origin (5744); Obed, an Israelite:--Obed. see HEBREW for 05744

G5602.text: ὧδε w|de hode {ho'-deh} from an adverb form of 3592; in this same spot, i.e. here or hither:--here, hither, (in) this place, there. see GREEK for 3592

G5603.text: ᾠδή wj/dhv ode {o-day'} from 103; a chant or "ode" (the general term for any words sung; while 5215 denotes especially a religious metrical composition, and 5568 still more specially, a Hebrew cantillation):--song. see GREEK for 103 see GREEK for 5215 see GREEK for 5568

G5604.text: ὠδίν wjdivn odin {o-deen'} akin to 3601; a pang or throe, especially of childbirth:--pain, sorrow, travail. see GREEK for 3601

G5605.text: ὠδίνω wjdivnw odino {o-dee'-no} from 5604; to experience the pains of parturition (literally or figuratively):--travail in (birth). see GREEK for 5604

G5606.text: ὦμος w\\mos omos {o'-mos} perhaps from the alternate of 5342; the shoulder (as that on which burdens are borne):--shoulder. see GREEK for 5342

G5607.text: εἰμί εἰμιν eijmiv eijmin on {oan} 包含阴性ousa {oo'-sah} 及中性 on {on} ousa oo'-sah; and the neuter on on present participle of 1510; being:--be, come, have. see GREEK for 1510

G5608.text: ὠνέομαι wjnevomai oneomai {o-neh'-om-ahee} middle voice from an apparently primary onos (a sum or price); to purchase (synonymous with the earlier 4092):-- buy. see GREEK for 4092

G5609.text: ᾠόν wj/ovn oon {o-on'} apparently a primary word; an "egg":--egg.

G5610.text: ὥρα w&ra hora {ho'-rah} apparently a primary word; an "hour" (literally or figuratively):--day, hour, instant, season, X short, (even-)tide, (high) time.

G5611.text: ὡραῖος wJrai'os horaios {ho-rah'-yos} from 5610; belonging to the right hour or season (timely), i.e. (by implication) flourishing (beauteous (figuratively)):--beautiful. see GREEK for 5610

G5612.text: ὠρύομαι wjruvomai oruomai {o-roo'-om-ahee} middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to "roar":--roar.

G5613.text: ὡς wJs hos {hoce} probably adverb of comparative from 3739; which how, i.e. in that manner (very variously used, as follows):--about, after (that), (according) as (it had been, it were), as soon (as), even as (like), for, how (greatly), like (as, unto), since, so (that), that, to wit, unto, when(-soever), while, X with all speed. see GREEK for 3739

G5614.text: ὡσαννά wJsannav hosanna {ho-san-nah'} of Hebrew origin (3467 and 4994); oh save!; hosanna (i.e. hoshia-na), an exclamation of adoration:--hosanna. see HEBREW for 03467 see HEBREW for 04994

G5615.text: ὡσαύτως wJsauvtws hosautos {ho-sow'-toce} from 5613 and an adverb from 846; as thus, i.e. in the same way:--even so, likewise, after the same (in like) manner. see GREEK for 5613 see GREEK for 846

G5616.text: ὡσεί wJseiv hosei {ho-si'} from 5613 and 1487; as if:--about, as (it had been, it were), like (as). see GREEK for 5613 see GREEK for 1487

G5617.text: Ὡσηέ WJshev Hosee {ho-say-eh'} of Hebrew origin (1954); Hosee (i.e. Hoshea), an Israelite:--Osee. see HEBREW for 01954

G5618.text: ὥσπερ w&sper hosper {hoce'-per} from 5613 and 4007; just as, i.e. exactly like:--(even, like) as. see GREEK for 5613 see GREEK for 4007

G5619.text: ὡσπερεί wJspereiv hosperei {hoce-per-i'} from 5618 and 1487; just as if, i.e. as it were:--as. see GREEK for 5618 see GREEK for 1487

G5620.text: ὥστε w&ste hoste {hoce'-teh} from 5613 and 5037; so too, i.e. thus therefore (in various relations of consecution, as follow):--(insomuch) as, so that (then), (insomuch) that, therefore, to, wherefore. see GREEK for 5613 see GREEK for 5037

G5621.text: ὠτίον wjtivon otion {o-tee'-on} diminutive of 3775; an earlet, i.e. one of the ears, or perhaps the lobe of the ear:--ear. see GREEK for 3775

G5622.text: ὠφέλεια wjfevleia opheleia {o-fel'-i-ah} from a derivative of the base of 5624; usefulness, i.e. benefit:--advantage, profit. see GREEK for 5624

G5623.text: ὠφελέω wjfelevw opheleo {o-fel-eh'-o} from the same as 5622; to be useful, i.e. to benefit:--advantage, better, prevail, profit. see GREEK for 5622

G5624.text: ὠφέλιμος wjfevlimos ophelimos {o-fel'-ee-mos} from a form of 3786; helpful or serviceable, i.e. advantageous:--profit(-able). see GREEK for 3786
